<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Why Every Webex Developer Needs This Troubleshooting Guide (And Yes, Even You) ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt57f68b5616b283e5/68f291730e43824eb6c2cb64/Picture99.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Why Every Webex Developer Needs This Troubleshooting Guide (And Yes, Even You)" /> <p>Hey Webex Developers! Ever found yourself staring blankly at a HTTP 500 error or scratching your head over an SDK that just won&#39;t behave? You&#39;re not alone. When developing with the Webex APIs and SDKs, encountering technical issues is sometimes inevitable. </p> <p>Having a structured, comprehensive troubleshooting process is essential to quickly identify and resolve problems. The steps found in the <a data-type='internal' to='/meeting/docs/api/guides/troubleshooting'>Webex API Troubleshooting Guide</a> are designed to help developers methodically diagnose issues, minimize downtime, and facilitate effective communication with support teams. </p> <p>Below, we’re going to walk through the usefulness of this guide, and for good measure, we’ll run through a mock scenario to illustrate how following these steps leads to efficient problem resolution. </p> <h6>The Value of a Structured Troubleshooting Guide</h6><p>The troubleshooting guide is a vital resource for several key reasons:</p> <ul> <li>Systematic and Structured Process: It provides a clear, logical sequence for narrowing down the root cause of any issue. </li> <li>Comprehensive Coverage: The guide addresses all common sources of problems, including network connectivity, authentication, code changes, and API updates. </li> <li>Best Practices: It encourages the use of logs, up-to-date documentation, and sample apps to support effective troubleshooting.</li> <li>Support-Ready Documentation: By guiding you through the process of gathering and formatting information, it ensures that any support ticket you open is complete and actionable.</li> <li>Encourages Good Habits: Ensuring the inclusion of comprehensive logging, well-structured sample applications, and clear, detailed documentation will greatly benefit you in the future and streamline ongoing maintenance and development efforts.</li> </ul> <h6>Using the Troubleshooting Guide</h6><p>Consider this scenario: You are a developer integrating the Webex Browser SDK into a company’s internal Employee Portal. Everything&#39;s going fine...until you release a new build on Monday morning and your “Join Meeting” button suddenly does nothing. </p> <p>Instead of panic, you crack open the Webex Troubleshooting Guide and follow the playbook: </p> <ol> <li>Initial Check<ul> <li>First, you try joining the meeting via the Webex desktop app. Works perfectly. ✅ That means the core Webex service isn&#39;t the issue and the problem’s likely in the integration layer.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Question Recent Changes<ul> <li>Turns out, the Webex dev team upgraded the SDK version over the weekend. That’s a clue. 🕵️</li> </ul> </li> <li>Investigate and Review Docs<ul> <li>After checking the <a href='https://web-sdk.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Browser JS SDK documentation</a> change log, you see there was a breaking change in the meeting join method between versions. Oops.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Test Hypotheses with Minimal Calls<ul> <li>To confirm, you run a direct API call using the People API with the current access token:<br> <strong>GET</strong> <code>https://webexapis.com/v1/people/me</code></li> <li>The request fails revealing that the token had expired after the environment refresh.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Check Authentication Details<ul> <li>Following the guide’s Review Authentication section, you generate a fresh Client Secret and reauthorize the integration to get new Access and Refresh Tokens, followed by running the call again, and it passes. Now the SDK starts partially working… but the join UI still doesn’t load.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Log Capture and SDK Sample Testing<ul> <li>Next you enable debug logging (logLevel: &#39;debug&#39;) and compares their integration to the Kitchen Sink Sample App. The sample works fine with the same token, meaning the remaining issue is in your code implementation.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Isolate and Fix<ul> <li>Comparing the logs and code side-by-side, you spots the incorrect parameter: <code>joinMeeting</code> was renamed <code>meeting.join</code> in the updated SDK version. Quick change → works like a charm. 🎉</li> </ul> </li> </ol> <h6>Why This Worked (And Saved the Day)</h6><p>Following the Webex Troubleshooting Guide gave You…</p> <ul> <li>A logical sequence to follow instead of guessing.</li> <li>Checkpoints that progressively narrowed the issue’s scope.</li> <li>Concrete tests that separated “Webex issue” from “my code issue.” </li> <li>The right tools and links (docs, changelogs, SDK samples, and logging details) at the exact moment they were needed.</li> </ul> <h6>The Power of the Reporting Template</h6><p>But wait! What if it’s not fixed? The guide’s Developer Support template would have provided detailed logs, reproduction steps, and tracking IDs so the support team could jump straight to the root cause without back-and-forth emails. Instead of sending a cryptic email (“webex broke pls help”), you submit a beautifully detailed ticket: </p> <p><em>Description</em> </p> <p><em>After upgrading the Webex Browser SDK from v1.8.0 to v1.9.2, the &quot;Join Meeting&quot; button within our internal meeting tool is unresponsive. No errors are shown in the UI. The same meetings can be joined successfully from the standalone Webex desktop and mobile apps.</em></p> <p><em>Environment:</em></p> <p><em>Device Type/Model: Dell XPS 13 (2023)</em> </p> <p><em>OS: Windows 11 Pro, 23H2</em> </p> <p><em>Software type, name, and/or version:</em> </p> <ul> <li><em>Custom internal meeting tool using Webex Browser JS SDK v1.9.2</em> </li> <li><em>Google Chrome v126.0.6478.63 (64-bit)</em></li> </ul> <p><em>Tester/Affected User: Jamie Smith, <a href='mailto:jamie.smith@example.com' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>jamie.smith@example.com</a></em> </p> <p><em>Connection Type/Strength: Corporate gigabit Ethernet via VPN</em> </p> <p><em>Rate of Reproduction:</em> </p> <p><em>Continuous. Issue occurs 100% of the time after SDK upgrade.</em> </p> <p><em>Prerequisites:</em> </p> <ul> <li><em>Access token obtained from OAuth integration.</em> </li> <li><em>Meeting must already exist and be joinable through Webex desktop app.</em></li> </ul> <p><em>Expected Results:</em> <em>Clicking &quot;Join Meeting&quot; triggers</em> <code>webex.meetings.join()</code> <em>and opens the meeting window in-browser, connecting the authenticated user to the meeting.</em> </p> <p><em>Observed Results:</em> <em>UI remains unchanged after clicking &quot;Join Meeting.&quot;</em></p> <p><em>API GET request to</em> <code>https://webexapis.com/v1/people/me</code> <em>initially failed with</em> <code>401 Unauthorized</code> <em>due to expired access token; after refreshing token, requests succeed but join action still fails.</em></p> <p><em>Attached Logs and Other Supporting Materials:</em></p> <ul> <li><em>HAR file from Chrome Developer Tools captured during reproduction (attached as</em> <code>join-meeting-issue.har</code>)<em>.</em> </li> <li><em>Debug log excerpt showing &quot;meetings.join() function is failing&quot; after SDK upgrade.</em> </li> <li><em>Side-by-side code snippet comparison from internal tool vs. Kitchen Sink sample app showing usage of the meetings.join() function.</em> </li> <li><em>Screen recording of reproduction steps (hosted at</em> <code>https://vidcast.io/example-join-meeting-issue</code><em>).</em></li> <li><em>Screenshot of Chrome console error attached as</em> <code>console-error.png</code><em>.</em></li> </ul> <p>With all of these details provided Webex Developer Support sees the trackingID, reviews the logs, and quickly spots the problem. Resolution time: minutes, not days.</p> <h6>Pro Tips for Using the Guide</h6><ul> <li>Bookmark it: you will need it again. We promise.</li> <li>Always run the &quot;Initial Check&quot; first: it’s a lightning-fast way to isolate issues.</li> <li>Use the API and SDK samples: they’re not just demos, they’re diagnostic tools.</li> <li>Capture logs early: they’re gold for both self-debugging and support escalation.</li> </ul> <h6>Final Word</h6><p>Debugging Webex integrations doesn’t have to be frustrating. The Webex Troubleshooting Guide gives you a repeatable, proven process for solving issues faster while making sure that if needed, you’ll be providing our support team with exactly what they need to assist you. </p> <p>So next time things go sideways? Grab your coffee, fire up the guide, and get back to building awesome Webex-powered experiences in record time. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Announcing The Official Webex Postman Workspace ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbfd70d890e89fae6/66b24336bc06cc2e3e6bdc12/flowdesigner_evolvecx-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Announcing The Official Webex Postman Workspace" /> <div><Callout type="info">This blog post was co-authored with Senior Technical Leader, Arun Ganeshan</Callout></div> <p>For developers working with Webex APIs, the typical starting point is the <a data-type='internal' to='/'>Webex for Developers Portal</a>. It&#39;s a fantastic resource with comprehensive documentation and a handy &quot;Try It&quot; feature to test API calls directly in the browser. But what if you could take your API exploration and development to the next level?</p> <p>Enter the official <a href='https://www.postman.com/webexdev/webex-public-workspace' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Public Workspace on Postman</a>. This curated collection of Postman resources is a game-changer for anyone building with Webex. It’s more than just a list of endpoints; it’s a complete development environment that can significantly streamline your workflow.</p> <p>This blog post will explore the key advantages of using the Webex Postman collection and how it can make you a more efficient and effective Webex developer.</p> <h6>Postman vs. developer.webex.com: A Better &quot;Try It&quot; Experience</h6><p>While the &quot;Try It&quot; feature on the developer portal is great for quick, one-off tests, it has its limitations. Postman elevates this experience in several crucial ways:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Persistent Environments:</strong> Postman allows you to save variables, authentication tokens, and other settings in environments. No more re-entering your bearer token for every single API call. Set it once in your environment, and Postman handles the rest.</li> <li><strong>Complex Workflows:</strong> You can chain multiple API requests together to simulate real-world scenarios. For example, you can create a room, add a user to it, and then send a message, all in a sequence that can be saved and re-run with a single click.</li> <li><strong>Code Generation:</strong> Postman can automatically generate code snippets for your API requests in various languages (cURL, Python, Node.js, etc.). This is a huge time-saver when you&#39;re ready to move from exploration to building your application.</li> <li><strong>Collaboration:</strong> Postman workspaces are built for teamwork. You can share collections, environments, and test results with your colleagues, ensuring everyone is on the same page.</li> </ul> <h6>The Power of the OpenAPI Specification in Postman</h6><p>Since the Webex team builds their API specifications using the OpenAPI standard, when this is exported into Postman, it provides several benefits:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Automatic Collection Generation:</strong> The entire Webex API collection in the public workspace is generated directly from the official OpenAPI spec. This means it&#39;s always up-to-date and accurately reflects the current state of the APIs.</li> <li><strong>Structured and Searchable:</strong> The collection is neatly organized, with every endpoint, parameter, and request body clearly defined. You can easily search for the specific API you need and see all the required and optional parameters at a glance.</li> <li><strong>Built-in Documentation:</strong> The documentation for each API call is embedded directly within Postman, right where you need it. No more switching back and forth between your testing tool and the documentation website.</li> </ul> <h6>The Importance of the Postman Public Network</h6><p>By hosting their collection on the Postman Public Network, the Webex team has made it incredibly easy for developers to get started.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Discoverability:</strong> Developers can easily find the official Webex collection by searching on Postman. This increases the visibility and adoption of the Webex platform.</li> <li><strong>One-Click Access:</strong> You can &quot;fork&quot; the collection into your own Postman workspace with a single click. This creates a copy that you can modify and experiment with, while still being able to pull in updates from the original collection.</li> <li><strong>Community and Feedback:</strong> The public workspace fosters a sense of community. You can see how others are using the APIs, and it provides a channel for providing feedback to the Webex team.</li> </ul> <h6>Other Advantages</h6><ul> <li><strong>Automated Testing:</strong> Postman has a powerful test runner that allows you to write scripts to validate the responses of your API calls. You can create a suite of tests to ensure that your integrations are working as expected.</li> <li><strong>Mock Servers:</strong> You can create mock servers in Postman to simulate the Webex APIs. This is incredibly useful for frontend development or for testing your application when you don&#39;t have a live connection to the Webex services.</li> <li><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Postman allows you to set up monitors that will run your collections at a specified interval. This can be used to check the health of the Webex APIs or to ensure that your own integrations are still functioning correctly.</li> </ul> <h6>Getting Started: Your First Steps with the Webex Postman Collection</h6><p>Alright, you&#39;re convinced, right? Now, let&#39;s get you hands-on with the Webex Public Workspace on Postman. It&#39;s incredibly easy to get up and running, and you&#39;ll be making API calls in minutes.</p> <p>Here’s a quick guide to kick off your Webex API journey with Postman:</p> <h6>Step 1: Find the Webex Public Workspace</h6><p>First things first, you need to access the Webex Public Workspace. You can do this in a couple of ways:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Direct Link:</strong> The easiest way is to use the direct link: <a href='https://www.postman.com/webexdev/webex-public-workspace' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://www.postman.com/webexdev/webex-public-workspace</a>. Just click it, and it will open the workspace directly in your Postman desktop app or web client (if you&#39;re logged in).</li> <li><strong>Search in Postman:</strong> Open your Postman application. In the top bar, you can search for &quot;Webex Public Workspace&quot; to find the official workspace.</li> </ul> <p>Once you&#39;re in the Webex Public Workspace, you&#39;ll see a variety of collections. For our first steps, we&#39;ll focus on the &quot;Webex Messaging&quot; collection, as it contains the APIs we&#39;ll use for our initial tests.</p> <h6>Step 2: Fork a Collection (Make it Your Own!)</h6><p>This is a crucial step! When you &quot;fork&quot; a collection, you&#39;re essentially creating your own personal, editable copy of it in your private Postman workspace. This allows you to experiment, modify requests, and save your work without affecting the original public collection.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Locate the &quot;Webex Messaging&quot; Collection:</strong> In the Webex Public Workspace, find the <strong>&quot;Webex Messaging&quot;</strong> collection and select it.</li> <li><strong>Click the &quot;Fork&quot; Button:</strong> Hover over the collection name or click the ellipsis (...) next to it. You should see a &quot;Fork&quot; button or option. Click it!</li> <li><strong>Choose Your Workspace:</strong> A dialog box will appear asking you to select the workspace where you want to fork the collection. Choose your personal workspace.</li> <li><strong>Name Your Fork (Optional):</strong> You can give your forked collection a custom name if you wish, but the default is usually fine.</li> <li><strong>Select the Environment (Optional):</strong> Select the “Webex Prod US1” environment for seamless connection to Webex servers.</li> <li><strong>Hit &quot;Fork Collection&quot;:</strong> Confirm your choice, and Postman will create a copy in your selected workspace.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Pro-Tip:</strong> The &quot;Webex Messaging&quot; collection is a great starting point, but feel free to explore and fork other collections like &quot;Webex Meetings&quot; or &quot;Webex Calling&quot; as you dive deeper!</p> <h6>Step 3: Set Up Your Authentication Token</h6><p>Remember how I mentioned simplified authentication? This is where it pays off! You&#39;ll need a Webex access token to make authenticated API calls.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Get Your Webex Token:</strong> If you don&#39;t have one already, head over to the <a data-type='internal' to='/'>Webex for Developers Portal</a>. Log in with your Webex account, and it will generate a temporary bearer token for you. Copy this token.</li> <li><strong>Open Your Forked Collection:</strong> In your personal Postman workspace, navigate to the forked collection you just created (e.g., &quot;Webex Messaging&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Go to the &quot;Variables&quot; Tab:</strong> Click on the name of your forked collection in the left sidebar. Then, in the main Postman window, select the <strong>&quot;Variables&quot;</strong> tab.</li> <li><strong>Add Your Token:</strong> Create a variable named <code>access_token</code>. Paste your copied bearer token from the developer portal into the <strong>&quot;Value&quot;</strong> column for this variable.</li> <li><strong>Update Auth:</strong> Change the “Auth Type” field to “Bearer Token”, and in the “Token” field type <code>{{access_token}}</code> (which tells Postman to use your variable you just created).</li> </ul> <p>That&#39;s it! The collection is pre-configured to use this environment variable for all its requests, so you won&#39;t have to paste your token into every single API call.</p> <h6>Step 4: Make Your First Webex API Call!</h6><p>Now for the fun part – let&#39;s make an API call!</p> <ul> <li><strong>Expand Your Collection:</strong> In the left sidebar, expand your forked &quot;Webex Messaging&quot; collection to see the folders and individual API requests.</li> <li><strong>Choose a Simple Request:</strong> I recommend starting with something simple and safe, like:<ul> <li><code>GET Get My Own Details</code> (found under the <strong>&quot;People API&quot;</strong> folder) - This is <code>GET /v1/people/me</code> and will retrieve details about your own Webex user account.</li> <li><code>GET List Rooms</code> (found under the <strong>&quot;Rooms API&quot;</strong> folder) - This is <code>GET /v1/rooms</code> and will list the Webex spaces (rooms) you are a part of.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Click &quot;Send&quot;:</strong> Select the request you want to make, and then click the blue <strong>&quot;Send&quot;</strong> button in the main Postman window.</li> <li><strong>Check the Response:</strong> If everything is set up correctly, you should see a successful response (usually a <strong>200 OK</strong> status) in the response pane at the bottom, along with the JSON data returned by the Webex API.</li> </ul> <p>Congratulations! You&#39;ve successfully used the Webex Postman Collection to make your first API call.</p> <p>From here, explore other requests, chain them together, and start seeing how powerful this collection is for your Webex development.</p> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>The Webex Public Workspace on Postman is an indispensable tool for any developer working with Webex APIs. It provides a rich, interactive environment that goes far beyond the basic &quot;Try It&quot; functionality of the developer portal. By leveraging the power of Postman, you can accelerate your development, improve the quality of your integrations, and become a more proficient Webex developer.</p> <p>So, head over to the <a href='https://www.postman.com/webexdev/webex-public-workspace' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Public Workspace</a>, fork the collection, and start exploring the world of Webex APIs in a whole new way!</p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – September 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – September 2025" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers! We have another round of new content and events for you to discover this month. Read on to get all the latest updates and community announcements for the full Webex Developer ecosystem.</p> <h6>📺 Public Developer Webinar: Discover and Build with Webex Service Apps</h6><p>On Wednesday, October 22<sup>nd</sup> at 1:00PM EDT, join our next public webinar to simplify your Webex API development and resolve common issues more effectively. We will explore the newly published <a data-type='internal' to='/explore/docs/api/guides/troubleshooting'>Webex API Troubleshooting Guide</a>, offering developers practical strategies to quickly diagnose and fix problems. This session will cover how to understand error codes, troubleshoot API request failures, authorization, and rate limiting issues. We will also go over best practices for preventing issues and using essential tools for quicker solutions. Whether you&#39;re a new or experienced Webex developer, this webinar will help you build more reliable integrations with confidence. Register now to become a Webex API troubleshooting expert!</p> <p>If you can’t make it to the live session, no problem! You can watch all our previous webinar recordings on-demand, including the most recent one, <strong>Building with the Webex Mobile SDK - Introduction and Key Flavors</strong>, right on our webinars page. Come and explore our growing library!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <h6>🧑🏽‍🔧 Using WebSockets with the Webex JavaScript SDK</h6><p>In an updated blog post by Dev Support Engineering Leader, Janos Benyovszki, learn how to leverage WebSockets in the Webex JavaScript SDK to maintain persistent connections and allow direct communication with the Webex API. This approach can also be an effective solution if your app needs to run behind a corporate firewall or in restrictive environments. In this blog, Janos walks us through creating and using WebSockets with the SDK to listen for events sent from Webex, and have your application react accordingly.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/using-websockets-with-the-webex-javascript-sdk'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🏋️‍♀️ Webex Academy Training Program at WebexOne 2025 in San Diego</h6><p>Register for WebexOne 2025 in San Diego that takes places on SEP 28 - OCT 1 and join the Webex Academy Training Program! With the Conference Pass + Training ticket, you get access to 4 days of in-person technical training classes and hands-on labs, plus Cisco Continuing Education credits for your participation. After the event, you’ll also get exclusive access to all the classes on-demand.</p> <p>Get a 50% discount with promo code: <strong>WX1ACADEMY50</strong></p> <p><a href='https://www.webexone.com/training.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register today →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Now in the Developer βeta Program - Webex Contact Center Widgets</h6><p>Simplify your contact center integration with Webex Contact Center Widgets—a collection of ready-to-use, modular components designed to seamlessly bring contact center functionalities into any third-party web application. These widgets eliminate the need for customers to build and manage their own UI components or handle the complexities of API interactions and business logic, letting you focus on delivering exceptional user experiences. Join the public beta to get early access today!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>🗝️ Service Apps Token Management: A Developer&#39;s Guide to Automation</h6><p>Devices in the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series have very flexible administration capabilities via the Webex Calling APIs, to automate lifecycle management, customization, and post-activation configurations on devices. In a new blog, Senior Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti, highlights some key distinctions between Cisco 9800-series phones and Cisco MPP devices, to clarify some of the notable differences in how they are respectively set up and managed. Phil also goes through all the Webex APIs for the 9800 Series and groups them into specific feature categories for easier understanding and usage.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/service-app-token-management-a-developer-s-guide-to-automation'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📝 Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>Highlighting some important updates recently listed in the Webex API Changelogs:</p> <ul> <li><strong>UPDATED IN WEBEX CONTACT CENTER–</strong> September 10, 2025: We have added a new field <code>alg</code> to the public key schema used in the Bring Your Own Device Service BYODS framework. This is an additive change that maintains backward compatibility.<ul> <li><strong>Added Field:</strong> <code>alg</code> - Algorithm identifier for the public key</li> <li><strong>Location:</strong> Public key objects within the BYODS framework</li> <li><strong>Type:</strong> String (expected values may include standard algorithm identifiers like &quot;RS256&quot;, &quot;ES256&quot;, etc.)</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Full Webex Contact Center API Changelog →</a> </p> <ul> <li><p><strong>WARNING FOR THE WEBEX APIs</strong>– September 8, 2025: We&#39;ve implemented stricter validation for API request headers. If your API calls suddenly stop working and you haven&#39;t made any changes on your end, please double-check your headers for correctness. Requests with incorrect or missing headers will now be rejected.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>BREAKING CHANGE FOR THE WEBEX APIs</strong>– September 10, 2025: We will follow a stricter implementation for the JWT guest token to follow the standards more closely. Previously a string was accepted in the exp field to indicate when the token expires. We are changing this field to allow an Integer only and this change will be enforced <em>Nov 1, 2025</em>. You can make the change right now as today both string and int will be accepted.</p> </li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/api/changelog/webex-admin'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Service App Token Management: A Developer's Guide to Automation ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf7c86f81d8ba3ecd/689a3184f5baf53e9f692078/service-app-token-management-blog.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Service App Token Management: A Developer's Guide to Automation" /> <p>If you&#39;re building Webex applications with service apps—whether for contact center integrations, meeting scheduler apps, messaging applications, or data source management—you&#39;ve likely encountered the same challenge: <strong>service app tokens expire, and manual token refresh doesn&#39;t scale</strong>.</p> <p>Today, we&#39;ll explore practical strategies for automating service app token management, using our recently enhanced <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>BYODS management tool</a> as a reference implementation that you can adapt for any service app scenario.</p> <h6>The Universal Service App Challenge</h6><p>Service apps are powerful because they operate independently of user sessions, making them perfect for:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Contact Center integrations</strong> that need 24/7 operation</li> <li><strong>Meeting scheduler apps</strong> that manage scheduled meetings automatically</li> <li><strong>Messaging applications</strong> that respond to events</li> <li><strong>Data source management</strong> for analytics and AI applications</li> <li><strong>Workflow automation</strong> that runs unattended</li> </ul> <p>But here&#39;s the universal problem: <strong>service app tokens expire</strong>. When they do, your application stops working until someone manually intervenes.</p> <h6>The Token Refresh Architecture Every Service App Needs</h6><p>The solution requires understanding that <strong>you need two different Webex applications</strong> working together:</p> <h6>Your Service App (The Worker)</h6><p>This is your main application that does the actual work—managing data sources, sending messages, joining meetings, etc.</p> <h6>A Token Manager Integration (The Refresher)</h6><p>This is a separate OAuth integration whose sole purpose is to refresh your service app tokens using the <a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/service-apps'>Applications API</a>.</p> <p>Here&#39;s why you need both, illustrated with our BYODS tool&#39;s configuration:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;serviceApp&quot;: { &quot;appId&quot;: &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL0FQUExJQ0FUSU9OL...&quot;, &quot;clientId&quot;: &quot;C6bf3862a86d0deb6f7dadfb88f548e6c...&quot;, &quot;clientSecret&quot;: &quot;786ecee3ed337ddea578adbc42f65f5b...&quot;, &quot;targetOrgId&quot;: &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL09SR0FOSVpBVElPTi8...&quot; }, &quot;tokenManager&quot;: { &quot;personalAccessToken&quot;: &quot;YzdhODg5M2ItYjRiMS00NTI2LWE3MDUtOTI0Y2NlZmZh...&quot;, &quot;integration&quot;: { &quot;clientId&quot;: &quot;Cb547075e258bcb63d2008d61c17e3038...&quot;, &quot;clientSecret&quot;: &quot;4bf699aa9ca098aab75b8c4ad0971d1a...&quot;, &quot;refreshToken&quot;: &quot;MDU1NWNjZDUtYjU1ZC00ZWZjLTg1ZTEtYTFlMDM1YmU3M2E5...&quot; } } } </code></pre> <br/> <h6>Implementation Strategy: A Three-Tier Approach</h6><p>Our BYODS tool demonstrates a robust three-tier refresh strategy that you can adapt for any service app:</p> <h6>Tier 1: Service App Refresh Tokens (Fastest)</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python">def _refresh_with_refresh_token(self, refresh_token: str) -&gt; str: &quot;&quot;&quot;Use service app refresh token - fastest method&quot;&quot;&quot; url = &quot;https://webexapis.com/v1/access_token&quot; headers = {&#39;Content-Type&#39;: &#39;application/x-www-form-urlencoded&#39;} data = { &#39;grant_type&#39;: &#39;refresh_token&#39;, &#39;client_id&#39;: service_app[&#39;clientId&#39;], &#39;client_secret&#39;: service_app[&#39;clientSecret&#39;], &#39;refresh_token&#39;: refresh_token } response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=data) # Handle response and update stored tokens </code></pre> <p>When you first obtain service app tokens, you get both an access token and a refresh token. The refresh token can be used to get new access tokens without external dependencies.</p> <h6>Tier 2: Applications API with Personal Token</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python">def _refresh_with_personal_token(self) -&gt; str: &quot;&quot;&quot;Use Applications API when refresh token expires&quot;&quot;&quot; url = f&quot;https://webexapis.com/v1/applications/{service_app[&#39;appId&#39;]}/token&quot; headers = { &#39;Authorization&#39;: f&quot;Bearer {personal_token}&quot;, &#39;Content-Type&#39;: &#39;application/json&#39; } payload = { &#39;clientId&#39;: service_app[&#39;clientId&#39;], &#39;clientSecret&#39;: service_app[&#39;clientSecret&#39;], &#39;targetOrgId&#39;: service_app[&#39;targetOrgId&#39;] } response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload) # Returns fresh access and refresh tokens </code></pre> <p>This uses the <a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/api/v1/applications/get-application-token'>Applications API</a> to get completely fresh service app tokens. The key requirement: you need a token with <code>spark:applications_token</code> scope to authenticate this request.</p> <h6>Tier 3: OAuth Integration Refresh</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python">def _refresh_personal_token_oauth(self, integration_config: Dict) -&gt; str: &quot;&quot;&quot;Auto-refresh the personal token used for Applications API&quot;&quot;&quot; url = &quot;https://webexapis.com/v1/access_token&quot; data = { &#39;grant_type&#39;: &#39;refresh_token&#39;, &#39;client_id&#39;: integration_config[&#39;clientId&#39;], &#39;client_secret&#39;: integration_config[&#39;clientSecret&#39;], &#39;refresh_token&#39;: integration_config[&#39;refreshToken&#39;] } # Keeps the Applications API token fresh automatically </code></pre> <p>This automatically refreshes the token used to call the Applications API, creating a fully autonomous system.</p> <h6>The Smart Refresh Logic</h6><p>Here&#39;s how to orchestrate these tiers for maximum reliability:</p> <pre><code class="language-python">def refresh_token(self) -&gt; str: &quot;&quot;&quot;Smart refresh with automatic fallback&quot;&quot;&quot; # Try service app refresh token first (fastest) current_refresh_token = self._get_current_refresh_token() if current_refresh_token: try: return self._refresh_with_refresh_token(current_refresh_token) except Exception as e: print(f&quot;Refresh token failed, falling back: {e}&quot;) # Fallback to Applications API (with auto-refresh of personal token) return self._refresh_with_personal_token() </code></pre> <p>This approach ensures your service app keeps running even when individual token types expire.</p> <h6>Setting Up Your Token Manager Integration</h6><p>The key to automation is creating a proper token manager integration. Our BYODS tool includes an OAuth helper that demonstrates the process:</p> <h6>Step 1: Create the Integration</h6><p>At <a data-type='internal' to='/'>developer.webex.com</a>:</p> <ol> <li>Create a new <strong>Integration</strong> (not service app)</li> <li>Set redirect URI to <code>http://localhost:3000/callback</code></li> <li><strong>Critical</strong>: Add <code>spark:applications_token</code> scope</li> <li>Save and note the client ID and secret</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Step 2: OAuth Authorization Flow</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python"># Build authorization URL auth_params = { &#39;client_id&#39;: client_id, &#39;response_type&#39;: &#39;code&#39;, &#39;redirect_uri&#39;: &#39;http://localhost:3000/callback&#39;, &#39;scope&#39;: &#39;spark:applications_token&#39;, &#39;state&#39;: &#39;token_manager_setup&#39; } auth_url = &quot;https://webexapis.com/v1/authorize?&quot; + urllib.parse.urlencode(auth_params) </code></pre> <br/> <h6>Step 3: Exchange Code for Tokens</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python"># After user authorizes, exchange code for tokens token_data = { &#39;grant_type&#39;: &#39;authorization_code&#39;, &#39;client_id&#39;: client_id, &#39;client_secret&#39;: client_secret, &#39;code&#39;: auth_code, &#39;redirect_uri&#39;: &#39;http://localhost:3000/callback&#39; } response = requests.post(&#39;https://webexapis.com/v1/access_token&#39;, data=token_data) tokens = response.json() # Store both access_token and refresh_token </code></pre> <br/> <h6>Adapting This Pattern to Your Service App</h6><p>The patterns demonstrated in our BYODS tool apply to any service app scenario:</p> <h6>For Contact Center Integrations:</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python"># Your contact center service app tokens service_app_config = { &quot;appId&quot;: &quot;your_contact_center_service_app_id&quot;, &quot;clientId&quot;: &quot;your_cc_client_id&quot;, &quot;clientSecret&quot;: &quot;your_cc_client_secret&quot;, &quot;targetOrgId&quot;: &quot;your_org_id&quot; } # Separate integration for token refresh token_manager = TokenManager(service_app_config) fresh_token = token_manager.refresh_token() </code></pre> <h6>For Meeting Scheduler Applications:</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-python"># Meeting scheduler service app meeting_scheduler_config = { &quot;appId&quot;: &quot;your_meeting_scheduler_app_id&quot;, # ... other config } # Same refresh pattern works if not is_token_valid(current_token): current_token = refresh_service_app_token() </code></pre> <br/> <h6>For Messaging Applications:</h6><p>The same principles apply—separate your working service app from your token refresh integration.</p> <h6>Storage and Security Considerations</h6><p>Our BYODS tool demonstrates secure token storage patterns:</p> <h6>Environment Variables for Runtime Tokens</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-bash"># Current working tokens (can change frequently) WEBEX_SERVICE_APP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_current_access_token WEBEX_SERVICE_APP_REFRESH_TOKEN=your_current_refresh_token </code></pre> <br/> <h6>Configuration File for OAuth Credentials</h6><br/> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;serviceApp&quot;: { /* Service app credentials */ }, &quot;tokenManager&quot;: { &quot;integration&quot;: { /* OAuth integration credentials */ } } } </code></pre> <p><strong>Key security practices:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Never commit actual tokens to version control</li> <li>Use environment variables for runtime tokens</li> <li>Keep OAuth credentials in separate, secure configuration</li> <li>Rotate OAuth refresh tokens periodically</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Monitoring and Alerting</h6><p>Implement monitoring for your token refresh system:</p> <pre><code class="language-python">def refresh_with_monitoring(self) -&gt; str: &quot;&quot;&quot;Refresh with monitoring and alerting&quot;&quot;&quot; try: new_token = self.refresh_token() # Log success self.log_refresh_success() return new_token except Exception as e: # Alert on failure self.alert_refresh_failure(str(e)) raise </code></pre> <p>Consider alerting when:</p> <ul> <li>Service app refresh tokens fail</li> <li>Applications API calls fail</li> <li>OAuth refresh tokens expire</li> <li>Multiple refresh attempts fail</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Testing Your Implementation</h6><p>The BYODS tool includes validation methods you can adapt:</p> <pre><code class="language-python">def is_token_valid(self) -&gt; bool: &quot;&quot;&quot;Test token validity against appropriate endpoint&quot;&quot;&quot; try: headers = {&#39;Authorization&#39;: f&#39;Bearer {current_token}&#39;} # Use an endpoint your service app actually needs response = requests.get(&#39;https://webexapis.com/v1/dataSources&#39;, headers=headers) return response.status_code == 200 except Exception: return False </code></pre> <p><strong>Important</strong>: Test against endpoints your service app actually uses, not generic endpoints like <code>/people/me</code>.</p> <h6>Sample Implementation</h6><p>You can study the complete implementation in our <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webex-byods-manager repository</a>. Key files to examine:</p> <ul> <li><code>token_manager.py</code> - Core refresh logic and multi-tier strategy</li> <li><code>setup_oauth.py</code> - OAuth integration setup helper</li> <li><code>refresh_token.py</code> - Manual refresh script for testing</li> <li><code>TOKEN_MANAGEMENT.md</code> - Complete setup documentation</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Beyond BYODS: Universal Patterns</h6><p>These patterns work for any Webex service app:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Webex Contact Center</strong>: Managing agent states, handling customer interactions</li> <li><strong>Meeting Applications</strong>: Managing scheduled meetings, handling meeting resources</li> <li><strong>Messaging Bots</strong>: Responding to messages, managing spaces</li> <li><strong>Analytics Platforms</strong>: Collecting usage data, generating reports</li> <li><strong>Workflow Automation</strong>: Triggering actions based on events</li> </ul> <p>The core principle remains the same: <strong>separate your working service app from your token refresh mechanism</strong>.</p> <h6>Getting Started</h6><ol> <li><strong>Examine the reference implementation</strong> in the BYODS tool</li> <li><strong>Create your token manager integration</strong> with <code>spark:applications_token</code> scope</li> <li><strong>Implement the three-tier refresh strategy</strong> for your service app</li> <li><strong>Set up monitoring and alerting</strong> for token refresh failures</li> <li><strong>Test thoroughly</strong> in development before deploying</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>Service app token management doesn&#39;t have to be a manual burden. By implementing a proper refresh architecture—separating your working service app from your token refresh integration—you can build Webex applications that run autonomously and reliably.</p> <p>The patterns demonstrated in our BYODS management tool provide a roadmap for any service app developer. Whether you&#39;re building contact center solutions, meeting scheduler apps, or data analytics platforms, these token management strategies will help you move from proof-of-concept to production-ready applications.</p> <hr> <p><em>Ready to implement robust token management in your service app? Check out the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webex-byods-manager repository</a> for a complete reference implementation, and join the discussion in the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Community</a>.</em></p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – August 2025 ]]>

</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – August 2025" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers. This month is chock-full of new content and events for you to discover. Get all the latest updates and community announcements for the entire Webex Developer ecosystem right here!</p> <h6>📺 Public Webinar: Unleash the Full Potential of Your Apps with the Webex Contact Center SDK</h6><p>On Wednesday, August 20<sup>th</sup> at 1:00PM EDT, join us for an interactive webinar where we demonstrate how Webex Contact Center SDK can transform the way you build and manage contact center solutions for your better customer experience. Through a live coding session, you’ll learn how to seamlessly integrate the SDK into any third-party application and leverage powerful features like Agent Station Login using various modes, managing incoming tasks across voice and digital channels, and utilizing key controls such as hold/resume, pause/resume recording, consult, transfer, and task wrap-up.</p> <p>If you can’t make it to the live session, no problem! You can watch all our previous webinar recordings on-demand, including the most recent one, <strong>A Deep Dive into the New Webex Developer Portal and AI Assistant</strong>, right on our webinars page. Come and explore our growing library!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Now in the Developer βeta Program - Webex Contact Center Widgets</h6><p>Simplify your contact center integration with Webex Contact Center Widgets—a collection of ready-to-use, modular components designed to seamlessly bring contact center functionalities into any third-party web application. These widgets eliminate the need for customers to build and manage their own UI components or handle the complexities of API interactions and business logic, letting you focus on delivering exceptional user experiences. Join the public beta to get early access today!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>🏋️‍♀️ Webex Academy Training Program at WebexOne 2025 in San Diego</h6><p>Register for WebexOne 2025 in San Diego that takes places on SEP 28 - OCT 1 and join the Webex Academy Training Program! With the Conference Pass + Training ticket, you get access to 4 days of in-person technical training classes and hands-on labs, plus Cisco Continuing Education credits for your participation. After the event, you’ll also get exclusive access to all the classes on-demand.</p> <p>Get a 50% discount with promo code: <strong>WX1ACADEMY50</strong></p> <p><a href='https://www.webexone.com/training.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register today →</a></p> <h6>🪤 The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Captures API</h6><p>The data associated with actions performed by Webex Contact Center agents are often recorded &amp; stored by Webex and made available to developers with access to various APIs that consume the data. In a latest edition of the &quot;A - Z of Contact Center APIs&quot; series, Developer Evangelist, Joe Zanini, explores the <strong>Captures API</strong>, that enables integrations to automate the retrieval of telephony recordings, email transcripts, and task events all with minimal manual effort.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📞 Webex APIs for the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series</h6><p>Devices in the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series have very flexible administration capabilities via the Webex Calling APIs, to automate lifecycle management, customization, and post-activation configurations on devices. In a new blog, Senior Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti, highlights some key distinctions between Cisco 9800-series phones and Cisco MPP devices, to clarify some of the notable differences in how they are respectively set up and managed. Phil also goes through all the Webex APIs for the 9800 Series and groups them into specific feature categories for easier understanding and usage.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-apis-for-the-cisco-desk-phone-9800-series'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🤖 Building Webex BYOVA Apps? This New Tool&#39;s Got Your Back</h6><p>If you are looking to create &quot;Bring Your Own Virtual Agent&quot; (BYOVA) apps for Webex Contact Center, discover a new command-line tool that simplifies data source management and refreshes during development: <code>webex-byods-manager</code>. In a recent blog by the Technical Leader for Webex Developer Relations, Adam Weeks, learn how this tool can help keep your projects moving and why the &quot;Bring Your Own Data Source&quot; (BYODS) Node.js SDK is still king for production.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/building-webex-byova-apps-this-new-tool-s-got-your-back'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🧩 What the Base? Decoding Webex API IDs</h6><p>Ever found yourself staring at a Webex API ID, thinking, &quot;What in the byte-sized world is that?&quot; But fear not, because it&#39;s time to pull back the curtain and reveal the not-so-secret sauce behind these special IDs. In another helpful blog by Adam Weeks, he unravels the enigma of Webex ID values by showing us why these seemingly random strings are Base64 encoded and how to save yourself from URL encoding headaches. Get ready to decode the magic and understand what&#39;s really inside!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/what-the-base-decoding-webex-api-ids'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📝 Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>Highlighting some important updates recently listed in the Webex API Changelogs:</p> <ul> <li><strong>NEW IN WEBEX CONTACT CENTER–</strong> July 31, 2025: A new resource scheduled-callback has been added which allows an agent to schedule a callback request for a later date or time via the APIs.</li> <li><strong>NEW IN WEBEX CONTACT CENTER–</strong> July 23, 2025 – In campaign manager APIs now have the ability to configure preview specific parameters like offer timeout, auto-action and disabled actions:<ul> <li>Added support for two new preview modes: Preview Standard and Preview Direct.</li> <li>Added new preview task APIs to allow the agents to accept, skip, or remove contacts offered during a preview campaign.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Full Webex Contact Center API Changelog →</a> </p> <ul> <li><strong>WARNING FOR THE WEBEX ADMIN APIs</strong>– July 31, 2025: We are updating the rate limits on the <a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/api/v1/people'>People API</a> to ensure fair access for all customers. This change is being made because some accounts were making extremely frequent calls, impacting the experience for others. With the new limits, most customers will benefit from improved access. Some users may notice an increase in 429 (Too Many Requests) responses, though we are working to keep this to a minimum. Thank you for your understanding and support.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/api/changelog/webex-admin'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex APIs for the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4f785032ac4a85d8/6893c665139c9229ff69a8c6/webex-apis-for-the-cisco-desk-phone-9800-series-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex APIs for the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series" /> <p>Devices in the <a href='https://www.webex.com/us/en/devices/phone-series/cisco-phone-9800-series.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series</a> have a robust feature set, with brilliant audio &amp; video quality, enhanced security, and user-friendly designs. The 9800 Series runs on the <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n1trwjh/Release-Notes-for-Cisco-PhoneOS-Phones-9800-and-8875' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>PhoneOS</a> operating system that provides flexible control and scalability in modern cloud-based collaboration environments. This makes the Desk Phone 9800 Series ideal for enterprises seeking robust, programmable, and future-proof communication solutions.</p> <p>When used in a Webex Calling environment, Cisco 9800 Series phones deliver a seamless and intuitive communication experience that simplifies device management through centralized control. This enables efficient configuration updates, policy enforcement, and bulk changes across locations or the entire organization without the need for physical access to each phone.</p> <p>What also makes these phones a preferred choice for enterprises are the flexible administration capabilities via the Webex Calling APIs, that can automate lifecycle management, customization, and post-activation configurations on devices. This article will detail how the Webex Calling APIs can be leveraged for integrations that automate the setup and configuration of Cisco 9800 Series phones. While we are mainly focusing on 9800 Series, the APIs covered in this article also pertain to the <a href='https://www.webex.com/us/en/devices/phone-series/cisco-video-phone-8875.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Cisco Video Phone 8875</a>, which also runs on PhoneOS.</p> <p>The first section highlights key distinctions between Cisco 9800-series phones and Cisco MPP devices, to clarify some of the notable differences in how they are respectively set up and managed. In the second section, we go through the Webex Calling APIs for the 9800 Series phones, grouped into specific feature categories for easier understanding and usage.</p> <h6>Cisco 9800 Series (PhoneOS) vs. Cisco Multiplatform Phones (MPP)</h6><p>For those who have previously managed Cisco Multiplatform Phones (MPP) devices, there are some important differences to note when setting up and configuring a Cisco 9800 Series (PhoneOS) device. The main aspects of the 9800 Series and MPP devices are compared in the table below.</p> <table> <tr> <td> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </td> <td> <p><strong>Cisco Desk Phone 9800-Series</strong>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> </td> <td> <p><strong>Cisco Multiplatform Phone (MPP)<strong>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>Operating System</em></p> </td> <td> <p>PhoneOS, a modern, unified OS designed for cloud and hybrid use.</p> </td> <td> <p>MPP firmware, legacy platform.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>Provisioning</em></p> </td> <td> <p>Supports zero-touch provisioning via activation codes and APIs.</p> </td> <td> <p>More configurations possible before activation; conventional provisioning methodology.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>Configuration Timing</em></p> </td> <td> <p>Many configurations require the device to be online to apply changes via APIs.</p> </td> <td> <p>More pre-activation configuration possible before device is online.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>API Support</em></p> </td> <td> <p>Extensive Webex Calling APIs for device and call settings.</p> </td> <td> <p>Limited API support; more manual or CUCM-based configuration.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>Feature Set</em></p> </td> <td> <p>Integrated with Webex ecosystem, supports desk reservation, hot desking, AI noise removal, and advanced security features.</p> </td> <td> <p>Supports core calling features; fewer integrated collaboration features.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><em>Management</em></p> </td> <td> <p>Managed primarily via Cisco Control Hub and Webex Calling APIs.</p> </td> <td> <p>Managed via CUCM or legacy management tools.</p> </td> </tr> </table> <p>As you can see, one of the very significant differences Is the “Configuration Timing” of the two platforms. With MPP, most settings can be preconfigured before the device is online, including provisioning files and settings pushed prior to registration. In PhoneOS, phones must <em>first</em> come online and communicate their capabilities before most configuration options can be set. This means <em>after</em> plugging-in a phone, entering an activation code, and then waiting for a reboot. Most configurations, such as applying line key templates, device settings, and layout modifications, can be done via APIs after the PhoneOS device is online and registered.</p> <p>Another key aspect is that Cisco MPP OS does not support the broad range of Webex Calling APIs that are available for PhoneOS devices. This means many of the APIs mentioned here are limited or unavailable for MPP devices. Conversely, PhoneOS devices are designed to be extensively managed and configured through the Webex Calling APIs after activation and registration.</p> <p>It’s also important for developers to note that 9800 Series phones (PhoneOS) are referenced in Webex API calls by the Device ID value: <code>deviceId</code>, which is generated for any Webex Device as it connects to Webex. Conversely, MPP and third-party phones are referenced in API calls by the Webex Calling Device ID: <code>callingId</code>, which is the unique identifier for a device within the scope of calling services.</p> <p>For context, the example JSON snippet below shows that the <a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/get-device-details'>Get Device Details API</a> returns both the device <code>id</code> and <code>callingId</code> of a registered 9800 Series phone. The device <code>id</code> is the value used in subsequent API calls to configure and manage the phone.</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;items&quot;: [ { &quot;id&quot;: &quot;Y2lzY29sd42gdvfsfxxxxxxx&quot; , //deviceId &quot;webexId&quot;: &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3Vybxxxxxxx&quot;, &quot;callingId&quot;: &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3Vybjxxxxxxx&quot; , &quot;displayName&quot;: &quot;Phil&#39;s Desk Phone&quot;, &quot;placeId&quot;: &quot;YTQ0LTRmZwQt0GZjYS05ZGY0YjRmNDE3Zjxxxxxxx&quot;, &quot;workspaceId&quot;: &quot;YTQ0LTRmZWQt0GZjYS05ZGY0YjRmNDE3ZjUxxxxxxxx&quot;, &quot;personId&quot;: &quot;YTQ0LTRmZWQt0GZjYS05ZGYOYjRmNDE3ZjUxxxxxxx&quot;, &quot;orgId&quot;: &quot;LTEXZTUtYTE1M11mZTM00DE5Y2RjOWExxxxxxxx&quot;, ... ... ... } ] } </code></pre> <p>Next up is a walkthrough of the Webex Calling APIs that are available for the 9800 Series Phones, grouped into general feature categories.</p> <h6>Webex Calling APIs for the Cisco 9800 Series (PhoneOS)</h6><p>This section explores the Webex Calling APIs for <a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices'>Devices</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings'>Device Call Settings</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/devices/docs/api/v1/device-configurations'>Device Configurations</a> that are used to set up and configure 9800 Series phones. Again, the APIs are grouped by feature categories here to highlight how they are generally used by device integrations.</p> <h6>1. Device Lifecycle Management APIs</h6><p>This first set of Calling APIs help manage the registration, activation, and inventory of phones, which is the first step before 9800 Series devices can be configured:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/create-a-device-activation-code'>Create a Device Activation Code</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Generate an activation code to enable zero-touch provisioning for a new phone, allowing automatic registration with Webex Calling upon first power-up.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/create-a-device-by-mac-address'>Create a Device by MAC Address</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Register a new phone by its MAC address and assign it to a user or workspace before a physical deployment.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/delete-a-device'>Delete a Device</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Remove decommissioned or lost phones to free licenses and prevent unauthorized use.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/get-device-details'>Get Device Details</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve detailed data about a phone’s configuration, capabilities, status, and assigned user.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/list-devices'>List Devices</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Obtain an inventory list of all registered phones for management.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/devices/modify-device-tags'>Modify Device Tags</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Update metadata tags to classify phones by location, department, or usage for easier filtering.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/validate-a-list-of-mac-address'>Validate a List of MAC Addresses</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Verify batches of MAC addresses before provisioning to ensure device validity and support.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>2. Device Configuration and Settings APIs</h6><p>This extensive group of Calling APIs is for managing, customizing, and applying configuration settings on Cisco 9800 Series phones. They are classified here in three types – Device Settings, Layout/Line Key Management, and Other Device Configurations. As mentioned earlier, these and the other remaining APIs are utilized after the phone is activated.</p> <p><strong>APIs for Device Settings Management</strong> (<a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/uil72l/Configure-and-modify-device-settings-in-Webex-Calling' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>help article</a>)</p> <p>The Device Settings APIs enable administrators to centrally manage and customize Cisco phone settings at various scopes – organization, location, workspace, device, and user. Settings include audio, network, security, and feature preferences, among others:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/change-device-settings-across-organization-or-location-job'>Change Device Settings Across Organization or Location Job</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Execute bulk updates for all phones in a location or organization.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/read-the-device-override-settings-for-a-organization'>Read the Device Override Settings for an Organization</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the settings for a phone that can supersede configurations at other levels across the organization.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-location-device-settings'>Get Location Device Settings</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the custom phone configuration values for a location that supersede the broader organization-wide defaults.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-device-settings-for-a-workspace'>Get Device Settings for a Workspace</a><ul> <li><em>Retrieve the custom phone configuration values for a workspace (office, meeting room, etc.) that supersede the location and organization level defaults.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/update-device-settings-for-a-workspace'>Update Device Settings for a Workspace</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Enable hot desking or modify settings for all phones in a shared workspace.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-device-settings'>Get Device Settings</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the custom configuration values for a specific phone that supersede the workspace, location, and organization level defaults.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/update-device-settings'>Update Device Settings</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Remotely apply settings changes, such as call handling preferences or line key assignments.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/apply-changes-for-a-specific-device'>Apply Changes for a Specific Device</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Prompt a phone to download and apply an updated configuration.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-device-settings-for-a-person'>Get Device Settings for a Person</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the custom phone configuration values for a user, some of which may supersede the defaults on other levels.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/update-device-settings-for-a-person'>Update Device Settings for a Person</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Modify user-specific settings like call forwarding or line appearances.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <p><strong>APIs for Device Layout and Line Key Template Management</strong> (layout <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/g19k2r/Create-and-manage-line-key-templates' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>help article</a>, templates <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/g19k2r/Create-and-manage-line-key-templates' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>help article</a>)</p> <p><strong>This set of APIs</strong> are used to create and bulk assign templates to phone layouts using line key templates. These are used to customize layout modes for various functionalities like line appearances, speed dials, and feature access:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-device-layout-by-device-id'>Modify Device Layout by Device ID</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Customize the programmable line keys (PLK) on a phone, to match a specific layout based on the user role.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-device-layout-by-device-id'>Get Device Layout by Device ID</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the PLK information from a phone to verify or audit the current button layout of a phone.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/create-a-line-key-template'>Create a Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Define a custom button layout template to standardize line keys across a department.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/apply-a-line-key-template'>Apply a Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Quickly configure a phone’s button layout by applying a predefined template.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-a-line-key-template'>Modify a Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Update existing templates to add or remove buttons based on user needs.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/delete-a-line-key-template'>Delete a Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Remove obsolete templates to maintain a clean configuration environment.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-details-of-a-line-key-template'>Get Details of a Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Fetch the current line key template details, including key labels, functions, and layout, to ensure consistent and up-to-date device configurations across the organization.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/preview-apply-line-key-template'>Preview Apply Line Key Template</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Simulate template application to verify changes before deployment.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/read-the-list-of-line-key-templates'>Read the List of Line Key Templates</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: List all available templates for selection or modification.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <p><strong>APIs for Other Device Configuration</strong> (<a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n72q8yeb/Configure-9800-Series-and-8875-Phones-on-Control-Hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>help article</a>)</p> <p>This unique set of APIs are more commonly used to configure RoomOS devices but can also manage certain configuration settings on Cisco 9800 Series phones:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/devices/docs/api/v1/device-configurations/list-device-configurations-for-device'>List Device Configurations for device</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the current configuration settings of a Series 9800 phone by its deviceId, such as phone lines, softkeys, network settings, directory services, power saving features, SIP and audio settings, custom wallpaper, firmware updates, and other device behaviors.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/devices/docs/api/v1/device-configurations/update-device-configurations'>Update Device Configurations</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Automate bulk configuration changes to ensure consistent settings across phones.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>3. Workspace Devices APIs</h6><p>The Workspace Devices APIs allows administrators to manage and audit Webex Calling devices in fixed workspaces, including the 9800 Series. This facilitates the monitoring and administration of phones used in collaborative environments, like meeting rooms:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-workspace-devices'>Get Workspace Devices</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve devices assigned to shared workspaces to automate inventory audits.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-workspace-devices'>Modify Workspace Devices</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Manage hot desking by adding or removing devices from shared workspaces.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>4. Device Members and Hoteling APIs</h6><p>The Device Members APIs allows the identification and management of phones and other calling devices assigned to specific <em>users</em> or <em>workspaces</em> within the organization. The Hoteling APIs manages the feature that allows users to temporarily load their phone profile onto a shared (host) phone, enabling them to make calls with their work number and access their calling features from any designated host device. When used together, these APIs are especially useful for managing shared phones in flexible workspaces, such as a hot-desking or co-working environments:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-device-members'>Get Device Members</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Fetch device membership information to verify correct user assignments, detect unauthorized changes, or prepare for device reassignments.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/search-members'>Search Members</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Search for users or members to associate with devices or apply user-specific settings.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/update-members-on-the-device'>Update Members on the Device</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Add or remove members from shared lines or group call features.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-person-devices'>Get Person Devices</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Audit user device assignments to enable targeted configuration, troubleshooting, or call settings management on the devices linked to that person.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-hoteling-settings-for-a-person-s-primary-devices'>Modify Hoteling Settings for a Person’s Primary Devices</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Assign or modify hoteling hosts and configure association time limits programmatically.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>5. Job and Monitoring APIs</h6><p>This group confirms the status for device configuration changes and applying templates. This helps diagnose if there are any failures in these processes, for efficient device management and operational reliability:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-the-job-status-of-an-apply-line-key-template-job'>Get the Job Status of an Apply Line Key Template Job</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Monitor the progress and completion of line key template application jobs, ensuring that the changes have been successfully applied or to reveal any issues during the process.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/rebuild-phones-configuration'>Rebuild Phones Configuration</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Trigger a rebuild job on phones in a location if the network configuration switches from “public” to “private” and vice versa.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-the-job-status-of-a-rebuild-phones-job'>Get the Job Status of a Rebuild Phones Job</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Track the status a phone rebuilding job to confirm it has been completed successfully.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-job-errors-for-an-apply-line-key-template-job'>Get Job Errors for an Apply Line Key Template Job</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve the <code>trackingID</code> of an error when a line key template job fails, for further troubleshooting.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/get-job-errors-for-a-rebuild-phones-job'>Get Job Errors for a Rebuild Phones Job</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Obtain error reports for phone rebuild jobs to troubleshoot issues.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/list-change-device-settings-jobs'>List Change Device Settings Jobs</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: List all device settings change jobs for audit and tracking</em>.</li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/list-change-device-settings-job-errors'>List Change Device Settings Job Errors</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: View errors associated with device settings change jobs.</em></li> </ul> </li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/list-rebuild-phones-jobs'>List Rebuild Phones Jobs</a><ul> <li><em>Use Case: Retrieve all phone rebuild jobs to monitor configuration refresh activities.</em></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Check Out Our Vidcast</h6><br/> <div style="padding-bottom: 56.25%; position: relative; display: block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/7b9ad3f2-24eb-483c-87d2-e8003c23ed43?disableCopyDropdown=1" width="100%" height="100%" title="Webex APIs for the Cisco Desk Phone 9800 Series" loading="lazy" allow="fullscreen *;autoplay *;" style="position: absolute; top:0; left: 0; border: solid; border-radius: 12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>We Are Here to Help!</h6><p>We are always eager to provide support for these Calling APIs and integrations. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>. Until next time, happy integration building!</p> ]]>
