<title>
<![CDATA[ The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Capture APIs ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt65e29336bb9601c1/6890f95e753ffb3b67d0de4d/captures-blog-1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Capture APIs" /> <div style="padding-bottom: 56.25%; position: relative; display: block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/b0b80853-df73-4613-9761-7b8ca0a83153?disableCopyDropdown=1" width="100%" height="100%" title="Captures API" loading="lazy" allow="fullscreen;autoplay;" style="position: absolute; top:0; left: 0; border: solid; border-radius: 12px;"></iframe> </div> <p>As a reader of this blog, hopefully you are continuing a journey of another installment of the blog series, “<a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis-audio-files'>The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs</a>”. This time we are talking about capturing Task recordings that become available to developers via the Webex Contact Center Captures API. According to the Webex developer documentation, a “Task represents a request or demand for attention/work from agents. Concretely, a telephony Task is an incoming call. For chat, a Task is a chat session. For email, a Task is an email chain.” The data associated with actions performed by Webex Contact Center agents are often recorded and stored by Webex and made available to developers that have access to various APIs that consume the data. Below we will explore how to leverage the Captures API to do things like get telephony recordings and email transcripts.</p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Developer Sandbox</h6><p>A good place to start when developing apps that work with the Webex Contact Center is with requesting a <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/sandbox_cc'>Webex Contact Center Developer Sandbox</a>. This tool provides developers with an org that they can use to provision up to 10 licensed Webex users of various roles. They can then generate content in the sandbox and build applications without worrying about whether they are going to disrupt the operations of an org that is handling customer support in real time. Freely build and break things without consequence by logging into the developer portal and requesting a sandbox today!</p> <h6>Register a Client Application</h6><p>Webex provides developers with two client application types to employ when leveraging the Captures APIs. One option a developer can go with is a Webex Contact Center Integration and the other is a Webex Contact Center Service App.</p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Integrations</h6><p>A <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/guides/integrations'>Webex Contact Center Integration</a> requires the developer to implement an <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/authentication-cc'>OAuth 2.0 flow</a> using the provided client credentials. Once a user authorizes the client application to make API requests on their behalf, the developer can get an access token to start gathering a Webex Contact Center organization’s historical recording data, and setting the proper webhooks to get notified when new recordings become available. here are several caveats to think about in this scenario. The user that authorizes the app in the OAuth 2.0 flow has to be an administrator with the proper permissions to make API calls that align with either the <code>cjp:config_read</code> or <code>cjp-analyzer:read</code> scopes, and others. To initiate this flow, which is manual, you typically need to present a web page or button to &quot;Connect with Webex&quot;.</p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Service Apps</h6><p>A <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/service-apps'>Webex Contact Center Service App</a> is like a Integration in that the goal of obtaining an access token to make API calls is the same, but the mechanism for obtaining the access token is not dependent on the developer having a user interface for a user to kick off an OAuth 2.0 flow, instead the Service App is approved by an administrator in Control Hub. Also, when a developer ultimately gets an access token to use in their client application, they are not making API calls on behalf of a single user or administrator as is the case with an Integration leveraging OAuth 2.0. The Service App is a virtual admin and is recognized by Webex services as a machine account. This virtual admin can perform administrator tasks through the Webex Contact Center APIs. Any administrator with access to the control hub can authorize a Service App by navigating to the Control Hub’s Application section given they have matching permissions that align with the <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/integrations#scopes'>scopes</a> that the developer selected when registering the Service App.</p> <p>One caveat here is that for a developer who wants to productize their Service App and make it available to any Webex user that has access to the Control Hub, they would need to submit and publish the Service App on the <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex App Hub</a>. Alternatively, an in-house developer could register the Service App and make the app available to the admin for the organization they belong to by requesting the administrator’s approval from the Service App’s page in the developer portal.</p> <p>Once an app is approved by an administrator the developer can obtain the access token and refresh token in the Webex Developer Portal or build a separate <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/service_app_token_getter' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>client integration</a> to automate the token retrieval process via API. Since the access token turns the Service App into a Virtual Admin, the developer can set the scopes for the token to include the required <code>cjp:config_read</code> or <code>cjp-analyzer:read</code> as required by the Captures API set.</p> <h6>Captures APIs</h6><p>Let’s break down the API endpoints that make capturing Task and recording data happen:</p> <h6>Captures Webhook</h6><p><a href='https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/v2/subscriptions' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/v2/subscriptions</a></p> <p>The first thing a developer may want to do, once they have obtained an access token, is to set <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/guides/webhooks-cc'>webhooks</a> that will instruct Webex services to let the client application know when a new recording or Capture is available. This can be accomplished leveraging the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/subscriptions'>Subscriptions API</a>. This API can monitor several event types, but to stay on topic for this blog we will focus on the Captures event, capture:available. In the body of an API request to this endpoint, the developer is required to name the webhook, provide the events we are subscribing to (Captures in this case) in the event type parameter, include an orgId, and a resource version. The resource version can be obtained by using the List Event Types API.</p> <p>The event payload that the client application receives when this webhook is triggered will include a taskId and a link to the downloadable recording. The Subscriptions API for webhooks requires <code>the cjp:config_read</code> or <code>cjp:config_write scopes</code>.</p> <h6>List Event Types</h6><p>This API should be used to get the resource version data that is needed in the Captures Webhook/Subscription API request. Requires <code>cjp:config_read</code> scope.</p> <h6>List Captures</h6><p><a href='https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/v1/captures/query' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/v1/captures/query</a></p> <p>This is the API that has the recording and Task data that most developers looking at this blog is interested in. Initially, a developer may want to call this after setting hooks so that they can store any available historical recording and Task data.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Using Websockets with the Webex JavaScript SDK ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte4bd71f4d740504e/5d8b6c07d6a10e0cc7a9fd20/WebexDevBlog_HowTo_F_R1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Using Websockets with the Webex JavaScript SDK" /> <div><Callout type="info">This blog post was originally published in September 2019 and has now been updated for 2025.</Callout></div> <p>Most developers who have created applications for Webex are familiar with the concept of <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/webhooks'>Webhooks</a>. Webhooks are registered on resources like ‘messages’ or ‘memberships’ to notify applications of events on these resources. When the registered event has occurred - for example a message was created or a membership was deleted - an HTTP POST event with a JSON payload is sent and your application can react to it accordingly.</p> <p>When your application runs as a web server using a publicly-accessible URL, you don’t need to do much else beyond creating a webhook and having an app running at the webhook&#39;s <code>targetUrl</code> to process the webhook payload. This approach can be a problem though if your app needs to run behind a corporate firewall or in restrictive environments. To get around this problem, we recently introduced functionality in the Webex JavaScript SDK that allows applications to &quot;listen&quot; for Webex messaging events using websockets, a technology that does not require a web server running on a public IP address.</p> <p>Websockets are persistent connections established over HTTP that allow direct communication between servers (the Webex API in this case) and clients (the Webex JavaScript SDK). In this post, we will walk you through creating and using websockets to listen for events sent from Webex.</p> <h6>Websocket example</h6><p>Websockets are not created by sending a POST request to the API like you would to create a webhook. Websockets are created programmatically with the help of the JavaScript SDK, as they&#39;re a unique concept that requires additional behind the scenes setup.</p> <p>Websocket listeners can be created for <strong>memberships</strong>, <strong>rooms</strong>, <strong>messages</strong>, or <strong>attachmentActions</strong>. Each of these resources has a <code>listen()</code> method in the JavaScript SDK, which you need to call in order to start your websocket. Once the listener is started, you can specify the type of event you would like to be notified about, by calling the <code>on()</code> method. As mentioned earlier, there is no need for a <code>targetURL</code>, like you need for a webhook, because the events from the server are not sent via HTTP. Instead, they&#39;re routed through the websocket, and any <code>on()</code> handlers you have registered for the event are called directly by the SDK.</p> <p>Applications which use the Webex JavaScript SDK can make use of websockets today! Additionally, support for websockets has been added to the <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-flint' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Node Flint framework</a>.</p> <p>If your application isn&#39;t written in JavaScript, don&#39;t worry, you can still take advantage of websockets. In the following sections, we will go through each step of creating a node.js based websocket listener app, built specifically to forward Webex events to another locally running application. In this sample, we will listen for &quot;message:created&quot; events and forward them to a specified localhost/PORT. On the other side of it, we will have a sample Java app listening on localhost/PORT, interpreting the request and sending a reply to the room the message was sent from.</p> <h6>Requirements</h6><br/> <h6>The node.js app</h6><p>Before getting started with websockets, make sure you have everything that&#39;s needed to get up and running with Node.js and NPM - more information can be found in the <a data-type='internal' to='/messaging/docs/sdks/node'>Node.js SDK documentation</a> and the <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/blob/master/README.md' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>JavaScript SDK&#39;s GitHub repo</a>. Once you have that covered, go the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/hookbuster' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>hookbuster example repo</a> and follow the instructions for installation.</p> <h6>The Java app</h6><p>Our app uses Maven to build the project, so you will need that set up before you can run the example. You will also need Java 1.6 or higher installed. Once both are functional, open the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/javabot' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>GitHub repo</a> and follow the instructions to install and run it.</p> <h6>Everything else</h6><p>You will also need a bot access token (it&#39;s much easier and simpler to test with a bot token vs an integration token accessing your personal data). Even though you won&#39;t need the token in the application code itself, it will be necessary later to run the demo. To create one, see our <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/bots'>Bots Guide</a> and hang onto the access token for now.</p> <h6>Creating a Websocket listener -- the node.js app</h6><br/> <h6>Step 1: Authentication</h6><p>Once the node.js app is up and running, per the instructions mentioned in the Github repo earlier, you&#39;ll need to provide it with an access token. This will be entered in the console and we need to use it to make the demo functional. The token is then used to initialize a Webex object, which is used to communicate with the Webex API. Here is the code where we retrieve the access token provided in the Console:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">function _initializeWebex(accessToken) { webex = Webex.init({ config: { logger: { level: &#39;error&#39; } }, credentials: { access_token: accessToken } }); webex.once(&#39;ready&#39;, () =&gt; { console.log(fonts.info(&#39;Webex Initialized&#39;)); }) } </code></pre> <p>To make sure the access token is valid, we do a call to the Webex API&#39;s <code>/people/me</code> endpoint:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">return new Promise((resolve, reject) =&gt; { webex.people.get(&#39;me&#39;).then(person =&gt; { resolve(person); }).catch(() =&gt; { reject(&#39;not authenticated&#39;); } ); }); </code></pre> <p>We use this call to do the validation because everyone has access to view the &quot;person&quot; associated with the token they&#39;re using; it will rarely fail for any other reason besides the access token being invalid.</p> <h6>Step 2: Start listening</h6><p>The app will then ask for a destination and a port that it will use for forwarding the incoming websocket events to via POST request; in our example, we will use port 5000 but you can set that to whichever port you prefer.</p> <p>After that, we will be prompted to select our resource and event. We will select <strong>messages</strong> and <strong>created</strong>, respectively. This will start the websocket listener and it will then listen for incoming messages. Please note - only messages where our bot is mentioned will be triggered; this is because bots are restricted and can only access messages where the bot is explicitly mentioned. Here is a screenshot showing both steps 1 and 2:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt32748a2df56c1965/5d8a8f045624367917a5d6e9/websockets-hookbuster-example.png" alt="Hookbuster example"></p> <p>This is the node.js code triggered by the above console commands for the resource and event selection:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">webex.messages.listen().then(() =&gt; { //logging a formatted info message in the console console.log(fonts.info( &#39;listener is running for &#39;) + fonts.highlight(` ${resource.toUpperCase()}:${event.toUpperCase()} `) ); webex.messages.on(event, request =&gt; { let request_string = JSON.stringify(request); _forwardRequest(request_string); }); }).catch(reason =&gt; { console.log(fonts.error(reason)); }); </code></pre> <h6>Step 3: Forward the request</h6><p>Make sure the Java application for the bot is also running, and then send a simple message to the bot via Webex. Since <strong>&#39;hello&#39;</strong> is all our Java bot is built to understand, we will only send that command. We&#39;re sending the test via a group space, but a direct message would work as well:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8aacdaa0ea527a9a/5d8a8f03f38cef798fc9fca5/websockets-hookbuster-example-message.png" alt="Webex message"></p> <p>As soon as the message is posted, the server triggers a POST request, the same way it would for a webhook. The difference is, instead of a public <code>targetURL</code>, the message is sent to our websocket because we registered a listener for all messages created for our bot (we told the system to listen for our bots messages specifically, when we entered our bot access token in the node.js app earlier). Once the message reaches our running code, it is directly forwarded to localhost:5000, as shown below:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">function _forwardRequest(request) { //logging info to the console console.log(fonts.info(&#39;request received&#39;)); //gathering some details const options = { hostname: &#39;localhost&#39;, port: specifications.port, method: &#39;POST&#39;, headers: { &#39;Content-Type&#39;: &#39;application/json&#39;, &#39;Content-Length&#39;: request.length } }; //creating the forward request const req = http.request(options, res =&gt; { console.log(`statusCode: ${res.statusCode}`); }); req.on(&#39;error&#39;, error =&gt; { console.log(fonts.error(error.message)); }); //sending the request req.write(request); req.end(); console.log(fonts.info(`request forwarded to localhost:${specifications.port}`)); console.log(fonts.info(request)); } </code></pre> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt79f9e38b1c5b0196/5d8a8f03f0e07b2dd96a50e8/websockets-hookbuster-sample-message.png" alt="Hookbuster sample output"></p> <h6>Step 4: Stop listening</h6><p>This might seem like we&#39;re getting a little ahead of ourselves, but it is important to note - if we do not clean up the listener after it is no longer needed, we might run into trouble later. This is why our node.js app stops all listeners once you exit the app. The following code handles the clean up process:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">webex.messages.stopListening(); webex.messages.off(event); </code></pre> <h6>Listen to incoming request -- the Java bot application</h6><br/> <h6>Step 1: Authentication</h6><p>Just like our node.js websocket listener app, our <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/javabot' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Javabot</a> application needs an access token to function. After you start up the app, it will ask for the token. Here we use the same bot token as before, because we want to post our simple replies with the same identity. After entering the token, it is verified with the below code:</p> <pre><code class="language-java">private static boolean verifyAccount(String accessToken) { boolean isValid = false; Bot bot = new Bot(accessToken); try { Console.printInfo(&quot;Verifying account&quot;); Person me = bot.getMyDetails(); isValid = true; Console.printInfo(&quot;Account verified as &quot; + me.getDisplayName().toUpperCase()); } catch (Exception e) { Console.printError(&quot;Access token invalid&quot;); } return isValid; } </code></pre> <p>The verification is done by our Bot object, which is actually a wrapper for the Java SDK&#39;s Spark object:</p> <pre><code class="language-java">public Person getMyDetails() { return spark.people().path(&quot;/me&quot;).get(); } </code></pre> <h6>Step 2: Start listening</h6><p>The only other parameter needed for our Java app is a port to listen on. We will use the same 5000 port, that we used with the node.js app.</p> <p>This is all we need to start listening for incoming requests on localhost:5000. With the parameters gathered and verified, we can now instantiate the socket and begin accepting incoming messages using the following code:</p> <pre><code class="language-java">public void run() { Console.printInfo(&quot;Service listening on localhost:&quot; + port); try { ServerSocket serverSocket = new ServerSocket(port); while (true) { try { //waits for incoming request Socket socket = serverSocket.accept(); JSONObject requestBody = getRequestBodyFromInput(socket); evaluateRequest(requestBody); } catch (Exception e) { Console.printError(e.getMessage()); } } } catch (IOException e) { //socket already in use Console.printError(e.getMessage()); Console.printError(&quot;Service not running&quot;); } } </code></pre> <p>Here is a screenshot showing the Console workflow for the above code:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb6d64d1b9edcf18d/5d8a8f0476c2640d16348c44/websockets-javabot-example.png" alt="Javabot example output"></p> <h6>Step 3: Evaluating the request</h6><p>Once we receive our &quot;hello&quot; message from the node.js app, the request is interpreted using the below code:</p> <pre><code class="language-java">private void evaluateRequest(JSONObject requestBody) { //print info to the console Console.printInfo(&quot;Request received&quot;); Console.printInfo(requestBody.toString()); String resource = (String) requestBody.get(&quot;resource&quot;); JSONObject data = getDataObjectFromJson(requestBody); String roomId = (String) data.get(&quot;roomId&quot;); if (resource.equals(&quot;messages&quot;)) { String messageId = (String) data.get(&quot;id&quot;); Message message = bot.getMessageById(messageId); if (!message.getPersonEmail().contains(&quot;@webex.bot&quot;)) { //split the message along spaces String[] trimmedMessage = message.getText().split(&quot;\\\s&quot;); //convert the message array into a searchable list ArrayList&lt;String&gt; messageList = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Arrays.asList(trimmedMessage)); if (messageList.contains(&quot;hello&quot;)) { bot.sayHello(roomId); } } } } </code></pre> <h6>Step 4: Sending a reply</h6><p>The Java SDK includes prebuilt methods we then call to send the actual reply back to the space/room where the original &quot;hello&quot; originated:</p> <pre><code class="language-java">void sayHello(String roomId) { Message message = new Message(); message.setRoomId(roomId); message.setMarkdown(&quot;hello there \uD83D\uDC4B&quot; ); spark.messages().post(message); } </code></pre> <p>This is how it looks like, back in Webex:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt27e5f19e1811ebbd/5d8a8f022d73960d2a506ec3/websockets-javabot-sample-message.png" alt="Webex sample message - hello"></p> <p>If you have any questions, please don&#39;t hesitate to contact our <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support team</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – July 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – July 2025" /> <p>Greetings everyone! This month&#39;s newsletter is all about the new converged Webex for Developers portal and AI Assistant, where content for the Webex Suite and Contact Center platforms is now united. So, sit back, relax, and keep reading to get the full scoop on the developer.webex com redesign.</p> <h6>📺 Public Webinar: A Deep Dive into the New Webex Developer Portal and AI Assistant</h6><p>On Wednesday, July 30th at 1:00PM EDT, join the Webex Developer Evangelism team for an exclusive webinar that unveils two pivotal advancements designed to revolutionize your development workflow: the new converged Webex Developer Portal and the powerful AI Assistant on <a data-type='internal' to='/'>developer.webex.com</a>.</p> <p>During this session, our experts will provide a comprehensive walkthrough of both the converged portal&#39;s intuitive interface and the AI Assistant&#39;s practical applications, demonstrating how these tools empower you to innovate faster and more efficiently with Webex. Don&#39;t miss this opportunity to optimize your Webex development journey!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <p><strong>You can get a head-start on all the topics that will be discussed in the July webinar by checking out three recently published blogs, which introduce and explain the new Webex Developer Portal and AI Assistant:</strong></p> <h6>🧩 Presenting the Converged Webex and Contact Center Developer Portal</h6><p>In the first article Leader of Webex Developer Documentation, John Francis, formally announces the new converged Webex for Developers portal, that has both Webex Suite and Contact Center content coalesced on one site. Learn all about the new unified access, flexible navigation, API publishing automation, expanded &quot;try it now&quot; functionality, and full accessibility that the new portal brings to the table.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/presenting-the-converged-webex-and-contact-center-developer-portal'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Behind the Docs: How UX Shapes Our New Developer Experience</h6><p>In the next article, Webex Design Leader, Athena Perez, takes you behind the scenes to show how we redesigned developer documentation information architecture for a unified, seamless experience. Get to know the overarching strategy for bringing Webex Suite and Contact Center content together, with a re-imagined the navigational experience that focuses on discoverability, scalability, and taxonomy, all while creating a seamless, user-first experience.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/behind-the-docs-how-ux-shapes-our-new-developer-experience'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🤖 Supercharge Your Webex Development with Cisco AI Assistant</h6><p>In the third article, we introduce the <a data-type='internal' to='/messaging/docs/webex-aI-assistant-for-developers'>Webex AI Assistant for Developers</a>, a chat interface powered by a large language model (LLM) available on the Webex developer portal for Webex Contact Center and Webex Suite. It assists developers by handling complex tasks, presenting relevant API documentation, and generating code snippets to aid in building Webex integrations. The assistant offers different layout options and is accessible to all signed-in users on developer.webex.com.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/supercharge-your-webex-development-with-cisco-ai-assistant-in-webex-developer-portal'>Read the blog →</a></p> ]]>

</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Supercharge Your Webex Development with Cisco AI Assistant in Webex Developer Portal ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt018aeacecc95a805/6887864d4a30ae8466991b56/developer-ai-assistant-blog--1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Supercharge Your Webex Development with Cisco AI Assistant in Webex Developer Portal" /> <p>We&#39;re excited to announce the launch of Cisco AI Assistant in the Webex Developer Portal, a game-changing tool designed to empower Webex developers like you! This intelligent chat interface, powered by a large language model (LLM), is now available on the Webex developer portal for Webex Contact Center and Webex Suite, ready to help you build amazing integrations and applications faster than ever before.</p> <h6>What the AI Assistant Can Do for You</h6><p>The AI Assistant can help you out with the following tasks:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Instant Access to Relevant Resources:</strong> Say goodbye to endless searching! The AI Assistant provides you with the documentation, APIs, and SDKs you need, right at your fingertips.</li> <li><strong>Code Generation on Demand:</strong> Need a code snippet? Just ask! The AI Assistant can generate code to kickstart your projects. Refine, regenerate, or customize the code to fit your exact needs.</li> <li><strong>Guided Exploration:</strong> Not sure where to start? Select <strong>Start building with Webex for Developers</strong> for a guided tour of the AI Assistant. Choose a specific Webex product, and the assistant will suggest follow-up questions to guide you.</li> <li><strong>Clarification and Precision:</strong> The Assistant will ask clarifying questions to ensure it understands your intent, providing you with the most relevant and accurate information.</li> <li><strong>Iterative Enhancement:</strong> Use the provided tools to further refine generated code to get to an output which is aligned with your requirements.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Get Started with the AI Assistant</h6><p>To get started with the AI Assistant:</p> <ol> <li>Visit <a href='http://www.developer.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Portal</a></li> <li>Log in with your Developer portal ID (or sign up for free if you don&#39;t have one).</li> <li>Select the AI Assistant icon next to your profile picture.</li> <li>Start building! Select a quick action or type your query. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc39ce19638d7147d/developer-ai-assistant-blog--2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <h6>Making the Most of the AI Assistant</h6><p>The AI Assistant makes it easier to build on Webex, with different layout options, the ability to tweak generated code output in multiple ways and collaborate to get your desired results.</p> <h6>Layout Options</h6><p>Choose between full screen, floating, or docked view, to align with your development environment</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta66ad53e74432c2f/developer-ai-assistant-blog--3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Refine Your Generated Code</h6><p>Tweak code using the edit bar options, <strong>Refine</strong>, <strong>Regenerate</strong>, or <strong>Customize</strong>. You can also change specific parts of the code by selecting/highlighting the specific lines and right clicking to get the option to refine or customize.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte699f22a8d6be70f/developer-ai-assistant-blog--4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><strong>Refine</strong> provides some pre-defined change options like <strong>Make modular</strong>, <strong>Add annotation</strong> and <strong>Simplify code</strong> which can be used either on the entire code or specific sections. <strong>Customize</strong> allows you to enter custom queries to edit the code with specifics. For example, you could ask the assistant to elaborate on the error cases and handle different possible error scenarios with error codes!</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta8d5cd3507a8f000/developer-ai-assistant-blog--5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Each refinement/regeneration creates a new version of the code, allowing you to work across multiple versions and choose the one that suits your needs the best. The assistant allows up to 5 versions for each generated code block.</p> <h6>Share and Collaborate</h6><p>Easily copy, export, or share your generated code directly to a Webex space for seamless collaboration with the options provided on top of the code block.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt28542abbdcad0600/developer-ai-assistant-blog--6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Important Considerations</h6><p>Please keep these considerations in mind when using the AI Assistant:</p> <ul> <li>Usage is limited to fifteen prompts per day.</li> <li>The AI Assistant is currently available to organizations in the following regions: US, EU.</li> <li>The AI Assistant may occasionally make mistakes, so please validate the generated information and code.</li> <li>Currently, only Webex APIs are supported for code generation (SDK support is coming soon!).</li> <li>To change the language of your generated code, just post a follow up query with the language you want it in</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>We Value Your Feedback</h6><p>Help us make the AI Assistant even better! Share your thoughts by selecting Thumbs Up or Thumbs Down for each response. You can also share the entire chat as context for improvement.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>The Webex AI Assistant is your new partner in Webex development. Start exploring its capabilities today and unlock a new level of efficiency and innovation!</p> <p>Check out our <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/webex-aI-assistant-for-developers'>guide to using the AI Assistant</a> in Webex Developer Portal for more information.</p> <p>If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Building Webex BYOVA Apps? This New Tool's Got Your Back ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt805e851eff7242d3/688290380fefd625fa7729f5/byods-command-line-tool-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Building Webex BYOVA Apps? This New Tool's Got Your Back" /> <p>If you&#39;re tinkering with &quot;<a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/bring-your-own-virtual-agent'>Bring Your Own Virtual Agent</a>&quot; (BYOVA) applications for Webex, you know it&#39;s all about making Webex smarter and more automated. As you get deep into building these cool solutions, keeping your <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/bring-your-own-datasource'>data sources</a> in check is a big deal, especially when you&#39;re still in the development phase. Good news! We&#39;ve got a new command-line tool, <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webex-byods-manager</a>, that&#39;s here to make that part of your BYOVA development life a whole lot easier.</p> <div style="padding-bottom: 56.25%; position: relative; display: block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/63e954e4-f0ae-4c20-82c3-c666cda6aad3?disableCopyDropdown=1" width="100%" height="100%" title="Webex BYODS Manager Tool" loading="lazy" allow="fullscreen;autoplay;" style="position: absolute; top:0; left: 0; border: solid; border-radius: 12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>The BYOVA Dev Headache: Keeping Data Sources Fresh</h6><p>The Webex <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/bring-your-own-datasource'>Bring Your Own Data Source</a> (BYODS) APIs let you connect outside data to Webex Contact Center. This is basically the engine powering the connection for your BYOVA apps. We&#39;re talking real-time interactions with clever voice virtual agents in Contact Center.</p> <p>Now, to keep these BYODS hook-ups secure and working right, you&#39;ve got to refresh their authentication tokens regularly. Think of it like a security check – these tokens only last at most 24 hours. If you don&#39;t, they expire, and data stops flowing. While this is super important for security, it can be a real pain when you&#39;re trying to quickly build and test stuff. Manually refreshing these things via curl or Postman can eat up your time and break your concentration.</p> <h6>Meet webex-byods-manager: Your Dev Buddy</h6><p>That&#39;s where the new <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webex-byods-manager</a> command-line tool steps in. You can find it as a Webex Samples project on GitHub. This tool was made specifically to help developers like you handle their BYODS data sources easily while you&#39;re building.</p> <p>The <code>webex-byods-manager</code> takes the headache out of refreshing data sources. You can quickly update those important tokens and settings without digging into complicated API calls or doing things by hand. This means less time messing with setup and more time actually building and refining what your virtual agent does.</p> <p>Imagine you&#39;re deep into coding a new feature for your BYOVA that pulls info from some external system. If your data source token suddenly goes stale, a quick command with <code>webex-byods-manager</code> can get you reconnected and back to coding in no time. This ability to quickly refresh is a game-changer for keeping your development smooth and productive.</p> <h6>Dev Tool vs. Production Powerhouse: Know the Difference</h6><p>It&#39;s super important to remember that <code>webex-byods-manager</code> is a <strong>development tool</strong>. It&#39;s great for quick, on-the-fly management in your local setup. Perfect for a single developer or a small team moving fast on BYOVA features.</p> <p>But for your actual live, production applications, you&#39;ll want something more robust, something that handles token rotation and data source management automatically and at scale. That&#39;s what the <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/sdks/byods-nodejs-sdk-introduction'>Webex BYODS Node.js SDK</a> is for. The SDK gives you features like custom storage, managing service app tokens, and automatically refreshing JWS tokens. It&#39;s built to give your production BYOVA apps a secure and reliable foundation. It takes care of all the tricky bits, like keeping tokens fresh and verifying them, making sure your live apps are secure and always running.</p> <h6>Ready to Give It a Spin?</h6><p>If you&#39;re building BYOVA apps for Webex, definitely check out <code>webex-byods-manager</code> and add it to your development toolkit. It&#39;s a simple tool that can make a big difference in how productive you are.</p> <p>To get started:</p> <ul> <li>Check out the <code>webex-byods-manager</code> tool on GitHub: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-byods-manager</a></li> <li>For the real deal in production, learn about the Webex BYODS Node.js SDK: <a data-type='internal' to='/create/docs/sdks/byods-nodejs-sdk-introduction'>/create/docs/sdks/byods-nodejs-sdk-introduction</a></li> </ul> <p>Happy coding!</p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ What the Base? Decoding Webex API IDs ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc7708cc5278701e5/6852db971a384240a5d3e608/what-the-base-decoding-api-ids-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="What the Base? Decoding Webex API IDs" /> <p>Hey there, Webex developers! Ever found yourself staring at a Webex API ID, thinking, &quot;What in the byte-sized world is that?&quot; You&#39;re not alone! Those seemingly random strings of characters that uniquely identify everything from users to rooms to messages might look a little mysterious at first glance. But fear not, because today we&#39;re going to pull back the curtain and reveal the not-so-secret sauce behind these special IDs.</p> <p>Get ready to answer “What the base?” (64, that is!) and decode the magic! ✨</p> <h6>The Mystery of the Webex API ID</h6><p>You&#39;ve seen them. They look something like <code>Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL1BFT1BMRS8wNjc2YWI1Mi1mNzYxLTQwMTUtYTAxZC01YjYyZDYwYzgxMTM=</code> or <code>Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL1JPT00vZmI2NDUzYzAtNzQ3MS0xMWU4LTkxNzktNzU0YTEwZDc0YzU0</code>. Long, a bit jumbled, and definitely not UUIDs.</p> <p>But there&#39;s a brilliant reason for this apparent complexity!</p> <h6>The &quot;Why&quot;: Taming Special Characters</h6><p>Here&#39;s the lowdown: Webex IDs, internally, can contain all sorts of characters – including those that would make a URL parser throw a tantrum. Think colons, slashes, and other bits that need special handling when you&#39;re sending them as part of a URL. Normally, you&#39;d have to URL encode these characters, which can make your URLs look even <em>more</em> like a secret alien language and frankly, be a bit of a headache to manage.</p> <p><strong>But Webex, in its infinite wisdom, had a better idea!</strong></p> <p>To save you the hassle of endless URL encoding and decoding, Webex API IDs are Base64 encoded. This means that the original, potentially &quot;messy&quot; internal ID is transformed into a clean, URL-safe string that can be passed around without any extra fuss. It&#39;s like giving your ID a superhero costume that makes it invisible to URL-encoding villains! </p> <p>For the more visual learners and a deeper dive into Base64 encoding, I suggest checking out <a href='https://lucid.co/techblog/2017/10/23/base64-encoding-a-visual-explanation' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Lucid&#39;s Base64 Encoding: A Visual Explanation blog</a>.</p> <h6>Show Me the Magic!</h6><p>Let&#39;s get our hands dirty and see this in action. We&#39;ll take a common Webex API ID and reverse-engineer it.</p> <p>Imagine you have a Webex user ID like this from an API response:</p> <p><code>Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL1BFT1BMRS8wNjc2YWI1Mi1mNzYxLTQwMTUtYTAxZC01YjYyZDYwYzgxMTM=</code></p> <p>This is the Base64 encoded version. To see what&#39;s truly inside, we need to decode it.</p> <p>Most programming languages have built-in Base64 decoding functions. Let&#39;s look at a few examples:</p> <h6>Python</h6><pre><code class="language-python">import base64 encoded_id = &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL1BFT1BMRS8wNjc2YWI1Mi1mNzYxLTQwMTUtYTAxZC01YjYyZDYwYzgxMTM=&quot; decoded_bytes = base64.b64decode(encoded_id) decoded_string = decoded_bytes.decode(&#39;utf-8&#39;) print(decoded_string) </code></pre> <h6>JavaScript (in Your Browser&#39;s Console or Node.js)</h6><pre><code class="language-javascript">const encodedId = &quot;Y2lzY29zcGFyazovL3VzL1BFT1BMRS8wNjc2YWI1Mi1mNzYxLTQwMTUtYTAxZC01YjYyZDYwYzgxMTM=&quot;; const decodedString = atob(encodedId); // `atob` is for Base64 decoding in browsers console.log(decodedString); </code></pre> <h6>The Grand Reveal!</h6><p>No matter which language you use, the decoded string will be:</p> <p><code>ciscospark://us/PEOPLE/0676ab52-f761-4015-a01d-5b62d60c8113</code></p> <p>Aha! Now that looks much more familiar. You can clearly see the <code>ciscospark://us/PEOPLE/</code> prefix followed by the actual UUID for the user.</p> <p>Similarly, for a room ID like <code>Y2lzY29zcGFazovL3VzL1JPT00vZmI2NDUzYzAtNzQ3MS0xMWU4LTkxNzktNzU0YTEwZDc0YzU0</code>, decoding it would reveal:</p> <p><code>ciscospark://us/ROOM/fb6453c0-7471-11e8-9179-754a10d74c54</code></p> <p>See? The decoded string often contains internal identifiers (like UUIDs) and a type prefix (<code>PEOPLE</code>, <code>ROOM</code>, <code>MESSAGE</code>, etc.) that Webex uses internally to identify the resource.</p> <h6>When Do You Need to Decode?</h6><p>For most of your Webex API interactions, you won&#39;t actually <em>need</em> to decode these IDs. When you receive them in API responses, you can typically use them directly in subsequent API requests. The Base64 encoding is handled transparently by the API.</p> <p>However, understanding this encoding is super useful for:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Debugging:</strong> When you&#39;re trying to figure out what a specific ID refers to, decoding it can give you immediate clarity.</li> <li><strong>Logging</strong><strong>:</strong> If you&#39;re logging IDs, decoding them can make your logs much more human-readable.</li> <li><strong>Curiosity!</strong> Because hey, we&#39;re developers, and we love knowing how things work under the hood!</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Now You Know!</h6><p>So there you have it! Those &quot;mysterious&quot; Webex API IDs are simply well-dressed, Base64-encoded versions of their internal selves. This clever trick saves you from the headaches of URL encoding and allows for smoother, more predictable API interactions.</p> <p>Now go forth, build amazing things, and confidently drop the base knowing you&#39;re working with some truly smart IDs! Happy coding!</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Behind the Docs: How UX Shapes Our New Developer Experience ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2da15eadff78844e/683f5ebd02d90112601f4033/Picture1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Behind the Docs: How UX Shapes Our New Developer Experience" /> <p><span style="font-size:18px"><em>How we redesigned developer documentation information architecture for a unified, seamless experience</em></span> </br></p> <p>At Webex by Cisco, we know that clear, intuitive documentation is essential for empowering our developer community - we want to make it easy for you to build with us! With that in mind, we’ve just rolled out a major update to our developer documentation. We’ve combined the Webex Contact Center and Webex Suite developer docs into one site and reimagined the navigational experience from the ground up - focusing on discoverability, scalability, and taxonomy, all while creating a seamless, user-first experience.</p> <br/> <span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">The Challenge: Separate Experiences </span> <p>Previously, we had separate websites for developers building with the Webex Contact Center and Webex Suite products. While each site offered valuable content, the flat navigational structure across two platforms made it harder to stay oriented. Whether searching for an API reference, trying to understand how different features or systems interact, or looking for an educational webinar or blog, developers and admins often had to jump between product areas and sites - potentially disrupting the all-important flow state.</p> <p>As more of our customers adopt the full Webex platform - including both Contact Center and Suite - we’re meeting you where you are. By bringing everything together in one place, we’ve reduced friction and empowered you to build more with Webex, making it easier to find what you need, stay focused, move faster, and remain in flow.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt0523e821a2e54090/683f4bc4df1392a92cf5d125/Two_developer_websites.png" alt="Two developer websites example"></p> </br> <p><span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">Our UX Approach: Principles and Process </span></p> <p><span style="color:#5C5C5C;font-size:18px;font-weight:600">1. Findability </span></p> <p>One of our core goals was to make key tasks and topics easier to find. As part of that effort, we invited our developer community to take part in early feedback and our <a href='https://gobeta.webex.com/key/dev-platform' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Beta Program</a>. While participation was limited, the insights we gathered - along with our own usability testing - revealed that important content was often buried too deep or grouped in unintuitive ways. So we made some meaningful changes: &nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Restructured content to better reflect how developers and admins actually work - and how our products work together</li> <li>Updated labels and categories for consistency, clarity, and scanability</li> <li>Simplified navigation to help you reach essential info faster &nbsp;</li> </ul> <p>Card sorting played a crucial role in shaping our new groupings, and the result is a system that’s easier to browse at a glance, and faster to search through with intent. Now that we’re live, we’ve already received valuable feedback from the community and we’ve heard you. Based on that input, one of our next iterations will include adding an “All APIs” list. We’re also actively working to get search back up and running as soon as possible. </br></p> <p><span style="color:#5C5C5C;font-size:18px;font-weight:600">2. Scalability </span></p> <p>As we integrated both the Suite and Contact Center docs, we also kept future growth in mind. We needed a flexible structure that could accommodate new products and features without becoming cluttered or overly complex. By eliminating deep, inconsistent nesting <span> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc87dc347c302fd33/683f4bc4f809c11e8b3e263b/New_global_navigation.png" alt="Updated global navigation view" width="50%" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto"> </span> and creating clear, concise categories, we laid the groundwork for a scalable system. Each category was designed to grow organically, allowing us to add new documentation without requiring another structural overhaul. For example, in the global navigation, you can now find high-level groupings that address specific areas of our product suite such as Meetings, Contact Center, Devices, and more.</p> <p>This approach not only supports what we offer today but also prepares us for long-term expansion. <br/></p> <p><span style="color:#5C5C5C;font-size:18px;font-weight:600">3. Harmonious Taxonomy </span></p> <p>Perhaps the most important aspect of this redesign was the unification of language and taxonomy, specifically within the left navigation. Labeling inconsistencies, like some overview pages being labeled “Overview” and others “Introduction”, created unnecessary cognitive load for developers and admins navigating between the Suite and Contact Center docs. It’s not something we often consider consciously, but having to stop a flow to think through inconsistencies like this really adds up over time.</p> <p>Through cross-team collaboration and user research, we developed a unified vocabulary for the left navigation ensuring that labels and categories were consistent, clear, and intuitive across both the Suite and Contact Center docs. While this improvement has greatly enhanced navigation clarity for external users, it also delivered a significant internal benefit: it helped us align on consistent naming conventions for the structure of our information. By codifying levels such as Level 1: Global Navigation, Level 2: Secondary Navigation, Level 3: Parent Page, and Level 4: Child Page, etc. we created a shared language that makes it easier for cross-functional teams to collaborate and communicate clearly. This alignment ensures that when we talk about structure, we’re all speaking the same language both internally and externally.</p> <p>We continue to refine the overall vocabulary across the entire site and product suite - an effort that spans many different engineering teams. This shared language not only supports a more unified experience for users, but also sets a consistent standard internally as our platform grows. </br><br/></p> <p><span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">Accessibility from the Start </span></p> <p>As part of this work, we partnered closely with our accessibility team to better understand how our documentation experience could support all users. Through user research and an accessibility-focused study, we identified key areas for improvement - particularly around tab order, screen reader clarity, and overall navigability. In this first release,<br><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt94e353785b05ca4b/683f4bc4a1ab65d7fc9afdf7/Accessibility_example.png" alt="Accessibility specs and markup for engineering"> we’ve addressed several of these issues, including improved keyboard navigation and ensuring that all navigation elements are clearly labeled for assistive technologies. Accessibility is a long-term commitment, and we’ll continue rolling out additional improvements in future iterations to ensure our documentation is inclusive and usable for everyone. <br/><br/></p> <p><span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">What’s New in the Experience </span></p> <p>With these foundational changes in place, the new experience brings together documentation for both the Suite and Contact Center under a single navigation system. No more bouncing between separate sites - everything now lives under one roof with a clean, unified structure. &nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>We’ve simplified and renamed categories to make it easier to locate what you need without digging through layers of menus. Look for the API Reference section to find a list of all APIs related to each product.</li> </ul> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt795703d891f52dcd/683f4bc3bac1ae2d143ce314/API_reference_header.png" alt="Example of API reference header in left nav" width="40%" style="display: block; margin-top: 2%; margin-left: 3%"> <p>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Frequently used resources are now easier to access. For example, your access token and Org ID are located in the user profile dropdown-available at any point in your journey, no matter where you are on the site. We’ve also heard your feedback about needing to re-copy the access token, and we’re actively working on a fix to make that experience smoother.</li> </ul> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt59eb062e01d9bf7f/683f4bc473466cd0fb9f27a3/Token_and_Org_ID_placement.png" alt="Token and org id placement in profile dropdown" width="40%" style="display: block; margin-top: 2%; margin-left: 3%"> &nbsp; - You’ll also now find documentation for all three of our API types in one place: REST (used by most of our Suite features), GraphQL (used for WxCC Search), and gRPC (used for additional WxCC capabilities). &nbsp; - Landing pages across the site have been, and continue to be, refreshed with clearer overviews, direct access to key APIs and guides, and step-by-step getting started flows to help users orient quickly. <br/><br/> <p><span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">What This Means for You </span></p> <p>These changes translate directly into a better day-to-day experience. You’ll get faster time to value, with less time spent figuring out where things are and more time doing meaningful work. A consistent structure and language help you navigate seamlessly between product areas, reducing confusion and improving efficiency. The new information architecture is designed to scale as we do, without adding clutter or complexity. Whether you&#39;re a developer implementing a feature or an admin configuring settings, you&#39;ll find what you need faster and in a more familiar format. <br/><br/></p> <p><span style="color:#7540DD;font-size:24px;font-weight:500">What’s Next </span></p> <p>This launch is just the beginning. We’re already working on the next wave of improvements, including enhancing our overview pages with easy-to-follow, step-by-step guides, expanding content across additional products and advanced use cases, and implementing search behavior to be even more contextual and accurate (think AI Assistant). We’ll also continue our accessibility work - especially on mobile and dynamic elements - and longer term, we’re focusing on better onboarding experiences for both developers and admins.</p> <p>Looking further ahead, we’re exploring ways to make our documentation more interactive and responsive to your needs - think building in-line within the context of our documentation with our AI assistant, helping you complete tasks, answer questions, and move faster without leaving the page.</p> <p>As always, we’re building in the open, and your feedback helps us make it better. If you have suggestions or spot something we’ve missed, <a data-type='internal' to='/explore/support'>reach out to our developer support team</a>. You can also help shape future features and experiences by joining the <a href='https://gobeta.webex.com/key/dev-platform' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Beta program</a>. This is your documentation too. <br/></p> ]]>
...

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – May 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – May 2025" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers. This month has more new content for you to discover. Get all the latest updates and announcements for the entire Webex Developer ecosystem right here!</p> <h6>🎪 Webex for Developers at Cisco Live San Diego 2025</h6><p>We’re heading to sunny San Diego for Cisco Live 2025 on <strong>June 9–13, 2025</strong>, and the Webex for Developers team is ready to connect with you! From building with our APIs and SDKs to previewing what’s coming next, this is your opportunity to learn, share, and build better collaboration experiences. The Leader of Webex Developer Evangelism, Adam Weeks, gives you all the details on the sessions that are scheduled and other activities for the event in a new blog post. We hope to see you there!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-for-developers-at-cisco-live-san-diego-2025'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📺 Public Developer Webinar: Discover and Build with Webex Service Apps</h6><p>On Wednesday, June 25<sup>th</sup> at 1:00PM EDT, join our next developer webinar to discover the power of Webex Service Apps in transforming your Unified Communications infrastructure. As business trends shift towards continuous, user-independent automation, this session will guide you through everything you need to know to get started with Webex Service Apps.</p> <p>If you can’t make it to the live session, no problem! You can watch all our previous webinar recordings on-demand, including the most recent one, <strong>Exploring the Webex Developer Beta Program</strong>, right on our webinars page. Come and explore our growing library!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Now in the Developer βeta Program - Webex Contact Center SDK</h6><p>As announced last month, the <strong>Webex Contact Center SDK</strong> is now available for testing in the Webex Developer Beta program. This powerful JavaScript library lets you embed Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop functionalities into your web applications. The SDK allows you to manage agent statuses, control calls (accept, decline, hold, end), and create custom softphone solutions. You can also use the SDK to integrate with existing CRM solutions and build custom widgets. To miss out on this opportunity to get hands-on early!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>🧑🏽‍🔧 Introducing Service Apps for Webex Contact Center</h6><p>We are pleased to announce that Service Apps have been made available for Webex Contact Center. With Service Apps, mission critical Contact Center integrations can now be deployed on behalf of an organization instead of individual users. Service Apps can request data for multiple users throughout an organization and provides much more flexibility for tasks that run continually on a long-term basis. To get all the details, check out this blog post by Sr. Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/introducing-service-apps-for-webex-contact-center'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🎛️ Getting Started with the Converged Recordings APIs for Webex Calling</h6><p>Webex Calling recently added the option to select “Webex” as the call recording provider for an organization, which utilizes the same mechanism as Webex Meeting recordings to output high quality audio files. The Webex call recording option also gives developers access to a new set of APIs to automate the management of call recordings in Webex Calling – <a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings'>Converged Recordings APIs</a>. In another new blog post, Phil Bellanti explores the new Converged Recordings API endpoints and explains how they work for different Webex user roles. ecosystem.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/getting-started-with-the-converged-recordings-apis-for-webex-calling'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📝 Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>Highlighting some important updates recently listed in the Webex API Changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>NEW –</strong> April 29, 2025: For The new <a href='https://app.use.webex.com/e/er?s=1485857328&lid=10553&elqTrackId=488fb1335f9f4bdb8b030e0e41b941c9&elq=79ef36105ddb4d59ad44ae34d647c9b7&elqaid=9957&elqat=1&elqak=8AF566B489263A5B3EF28AF142FB94A5E5830316BAD924A6CF7DC9A5742F3D100DF1' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Update a Virtual Extension</a> and <a href='https://app.use.webex.com/e/er?s=1485857328&lid=10552&elqTrackId=e705e8cf6f484dbbac0952d21c1c2d37&elq=79ef36105ddb4d59ad44ae34d647c9b7&elqaid=9957&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5CC81E8A5B86A41DCC76E5B610FB65B3F0316BAD924A6CF7DC9A5742F3D100DF1' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Delete a Virtual Extension</a> APIs require the <code>Identity:contact</code> scope in addition to the roles and scopes already documented.</li> <li><strong>BREAKING CHANGE</strong> – May 12, 2025 – In the near future, the <code>numberOfRings</code> parameter will be limited to values between 2 and 20 for User, Workspace, and Virtual Profile Call Forwarding, and Voicemail <code>PUT</code> APIs. The same validation will also apply to <code>numberOfRings</code> and <code>baseLocationNumberOfRings</code> for the Workspace Sequential Ring API.</li> <li><strong>NEW</strong>– May 15, 2025: Admins can now update the <code>ownerID</code> in a request when using <a href='https://app.use.webex.com/e/er?s=1485857328&lid=10551&elqTrackId=41848607f0ad46dc8f69953226ab6b2c&elq=79ef36105ddb4d59ad44ae34d647c9b7&elqaid=9957&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5E8EA0B97F82C3F194839963AAE1BA55E0316BAD924A6CF7DC9A5742F3D100DF1' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Reassign Recordings</a> to change the owner of a recording. This is particularly useful in cases involving virtual lines or workspaces that do not have an associated email address.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/api/changelog/webex-admin'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Presenting the Converged Webex and Contact Center Developer Portal ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta2e52c3130645344/6830b1a0ad580985f05a7278/Picture1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Presenting the Converged Webex and Contact Center Developer Portal" /> <p>Today, we’re proud to announce the debut of our newly converged Webex Contact Center and Webex Suite developer portal. We’ve focused on usability and discoverability and implemented the following key features:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Unified Access</strong>: Developers no longer need to log into two different portals for Webex Suite and Contact Center, making it easier to access all necessary content in one place.</li> <li><strong>Flexible Navigation</strong>: We now support a much more flexible and extensible navigation interface, meaning that information is grouped logically and is more easily discoverable and digestible.</li> <li><strong>API Publishing Automation</strong>: While transparent to you, our API publishing backend is completely automated and includes extensive error flagging and checking to minimize defects that may disrupt customer satisfaction.</li> <li><strong>Expanded Try it Now Functionality</strong>: Our new Try it Now widget had expanded functionality including support for gRPC and GraphQL search in Contact Center. In addition, we’ve added expanded configuration options (Server, Variables, and Global Headers) as well as code generation support for Curl, Python and Node.js. And you can even add your own query params as well as custom headers in your requests!</li> <li><strong>Full Accessibility</strong>: The converged portal is now completely accessible according to <a href='https://www.section508.gov/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>section 508 guidelines</a>.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>What’s Included?</h6><p>The converged portal includes all current content from both the Webex Developer Portal and Webex Contact Center Developer Portal. This includes:</p> <ul> <li>Webex Suite REST APIs for Calling, Messaging, Meetings, and Devices</li> <li>Administration REST APIs for both Contact Center and Webex Suite</li> <li>Device REST APIs</li> <li>SDK documentation for Webex Suite</li> <li>gRPC and the Search GraphQL APIs for Webex Contact Center</li> <li>All guides and other long form documentation from both Suite and Contact Center portals</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>A Tour of the Converged Portal</h6><p>Next, let’s take a brief tour of the new portal:</p> <ol> <li>Visit <a data-type='internal' to='/'>https://developer.webex.com</a>and login with your Webex ID.</li> <li>For the most part, the main landing page hasn’t changed, but you’ll see some new top menu items: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt693cafda1f403834/converged-developer-portal-blog-1.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>The <strong>Documentation</strong> menu expands to list all our current documentation areas including Webex Suite (<strong>Calling</strong>, <strong>Meetings</strong> and <strong>Messaging</strong>), <strong>Contact Center</strong>, <strong>Webex Connect</strong>, <strong>Admin</strong>, <strong>Compliance</strong> etc.: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb1e9d82c14bf77a4/converged-developer-portal-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>In addition, we’ve added a <strong>Create</strong> menu options to get you quickly to our many integration options including <strong>Bots</strong>, <strong>Embedded Apps</strong>, <strong>Service Apps</strong>, <strong>Instant Connect</strong> and much more.</li> <li>If you select, for example, <strong>Webex Calling</strong>, you’ll see a new hierarchical left-hand navigation system divided into logical sections: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt43faebd63fc5b3d0/converged-developer-portal-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>You can expand any section to see further subtopics by selecting the chevrons adjacent to a topic: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltfbfa31758063f4bf/converged-developer-portal-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>An important point to note is that you can now retrieve your Personal Access Token as well as your <code>OrgId</code> for Contact Center APIs by selecting your profile picture and choosing <strong>Copy to Clipboard</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6e6cf2af35d7e3ac/converged-developer-portal-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <p>At this point, we’ll encourage you to navigate around the interface and explore the various options. We are aiming to have a more intuitive interface that simultaneously offers more flexibility for more complicated information layouts rather than the static layout of the old site.</p> <h6>A Quick REST Example</h6><p>Here’s a basic “Hello World” example for you to try out:</p> <ol> <li><p>Make sure you’re logged into <a data-type='internal' to='/'>https://developer.webex.com</a> with your Webex account.</p> </li> <li><p>In the main banner, expand <strong>Documentation</strong> and then select either <strong>Calling</strong>, <strong>Meetings</strong> or <strong>Messaging</strong>.</p> </li> <li><p>Under <strong>API REFERENCE</strong> expand <strong>All APIs</strong> and navigate to the Webex <strong>People</strong> API.</p> </li> <li><p>Select <strong>Get My Own Details</strong>.</p> </li> <li><p>Select <strong>Run</strong>. You should see a 200 response code and information on your Webex account similar to:</p> <p> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt721b9338844eb707/converged-developer-portal-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> </ol> <h6>Current Limitations and Caveats</h6><p>At this time, please keep the following limitation in mind:</p> <ol> <li>We are completely rearchitecting our site search to improve performance, relevance and maintainability. We expect a first search release shortly.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>We Value Your Feedback</h6><p>Feel free to contact us with any feedback at <a href='mailto:devsupport@webex.com' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>devsupport@webex.com</a>, and we’ll make sure it gets routed to the appropriate team. We are interested in any criticism as well as suggestions for improvement. Keep in mind, too, that we’ll be actively working on improving your experience moving forward as well.</p> <h6>Documentation Site Map</h6><p>To help you get your bearings when you&#39;re looking for a documentation for a particular feature, here&#39;s a basic site map:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2377dcbb66c517fb/Webex-Dev-Portal-Docs.png" alt="Webex Converged Portal Site Map"></p> ]]>
...
</description>
