<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Getting Started with the Converged Recordings APIs for Webex Calling ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7ce13424ca828a3a/682e121064f73f2507903f90/webex-calling-converged-recordings-api-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Getting Started with the Converged Recordings APIs for Webex Calling" /> <p>The Webex Calling product recently added the option to have “Webex” be the call recording provider for an organization, alongside the previous set of third-party call recording partners. When selecting <em>Webex</em> as the call recording provider, it utilizes the same mechanism as Webex Meeting recordings to output high quality audio files. Webex call recording is accessible to all users in a Calling organization and provides unlimited recording capabilities. Currently, Webex recordings have a retention period of one year, with each organization allotted 100GB of storage. Another great feature of Webex call recordings is the ability to receive <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/9leme/Webex-App-%7C-AI-generated-summaries-for-call-recordings' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>AI-generated summaries</a>, where you can quickly catch up on a discussion and get a better understanding of the conversation at a glance.</p> <p>The Webex call recording option also gives developers access to a new set of APIs to automate the management of call recordings in Webex Calling – <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings'>Converged Recordings APIs</a>. These endpoints can be used for integrations that automate the archival of older recordings for long-term storage, satisfy compliance archival requirements, dynamically link conversations to customer profiles in a CRM, generate custom reports based on call recording metadata, route flagged recordings for supervisor review, and more.</p> <p>In this article, we will first show how the Webex Call Recording option is selected in Control Hub. Then we will explore the new Converged Recordings API endpoints and explain how they work for different Webex user roles.</p> <h6>Webex Call Recording in a Developer Sandbox</h6><p>The first step to start using the Converged Recordings APIs is for an admin to enable Webex as the call recording provider for the organization. This is where a <a data-type='internal' to='/admin/docs/developer-sandbox-guide'>Webex Developer Sandbox</a> comes in handy, which provides administrator-level access to your own Webex organization. The instructions to enable Webex as the recording provider in Control Hub are rather straightforward:</p> <ol> <li>Once you have access to a Developer Sandbox, log in to Control Hub with your admin credentials.</li> <li>Go to <em>Services &gt; Calling &gt; Service Settings</em>.</li> <li>Under <strong>Call Recording</strong>, select “Webex” as the call recording provider from the drop-down list. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltfa64baabde6ef4bc/webex-calling-converged-recordings-api-blog-2.jpeg" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Click “Save”.</li> </ol> <ul> <li>For the most up to date instructions on enabling Webex call recording at an organizational level, see <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/ilga4/Manage-call-recording-for-Webex-Calling#Cisco_Task.dita_bdcfdaed-bd71-4a2e-a420-a43d2128f4c1' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>these instructions</a>.</li> <li>To configure your sandbox for call transcriptions (currently available only in the Webex app) and AI-generated summaries that includes Notes and Action Items (available on both the Webex app and Converged Recordings APIs), see <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/ilga4/Manage-call-recording-for-Webex-Calling#concept-template_185f248b-c355-45ca-96ea-e44fe86340a8' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>the instructions here</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Since the developer sandboxes do not include public telephone access in Webex Calling, the easiest way to make test calls is by utilizing “extension dialing”.&#xa0; This allows calling between test users without the need for setting up a paid PSTN number. In this scenario, the calls are supported by Webex and not through the public telephone network. Test users can essentially be assigned any number string as a dialable extension. A test user can dial another user’s extensions, answer incoming calls, and execute in-call actions (including recording) <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n3xx7vcb/Get-started-with-Webex-App#Cisco_Concept.dita_117a2dd6-a84e-4247-a9fc-84a8d5644ee7' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>inside the Webex app</a> or by leveraging the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/call-controls'>Call Control APIs</a>.</p> <ul> <li>For instructions on setting up extension dialing on a developer sandbox, <a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/974fc2b9-9ba1-4889-9d04-ea7751f92c33' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>watch this helpful Vidcast</a>.</li> <li>To get more familiarized with the Call Control APIs, check out <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-calling-getting-started-with-call-control-apis'>my previous blog</a> on this subject.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Exploring the Converged Recordings APIs</h6><p>While the Webex Meetings and Calling products can share the same method of recording when Webex is selected as the call recording provider, the <a data-type='internal' to='/meeting/docs/api/v1/recordings'>Recording APIs</a> are still the exclusive to Meetings and Converged Recordings APIs are exclusive to Calling. In the future, Meeting Recordings will also be included in the Converged Recordings APIs. Until then, both sets of APIs do share the same basic schema that makes it easy to transition from one endpoint to the other.</p> <p>In this section, we’ll break down the functionality for the Converged Recordings APIs based on specific roles in Webex.</p> <h6>User Level APIs</h6><p>Integrations for <em>regular Webex users</em> have access to the following Converged Recordings APIs:</p> <ul> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/list-recordings'>List Recordings</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint is usually the first API call used to retrieve the <code>ID</code> that corresponds to a specific recording that is required for subsequent API calls. This API also returns some general data about the file and the available <code>status</code> of the file. If the <code>status</code> is specified as <code>deleted</code>, the recording has been moved to the <em>recycle bin</em>.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-details'>Get Recording Details</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires the <code>recordingID</code> that is retrieved from the <em>List Recordings API</em> noted priorly. This returns the unique download links for the call recordings, AI-generated summaries (action items, suggested notes, and short notes), along with other data of the recording file.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-metadata'>Get Recording metadata API</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> to retrieve the metadata of the recording file which contains much more details of the recording, including sensitive data such as phone numbers. If the query parameter showAllTypes is <code>true</code>, the additional details about <code>mediaStreams</code>, <code>participants</code>, <code>redirectInfo</code> and <code>redirectedCall</code> are included in the response body.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/move-recordings-into-the-recycle-bin'>Move Recordings into the Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> to move individual recordings to the recycle bin (soft delete). To move all recordings of the user to the recycle bin, the <code>trashAll</code> parameter that is set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body and no <code>recordingID</code>is required.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/purge-recordings-from-recycle-bin'>Purge Recordings from Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> that has a <code>status</code> specified as <code>deleted</code> to purge individual recordings from the recycle bin (hard delete). To purge all recordings of the user from the recycle bin, the <code>purgeAll</code> parameter that is set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body and no <code>recordingID</code>is required. Recordings are fully purged from the recycle bin only after the 30-day retention policy is met and cannot be restored after that. During the retention period, an admin or compliance officer can still restore recordings purged by the user.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/restore-recordings-from-recycle-bin'>Restore Recordings from Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> that has a <code>status</code> specified as <code>deleted</code> to restore individual recordings from the recycle bin. To restore all recordings of the user from the recycle bin, the <code>restoreAll</code> parameter set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body and no <code>recordingID</code>is required.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Administrator and Compliance Officer Level APIs</h6><p>Integrations for <em>Webex administrators</em> and <em>compliance officers</em> have access to larger set of Converged Recordings APIs, some of which are exclusive to either role:</p> <ul> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/list-recordings-for-admin-or-compliance-officer'>List Recordings for Admin or Compliance Officer</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_read</code>, <em>required scope for compliance officer is</em> <code>spark-compliance:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint works much like the List Recordings API for users to retrieve the <code>recordingID</code> for each file, except there are a variety of extra query parameters to filter by specific owners, dates, locations, etc.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-details'>Get Recording Details</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_read</code>, <em>required scope for compliance officer is</em> <code>spark-compliance:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint requires the <code>recordingID</code> that is retrieved from the <em>List Recordings for Admin or Compliance Officer API</em> noted priorly. This returns the unique download links along with other data of the recording file.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-metadata'>Get Recording metadata API</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_read</code>, <em>required scope for compliance officer is</em> <code>spark-compliance:recordings_read</code></p> <ul> <li>Just like the user level scope, this endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> to retrieve the metadata of the recording file which contains much more details of the recording, including PII data. If the query parameter showAllTypes is true, the additional details about <code>mediaStreams</code>, <code>participants</code>, <code>redirectInfo</code> and <code>redirectedCall</code> are included in the response body.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/move-recordings-into-the-recycle-bin'>Move Recordings into the Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>Just like the user level scope, this endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> to move individual recordings to the recycle bin (soft delete). To move all recordings of the user to the recycle bin, the <code>trashAll</code> parameter that is set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body. In this case, an <code>ownerEmail</code> is now required and a <code>recordingID</code>is not.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/purge-recordings-from-recycle-bin'>Purge Recordings from Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>Just like the user level scope, this endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> that has a <code>status</code> specified as <code>deleted</code> to purge individual recordings from the recycle bin (hard delete). To purge all recordings of the user from the recycle bin, the <code>purgeAll</code> parameter that is set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body. In this case, an <code>ownerEmail</code> is now required and a <code>recordingID</code>is not. Recordings are fully purged from the recycle bin only after the 30-day retention policy is met and cannot be restored after that. See the <a data-type='internal' to='/compliance/docs/compliance'>Compliance Guide</a> for more information on recording file retention policy.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/restore-recordings-from-recycle-bin'>Restore Recordings from Recycle Bin</a> – <em>required scope for admin is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>Just like the user level scope, this endpoint requires a <code>recordingID</code> that has a <code>status</code> specified as <code>deleted</code> to restore individual recordings from the recycle bin. To restore all recordings of the user from the recycle bin, the <code>restoreAll</code> parameter that is set to <code>true</code> can be added to the request body. In this case, an <code>ownerEmail</code> is now required and a <code>recordingID</code>is not.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/reassign-recordings'>Reassign Recordings</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark-admin:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint is <strong>exclusive toadministrators</strong> and requires two parameters: <code>reassignOwnerEmail</code> for the account the recordings will be moved into, and <code>recordingIds</code> which accepts a list of one or more <code>recordingID</code> values that specify the files to be reassigned.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><a data-type='internal' to='/calling/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/delete-a-recording'>Delete a Recording</a> – <em>required scope is</em> <code>spark-compliance:recordings_write</code></p> <ul> <li>This endpoint is <strong>exclusive to compliance officers</strong> and requires a <code>recordingID</code> to permanently delete a call recording. Once a recording is deleted by a compliance officer, it becomes inaccessible no matter the user role and purged from Webex altogether.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Need Some More Help? We’ve Got You Covered</h6><p>We are excited to provide support for these new APIs and eager to see some of the outcomes from our developer community! As always, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist if you gave any questions or need help. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>. Until next time, happy developing!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

From building with our APIs and SDKs to previewing what’s coming next, this is your opportunity to learn, share, and build better collaboration experiences.</p> <ul> <li>📍 Where: Cisco Live San Diego 2025</li> <li>📅 When: June 9–13, 2025</li> <li>🧠 Who: Webex Product, Engineering, and Developer Relations</li> <li>🏁 Find us: Webex for Developers Booth in the DevNet Zone (Tuesday &amp; Wednesday)</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Why You Should Join</h6><br/> <ul> <li>Dive into Webex APIs, SDKs, Embedded Apps, and Contact Center integrations</li> <li>Attend sessions led by Webex engineers and evangelists</li> <li>Learn how to get published on the App Hub</li> <li>Visit the Webex for Developers booth to ask questions and explore use cases</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Webex Developer Session Lineup</h6><p>All sessions are listed in the Cisco Live Session Catalog: <a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/global/learn/session-catalog.html#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://www.ciscolive.com/global/learn/session-catalog.html#/</a>.</p> <h6>Lab Sessions</h6><br/> <ul> <li>Configuring Business Outcome using Proactive Digital Channels with AI Agent and AI Assistant<ul> <li>Session ID: LTRCCT-2015</li> <li>Speaker: Rue Green, Sr. Solutions Engineer / Full Stack Developer, Cisco - Distinguished Speaker</li> <li>Date: Monday, Jun 9</li> <li>Time: 2:00 PM - 2:30 PM PDT</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>DevNet Lightning Talk Sessions</h6><br/> <ul> <li>Navigating the Webex App Hub Review Process: Best Practices for Developers<ul> <li>Session ID: DEVLIT-1203</li> <li>Speaker: Joe Zanini, Developer Evangelist, Cisco</li> <li>Date: Tuesday, Jun 10</li> <li>Time: 3:30 PM - 3:50 PM PDT</li> </ul> </li> <li>Exploring the Webex Developer Beta Program: Engage, Test, and Innovate<ul> <li>Session ID: DEVLIT-1843</li> <li>Speaker: Adam Weeks, Senior Engineering Manager, Cisco - DEVNET-1699<ul> <li>Session ID: DEVNET-1699</li> <li>Speaker: Adam Weeks, Senior Engineering Manager, Cisco - Distinguished Speaker</li> <li>Date: Wednesday, Jun 11</li> <li>Time: 1:00 PM - 1:45 PM PDT</li> </ul> </li> <li>Integrating Webex Contact Center Agent Functionality into Web Applications with the WxCC SDK<ul> <li>Session ID: DEVNET-2082</li> <li>Speaker: Arun Ganeshan, Software Engineering Technical Leader, Cisco</li> <li>Date: Tuesday, Jun 10</li> <li>Time: 1:30 PM - 12:45 PM PDT</li> </ul> </li> <li>Implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization for Webex Integrations <ul> <li>Session ID: DEVNET-2675</li> <li>Speaker: Joe Zanini, Developer Evangelist, Cisco</li> <li>Date: Thursday, Jun 12</li> <li>Time: 11:30 AM - 10:15 AM PDT</li> </ul> </li> <li>Extending Webex Contact Center with Flow Designer Extensibility<ul> <li>Session ID: DEVNET-2915</li> <li>Speaker: Adam Weeks, Senior Engineering Manager, Cisco - Distinguished Speaker</li> <li>Date: Thursday, Jun 12</li> <li>Time: 10:30 AM - 11:15 AM PDT</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>DevNet Workshop Sessions</h6><br/> <ul> <li>Build-a-Bot with Webex<ul> <li>ID: DEVWKS-1149</li> <li>Speaker: Phil Bellanti, Sr. Webex Developer Evangelist, Cisco - <item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – April 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – April 2025" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers. We&#39;ve had another busy month with a lot of new content for you to check out. Keep reading to get all the latest updates, announcements, and how-to guides for the entire Webex Developer ecosystem!</p> <h6>📊 The Evaluation of Generative AI Performance in Webex Contact Center</h6><p>There was a new blog posted by Cloud Engineering Technical Leader, Anupam Mukherjee, for evaluating Generative AI performance in Webex Contact Center. In this article, discover how the scoring system ensures top-tier quality, consistency, and reliability in AI-generated outputs. You will also learn about innovative algorithms, contextual assessments, and the importance of Responsible AI in creating more accurate and trustworthy content.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-evaluation-of-generative-ai-performance-in-webex-contact-center'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📺 Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On Wednesday, April 30th at 1:00PM EDT, get ready to unlock early access to the latest innovations in the Webex developer ecosystem through the <strong>Webex Developer Beta Program</strong>. This webinar provides a comprehensive overview of the program, highlighting how developers can engage with beta releases, offer insightful feedback, and help shape the evolution of Webex APIs and SDKs. Covering all facets of the Webex ecosystem, including Messaging, Meetings, Calling, and Contact Center, this session will walk you through a real-world example of participating in a beta test. Discover the benefits of joining the beta community and how you can influence the future of Webex solutions by participating in this dynamic program.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Webex Developer βeta Activities</h6><p>Attention While on the topic of the Webex Developer Beta program, we have a brand-new entry that is now available for testing – the <strong>Webex Contact Center SDK</strong>. This powerful JavaScript library lets you embed Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop functionalities into your web applications! You can manage agent statuses, control calls (accept, decline, hold, end), and create custom softphone solutions. You can also integrate with existing CRM solutions and build custom widgets!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>📡 Live Streaming via the Meeting APIs</h6><p>Webex Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti, has a new blog post detailing a recent update to the Meeting APIs that allows meeting hosts to automate the setup of live streaming through services, such as IBM Video Streaming, Facebook Live, Vbrik Rev, and YouTube Live. This feature is ideal to help your meetings reach a wider audience for product launches, company announcements, expert panel discussions and more. Discover how it comes together to increase the exposure of your important meetings!</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/meeting-apis-now-support-live-streaming'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🔊 The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Audio Files</h6><p>Webex Developer Evangelist, Joe Zanini, just published the third installment of the blog series, “The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs”. This is the series where we are attempting to traverse the vast set of RESTful API endpoints available for Webex developers. In this edition, we go over the Audio Files APIs, how audio files are used, and how to manage them in the Webex Contact Center ecosystem.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis-audio-files'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📄 App Pagination Hands-on Guide</h6><p>In a recent article authored by Webex Software Engineer, Rudrakshi Srivastava, discover how the <em>Paginate</em> app transforms your browsing experience to simplify access to content. Paginate is a powerful GUI tool designed to streamline robust interactions with the Webex API, enabling you to execute a variety of queries and efficiently export the results. It is particularly beneficial when dealing with extensive datasets that necessitate pagination, such as retrieving comprehensive lists of spaces.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/an-app-pagination-hands-on-guide'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🐢 Webex API Rate Limiting</h6><p>A popular blog post by Technical Solutions Specialist, Taylor Hanson, has been updated for 2025. This article covers how the Webex API has rate limits in place for different resources, such as <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/messages'>/messages</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/rooms'>/rooms</a>, to protect from distributed denial of service attacks. These limits will vary depending on the calls being made, how resource intensive that call is on the servers, and how many servers are actively in routing – and is subject to change as needed to protect all use cases from failing in the event of a large batch of requests. Check out the blog to learn how to handle these API rate limits in your app and keep things running smoothly.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/rate-limiting-and-the-webex-api'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📝 Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>There were some important API updates recently listed in the Webex API Changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>BREAKING CHANGE</strong> – April 4, 2025: For user convenience, the previous <em>List Meetings of a Meeting Series API</em> has been merged into the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/list-meetings'>List Meetings API</a>.</li> <li><strong>NEW</strong> – April 7, 2025 – As Partner organizations that manage their customers through Webex Partner Hub can now download Partner Hub reports directly using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/partner-reports-templates'>Partner Reports Template API.</a></li> <li><strong>BREAKING CHANGE</strong> – April 15, 2025: Previously, authorized bots could access a person&#39;s pronouns based on Control Hub settings. However, to prioritize customer privacy and ensure data is used only when it’s necessary, we are disabling this feature. This change should go into effect at the end of April 2025.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Full Webex API Changelog <span class="Hyperlink">→</a></p> ]]>

</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Introducing Service Apps for Webex Contact Center ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt645b73ebf4f1f5cf/68080d49e8bf0d39ccf059e1/intro-to-service-apps-for-contact-center-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Introducing Service Apps for Webex Contact Center" /> <p>We are pleased to announce that <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/contact-center-service-apps'>Service Apps</a> have been made available for Webex Contact Center. With Service Apps, mission critical Contact Center integrations can now be deployed on behalf of an organization instead of individual users. With a standard integration, if the authorizing user departs or updates their password, the integration will simply stop working. Conversely, a Service App can request data for multiple users throughout an entire organization, rather than just a single user. This provides much more flexibility for tasks that run continually in an organization. Let’s explore some of the most optimal use cases for Service Apps in Contact Center.</p> <h6>Service App Use Cases for Contact Center</h6><p>When Service Apps were <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/service-apps-revolutionizing-business-apps-for-more-efficient-workflows'>first introduced</a> to Webex for Developers, they were targeted towards Webex administrator tasks such as automated provisioning, Compliance Officer tasks that poll the Events API, and creating Webex guest accounts. The original Service Apps guide for those application types can be found <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>here</a>. In Webex Contact Center, Supervisor-level tasks that are needed on a persistent basis are the most prominent use for Service Apps. This can be things like monitoring agent performance, improving customer escalations, and generating analytics for active reporting.</p> <p>One example would be a Service App for agent call recording, using the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/captures'>Captures API or Webhooks</a> to retrieve and analyze recorded interactions. This can be for supervisors to ensure quality control and compliance throughout the organization, provide training and feedback to agents, and handle dispute resolutions more effectively. Call recording is certainly an ideal scenario for a Service App since it will need to be active every business day for all agents on duty.</p> <p>Another great way a Service App can be leveraged in Webex Contact Center is for a reporting system through the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/search'>Search API or Webhooks</a>. Again, this type of app needs to stay active on a long-term basis to extract all the report data for each day. From there, it can send that data to a third-party service such as <a href='https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Microsoft Power BI</a> or <a href='https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/analytics/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Snowflake</a> to create visual representations or populate dashboards with specific metrics. For more information on how to work with this endpoint, check out the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/getting-started-with-search-api'>Getting Started with the Search API</a> guide.</p> <h6>Developer Workflows for Contact Center Service Apps</h6><p>Webex Service Apps and traditional integrations do have several similarities, as both are based on the OAuth 2.0 protocol. While the OAuth client creation and scope selection occur for both, the process for obtaining access tokens is different for Service Apps. The process can either be done completely within the GUI interface of the Webex Developer portal or automated via API and webhooks. Regardless of the method, it is first contingent upon administrator authorization in Control Hub to start the process for obtaining the Service App tokens. To start testing this out, make sure to get a free <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/sandbox_cc'>Contact Center Developer Sandbox</a> that provides administrator access and licenses to your own organization.</p> <p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/contact-center-service-apps#token-retrieval-via-api'>developer guide</a> has step-by-step instructions on how to create a Service App for Contact Center and retrieve access &amp; refresh tokens. When creating a new Service App for Contact Center, any of the integration scopes <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/guides/integrations#scopes'>documented here</a> are valid (depending on the use case), except for <code>spark:applications_token</code> and <code>spark:kms</code>. These two scopes are still important to Service Apps, as they correspond to the <em>Access Token API</em> for automating the token retrieval process. In this scenario, a token retrieval app needs to be created as a <em>separate</em> integration from the Service App that will implement the tokens to access the APIs. You can also find more information on retrieving the Service App tokens via API by referring to the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/authentication-cc'>authentication guide</a>.</p> <p>To see how it all comes together, check out this Node.js <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/service_app_token_getter' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Service App Token Getter</a> demo app that incorporates the entire Service App authorization workflow to obtain access and refresh tokens. The app first creates a Node.js server to manage OAuth processes for a Webex Integration and creates webhooks for Service App authorization events. From there, the server listens for HTTP requests and processes them to manage authorization and tokens. You can even run the demo locally on your machine for quick testing.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? No Problem!</h6><p>As always, we are happy to provide developer support for any of the features mentioned here. If you need help or have any questions, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is always eager to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>. Until next time, happy developing on Webex!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Audio Files ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9864ac0183200591/67fd4c6d4eec13512f95e10e/audio-files-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Audio Files" /> <p>Thank you for checking out the third installment of the blog series, “The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs”. This is the series where we are attempting to traverse the vast set of RESTful API endpoints available for Webex developers. In this edition we will be going over the Audio Files APIs and how audio files are used in the Webex Contact Center ecosystem. </p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Audio Files</h6><p>Webex Contact Center administrators will strategically use <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/be12vp/Manage-audio-files#concept-template_d1a97755-4e53-4993-a65f-9859a2134332' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>audio prompts</a>, <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/be12vp/Manage-audio-files#concept-template_10502595-49be-4026-94c8-c5de36f2f03d' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>custom agent greetings</a>, and <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>courtesy callback</a> messages throughout the <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nhovcy4/Build-and-manage-flows-with-Flow-Designer' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Flow Designer</a> setup and routing configuration process.</p> <h6>Audio File Management</h6><p>There are various options for Webex Contact Center users to manage audio files in the system. #### </p> <h6>The Control Hub</h6><p>The Webex Control Hub is a web-based, central management portal that allows Webex administrators to manage a Webex organization, users, assign services, view analytics, and more. Because the Control Hub is the mothership for the entire Webex Suite (Messaging, Meeting, Calling, Vidcast, Contact Center, Connected UC and Hybrid Services), the following material will focus on the Webex Contact Center use case. It can be easy to get caught up in managing <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5y120ab/Manage-announcement-repository' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>announcement audio files for Webex Calling</a> and the APIs mentioned in this blog will not populate audio files for that service.</p> <p>To manage Webex Contact Center audio files using the Control Hub, start by signing in at admin.webex.com as an administrator. Then go to Services &gt; Contact Center &gt; Customer Experience &gt; Audio Files. Here an administrator can create and upload new audio files. Also, they can update and delete existing files.</p> <h6>Third Party Integrations</h6><p>One of the benefits of being a Webex Contact Center user is that there is a robust set of open RESTful APIs available for teams to use to build apps that automate the heavy lifting when it comes to migrating from say an on-prem contact center solution to a cloud-based solution like the Webex Contact Center. One such application is <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/univonix-cc-accelerator-uccx-to-webex-contact-center-univonix' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Univonix CC Accelerator</a>. This tool automates UCCX Discovery and Migration to the Webex Contact Center. The service is a set of tools designed to streamline the migration process by automating data provisioning, thus accelerating time to consumption. You can see more information about this integration, and many more, on the Webex App Hub.</p> <h6>Internal Tools for Automation</h6><p>Some organizations have technical talent on various teams that help automate processes like migration or build internal tools for managing files. The developer docs on the Webex developer portal are awesome, but sometimes it helps to learn about a developer’s experience with the tools of the task when approaching a new project. That is why this blog series exists, to give developers a glimpse of what happens beyond what is documented.</p> <h6>Audio Files APIs</h6><p>Let’s break down the API endpoints that make audio file magic happen:</p> <h6>Create a New Audio File</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/create-a-new-audio-file'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/create-a-new-audio-file</a></p> <p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/create-a-new-audio-file'>Create a New Audio File API</a> is self-explanatory. This is the endpoint a developer is going to use when building apps for uploading new files to the audio file library. This API also will be used in migration applications. Integrations will require an administrators access token and the <code>cjp:config</code> scope.</p> <p>There are some caveats that are worth noting when implementing this API call. For example, the documentation calls for two objects to be sent in the body of the request, audioFileInfo and audioFile. The audioFileInfo object is a JSON object that contains things like the file name, the Webex organization id, the file content type (AUDIO_WAV, AUDIO_X_WAV), an optional blob id, download URL, and description. The audioFile is a binary representation of the file data.</p> <p>The audioFileInfo JSON object is pretty straight forward but there are some things to consider when building it. For example, the <code>id</code>, <code>createdTime</code>, <code>lastUpdatedTime</code>, and <code>url</code> are optional parameters to include, but a developer does not want to include a value for these when initially creating or uploading an audio file via API because the Webex Contact Center system will build these on a successful upload. The audioFile object must be binary. A developer is not limited when it comes to file to binary conversion methods. See the below sample code for an idea of how one can accomplish this conversion.</p> <p>When both objects are compiled, the developer can then use a form data interface to construct a set of key/value pairs representing form fields and their values that are then consumed by Webex Contact Center. Below is a sample of how to implement this API using JavaScript, on a Node server.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">import axios from &#39;axios&#39; import FormData from &#39;form-data&#39;; import fs from &#39;fs&#39;; import path, { resolve } from &#39;path&#39;; import { fileURLToPath } from &#39;url&#39;; const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url); const __dirname = path.dirname(__filename); /* a helper function for writing a file that was passed locally to later be read/converted into binary. */ function writeFileLocally(file) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) =&gt; { const tempFilePath = path.join(__dirname, file.file.originalname); fs.writeFile(tempFilePath, file.file.buffer, (err) =&gt; { if (err) { reject(err); } else { resolve(tempFilePath); } }); }); } /* a function to be used in other parts of the backend. takes in a file and a user/administrator object. */ export const createAudioFileApi = async function (file, user) { //prep form data const formData = new FormData(); //construct JSON object to serve as audioFileInfo in API call. const fileInfo = { name: file.name, contentType: &#39;AUDIO_WAV&#39;, systemDefault: false } const writeFile = await writeFileLocally(file); //attach audioFile binary to formData formData.append(&#39;audioFile&#39;, fs.createReadStream(writeFile), { contentType: &#39;audio/wav&#39; }); //attach audioFileInfo JSON object to formData formData.append(&#39;audioFileInfo&#39;, JSON.stringify(fileInfo), { contentType: &#39;application/json&#39; }); //sample API call const response = await axios.post(`https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/organization/${user.orgId}/audio-file`, formData, { headers: { &#39;Accept&#39;: &#39;*/*&#39;, &#39;Authorization&#39;: `Bearer ${user.accessToken}` } }).catch(error =&gt; { if (error.response) { console.error(&#39;Request failed with status:&#39;, error.status); if (error.response.status === 404) { console.warn(&#39;Resource not found.&#39;); } } else if (error.request) { console.error(&#39;No response received:&#39;, error.request); } else { console.error(&#39;Error during request setup:&#39;, error.message); } return { success: false, message: error.message || &#39;An error occurred when accessing audio files.&#39;, code: error.code || &#39;AUDIO_FILES_ERROR&#39; }; }); return response.data; } </code></pre> <h6>Update a Specific Audio File by ID</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/update-specific-audio-file-by-id'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/update-specific-audio-file-by-id</a></p> <p>Developers will use the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/update-specific-audio-file-by-id'>Update a Specific Audio File by ID</a> if they want to do a complete overhaul of an existing audio file in the Webex Contact Center audio file library. The implementation is the same as the Create a New Audio File endpoint except that the id parameter, and desired updates, are required when calling this API. If the only desired change is something like the description, then a developer is advised to use the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/partially-update-audio-file-by-id'>Partially Update Audio File by ID</a> endpoint as the implementation is more efficient.</p> <h6>Get Specific Audio File by ID</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/get-specific-audio-file-by-id'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/get-specific-audio-file-by-id</a></p> <p>Developers can use <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/get-specific-audio-file-by-id'>Get Specific Audio File by ID</a> to retrieve an existing Audio File in a given organization. In this API request developers should include the Webex Contact Center Organization ID and the audio file resource ID in the path parameters. Developers can also include an optional <code>includeUrl</code> query parameter to indicate whether they need the download URL.</p> <h6>Delete Specific Audio File by ID</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/delete-specific-audio-file-by-id'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/delete-specific-audio-file-by-id</a></p> <p>With the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/delete-specific-audio-file-by-id'>Delete Specific Audio File by ID</a>, you guessed it, a developer can make a request, include Webex Organization ID and audio file resource ID information in the path parameters and delete a single audio file from the Webex Contact Center Audio File library.</p> <h6>Partially Update Audio File by ID</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/partially-update-audio-file-by-id'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/partially-update-audio-file-by-id</a></p> <p>This API was mentioned above. It is a lot simpler than not “partially” updating an audio file via API. The developer needs to include the Webex Organization ID and audio file resource ID information in the path parameters of the API request. In the body of the API call, the developer can include the changes to the description that are required and then look out for a successful response from the API server.</p> <h6>List References For a Specific Audio File</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-references-for-a-specific-audio-file'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-references-for-a-specific-audio-file</a></p> <p>A developer will maybe want to List <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-references-for-a-specific-audio-file'>References For a Specific Audio File</a> before deciding if they want to delete this file. This API will provide some context to the extent in which an audio file is being used within a Webex Contact Center’s day to day operations. This API provides insight into which CAD variables in specific Flows are tied to the audio file. If there are many teams using the file, maybe to do some additional checks before changing a file for deleting it.</p> <h6>List Audio Files</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-audio-files'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-audio-files</a></p> <p>Developers can obtain a complete set of audio files contained by a Webex Contact Center Organization with the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/audio-files/list-audio-files'>List Audio Files</a> endpoint. This API will also return all data available about each audio file in the library.</p> <h6>Agent Personal Greeting Files</h6><p>There is a brand-new set of APIs available for Webex Contact Center developers interested in zeroing in on audio files specifically for the Agent Personal Greetings feature. These APIs operate similarly to the Audio Files APIs except they will categorize the targeted files for this intended use case. You can check out the documentation <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agent-personal-greeting'>here</a>.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Rate Limiting and the Webex API ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt87afde604421d53d/5b4df57cf80cc8770b852c0c/WebexDevBlog_HowTo_C_R1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Rate Limiting and the Webex API" /> <div><Callout type="info">This blog has been updated for 2025. </Callout></div> <p>In this blog, we’ll provide a guide to implementing rate limiting with the Webex API to gracefully allocate resources across the shared Webex customer base, preventing excessive request errors in your own app, and ensure efficient API call management. We’ll examine practical solutions like using the <code>Retry-After</code> header to handle HTTP 429 errors and offers a Python code example for seamless integration in your own environment.</p> <p>To protect the Webex environment, especially from distributed denial of service attacks, the API has rate limits in place for the different resources available for use, such as <code>/messages</code> and <code>/rooms</code>. These limits will vary depending on the calls being made, how resource intensive that call is on the servers, and how many servers are actively in routing – and is subject to change as needed to protect all use cases from failing in the event of a large batch of requests.</p> <h6>A Rate Limiting Solution</h6><p>So, what should be done if you want to make API calls very frequently, but don’t want to hit errors and lose requests by going over the rate limit? The answer is to use the <code>Retry-After</code> Header that is returned with an <code>HTTP 429</code> error. The <code>Retry-After</code> header defines the number of seconds you’ll need to wait before sending API requests again.</p> <h6>Implementing Rate Limiting in Python</h6><p>The Python app that follows pulls the list of rooms available to the user (using a single user or bot’s bearer token), as fast as possible. Normally, it would be recommended to put wait time between continuous looping requests, to avoid hitting the rate limit entirely. However, since that rate limit might be reached anyway depending on the resource availability, it’s important to handle the likely possibility you’ll catch a 429 here and there.</p> <p>Basically, we make a call to the integrations URL continuously and look for an error in each response. If the error is a status code 429, we check the wait time relayed to us in the <code>Retry-After</code> header and sleep for the time specified before starting again. If there’s an error, but it isn’t a <code>429</code>, we break out of the loop because something else is wrong. Maybe you had a bad bearer token, or maybe there is a general error with the format of the request.</p> <div><Callout type="info">Since this code can run forever if implemented properly, you’ll need to Ctrl+C to kill it in the Terminal itself – make sure you don’t let it go on indefinitely or you could be flagged depending on how many requests are made and for how long. </Callout></div> <h6>The Python Application</h6><p>The initial portion of the application is making the call to the rooms resource to get the rooms over and over, whereas the latter section beginning with the line:</p> <pre><code class="language-python">except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: </code></pre> <p>defines what to do if a <code>429</code> error is encountered – print out the content of the error and then extract the value of the Retry-After header for use in the sleep. Here’s the full app (it’s short so we’ll provide the whole thing):</p> <pre><code class="language-python">import urllib.request import urllib.error import json import time def sendWebexGET(url): request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={&quot;Accept&quot;: &quot;application/json&quot;, &quot;Content-Type&quot;: &quot;application/json&quot;}) request.add_header(&quot;Authorization&quot;, &quot;Bearer &quot; + bearer) response = urllib.request.urlopen(request) return response bearer = &quot;PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE&quot; while True: try: result = sendWebexGET(&#39;https://webexapis.com/v1/rooms&#39;) print(result.getcode(), time.time(), result.headers[&#39;trackingId&#39;]) except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: if e.code == 429: print(&#39;code&#39;, e.code) print(&#39;headers&#39;, e.headers) print(&#39;Sleeping for&#39;, e.headers[&#39;Retry-After&#39;], &#39;seconds&#39;) sleep_time = int(e.headers[&#39;Retry-After&#39;]) while sleep_time &gt; 10: time.sleep(10) sleep_time -= 10 print(&#39;Asleep for&#39;, sleep_time, &#39;more seconds&#39;) time.sleep(sleep_time) else: print(e, e.code) break </code></pre> <p>It’s important to note that it’s possible to send a request after receiving a 429 without getting an error; there are many servers involved with handling a request, so just because you’ve hit the rate limit of one, does not mean you’ve hit the rate limit of all. However, you’re probably pretty close to failing on every server, so it’s best to wait for the time described by <code>Retry-After</code> upon detecting the very first <code>429</code>.</p> <h6>Run the Application</h6><p>To run the application, save the code in a filename with the extension .py, replace <code>PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE </code>with your personal access token from the Webex developer portal and enter:</p> <p><code>python &lt;your-filename.py&gt;</code></p> <p>You should see output along the lines of:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">$ python foobar.py 200 1743697618.5233638 ROUTERGW_1862482a-c1b9-4c73-bc6b-ffea30a609a7 200 1743697619.5045638 ROUTERGW_f2395a15-1b0d-4f01-9020-7a42fb480f8c 200 1743697620.6093526 ROUTERGW_e4fcb023-ba3a-40e3-b383-9a5ac31188cd 200 1743697621.1333084 ROUTERGW_cbdb5f0c-a9ba-4351-84a7-833a7a43e3db 200 1743697621.6740065 ROUTERGW_26fd34d4-0205-426a-88f1-68183d5cde80 200 1743697622.1625683 ROUTERGW_a4251c0d-b7a9-45e5-9c45-d8befc16157f 200 1743697622.6426196 ROUTERGW_b077d943-e515-41ba-81ba-d64df820aee3 </code></pre> <p>Terminate the script when you’re ready with <code>Ctrl-C</code>.</p> <p>The full code can be found on our <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/WebexRetryAfterDemo' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Github</a>.</p> <h6>In Closing</h6><p>As always, if you have any questions, please contact <a href='mailto:devsupport@webex.com' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>devsupport@webex.com</a> 24/7/365 - we’re happy to help!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Meeting APIs Now Support Live Streaming ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8f50b9591cb2e23f/67e19a82362ee3f1d355c730/meeting-apis-now-support-live-streaming-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Meeting APIs Now Support Live Streaming" /> <p>There was a great update recently released for the Meeting APIs that enables hosts to setup <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/a6cmw/Live-stream-meetings-and-webinars' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>live streaming of their meetings and webinars</a> through various services, such as <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/1gt29d/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>IBM Video Streaming</a>, <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/ka80pdb/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Facebook Live</a>, <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/i7a7v6/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Vbrik Rev</a>, and <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/d9zqvi/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>YouTube Live</a>. This feature is ideal to help your meetings reach a wider audience for product launches, company announcements, expert panel discussions and more. Another benefit of this feature is that instead of having to make an exhaustive list of meeting invitees, you can simply provide a link to your live stream, and anyone can view your live stream quickly and easily. Now that this can be enabled via the Meetings APIs, you can completely automate the process to set up a live stream of any Webex meeting or webinar and optimize efficiency.</p> <h6>Live Stream Attributes in the Meeting APIs</h6><p>Some new attributes have been added in the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting'>Create a Meeting</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/patch-a-meeting'>Patch a Meeting</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/update-a-meeting'>Update a Meeting</a> endpoints to set up live streaming. The main attribute that needs to be set first is <code>enabledLiveStream</code>, that can be <code>true</code> or <code>false</code>. When <code>enabledLiveStream</code> is set to <code>true</code>, an object called <code>liveStream</code> is then required to configure the live stream settings of the meeting using the following parameters:</p> <ul> <li><p><code>destination</code><em>(required)</em> - this is a text string that describes the destination of the live stream, such as “YouTube”.</p> </li> <li><p><code>rtmpURL</code><em>(required)</em> – this is for the <em>ingestion</em> stream that is used for sending the live video content from the Webex meeting to a streaming service. Refer to your specific live streaming service for this information.</p> <p> The URL will use the <code>rtmp/s</code> protocol such as: <code>rtmps://example.com:1935/LiveMedia/WebexMeetingStream</code>.</p> </li> <li><p><code>streamURL</code><em>(required)</em> – this is for the <em>playback</em> URL to view the Webex meeting live stream. This URL should use the M3U8 video format for HTTP Live Steaming (HLS), which is supported across a wide range of devices, including iOS &amp; Android devices, modern web browsers, smart TVs, and streaming devices. Again, refer to your live streaming service to obtain this information. The <code>URL</code> may look something like this example: <code>https://example.com/WebexStreaming/index_a.m3u8</code></p> </li> <li><p><code>layoutWithoutSharedContent</code> – this parameter sets the meeting layout that will be displayed on the live stream when no content is being shared. Any one of these strings are accepted:</p> <ul> <li><code>grid</code> – layout to see multiple meeting participants in a grid</li> <li><code>stack</code> – layout to display the active speaker on the stage and up to six participants in thumbnails across the top</li> <li><code>focus</code> - layout that only displays the active speaker</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><code>layoutWithSharedContent</code> – sets the meeting layout that will be displayed on the live stream when there is content being shared. The following strings are accepted in this field:</p> <ul> <li><code>stack</code> – layout to display the shared content on the stage and up to six participants in thumbnails across the top</li> <li><code>focusedContentWithActiveSpeaker</code> – layout to display the shared content in the main part of the screen and a large thumbnail of the active speaker in the upper right corner</li> <li><code>focusedContent</code> – layout that only displays the shared content in the main part of the screen and does not display the participants</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><code>allowChangeLayoutInMeeting</code> – when set to <code>true</code>, it will allow the changing of the live streaming layout in the meeting.</p> </li> <li><p><code>followStageLayoutWhenSynced</code> – when set to <code>true</code>, it will follow the stage layout when being <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nic6kmbb/Sync-your-stage-with-everyone-in-meetings,-webinars,-and-events>' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>synchronized</a>.</p> </li> <li><p><code>resolution</code> – this string sets the resolution of the live steam, such as <code>1920x1080</code>. If not specified, the default setting is <code>720x1280</code>.</p> </li> </ul> <p>In summary, the live stream setup in a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting'>Create</a>/<a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/patch-a-meeting'>Patch</a>/<a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/update-a-meeting'>Update</a> Meetings API request will include something like this in the JSON body:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;enabledLiveStream&quot;: true, &quot;liveStream&quot;: { &quot;destination&quot;: &quot;YouTube&quot;, &quot;rtmpUrl&quot;: &quot;rtmps://example.com:1935/LiveMedia/WebexMeetingStream&quot;, &quot;streamUrl&quot;: &quot;https://example.com/WebexStreaming/index_a.m3u8&quot;, &quot;layoutWithoutSharedContent&quot;: &quot;grid&quot;, &quot;layoutWithSharedContent&quot;: &quot;stack&quot;, &quot;allowChangeLayoutInMeeting&quot;: false, &quot;followStageLayoutWhenSynced&quot;: true, &quot;resolution&quot;: &quot;1920x1080&quot; } } </code></pre> <h6>Enabling the Webex Meeting Live Streaming Feature for Testing</h6><p>The Live Stream feature for Webex Meetings is not turned on by default and must first be enabled by a Webex administrator in Control Hub to start testing it. The best route to start testing the API is by using a free <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/developer-sandbox-guide'>Developer Sandbox</a>, which provides admin access to a Webex org of your own. Once you log into Control Hub as an admin, you will need to enable live streaming services on your Webex site, enable live streaming for individual users, and enable the live stream video resolutions. Refer to <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/xk37so/Enable-live-streaming-in-Webex-Meetings-and-Webex-Events' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>this help article</a> for the most up-to-date information on applying these settings inside of Control Hub.</p> <p>After you enabled the proper settings in Control Hub and setup the live stream with the Meetings API, you are ready to test it. First, start the meeting in the Webex app as the host. When the meeting is active, start live streaming from the meeting client by selecting the <em>three dots</em>, click <strong>Start live streaming</strong> and then <strong>Go live</strong>. You can then head over to your live streaming service to watch your meeting broadcast as a regular viewer.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? No Problem</h6><p>As always, we are standing by to provide developer support for any of the API features in this article. If you need help or have any questions, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is eager to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>. Until next time, happy developing!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<title>
<![CDATA[ The Evaluation of Generative AI Performance in WebEx Contact Center ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt316951667b16cc27/67d311fd61e60a4de656e8d9/generative-ai-scoring-webex-developer-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The Evaluation of Generative AI Performance in WebEx Contact Center" /> <div><Callout type="info">**Prasad N Kamath, Director of Software Engineering also contributed to this blog post.** </Callout></div> <p>This blog discusses the development of a Gen-AI scoring system in Webex Contact Center (WxCC), designed to evaluate the quality, consistency, and reliability of AI-generated outputs across various applications like conversational and non-conversational AI, including Voice over AI Agents, Chat-based AI Agents, QA systems, and summarization kind of generative tasks. The system employs innovative aggregation algorithms, contextual assessments, and Responsible AI ( <a href='https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/solutions/artificial-intelligence/responsible-ai/index.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/solutions/artificial-intelligence/responsible-ai/index.html</a> ) checks, including BERTScore ( <a href='https://huggingface.co/spaces/evaluate-metric/bertscore' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://huggingface.co/spaces/evaluate-metric/bertscore</a> ) for non-conversational tasks and a &quot;Pass@K&quot; paradigm ( <a href='https://medium.com/@yananchen1116/a-dive-into-how-pass-k-is-calculated-for-evaluation-of-llms-coding-e52b8528235b' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://medium.com/@yananchen1116/a-dive-into-how-pass-k-is-calculated-for-evaluation-of-llms-coding-e52b8528235b</a> ) for conversational consistency.</p> <p>To support deeper analysis and optimization, the final aggregated score is further backed by itemized entry-wise scores, providing a detailed breakdown for granular tuning. This comprehensive scoring framework ensures that the AI outputs are not only functional but also adhere to high standards of quality, consistency, and reliability, enabling more precise and meaningful AI-generated content in diverse applications.</p> <h6>The Importance of Quantifying AI Performance</h6><p>Generative AI has revolutionized various industries, from content creation to personalized marketing, by enabling machines to produce text, images, music, and more that mimic human creativity. As these systems become increasingly sophisticated, it’s crucial to have robust evaluation mechanisms to ensure their outputs are effective, reliable, and aligned with desired outcomes. One of the most prominent methods for evaluating generative AI is scoring-based evaluation. This method quantifies the performance of AI models, offering clear, objective metrics that can guide development, optimization, and deployment.</p> <h6>Generative AI Tasks in a Nutshell</h6><p>Generative AI covers a diverse array of tasks, each with distinct challenges and applications. Key areas include text generation, where models like GPT, Gemini are used for writing and coding; image generation, with tools like DALL-E creating visuals from text descriptions; and music and audio generation, where AI composes music and speech. Additionally, data synthesis allows for the creation of synthetic datasets for training other models, and design and style transfer enable AI to generate new product designs and transform art styles. Each of these tasks necessitates a specific evaluation approach, highlighting the importance of scoring schemes.</p> <h6>Different Traditional Scoring Schemes and Their Usefulness</h6><p>Evaluating generative AI requires tailored approaches depending on the specific task and desired outcome, as no single method fits all scenarios. Various scoring schemes are employed, including perplexity, which gauges the accuracy of text predictions; BLEU, which assesses text translation quality by comparing outputs to references; and ROUGE, which is used for summarization tasks, focusing on n-gram overlap. Additionally, human evaluation plays a critical role in assessing creative aspects, offering qualitative insights that complement these quantitative measures.</p> <h6>Evaluating Generative AI with Scoring Methods in Webex Contact Center</h6><p>In WxCC, we have developed a Gen-AI scoring system that evaluates the quality, consistency, and reliability of generated data, aggregating these metrics into an overall score using innovative, proprietary algorithms. This scoring framework is versatile, supporting both conversational and non-conversational AI applications, such as Voice over AI Agent, Chat-based AI Agent, QA systems, summarization, and various other generative AI scenarios. To qualify for evaluation, generated data must be accompanied by the relevant context and/or ground truth. For conversational use cases, the framework accepts chat and transcript data in a specified format, resolving coreferences and optimizing context for optimal results. In QA evaluations, it expects a query with context and optionally, ground truth. For non-conversational scenarios like summarization, it requires the generated summary and its reference counterpart.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc0baa5eaad231ab1/generative-ai-scoring-webex-developer-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>To initiate an evaluation, the system requires the configuration of the evaluation agent with various options as a prerequisite. Depending on the chosen agent and mode (conversational or non-conversational), the evaluation process begins. The framework then assesses both qualitative and quantitative aspects of each entity in the input data, mirroring the standards of manual evaluation. For quality assessment, it evaluates factors like accuracy, conciseness, coherence, fluency, and depth of thought, along with Responsible AI considerations such as harmfulness, maliciousness, controversy, gender bias, and insensitivity to name a few. The grading process follows a teacher-student pattern. In conversational mode, the framework implements a “Pass@K” paradigm to assess consistency, while reliability checks involve verifying the relevance and factuality of the generated data, including detecting hallucinations and jailbreak scenarios. Quality and relevance scores are aggregated at the entity level to compute an overall score using customized logic.</p> <p>In non-conversational mode, the framework also calculates BERTScore for the AI outputs, leveraging its ability to capture contextual and semantic similarities. BERTScore serves as a scaling factor in the overall score computation. In conversational mode, a percentile-based aggregation algorithm computes the overall quality and reliability of the entire conversation, with a logarithmic algorithm using the consistency score as a gentle scaling factor for the final overall score. The final score is supported by detailed itemized scores for each entry, allowing for more granular analysis and fine-tuning. This mode also features a cumulative mechanism to accurately calculate scores across multiple runs.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltff64a84bae387f4c/generative-ai-scoring-webex-developer-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Here are few salient points summarizing the discussion:</p> <ul> <li>The Gen-AI scoring system is designed to evaluate AI-generated outputs for quality, consistency, and reliability across both conversational and non-conversational applications.</li> <li>The system incorporates key metrics such as &quot;Quality Scoring&quot;, &quot;Reliability Validation&quot;, &quot;Consistency Check&quot;, and &quot;Responsible AI&quot; to ensure a thorough and responsible assessment of AI outputs.</li> <li>Innovative aggregation algorithms are used to compute overall scores, taking into account both qualitative and quantitative aspects of the AI-generated data.</li> <li>The system provides itemized scores alongside the final score, allowing for detailed analysis and fine-tuning of AI models to improve their performance.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Example Usage</h6><p>Our Gen-AI scoring system is a versatile Python package that can seamlessly integrate with any Python-based application, such as the following example:</p> <div><Callout type="info">The `agentprofile` library shown here isn't currently accessible for developers to try. </Callout></div> <p><strong>Installation:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-bash">!pip install OpenAI !pip install langchain langchain-openai --upgrade !pip install langchain-community langchain-core !pip install transformers bert-score logstash_formatter jproperties </code></pre> <p><strong>Import:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-python">import uuid from agentprofile.PerfComputer import PerformanceTracker ############################################################################## </code></pre> <p><strong>Sample Evaluation of Non-Conversational AI Output:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-python">api_key = &quot;LLM PROXY CI TOKEN&quot; gen_agent_prompt_tup = (&#39;gen_agent_id&#39;, &#39;&#39;) gen_performance_tracker_instance = PerformanceTracker() gen_performance_tracker_instance.add_updt_agent_config(gen_agent_prompt_tup, is_ref_available=True) gen_qa_container = [ { &quot;id&quot;: &quot;id-1&quot;, &quot;text&quot;: &quot;GEN AI OUTPUT&quot;, &quot;groundtruth&quot;: &quot;REFERENCE CONTENT AS GROUNDTRUTH&quot;, } ] gen_overall_result_dict = gen_performance_tracker_instance.compute_performance(&#39;gen_agent_id&#39;, gen_qa_container, api_key, mode=2) </code></pre> <p><strong>Evaluation Result Schema:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-python">{ &quot;overall_rating_computed&quot;: float, &quot;overall_quality&quot;: float, &quot;overall_reliability&quot;: float, &quot;componentized_rating&quot;: { &quot;accuracy_score&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;coherence_score&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;factuality_score&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;fluency_score&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;bertscore&quot;: [{&quot;Precision&quot;: float, &quot;Recall&quot;: float, &quot;F1&quot;: float}] } } ############################################################################## </code></pre> <p><strong>Sample Evaluation of Conversational AI Output:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-python">api_key = &quot;LLM PROXY CI TOKEN&quot; #Sample usage agent_prompt_json_str_id = &#39;agent_prompt_json_str_id&#39; agent_prompt_json_str = &#39;SERIALIZED PROMPT OBJECT INSTANTIATED using promptstore package&#39; #Refer to “&lt;em&gt;Note”&lt;/em&gt; section for instantiation of the prompt object agent_prompt_tup = (agent_prompt_json_str_id, agent_prompt_json_str) performance_tracker_instance = PerformanceTracker() performance_tracker_instance.add_updt_agent_config(agent_prompt_tup, sample_frac=0.7, k=2) qa_container = [ { &quot;id&quot;: &quot;UNIQUE ID&quot;, &quot;query&quot;: &quot;QUERY&quot;, “answer”: “AI OUTPUT”, &quot;groundtruth&quot;: &quot;REFERENCE ANSWER AS GROUNDTRUTH&quot;, } ] overall_result_dict = performance_tracker_instance.compute_performance(agent_prompt_json_str_id, qa_container, api_key, batch_size=4, consistency_threshold=90) </code></pre> <p><strong>Evaluation Result Schema:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-python">{ &quot;overall_rating_computed&quot;: float, &quot;overall_rating_perceived&quot;: float, &quot;overall_quality&quot;: float, &quot;overall_reliability&quot;: float, &quot;overall_consistency&quot;: float, &quot;consistency_k&quot;: int, &quot;componentized_rating&quot;: [ { &quot;id&quot;: str, &quot;query&quot;: str, &quot;groundtruth&quot;: str, &quot;answer&quot;: str, &quot;answers&quot;: [str], &quot;evaluation_result_details&quot;: { &quot;overall_rating&quot;: int, &quot;overall_quality&quot;: int, &quot;overall_reliability&quot;: int, &quot;classification&quot;: str, &quot;componentized_rating&quot;: { &quot;REFERENCE_ACCURACY_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;CONTEXT_ACCURACY_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;QUERY_CONTEXT_REL_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;RESPONSE_CONTEXT_REL_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;IDK_JB_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;score&quot;: float, &quot;reasoning&quot;: str}, &quot;COMPREHENSIVE_SCORER_Score_WO_Groundtruth&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;COMPREHENSIVE_SCORER_Score_W_Groundtruth&quot;: {&quot;reasoning&quot;: str, &quot;score&quot;: float}, &quot;ANSWER_IDK_JB_SCORER_Score&quot;: {&quot;score&quot;: float, &quot;reasoning&quot;: str} } } } ] } ############################################################################## &lt;strong&gt;Cumulative score (over multiple runs):&lt;/strong&gt; result_dict_cum = PerformanceTracker.aggregate_overall_final(history_result_dict) &lt;strong&gt;Cumulative score Schema (over multiple runs):&lt;/strong&gt; { &quot;overall_rating_computed&quot;: float, &quot;overall_quality&quot;: float, &quot;overall_reliability&quot;: float, &quot;overall_consistency&quot;: float } </code></pre> <h6>Final Thoughts</h6><p>The Gen-AI Evaluation system provides a structured yet adaptable approach to assessing AI-generated outputs. By incorporating quality scoring, reliability validation, consistency checks, and Responsible AI, it ensures models meet both technical and ethical benchmarks. Moreover, integrating this framework with a Gen-AI auto-tuning infrastructure can enable an unattended, intelligent tuning system — continuously refining models based on real-time evaluations. This synergy makes it a powerful tool for developers and stakeholders aiming to build reliable, self-improving AI solutions. The library is planned for GA in the 1st half of 2025. You may try out the SDK (subject to approval from AI Agent DLT team) once available. For any further information please contact the blog author.</p> ]]>
