<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Device Grant Flow, You Got It! ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt63d97827a2f53232/67be5a3454cf2f73fe7626ef/device-oauth-flow-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Device Grant Flow, You Got It!" /> <p>Have you ever wondered how you might accomplish a seamless login experience within your integration for your Webex users who are using a Webex Board, Desk Pro, Room Kit, tablet, mobile device or any other device that has a limited input device setup? Wonder no more, as Webex has you covered with support for the OAuth 2.0 Device Grant Flow. Webex supports this seamless flow, which can enrich user&#39;s interactions on input constrained devices or devices without suitable browsers for traditional OAuth interactions.</p> <p>In addition to ensuring a simple, and easy authorization flow. The Device Grant Flow also serves as a solution to mitigate the need for multiple Redirect URI for non-SaaS applications. Some developers have created singular/on-prem solutions, that are deployed to individual customer sites. In which brings the challenge of how you properly implement an OAuth Flow across disparate networks using the least amount of Redirect URI&#39;s. To solve this, within the Webex implementation of the Device Grant Flow. We provide multiple Redirect URI proxy URLs, which all implement PCKE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for an additional layer of security when orchestrating the Authorization request, and Token granting to your application.</p> <h6>Sample Code Walk Through</h6><p>To illustrate the Device Grant Flow implementation, we will be going over the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-device-oauth-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Device Grant Flow Sample App</a> from the Webex Samples GitHub repository.</p> <p>This sample app is a python script that uses Flask, Webex APIs, and an access token obtained via the device grant flow. This sample application also has functionality for generating QR codes, polling and refreshing tokens, and fetching user info from Webex /people API endpoint. It uses Flask routes to manage the authorization flow, token readiness, and user data display.</p> <p>In addition, in the templates/sign-in.html file, a JQuery-enabled script polls for an access token and loads the OAuth profile display page when the token is detected after authorization is successful.</p> <h6>Create an Integration and Retrieve Integration Authorization Information</h6><p>You&#39;ll need to create a Webex integration and retrieve its Client ID and Client Secret for use in the sample script.</p> <p>To create a new Webex integration:</p> <ol> <li>Navigate to the Webex Developer Portal at <a data-type='internal' to='/'>https://developer.webex.com</a></li> <li>Select <strong>Log in</strong> at the top right corner and log in with your Webex account credentials. If you don&#39;t have an account, create one.</li> <li>After logging in, <strong>select Start building apps</strong> in the body of the landing page.</li> <li>In the <strong>Integrations</strong> card, choose <strong>Create an Integration</strong>.</li> <li>Enter the following details for your new integration:<ul> <li><strong>Will this integration use a mobile SDK</strong>? Select <strong>No</strong>.</li> <li><strong>Integration name</strong>: Enter an alpha-numeric name for your integration.</li> <li><strong>Icon</strong>: Choose one of the default icons.</li> <li><strong>App Hub Description</strong>: Enter a brief description, for instance, <code>OAuth testing integration</code>.</li> <li><strong>Redirect URI(s)</strong>: Enter the following URLs:<ul> <li><code>https://oauth-helper-a.wbx2.com/helperservice/v1/actions/device/callback</code></li> <li><code>https://oauth-helper-k.wbx2.com/helperservice/v1/actions/device/callback</code></li> <li><code>https://oauth-helper-r.wbx2.com/helperservice/v1/actions/device/callback</code> These URLs are hosted by Webex on your behalf. And when you request a token from the Devices Authorize endpoint. We will poll these redirect URIs to obtain our access token, after a user has completed the OAuth Authorization process.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Scopes</strong>: Select the following scope for your integration: <code>spark:all</code></li> </ul> </li> <li>Select <strong>Add Integration</strong> at the bottom of the page to save your integration.</li> </ol> <p>After saving, you will be provided with a <strong>Client ID</strong> and <strong>Client Secret</strong>. Store these securely. You&#39;ll use them in the sample app.</p> <h6>Install Python Modules</h6><p>Install the following Python modules using pip (<strong>Note: It is highly recommended to use a python virtual environment. This will ensure no conflicts with your local version of python, and will keep the installed libraries for this sample code contained instead of being installed globally</strong>):</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">`pip install flask` `pip install requests` `pip install qrcode[pil]` </code></pre> <p>The flask module is a web framework for Python, which provides functionalities for building web applications.</p> <p>The requests module is used for making HTTP requests in Python. It abstracts the complexities of making requests behind a beautiful, simple API so that you can focus on interacting with services and consuming data in your application.</p> <p>The <code>qrcode[pil]</code> module is used to generate QR codes. The <code>[pil]</code> part is an extra requirement which means that it will also install the Pillow library, a fork of PIL (Python Imaging Library). It adds some user-friendly features.</p> <h6>Run the Sample App</h6><p>To run the sample app:</p> <ol> <li>Update the .env file with your Client ID, and Client Secret that you obtained when you created your integration: <code>CLIENT_ID=&lt;Client ID Goes here&gt;</code> <code>CLIENT_SECRET=&lt;Client Secret&gt;</code></li> <li>Open a terminal or command prompt.</li> <li>Navigate to the directory where <code>oauth.py</code> is located.</li> <li>Run the Python script using the following command: <code>python oauth.py</code></li> <li>Navigate to the non-loopback URL generated by the prompt, for example: <code>Running on http://10.26.164.77:10060</code></li> <li>Click <strong>Sign-In</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt96ac4c440cf43b3a/device-oauth-flow-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>You can scan the QR with any external device or if you are running this sample from a desktop. You can navigate to the verify URL in a separate tab and enter the authentication code. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2d8298c56185469b/device-oauth-flow-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Once you navigate to the verify URL. You will be presented with the below page. In which you will enter the <strong>User Code</strong> from the prior page: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2b494ff1bdfb13f5/device-oauth-flow-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Once the user code is verified, you will be asked to enter your Webex credentials. These credentials are for the user in which is going to authorize your integration: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5e8aa176b66acd7f/device-oauth-flow-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2c825b6cd7089645/device-oauth-flow-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb7bd7bc03d79085b/device-oauth-flow-blog-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Once authorization is successful. The <strong>Token Detection Logic</strong> page will automatically redirect&#xa0; to the below <strong>Profile</strong> page. This redirection is a confirmation that the user authorization was successful, and that a token was obtained on that user&#39;s behalf: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt56207012d6315280/device-oauth-flow-blog-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>When you click on the <strong>Profile</strong> button. The page will use the obtained access token to send an API request to: <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/people/get-my-own-details'>https://webexapis.com/v1/people/me</a> to retrieve the authorized users details. See the below example:</li> </ol> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt81f805d8988a3c73/device-oauth-flow-blog-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>I hope that you found this blog insightful, and have thoroughly enjoyed learning about the Device Grant Flow. And will dive deeper into the code sample for your personal/corporate use case.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – February 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – February 2025" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers! It has been another eventful month for our community that produced some newsworthy items. Check out all the latest updates and announcements right here.</p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Developer βeta: Webex Click-to-Call and Webex Developer AI Assistant</h6><p>Attention early adopters! We have some new features in the Developer βeta program that you can go check out.</p> <ul> <li>First is <strong>Webex Click to Call</strong>, which is designed to provide a user-friendly calling experience for guest users to call people within your organization. This powerful feature eliminates the need for downloads, accounts, and authentication, to ensure customers can connect with your enterprise effortlessly with just click of a button, improving overall customer satisfaction and engagement.</li> <li>Next is <strong>AI Assistant for Webex Developers</strong>, which is a chat interface powered by a large language model (LLM) to assist users to find the right Webex developer tools and code generation for their projects. Developers can either click through options or provide a plain text description of their intended project, and the assistant will handle the complex tasks, presenting relevant documentation and appropriate tools like APIs and SDKs. Additionally, the assistant can generate code snippets to aid in building integrations, thus enabling even customer administrators to create their own integrations.</li> <li>Finally, coming very soon to the beta program is a preview of the <strong>Converged Webex Developer Portal</strong>, which combines resources for both the Webex Suite and Webex Contact Center platforms. Today, we have two different portals for Contact Center and Webex Suite. This poses a challenge for a developer who is interested in developing an application/integration for Webex Suite and Webex Contact center as the documentation and APIs are available in two different portals. Having all the contents available in single portal will assist the developers to easily discover the contents.</li> </ul> <p>Don&#39;t miss out on testing these new features early!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>🖥️ Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On <strong>Wednesday, February 26, 2025, at 1:00PM EST</strong>, join us for our next public webinar where we&#39;ll demo the <em>Integrations Studio for Webex Connect</em>. The studio makes it easy to build, share and manage integrations that automate customer communication and customer experience workflows across various channels and regions at scale. See how you can bring your own functionality as well as third party APIs to Webex Connect&#39;s enterprise-grade flow builder to create repeatable, branded solutions exclusively for your customers, or market them on the Webex App Hub.</p> <p>Register for the live session or watch any of our previous webinar recordings on-demand later from our webinars page.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Attend or watch webinars →</a></p> <h6>👩🏻‍🔧 What&#39;s New for Webex Contact Center Administrators</h6><p>There are several new updates for Webex Contact Center that were recently announced. Here are some of the highlights:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Programmatic Flow Management with the List and Publish APIs</strong><ul> <li>These new APIs supplement the existing Import and Export APIs for flows and subflows, enabling the full automation of flow management for both new and migrating organizations. This update allows developers and partners to list, export, import, and publish flows and subflows programmatically between organizations, eliminating manual steps and thus enhancing efficiency in managing many flows and subflows.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Self-Service SMS (10DLC) and WhatsApp numbers</strong><ul> <li>United States customers can now request phone numbers, including 10DLC, directly through the Webex Connect as a self-service feature.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Cisco AI Assistant for Contact Center</strong><ul> <li>Get ready to transform your contact center operations and delight your customers with Cisco AI Assistant for Contact Center! AI Assistant revolutionizes customer service by enhancing your efficiency and elevating customer satisfaction with AI-generated call summaries, AI-powered Agent Wellbeing, Auto CSAT, and Topic Analytics.</li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Enhanced Zendesk Integration</strong><ul> <li>Agent productivity and customer support is now more streamlined and boosted with exciting new enhancements to our Zendesk Connector! Agents can now create Zendesk tickets and new customer tickets directly from Agent Desktop. They can also automatically populate ticket fields and link them to various contacts.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p><a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nv7abhz/What's-new-for-administrators-in-Webex-Contact-Center' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Learn more →</a></p> <h6>📝Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>We also have some important API updates recently listed in the Webex API Changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>NEW</strong>– February 6, 2025: Descriptions of the following fields have been added to <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports-detailed-call-history/'>Get Detailed Call History</a>: Caller ID number, External caller ID number, Redirecting party UUID, Device owner UUID, Call Recording Platform Name, Call Recording Result, Call Recording Trigger, and Public Calling IP Address.</li> <li><strong>NEW</strong> – February 11, 2025: As a host or cohost of a meeting, you can invite a SIP participant to join the meeting via the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-participants/call-out-a-sip-participant'>Call Out a SIP Participant API</a>. You can also cancel the call to a SIP participant before the ringing on the invited SIP device stops via the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-participants/cancel-calling-out-a-sip-participant'>Cancel Calling Out a SIP Participant API</a>.</li> <li><strong>NEW</strong> – February 14, 2025: As a meeting host, you can set up live streaming for a meeting with the <code>enabledLiveStream</code> and <code>liveStream</code> attributes when the meeting is created using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting'>Create a Meeting API</a>. When the meeting is started, the meeting host can start the live streaming by selecting the three dots, choosing <strong>Start live streaming</strong> and then <strong>Go live</strong> from the meeting client. The live streaming is started for the meeting without any ad-hoc configuration required. Live streaming can also be enabled for an existing meeting using <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/patch-a-meeting'>Patch a Meeting</a> or <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/update-a-meeting'>Update a Meeting</a> with the <code>enabledLiveStream</code> and <code>liveStream</code> attributes.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ The Webex Platform Developer Year in Review: 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6919ce81f008d584/679a8743cba7fcb478f3911b/year-in-review.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The Webex Platform Developer Year in Review: 2024" /> <p>As we look back on 2024, it&#39;s clear that it has been a year of significant advancements and enhancements for the Webex platform. From new API features and SDK improvements to innovative service apps and streamlined identity management, Webex has continued to evolve to meet the needs of its users. In addition, we&#39;ve added a variety of quality-of-life improvements as well as new content streams targeted at developers.</p> <p>In this blog post, we&#39;ll explore the most notable updates and features introduced in 2024, highlighting how they can enhance your Webex experience and streamline your workflows.</p> <h6>Guest-to-Guest Meetings</h6><p>A Guest-to-Guest meeting is a type of Service App used in combination with a new subscription for guest-only meetings. The feature allows for guest accounts that are admin approved and can be either persistent or ephemeral. Additionally, the Guest-to-Guest Developer Sandbox is now available, providing a dedicated environment for developers to test and integrate guest meeting functionalities. For more information, see <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps-as-g2g-meeting-facilitator-guide'>Service App Guest-to-Guest Meetings</a>.</p> <h6>Webex Service Apps</h6><p>Webex Service Apps are machine accounts that operate on behalf of an organization, independent of specific Webex user accounts. These apps are designed for your most critical and sensitive Webex integrations, making them an ideal solution for provisioning, active reporting, compliance, and more. They provide a robust and secure way to manage and automate various tasks within the Webex ecosystem. For more information, see <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>Using Webex Service Apps</a>.</p> <h6>Webex Calling API Update Highlights</h6><p>Moving on to APIs, in 2024, the Webex Calling API saw numerous updates aimed at enhancing provisioning and management capabilities. Some of the key highlights include:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Ability to Add and Manage Virtual Lines</strong>: Simplifies the process of handling virtual lines.</li> <li><strong>Ability to Manage Virtual Lines Call Settings</strong>: Provides more control over call settings for virtual lines.</li> <li><strong>DECT Devices - Phase 2</strong>: Expands support and functionality for DECT devices.</li> <li><strong>Device Configuration - Phase 3</strong>: Further improvements in device configuration capabilities.</li> <li><strong>New Workspace Call Settings API</strong>: Introduces new API for managing workspace call settings.</li> <li><strong>New Emergency Services API</strong>: Adds support for emergency services management.</li> <li><strong>New Device API</strong>: Enhances device management with a new API.</li> <li><strong>Enhanced PSTN Management</strong>: Improves management of PSTN services.</li> </ul> <p>For complete details, see <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/whats-new-calling'>Webex Calling API Updates</a>.</p> <h6>Enhanced Call Reporting</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports-detailed-call-history'>Webex Calling Detailed Call History API</a> was updated to include new fields that help customers identify PSTN provider details. These new fields include information such as PSTN Vendor Name and PSTN Legal Entity, providing more detailed insights into call history and improving overall call reporting capabilities.</p> <h6>New Converged Recordings APIs</h6><p>In 2024, Webex introduced new <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings'>Converged Recordings APIs</a> to streamline the management of call recordings. These APIs include:</p> <ul> <li><strong>List Recordings</strong>: Retrieve a list of recordings.</li> <li><strong>List Recordings for an Admin or Compliance Officer</strong>: Allow admins or compliance officers to list recordings.</li> <li><strong>Get Recording Details</strong>: Fetch detailed information about a specific recording.</li> <li><strong>Delete a Recording</strong>: Remove a recording from the system.</li> <li><strong>Get Recording Metadata</strong>: Access metadata associated with a recording.</li> <li><strong>Reassign Recordings</strong>: Reassign recordings to a different user.</li> </ul> <p>These APIs provide comprehensive tools for managing recordings, enhancing administrative control and compliance capabilities.</p> <h6>Webex Meetings API Update Highlights</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/meetings'>Webex Meetings API</a> introduced several new features to enhance meeting management and security:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Watermark Settings</strong>: Meeting hosts can now add watermark settings by specifying new attributes:<ul> <li><code>enabledAudioWatermark</code></li> <li><code>enabledVisualWatermark</code></li> <li><code>visualWatermarkOpacity</code></li> </ul> </li> <li><strong>Scheduling Options API</strong>: Users can leverage this API to retrieve and update scheduling permissions on behalf of another user with the new parameter: <code>delegateEmails</code>.</li> <li><strong>Delegate Emails API</strong>: Users can add and delete delegate emails, making it easier to manage scheduling permissions.</li> <li><strong>New Attributes for Meetings APIs</strong>: These attributes help better manage registrations, post-event surveys for webinars, breakout sessions, and joined participants.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Other Notable Webex API Updates</h6><p>We introduced several notable Webex API features that are designed to make administrators&#39; lives easier. One of the highlights is the new <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/identity-organization'>Identity Organization API</a>, which enables administrators to manage organizational details more efficiently. With this API, admins can retrieve comprehensive details about their organization, including the current name, status, and other important information. Additionally, the new functionality allows admins to easily update the organization&#39;s name through a simple API call.</p> <p>Another exciting update is the new <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/reassign-recordings'>Reassign Recording API</a>. This feature allows administrators to reassign a list of call recordings or all call recordings of a particular user to a new user, streamlining the management of call recordings within the organization.</p> <h6>SCIM 2.0: Streamlined User Identity Management</h6><p>The Webex platform enabled support for <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/scim-2-overview'>the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM)</a> v2.0 standard! With SCIM-enabled Webex APIs, you can easily configure or create SCIM 2.0 clients to manage users and groups. This automation simplifies the process of creating, updating, and deactivating user identities across applications, making identity management more efficient than ever.</p> <p>One real-world use case for SCIM 2.0 is ISI Analytics, Directory Import for Webex, which provides the following benefits:</p> <ul> <li>Seamless Directory Integration for Webex</li> <li>Consistent, Up-to-Date Data</li> <li>Enhanced Insights with Full User Profiles</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Webex SDKs</h6><p>In 2024, we focused on enhancing our SDKs for both web and mobile platforms to provide developers with more powerful and flexible tools. These improvements include a migration to a new Meetings Suite platform, significant updates to the Webex Web Meetings SDK, and new features for the Webex Mobile SDKs for iOS and Android. These updates aim to enhance security, improve user experience, and offer greater control over media streams and meeting functionalities.</p> <h6>SDK Migration to New Meetings Suite Platform</h6><p>We migrated our SDKs to a new Meetings Suite platform. This migration brought several advantages:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Unified Meeting Objects and Revised API Calls</strong>: Simplifies the development process by providing a more consistent and streamlined API.</li> <li><strong>Enhanced Security</strong>: Improves the overall security of meetings, ensuring that user data and communications are better protected.</li> <li><strong>Improved User Experience</strong>: Offers a more intuitive and seamless experience for both developers and end-users, making it easier to integrate and use Webex functionalities.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>New in Webex Web Meetings SDK V3</h6><p>The latest version of the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/webex-meetings-sdk-web-introduction'>Webex Web Meetings SDK</a>, V3, brings several exciting new features:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Stream Classes</strong>: New classes for Camera, Mic, and Display, providing more control over media streams.</li> <li><strong>Effects</strong>: Introduction of Background Noise Reduction and Virtual Background effects to enhance the meeting experience.</li> <li><strong>Transcription</strong>: Support for Live Transcription and Multilanguage transcription, making meetings more accessible and inclusive.</li> </ul> <p>Additionally, the SDK now supports <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/multistream-comprehensive-guide'>multistream</a>, allowing users to receive multiple concurrent media streams with configurable layouts, rather than a single switched media stream with fixed layouts. This provides greater flexibility and a more customized meeting experience.</p> <h6>Mobile SDK Updates: iOS and Android SDK v3.1x</h6><p>The latest updates to the Webex Mobile SDKs for <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/ios'>iOS</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/android'>Android</a> bring several new features:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Support for moving a user&#39;s meeting from one client to another</strong>: This allows users to seamlessly transition their meetings between different devices.</li> <li><strong>Boost inbound call audio</strong>: Enhances the audio quality for incoming calls.</li> </ul> <p>For the iOS SDK only:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Support for iPad USB Camera for video calls</strong>: Enables the use of external USB cameras with iPads for video calls.</li> <li><strong>Updated Kitchen Sink App with SwiftUI</strong>: The Kitchen Sink App has been updated to use SwiftUI, providing a more modern and efficient user interface.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Webex Click-to-Call Apps</h6><p>New <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/web-calling-sdk-click-to-call'>Click-to-Call functionality</a>, allows users to contact a resource with a simple click. This feature streamlines communication by enabling instant connection to contacts directly from the Webex platform, enhancing productivity and ease of use.</p> <h6>Webex Service Apps: Bring Your Own Datasource (BYODS)</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/bring-your-own-datasource'>Bring Your Own Datasource (BYODS)</a> feature for Webex Service Apps! This new capability streamlines development for Data Access Providers who want to manage Webex interaction data. It enhances real-time interactions within the Webex ecosystem and allows for direct exchanges between the Webex platform and data providers, making data management more seamless and efficient.</p> <h6>Updated Webex Meeting Widget</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/widgets'>Webex Meeting Widget</a> 1.28.0 made its debut. This update includes support for Node.js 20 and compatibility with React 18.3.1, making it easier than ever to enhance your web applications with Webex Meetings. In addition to this, the widget now supports providing the name for a guest as well as passwords or pins while joining meetings. A developer can also pass the name and password as inputs to the widget during initialization.</p> <h6>Webex Developer AI Assistant</h6><p>The Webex Developer AI Assistant is a cutting-edge tool designed to streamline the development process by providing intelligent code suggestions, automated documentation generation, and real-time debugging assistance for Webex APIs. This AI-powered assistant leverages advanced machine learning algorithms to enhance productivity and reduce development time, making it an invaluable resource for developers working with the Webex platform.</p> <div><Callout type="info">You'll need to be logged into the Webex Developer Portal to see the new AI Assistant Beta button adjacent your profile. </Callout></div> <h6>Webex Developer Playlist on YouTube</h6><p>We started up the <a href='https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2k86RlAekM_bIUrvVw4Haq_0xxTez9zU' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Playlist on YouTube</a>, featuring a curated collection of tutorials, demos, and deep dives into the latest Webex APIs and SDKs. This channel is designed to help developers get the most out of the Webex platform with easy-to-follow videos and expert insights.</p> <h6>Many New Listings in the Webex App Hub</h6><p>We added dozens of new apps to the Webex App Hub. To browse our new offerings, see <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/brand-new' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://apphub.webex.com/brand-new</a>.</p> <h6>Discover App Hub Listings Natively in Webex</h6><p>We&#39;re excited to announce that you can now discover App Hub listings directly within Webex! This means more visibility for your apps and bots without the need for context switching. Users can easily try out apps before adding them to their meetings or spaces, making the integration process smoother and more efficient:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt1d890fcca2203617/2024-year-in-review-1.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Looking Forward to 2025!</h6><p>We&#39;ve got even more ambitious plans for 2025 that we&#39;re looking forward to sharing with you in the coming months. Until then, best wishes for a great year!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – January 2025 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – January 2025" /> <p>Greetings and a very happy new year, Webex developers! There are a lot of exciting announcements and updates to share with you as we roll into 2025. So, let&#39;s get right to it and check out all the latest news!</p> <h6>🎤 Catch the Webex Developer Sessions at Cisco Live Amsterdam 2025</h6><p>We are happy to announce the lineup of sessions for Webex developers at Cisco Live Amsterdam 2025. Whether you&#39;re looking to enhance your virtual meeting applications, dive into AI innovations, or explore the latest in Webex platform APIs, there&#39;s something for everyone. Get ready to engage with industry experts, participate in hands-on workshops, and expand your skills with our diverse range of sessions at #CiscoLiveEMEA.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/announcing-webex-developer-sessions-at-cisco-live-amsterdam-2025'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🔌 Using the New HTTP Connector for Webex Contact Center APIs</h6><p>Webex Developer Evangelism Leader, Adam Weeks, recently published another blog that introduces a powerful new feature for Webex Contact Center: the ability to leverage Webex Contact Center (CC) APIs from within Flow Designer using a new Webex CC HTTP Connector. See how this new addition empowers organizations to seamlessly integrate public Webex CC APIs into the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer for creating powerful automated workflows.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/using-the-new-http-connector-for-webex-contact-center-apis'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🤖 How to Create Your Own RSS Feed Parser Bot for Webex</h6><p>In another helpful post by Developer Support Engineer, Raffaele Lagana, learn how to deploy your very own RSS parser bot that runs in Webex. The blog covers a sample application you can start off with that has the ability to read RSS feeds and update a messaging space through a Webex Bot.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/how-to-create-your-own-rss-feed-parser-bot-for-webex'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🖥️ Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On <strong>Wednesday, February 26, 2025, at 1:00PM EST</strong>, join us for our next public webinar where we&#39;ll demo the <em>Integrations Studio for Webex Connect</em>. The studio makes it easy to build, share and manage integrations that automate customer communication and customer experience workflows across various channels and regions at scale. See how you can bring your own functionality as well as third party APIs to Webex Connect&#39;s enterprise-grade flow builder to create repeatable, branded solutions exclusively for your customers, or market them on the Webex App Hub.</p> <p><a href='https://evangelism.webex.com/weblink/register/rf7b608feefcdadff117ff9543ad18a22' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register for the live webinar →</a></p> <p>In case you can’t make the live event, you can always watch the session recording later or check out all the past sessions on our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a>.</p> <h6>🦾 Look, Ma, No Hands: Using AI to Generate and Refine Webex GitHub Sample Documentation</h6><p>New APIs and features are frequently being added to the Webex Developer platform, which always means more work for the documentation team. This is another area where AI tools can help get the job done more quickly and efficiently. In an insightful blog post by Technical Documentation Leader, John Francis, shows us some of the ways that he&#39;s been integrating AI tools into his daily workflows, including creating cleaner GitHub pull requests descriptions, uncovering key marketing points for product teams, and simplifying the review process for new content submissions.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/look-ma-no-hands-using-ai-to-generate-and-refine-webex-github-sample-documentation'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>👩🏽‍💻 Developer βeta: Webex Click-to-Call and Webex Developer AI Assistant</h6><p>Currently, there are two features that are active for testing and providing feedback in the Developer βeta program:</p> <ul> <li>First is <strong>Webex Click to Call</strong>, a powerful new application type that is implemented through the Web Calling SDK. This can power use cases such as connect with a support desk or sales team at the click of a button, and the call happens right in the browser.</li> <li>The other beta feature is <strong>AI Assistant for Webex Developers</strong>, a chat interface powered by a large language model (LLM), accessible to all signed-in developers. Developers can provide a description of their intended project, and the assistant will handle the complex tasks, presenting relevant documentation, APIs, and suggested tools. Additionally, the assistant can generate code snippets to aid in building and deploying all kinds of Webex integrations.</li> </ul> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>🖱️📞 Using the Webex Click-To-Call Feature</h6><p>To help developers hit the ground running with the “Webex Click to Call” beta feature, Adhwaith Menon from the Web SDK Engineering team published a marvelous quick start guide inside a blog post. The blog includes detailed step-by-step instructions for getting set up and a helpful Vidcast to show how everything comes together.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/power-your-customer-experience-using-the-webex-click-to-call-feature'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📝Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>There are also two important changes, among others, that were recently listed in the Webex API Changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>NEW</strong>- January 13, 2025: Webhooks for Webex events are provided with a <code>X-Spark-Signature</code> when a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/webhooks#handling-requests-from-webex'>secret has been provided during webhook registration</a>. The signature corresponds to the <code>HMAC-SHA1</code> hash of the webhook payload. We now offer additional HMAC&#39;s namely <code>HMAC-SHA256</code> and <code>HMAC-SHA512</code>. These can be found in the new header <code>X-Webex-Signature</code>.</li> <li><strong>Breaking Change</strong> - January 21, 2025: Starting on <em>March 2, 2025</em>, the <code>sharedLineIndex</code> field will be mandatory when <code>lineKeyType</code> is <code>SHARED_LINE</code> for the following APIs <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-device-layout-by-device-id'>Modify Device Layout by Device ID</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/create-a-line-key-template'>Create a Line Key Template</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/device-call-settings/modify-a-line-key-template'>Modify a Line Key Template</a>.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

</description>

<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbd6c2cc741c9e959/67800e22d9df89403ce0276b/header.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Announcing Webex Developer Sessions at Cisco Live Amsterdam 2025" /> <p>We&#39;re thrilled to announce a lineup of exciting sessions tailored for Webex developers at Cisco Live Amsterdam 2025! Whether you&#39;re looking to enhance your virtual meeting applications, dive into AI innovations, or explore the latest in Webex platform APIs, we&#39;ve got something for everyone. Get ready to engage with industry experts, participate in hands-on workshops, and expand your skills with our diverse range of sessions at <code>#CiscoLiveEMEA</code>.</p> <p>In addition to our sessions, we will feature two booths inside the <strong>World of Solutions</strong>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Open Ecosystem Integrations</strong>: Try out some of the curated apps from the <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex AppHub</a>.</li> <li><strong>Webex for Developers</strong>: Explore all the developer features of Webex and see a demo in action.</li> </ul> <p>For a deeper dive into developer features, visit our booth in the <strong>DevNet Zone</strong> on Wednesday, Feb 12 for the <strong>Webex Takeover</strong>.</p> <h6>Classroom Sessions</h6><p><strong>Extending Webex Contact Center with Flow Designer Extensibility (NEW!)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Unlock the full potential of your contact center with Flow Designer&#39;s advanced features.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVNET-2915</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Adam Weeks</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Wednesday, Feb 12, 3:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVNET-2915#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Innovations with Cisco Webex: Transforming Industries through Smart Applications</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Discover how AI integrations with Cisco Webex SDKs are reshaping various industries.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVNET-2127</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Adam Weeks</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Monday, Feb 10, 2:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVNET-2127#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization for Webex Integrations</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Learn to implement OAuth flows for secure Webex app authorization.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVNET-2675</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Joe Zanini</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Thursday, Feb 13, 11:30 AM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVNET-2675#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>What’s New in Webex Platform APIs: Messaging, Meetings, Calling, SDKs, and Embedded Apps (NEW!)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Stay updated with the latest innovations in Webex Platform APIs and SDKs.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: BRKCOL-2907</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Phil Bellanti</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Tuesday, Feb 11, 9:30 AM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=BRKCOL-2907#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Enhance Your Contact Center with Webex: A Developer&#39;s Introduction to APIs and Automation</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Explore Webex Contact Center APIs for efficient troubleshooting and automation.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: CISCOU-2043</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Adam Weeks</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Thursday, Feb 13, 12:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=CISCOU-2043#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>How to Improve Digital Channels Customer Interactions with Video Combining Instant Connect and Webex Connect</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Enhance customer service with Instant Connect and Webex Connect integration.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVNET-2701</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Victor Vazquez</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Thursday, Feb 13 12:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=devnet-2701#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Workshops</h6><p><strong>Enhancing Virtual Meetings with Webex&#39;s Guest-to-Guest Platform (NEW!)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Create seamless virtual meetings for non-licensed users with hands-on coding experience.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVWKS-2903</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Phil Bellanti</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Monday, Feb 10, 3:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVWKS-2903#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Build-a-Bot with Webex</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: An interactive workshop to build your first Webex bot, enhancing collaboration and automation.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVWKS-1149</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Phil Bellanti</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Wednesday, Feb 12, 11:30 AM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVWKS-1149#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Building your First Embedded App on Webex</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Create a Webex Embedded App, covering development, testing, and app approval processes.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVWKS-1650</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Joe Zanini</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Thursday, Feb 13, 12:30 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVWKS-1650#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <p><strong>Deploying Webex Service Apps</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Description</strong>: Gain hands-on experience with creating and deploying Webex Service Apps.</li> <li><strong>Session ID</strong>: DEVWKS-2040</li> <li><strong>Speaker</strong>: Phil Bellanti</li> <li><strong>Date &amp; Time</strong>: Tuesday, Feb 11, 4:00 PM</li> <li><a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/emea/learn/session-catalog.html?search=DEVWKS-2040#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>More Info</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>See You Soon!</h6><p>Join us at Cisco Live Amsterdam 2025 for an unparalleled opportunity to network, learn, and innovate. <item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Power your Customer Experience Using the Webex Click-To-Call Feature! ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt3dcf42948c89a027/676463cf08d14f7bd6da5147/click-to-call-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Power your Customer Experience Using the Webex Click-To-Call Feature!" /> <p>Traditional Business to Consumer (B2C) focused enterprises often have difficulty maintaining seamless and simple customer support. Most enterprises usually require users to register accounts or manually dial support numbers. These methods add significant friction for regular consumers, thereby affecting the quality of the support. As a result, many of them experience reduced consumer conversion rates.</p> <p>Enter Click-to-Call, a feature provided by Webex through the Web Calling SDK, which allows enterprises to empower users to connect with customer support at the click of a button, significantly boosting the customer experience.</p> <h6>Check Out Our Vidcast Demo</h6><p>For a quick video demo of click to call, see:</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/352d44b0-cefd-4dd7-a06d-0e73cb076503" width="100%" height="100%" title="Demonstration of Click-to-call" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>An Example Problem Scenario</h6><p>Consider the scenario of a company that owns a travel bookings website called ‘Plan My Trip,’ which allows users to book hotels or flights. The website hosts many visitors, often amounting to over 10,000 a day. Users can browse the various products available and make a purchase.</p> <p>However, Plan My Trip faces a problem with their sales support. For any user who has decided to book a trip, they find it very hard to contact the appropriate agent. Most of the times, they would have to manually dial reference numbers spread across the website. This entire process adds significant friction for first-time users, thereby reducing conversion rates considerably.</p> <p>The company has taken note of this problem, and the leadership has decided to revamp their customer support by making it an easy and seamless process for users to obtain sales support. In order to achieve their objectives, they can decide to use the Webex Click-to-call feature.</p> <h6>Set up Click-to-call</h6><p>Let’s say you are a frontend developer for the Plan My Trip website, as Webex Click-to-call is currently in beta, here’s you can set up the prerequisites:</p> <ol> <li>Begin by visiting the <a href='https://gobeta.webex.com/project/feature/item.html?cap=c5d8c615-40bf-44a5-82d7-43084921dc90&amp;artid=9e93614c-2971-4c86-b51e-e5ca5967bcc6' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Click-to-Call Beta</a> page and register for the beta.</li> <li>Once you have access to the beta, proceed to setup all the prerequisites, as mentioned in the beta document.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Retrieve the Required Tokens</h6><p>Next, you need to retrieve the appropriate authorization tokens and extension numbers:</p> <ol> <li>You must then proceed to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>Webex Developer Portal</a> and obtain the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>Service App</a> access token and a user bearer token, which will be used for authentication.</li> <li>Login to your respective admin account in <a href='https://admin.webex.com/calling/numbers' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Control Hub</a> and copy the extension number of the Hunt Group or Call Queue that has been created.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Implement Click-to-Call</h6><p>Once all the prerequisites are finished, you can then integrate the click to call feature to their website via the Calling SDK. The language you will be writing the code to consume the SDK would be JavaScript. Here’s how you can do it:</p> <h6>Step 1 (Getting the Package)</h6><p>Using a package manager such as <strong>yarn</strong>or <strong>npm</strong>, install the Webex calling package using npm or yarn:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm install @webex/calling </code></pre> <p>or</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">yarn add @webex/calling </code></pre> <p>or</p> <p>Using CDN, you can access it directly from within the browser:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">&lt;script src=&quot;https://unpkg.com/webex/umd/calling.min.js&quot;&gt;&lt;/script&gt; </code></pre> <h6>Step 2 (Create the Code Setup)</h6><p>Use the following information and create the calling object within your code.</p> <ul> <li>By following the instructions in the beta document, you need to generate your guest token and JWE token.</li> <li>Using the references provided in the beta document, you can generate both the Webex configurations and the calling configurations.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Step 3 (Set up the Call in Code)</h6><p>Using the created calling object, add the calling logic to your code:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">calling.on(&#39;ready&#39;, () =&gt; { calling.register().then(async () =&gt; { callingClient = window.callingClient = calling.callingClient; const localAudioStream = await Calling.createMicrophoneStream({audio: true}); const line = Object.values(callingClient.getLines())[0]; line.on(&#39;registered&#39;, (lineInfo) =&gt; { // Create call object const call = line.makeCall(); // Trigger an outbound call call.dial(localAudioStream); }); line.register(); }); }); </code></pre> <h6>Results</h6><p>Using the capabilities of the click-to-call feature, the Plan My Trip website should look something like this:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb66b55530ed64c46/click-to-call-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>The <strong>Call Support</strong> button is linked to the click-to-call flow and allows users to directly reach out to support.</p> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>Using the power of the Webex Click-to-call feature, companies (just like our organization, Plan My Trip) can easily integrate the one click calling feature into their website, thereby boosting their customer support.</p> <h6>Need Some More Help?</h6><p>For any further questions or assistance, contact the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support</a> team. Conversations can also be started or joined at the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Community</a> site. Happy coding!</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Using the New HTTP Connector for Webex Contact Center APIs ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltddf465893ed30758/675787c830b280af12df27c3/wxcc-http-connector-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Using the New HTTP Connector for Webex Contact Center APIs" /> <p>We are excited to introduce a powerful new feature for Webex Contact Center: the HTTP Connector for Webex Contact Center APIs. This addition empowers organizations to customize their workflows by seamlessly integrating public Webex Contact Center APIs into the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer. With this low-code, no-code platform, flow developers can now easily orchestrate custom logic and enhance their contact center operations.</p> <h6>What is the Webex Contact Center API Connector?</h6><p>The Webex Contact Center API Connector is an entity within the Control Hub that allows organizations to make Webex CC API calls directly from the Flow Designer. This feature simplifies the process of invoking public Webex CC APIs by managing tokens natively, enabling developers to focus on building efficient workflows without worrying about the underlying complexities.</p> <p>In the past, using our Webex Contact Center APIs within Flow Designer required developers to manage tokens manually. This process involved several complex steps: creating an integration for admin login to provide access and refresh tokens, and building a separate token server to store, retrieve, and refresh these tokens. Now, with the introduction of the Webex CC API Connector, all this extra work and setup is no longer necessary! The Webex CC API Connector simplifies the process, allowing seamless integration without the need for additional infrastructure.</p> <p>In this blog, we are going to highlight one use case for the connector. For a complete walkthrough, be sure to check out the guide at <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/contact-center-http-connector'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/contact-center-http-connector</a>.</p> <h6>The Webex Contact Center API Connector in Action</h6><p>One practical application of the Webex Contact Center API Connector is enhancing customer service by leveraging the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/getting-started-with-search-api'>Search API</a> to improve call routing. Imagine a scenario where a customer calls back the contact center and it&#39;s beneficial for them to speak with the last agent they interacted with. By utilizing the Search API within the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer, you can efficiently look up the last agent the caller spoke with and automatically add the caller to that agent&#39;s call queue. This not only personalizes the customer experience but also improves resolution times by allowing agents who are already familiar with the customer&#39;s history to assist them more effectively. The Webex Contact Center API Connector makes this task much simpler than it used to be.</p> <h6>Webex Contact Center API Connector Setup</h6><p>Setting up the Webex Contact Center API Connector is straightforward. To get started, follow these high-level steps:</p> <ol> <li>Login to <a href='https://admin.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Control Hub</a> with an account that has one of the following privileges: <ul> <li>Full Administrator</li> <li>External Admin with Full Administrator Access</li> <li>Contact Center Service Administrator</li> </ul> </li> <li>Create a Webex Contact Center API Connector:<ol> <li>Navigate to <strong>Contact Center</strong> -&gt; <em><strong>Integrations</strong></em> -&gt; <strong>Connectors</strong> and select <strong>Set Up</strong> or <strong>Add More</strong> under the <strong>Webex Contact Center Connector</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt806817f8fa4b14da/wxcc-http-connector-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Give your connector a name that will be used in Flow Designer, choose the level of access (read or read/write), and authorize the connector: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt0e579ca71a8ad85c/wxcc-http-connector-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Your connector is ready, we will use the “WxCC Search Connector” shortly: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt1ca3b97177bc5939/wxcc-http-connector-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> </li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Flow Overview</h6><p>This is the flow that will route a caller to their previous agent. It has a lot of steps, but we will break them down:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9f6b076a34f980dd/wxcc-http-connector-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <ol> <li>When a new call comes in, we are going to get and set a few variables:<ul> <li><code>currentTime</code> is set to the current time of the call.</li> <li><code>goback_by_a_day</code> is set to the current time minus a day.</li> <li><code>ANITrim</code> is set to the caller&#39;s current number without the country code.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Use the Search API to find which agent this caller talked to recently.</li> <li>Set the <code>Agent_ID</code> based on what was found via the Search API</li> <li>Send to the agent&#39;s queue if found.</li> <li>Send to main queue if the agent is not available.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Calling the Search API with the New Connector</h6><p>The magic comes in at step 2 where we are calling the Search API. In our <strong>HTTPRequest</strong> activity, we will be doing things a little differently with the WebexCC API Connector:</p> <ol> <li>The general settings stay the same, label and description. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltfe694014a30d66c5/wxcc-http-connector-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>On the HTTP Request Settings, we are going to enable <strong>Use Authenticated Endpoint</strong>. Then, we will choose the <strong>WxCC Search Connector</strong> we just created. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6dcb4954513d0a59/wxcc-http-connector-blog-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Add the path to the API endpoint in <strong>Request Path</strong>. Note that this is a <strong>PATH</strong> not a <strong>URL</strong>; the connector handles the main part of the URL for us. We are making a request to the Search API so we are using the <code>/search</code> path. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8a145bc7766584b3/wxcc-http-connector-blog-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Finally, we store the results of the Search API in the <strong>Agent_ID</strong> flow variable.</li> </ol> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte8a6dc84355743e6/wxcc-http-connector-blog-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>We can now use the <strong>Agent_ID</strong> variable to route to that agent if the information was found!</p> <p>This was just a basic use case, but there are many different reasons for using our Webex Contact Center APIs within flows, and with the new Webex Contact Center API Connector, it is easier than ever!</p> <h6>Best Practices for Using the Webex Contact Center API Connector</h6><p>Keep in mind the following best practices when using the Webex Contact Center API Connector:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Access Rights</strong>: Choose <strong>Read-Only</strong> access rights if you intend on making only <code>GET</code> API calls. <strong>Read-Write</strong> connectors should be reserved for flows in which you intend on making <code>UPDATE</code>/<code>POST</code>/<code>PUT</code> API calls.</li> <li><strong>Avoid Storing Sensitive Information</strong>: Ensure no sensitive response data is stored in the flow logs.</li> <li><strong>Rate Limiting</strong>: Be aware that API calls from the Flow Designer are rate limited. Handle potential 429 errors gracefully.</li> <li><strong>Error Handling</strong>: Use a <strong>Case</strong> Activity to handle all error codes listed in the API definition. Optimize your flows by creating sub flows to manage error cases effectively.</li> </ul> <p>Learn more about <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/common-api-errors'>common API errors</a>.</p> <p>By following these guidelines and leveraging the Webex Contact Center API Connector, you can create robust, customized workflows that enhance your contact center&#39;s efficiency and effectiveness. Start exploring the possibilities today!</p> <h6>Where to Go Next</h6><p>For more detailed instructions and examples, visit the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs'>Webex Contact Center for Developers Portal</a>.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Look, Ma, No Hands: Using AI to Generate and Refine Webex GitHub Sample Documentation ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltffb3e647200582bc/674f1f7a2a72569686bf4caf/oauth-example-ai-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Look, Ma, No Hands: Using AI to Generate and Refine Webex GitHub Sample Documentation" /> <p>While the hype train for “artificial intelligence” (which is not and never will be) has been exhausting, as a technical writer, I&#39;ve found it to be a complete game-changing enhancement to my typical workflows. Your immediate question is probably, though, “John, don&#39;t you expect AI to completely eliminate your position??!!??”, to which I reply, “AHHHHAHAHHHAHAHAHAHHAHAH!” You see, like any tool, the usefulness of an AI assistant is directly correlated to the skill of the person using it (something I learned the hard way when I purchased an expensive fountain pen thinking that would magically imbue me with calligraphy talent. And then there was my attempt at shaving with a straight razor—the less said the better.). The tool most assuredly does not make the craftsperson, and if you have no idea what to ask an AI bot or how to evaluate the output, you&#39;re still working on a “garbage in; garbage out” basis (I&#39;m <strong>still</strong> struggling with AI image generation and producing something that doesn&#39;t look like Hieronymus Bosch on LSD).</p> <h6>How I&#39;m Using Gen AI</h6><p>That said, with some help from persons who <strong>DO</strong> have subject matter expertise, you can really boost your productivity even if you didn&#39;t waste years of your life in liberal arts colleges and graduate schools. Here are just a few of the ways that I&#39;ve been integrating AI tools into my daily workflows:</p> <ul> <li>I review a lot of GitHub pull requests for code comments and API descriptions. Many engineers don&#39;t speak English as a first language and are usually better coders than they are writers. With a few cleverly designed prompts, they can now clean up their existing descriptions and even create new basic descriptions from scratch, up to and including markdown formatting.</li> <li>Similarly, I work in a product management organization where many of the PMs are way more technical and product-savvy than they are key feature marketeers. With some thoughtful prompting they can get excellent overviews, use cases, and comprehensive grammar <em>repairing</em> (as opposed lukewarm waffling <em>suggestions</em> that you&#39;d get from products like Grammarly or the current incarnation of Word&#39;s Editor).</li> <li>Finally, I find tons of use with simple prompts like, “<em>Convert this HTML table to markdown</em>”, “<em>Check for issues with this blueprint data structure</em>” or “<em>create a brief teaser for this blog post</em>” that make things which would have required multiple steps or rounds of review now just a point and click exercise.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>The Sample Code Project</h6><p>With that in mind, when Ashton Jordan, one of our Engineering Technical Leaders came to me with a Python sample script he wanted to reference in our Webex Developer Portal documentation, I decided to have a go at seeing just how much work I could lay at the doorstep of both our Microsoft Copilot integrations for Visual Studio Code and Microsoft Word, as well as our own in-house ChatGPT implementation. My idea was that I&#39;d use Copilot for evaluating and explaining the sample Python code and our in-house chat bot to produce documentation specific to Cisco workflows.</p> <h6>Understanding the Application</h6><p>Ashton had created a Python Flask application to demonstrate the device OAuth 2 authorization workflow. Since this application was new to me, and I had no experience with the Flask framework (and I&#39;m also not an auth guru), I started by entering the entire sample in Microsoft Visual Code and used the Copilot <strong>Explain This</strong> function from the Copilot context menu:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb0adae3c7f103478/oauth-example-ai-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Interestingly, because Copilot was evaluating all the aspects of the code it prompted me to install dependencies before it would generate a description. Once I&#39;d installed the necessary modules, I repeated my request, and Copilot produced the following output in its chat panel:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte9957faf1f79c267/oauth-example-ai-blog-3.jpeg" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>You&#39;ll note that Copilot generates rather verbose descriptions for anything you select by default, and that is the case for the initial run through. More on that later…</p> <h6>Exploring the Functions</h6><p>I then went through each block and function, using <strong>Explain This</strong> to generate descriptions. Here, for instance, I asked it to explain the <code>poll_for_access_token</code> function:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf073bdd5393c4fbb/oauth-example-ai-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Like I mentioned at the beginning, I had no experience with Flask-based Python applications and when I noticed the decorators preceding various functions, I wasn&#39;t sure what was going on. So, I asked Copilot, and it explained how the decorators functioned in a Flask application, “<em>This decorator tells Flask that the function immediately following should be associated with the root URL of the web application</em>” along with a great deal of further details, useful if you&#39;re new to the concept:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbad8fa2cd76e6bab/oauth-example-ai-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>I did the same for final line, <code>if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;: app.run(debug=True, host=&#39;0.0.0.0&#39;, port=10060)</code> statement at the end, discovering that it&#39;s simply a way <em>“…ensure that certain code is only executed when the script is run directly, rather than when it is imported as a module in another script</em>.”</p> <h6>Refining the Application Description for a GitHub README</h6><p>Once I&#39;d answered all my questions and entertained myself by adding a few improvements (via Copilot, of course), I used further follow-on prompts such as <em>Reformat that response as an ordered list in markdown format</em> to tweak the presentation:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5fe2eb29059539c5/oauth-example-ai-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <div><Callout type="info">I added the Word formatting you see in all examples since that's what I'm using to produce this blog post (no judgment). At this point, Copilot for Word does **NOT** handle formatting using standard styles in a useful way. I expect that will eventually be remedied. </Callout></div> <p>The above description was a bit verbose for a GitHub readme (engineers don&#39;t need to be spoon-fed basic stuff), so I decided to condense it down a bit. This was generated after selecting the entry above in Microsoft Word and using the Copilot prompt, <em>Generate a concise single paragraph description using bulleted points as required</em>:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt982bfcdbb6f12748/oauth-example-ai-blog-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>I further followed that up with a request to <em>Describe the additional file dependencies for this Flask application</em> which I then cleaned up to remove irrelevant entries:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8d6b7c729ca81992/oauth-example-ai-blog-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <div><Callout type="info">Again, the formatted links were added post-generation. </Callout></div> <h4><a class='anchor-tag icon icon-link_16 icon-link' name='establishing-prerequisites-and-dependencies-title'></a>Establishing Prerequisites and Dependencies</h4><a class='offset-anchor-tag' name='establishing-prerequisites-and-dependencies'></a><p>The next thing I had to do was figure out what was required as far as prerequisites and dependencies to get the application to run as expected (meaning making Copilot tell <em>me</em> what was required…).</p> <h6>Install Python Modules</h6><p>Copilot was able to identify the required modules and provide the pip install statements (which are pretty simple):</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt253cc9d9c9a739ca/oauth-example-ai-blog-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>You&#39;ll notice Copilot also provided descriptions for each module as well, which I suppose I could have condensed as well.</p> <h6>Create an Integration and Retrieve Integration Authorization Information</h6><p>Ashton&#39;s application requires a back-end Webex integration to work correctly, but as expected, Copilot, was <strong>not</strong> able to identify that a Webex integration was required for the script to function. For this, I turned to our own in-house ChatGPT interface starting with the prompt, <em>Please provide step by step instructions for creating a new Webex Integration using the Webex Developer Portal, <a data-type='internal' to='/my-apps/new/integration'>Webex Developer Support Team</a></em>.</p> <p>Further prompt revisions included, <em>Revise the ordered list so it does not use unordered lists</em> followed by <em>Revise the previous response to be a single ordered list</em> as well as a further clarification, <em>Revise the previous response so it uses a single ordered list but does not include unordered lists following each ordered list entry</em>. While the former prompt flattened the structure somewhat, neither that nor the latter prompt accomplished exactly what I needed.</p> <p>The key problem with this part of the project was updating the outdated GPT-generated procedures that referenced our web docs and applications (even though this is Cisco-hosted and trained). The initial workflow generated by our own in-house ChatGPT implementation to get to the <strong>Create an Integration</strong> page had to be re-worked because the generated steps were erroneous. The steps for filling out the integration page were also incomplete and had to be keystroked. After making the required corrections, I triumphantly added an introductory sentence that I wrote <em>all by myself</em>:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltaf49790ee29fd904/oauth-example-ai-blog-10.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <div><Callout type="info">Our Webex AI Assistant is currently in beta, and, once released, it should markedly improve the accuracy of such queries. </Callout></div> <h6>Run the Sample</h6><p>To run the sample, all Copilot really had to say was <code>python oauth.py</code> and make sure you&#39;ve got your dependencies installed. Of course, while that&#39;s technically correct, there were a few more things I needed to add, including example output:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltad94aebdca5f7a5f/oauth-example-ai-blog-11.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Putting Everything Together</h6><p>Once I&#39;d finished writing, or, more appropriately, assembling, reviewing and editing, I converted the final document into Github markdown:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte92ca991452970b0/oauth-example-ai-blog-12.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <div><Callout type="info">You can take a look at the complete project here: <https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-device-oauth-sample>. </Callout></div> <h6>Key Takeaways</h6><p>There are tons of things that are best avoided when using GPT tools, including relationship advice, political analysis and generating a step-by-step guide to removing your own appendix, but an absolutely perfect use is augmenting your coding workflows. Assuming you know <em>what</em> you want to do (and that it&#39;s possible), you can get quick <em>working</em> answers to things like “<em>Display syntax highlighted code in a browser window</em>” or “<em>Base64 encode the output from this function</em>.” Relatedly, when you find something in a code base you don&#39;t understand, you can get extremely accurate explanations that you can use for documentation purposes or as a part of understanding and expanding functionality or solving issues.</p> <div><Callout type="info">To be honest, even when something sounded like the completely wrong thing to do, it was really instructive to ask Copilot how to do it-—it often suggested solutions that didn't seem obvious at first. </Callout></div> <p>As a final, note, I also recommend keeping a running list of the prompts that you use as well as the refinements, and keep testing them. You&#39;ll then have a library that you can share with team members that they can also contribute to, saving everybody time and effort.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>Remember, if you need help actually developing your application, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
