<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ How to create your own RSS Feed Parser Bot for Webex ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4c22bdae6e5d5d59/6740befd12a5eabe959335c2/rss-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="How to create your own RSS Feed Parser Bot for Webex" /> <p>Hello Webex Developers! If you&#39;re someone who has previously made use of the Cisco provided RSS Bot that was available through our <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex App Hub</a>, you&#39;re probably now aware that this bot was decommissioned recently and is no longer going to be offered. This bot was used for registering to any RSS feed out there, once there was a new feed entry it sent a notification to a Webex space of your choosing. Before it was decommissioned, the Bot sent a message to all users informing us of the same. It was a difficult decision to decommission the bot, but it had to be made due to the nature of the infrastructural changes that occurred to its dependencies which were no longer compatible with the bot and therefore we had to act.</p> <p>We understand that this was not ideal for our users, and that it affected numerous applications and some automations that were reliant on it. Therefore, we thought that we should at least help our developers implement their own bot. In this blog, we&#39;ll discuss some options to get you started with your own implementation of the RSS Bot, fully customizable to tailor to your needs. We&#39;ll also share an option to immediately get you up and running, if you generally only need to follow the Webex related RSS feeds. Let&#39;s get started!</p> <h6>Get updates on Webex RSS feeds right now</h6><p>If you generally only ever require updates on the Webex provided RSS feeds, then this is for you. We have a ready-made option where you can simply get added to some Webex spaces that are tailor-made for our main Webex RSS feeds. There, you will get updates in real-time, as the RSS Feeds are updated. To remind you, the Webex RSS feeds are (in bold is the actual name of the Webex Space for the same):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Webex Incidents:</strong> <a href='https://status.webex.com/incidents.rss' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://status.webex.com/incidents.rss</a></li> <li><strong>Webex Maintenance:</strong> <a href='https://status.webex.com/maintenances.rss' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://status.webex.com/maintenances.rss</a></li> <li><strong>Webex Announcements:</strong> <a href='https://status.webex.com/updates-upgrades.rss' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://status.webex.com/updates-upgrades.rss</a></li> <li><strong>Webex Developer API:</strong> <a data-type='internal' to='/api/content/changelog/feed'>https://developer.webex.com/api/content/changelog/feed</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Add yourself to the Spaces</h6><p>If you want to be added to these spaces related to the above feeds, then simply follow this link: <a href='https://eurl.io/#zE415kpu2' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://eurl.io/#zE415kpu2</a> and it will add the email you provide it to a Webex General Space, within a Team named <strong>Webex RSS External</strong>. This team contains all the Webex spaces for the above RSS feeds, named clearly to explain what RSS Feed they are for. You will be automatically added to those spaces by a bot named <em>TeamSync Ext</em> (email <a href='mailto:teamsync.ext@webex.bot' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>teamsync.ext@webex.bot</a>, you can check out its code <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/team-sync' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>). You can find a screenshot of the mentioned spaces below:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt19de2413c2ec8f5f/rss-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>How it works</h6><p>The above RSS feeds are displayed in the Webex spaces thanks to a Webex Bot named <em>Webex RSS</em>, with email: <a href='mailto:webexrss@webex.bot' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webexrss@webex.bot</a>. There is JavaScript code behind the bot that monitors the feeds for any new items and once a new item comes in it uses the bot&#39;s token to send a message to the related Webex space.</p> <p>The message is simple, it just contains the feed item&#39;s title, description and web link to the online version of the same update. Based on the description of the item, it also color-codes the message on Webex: <strong>Red</strong> when an issue is identified (mainly used for Issue/Incident updates), <strong>yellow</strong> when it&#39;s being monitored or an upgrade is in progress, and <strong>green</strong> when issue is fixed, or an upgrade was completed successfully.</p> <p>We&#39;ll explain below in more detail how the Webex RSS bot works, with code snippets taken from its repository. This should help you in building your own bot. The repository is found here, for your reference: <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss</a>. Feel free to clone it and start working on your own implementation.</p> <h6>Bot Implementation Details</h6><p>The production version of this bot is hosted on AWS. It uses Docker (a containerization software) to build the app container and manage it through that, then push it to an AWS service. There is a <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/Dockerfile' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Docker file</a> present in the repository already for your reference. You can use that <em>as is</em> or modify it to suit your needs, if you want to deploy your own version of this bot.</p> <p>The app has some environment variables that need to be configured. We usually create a <code>.env</code> file to store all these. <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/README.md#environmental-variables' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Here</a> you&#39;ll find which ones are mandatory or optional, along with the default values if applicable. At minimum, if you plan to deploy your own bot you should add the bot&#39;s token and the room ID(s) you want to use for the RSS Feed updates.</p> <p>The RSS feeds are configured as constants in this bot, as mentioned earlier there are 4 Webex feeds. They are hard-coded in the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/app.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>app.js</a> file but you can add them as Environment Variables if you prefer, or even create some UI or user friendly mechanism to allow the bot&#39;s users to add their own RSS feed URLs (more on this below). And while speaking about the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/app.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>app.js</a> file, this is where the app&#39;s logic is initiated. For the purposes of showing how this works we&#39;re just going to focus on one feed, that being the one for Webex Incidents. But all others follow pretty much the same logic, with just some minor tweaks to suit specific cases. The code samples you will see in this blog may not be the exact same as in the repository, simply because we&#39;re focusing on just one feed, but it is just slightly truncated, and all logic remains the same.</p> <h6>Reviewing the Code</h6><p>Initialization is done through an <code>init()</code> function. This function gets called <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/65879d725bfe26c7f6782765a749b4f726f626f8/app.js#L175' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a> (and defined <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/65879d725bfe26c7f6782765a749b4f726f626f8/app.js#L124' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>) and it gets the bot details and the Webex spaces/rooms where the bot will send notifications. A <code>parserService</code> object instance exists, to call some Webex related functions such as <code>getBot()</code> and <code>getRoom()</code>. This is coming from the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/src/parserService.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>parserService.js</a> Module we imported, we&#39;ll provide more details later on what this module does but basically its main task is to parse the feed entry we receive and format it so that we can then send a clear <em>RSS feed</em> update in the Webex Space.</p> <p>You&#39;ll also see that we are using a <code>logger</code> object instance. This is just an import of the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/src/logger.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>logger.js</a> module we&#39;ve built to log any useful information of events that occur within the app. This uses the commonly known <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/winston' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Winston package</a>, it is a very useful package for logging. Below is the <code>init()</code> function:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">async function init() { logger.info(`Webex RSS Integration, v${version}`); try { const bot = await parserService.getBot(); logger.info(`Bot Loaded: ${bot.displayName} (${bot.emails[0]})`); } catch (error) { logger.error(&#39;ERROR: Unable to load Webex Bot, check Token.&#39;); logger.debug(error.message); process.exit(2); } try { const incRoom = await parserService.getRoom(env.INC_ROOM); logger.info(`Inc Room: ${incRoom.title}`); } catch (error) { logger.error(&#39;ERROR: Bot is not a member of the Incident Room!&#39;); process.exit(2); } incidentWatcher.start(); logger.info(&#39;Startup Complete!&#39;); } </code></pre> <h6>Create a Feed Watcher and Listen to Events</h6><p>You&#39;ll see that we&#39;re calling <code>incidentWatcher.start();</code> This is an instance from the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/lib/feedWatcher.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>feedWatcher.js</a> Module, it starts the watcher. This module is key as this is the logic that <em>watches</em> each feed URL and emits events once new feed entries are detected. Within this module, we first parse the feed URL to ensure it is present and usable (we import the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/lib/parseRss.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>parseRss.js</a> module to do this. It&#39;s got some nifty code that you can look through). Then, a class named <em>Watcher</em> is defined and it extends <code>EventEmitter</code> class, which is an export from the Node.js <code>events</code> package. This is a clever way to create event listeners on the feeds, there are a number of functions such as <code>start(), stop(), watch()</code>, etc., which help to monitor the feeds for new item entries. Once a new entry is available, we process it.</p> <p>A constructor is also defined to take 2 parameters, <code>feedUrl</code> and <code>interval</code> (this constructor is used to create the <code>incidentWatcher</code> instance). The <code>interval</code> parameter defines how long the watcher waits before checking the feed again for new entries. By default this bot sets the interval to 5 minutes, you can change that in <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/app.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>app.js</a> within your own implementation if you wish by changing the value of <code>RSS_INTERVAL</code> env variable (in minutes).</p> <p>For the purposes of this bot, 4 <code>Watcher</code> object instances are created, aptly named to explain what they&#39;re for. We have <code>incidentWatcher</code>, <code>maintenanceWatcher</code>, <code>announcementWatcher</code> and <code>apiWatcher</code> and you&#39;ll find these in <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/app.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>app.js</a><code>.</code> We&#39;ll mainly focus on <code>incidentWatcher</code> to explain the code flow, as they all pretty much follow the same logic, with just some minor tweaks to suit specific needs. </p> <p>To begin <em>watching</em>, the <code>Watcher</code> instance is created:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">const incidentWatcher = new Watcher(incidentFeed, interval); </code></pre> <p>Then we start the instance as shown previously through the <code>init()</code> function. And then we <em>listen</em>, like so:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">incidentWatcher.on(&#39;new entries&#39;, (entries) =&gt; { entries.forEach((item) =&gt; { // Identify Item Type logger.debug(&#39;new incident item&#39;); const typeIndex = item.description.indexOf(&#39;&lt;strong &gt;&#39;); if (typeIndex !== -1) { const typeEnd = item.description.indexOf(&#39;&lt;/strong &gt;&#39;, typeIndex); const itemType = item.description.substring(typeIndex + 9, typeEnd); logger.debug(`detected as ${itemType}`); switch (itemType) { case &#39;resolved&#39;: case &#39;monitoring&#39;: case &#39;identified&#39;: case &#39;investigating&#39;: parserService.parseIncident(item, itemType); break; default: logger.debug(&#39;EVENT: UNKNOWN&#39;); logger.debug(item); } } }); </code></pre> <p>In the above code snippet, we check for new entries (thanks to the logic from <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/lib/feedWatcher.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>feedWatcher.js</a>) and for each new entry item we find, we check the item type through a switch statement. In the switch statement we want to see whether it&#39;s an incident that&#39;s just been reported and being investigated, or root cause has been identified, or fix has been deployed and being monitored, or if it&#39;s completely resolved. These are usually the 4 stages/states of a Webex Incident.</p> <h6>Parse and Format Each Feed Entry</h6><p>As we briefly touched on earlier, we have a <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/src/parserService.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>parserService.js</a> module which is used to parse any new incoming feed entry. Its main purpose is to parse the new RSS feed entry and format its content so that we can then send it as a message to the relevant Webex space. It&#39;s got a number of nested functions within the outer function named after the module it&#39;s in, that being <code>parserService(),</code> which gets exported for use elsewhere.</p> <p>Some of the nested functions include: <code>formatDescription(), formatBlockquote(), getBot(), getRoom(), parseIncident()</code>, etc. They&#39;re all clearly named so it shouldn&#39;t be difficult to understand their job. They essentially combine to give you a well formatted and clear Webex message like the below one, also using some html tags to “pretty-print” the message:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4dedf90387d34e4f/rss-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Handle Feed Errors and Stop the Watcher</h6><p>The bot has logic that checks for any possible errors with the feed (for example, if the feed URL is down). Code is simple but effective, see below:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">incidentWatcher.on(&#39;error&#39;, (error) =&gt; { logger.error(`Inc Feed Error: ${error}`); }); </code></pre> <p>We also handle graceful shutdown through SIGINT and stop the watcher at that point, see below:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">process.on(&#39;SIGINT&#39;, () =&gt; { logger.debug(&#39;Stopping...&#39;); incidentWatcher.stop(); logger.debug(&#39;Feeds Stopped.&#39;); process.exit(0); }); </code></pre> <h6>Send Webex Messages</h6><p>To send the Webex messages to each space, we&#39;ve got the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/src/httpService.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>httpService.js</a> Module. We import the <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>axios</a> npm package to aid this, it is a very useful package for sending HTTP Requests to RESTful APIs, such as ours. What I like most about Axios is that it also comes with additional packages <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios-retry' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>axios-retry</a> to retry API calls as required, and <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios-rate-limit' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>axios-rate-limit</a> to manage the API&#39;s rate-limiting by adding a timeout. These help developers manage API requests properly, ensuring minimal disruptions due to the API&#39;s rate-limiting policies and other issues that may require retries.</p> <p>The main function in this module is the <code>postMessage()</code> function. As the name suggests, this function posts the message to the related Webex space, using the <a href='https://webexapis.com/v1/messages' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://webexapis.com/v1/messages</a> API (documented <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/messages/create-a-message'>here</a>). This API requires a <code>roomId</code> (for group spaces/rooms) or one of <code>toPersonId</code> or <code>toPersonEmail</code>, if you want to send a direct/1:1 message. The bot only sends messages to group spaces/rooms in its current configuration, but it does have code within this function to handle cases where direct messages are sent. Below is the code snippet showing the initial POST request&#39;s <code>options</code> object being created and also the if/else statement handling the message type:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">return new Promise((resolve, reject) =&gt; { const directMessage = direct || false; const messageFormat = format || &#39;html&#39;; const options = { method: &#39;POST&#39;, url: &#39;https://webexapis.com/v1/messages&#39;, headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`, &#39;Content-Type&#39;: &#39;application/json&#39;, }, data: {}, json: true, }; if (directMessage) { options.data.toPersonId = destId; } else { options.data.roomId = destId; } // ... }); </code></pre> <p>As you can see, the <code>options</code> object contains the <code>method</code>, <code>url</code>, <code>headers</code>, <code>data</code> and <code>json</code> properties. Our request body will go in the <code>data</code> property, and with the following if/else statement we define whether to use <code>roomId</code> or <code>toPersonId.</code></p> <p>Beyond this, the API also requires the <code>text</code> or <code>markdown</code> fields to be passed in its request body. The bot only sends <code>markdown</code> messages given that it&#39;s formatting the message, below is code for how it adds it to the <code>data</code> property within <code>options</code>, in the same function:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">options.data[messageFormat] = message; if (messageFormat === &#39;markdown&#39;) { options.data[messageFormat] = message.replace(/\\\n/g, &#39;\n&#39;); } </code></pre> <p>Now, we send the request with <code>axios</code>. Here&#39;s how we build the request:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">axios .request(options) .then((response) =&gt; { // Check JSON payload is compliant with specs if (!response.data) { logger.debug(&#39;could not parse message details: bad or invalid json payload.&#39;); reject(response.status); } logger.debug(&#39;message sent&#39;); resolve(); }) .catch((error) =&gt; { logger.debug(`postMessage error: ${error.message}`); if (error.response &amp;amp;&amp;amp; error.response.headers.trackingid) { logger.debug(`tid: ${error.response.headers.trackingid}`); } reject(error); }); </code></pre> <p>There we go! This should now post your message with the feed update to the space, so we&#39;ve gone through the full basic flow of the app. And just to complete explaining this module, there is another function called <code>getField()</code>. Its main task is to do a <code>GET</code> to one of our APIs (which one exactly is determined by an <code>apiName</code> param we send in when calling the function). It&#39;s called twice in the <a href='https://github.com/jeremywillans/webex-rss/blob/main/src/parserService.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>parserService.js</a> Module, once each in the <code>getBot()</code> and <code>getRoom()</code> functions, and it&#39;s a nice example to showcase how the same code can get reused multiple times. You can use this in other <code>GET</code> requests if needed, where you need to do a GET to our APIs. Just send the <code>token</code> and <code>apiName</code> params (for example <code>/rooms</code> or <code>/people</code> API string names) and the function should take care of the request for you.</p> <h6>What if You Want to Use Non-Webex RSS Feeds?</h6><p>We&#39;ve got you covered. We&#39;ve simplified the code above into this <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/Boilerplate-RSS-bot' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Boilerplate template RSS Bot</a> so that you just have to add your own feed URL, bot token and room ID as environment variables. You can then run the bot in your own environment and it should respond with a simple message that includes the feed item&#39;s title, description and link (do make sure that your Feed URL has said properties. If not change them in the code).</p> <p>We&#39;ve basically stripped down the code we&#39;ve talked about above, so a lot of the formatting has been removed as well as some <em>feed-specific</em> code logic. It still does some minor formatting on the message but to a much lesser extent than what the code above has. The code logic remains very much the same, just simplified to make it easier to get started with your own implementation.</p> <p>To give you a view of what a message from this boilerplate code sample would look like, here is an image showcasing the same (we used a basic test RSS feed, so the content is just some <em>lorem ipsum</em> text, but you get the idea):</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt677f93294dbe2fbc/rss-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Allow users to add their own RSS Feed URL</h6><p>If you plan on building a sort of (or maybe even fully fledged) Production bot to cater for this use case, you may want to give users the option of adding their own RSS Feed URLs, instead of <em>hard-coding</em> them in the code. There are several ways to manage this, for example you could build a web UI where users can enter some initial details such as room ID, Feed URL, etc., and then you can store those in a database so that your bot can reference those later when working with said users. You could also add some additional logic with a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/integrations'>Webex OAuth Integration</a>, where the user authorizes this integration through your UI and the resulting access token created from that can be used to pull all the user&#39;s spaces, to give them a dropdown option (or similar UI option), allowing them to choose which space to add the bot to and set up the RSS feed notifications for. This would be somewhat like what the old RSS bot did, if you liked that process then this might be something to work on.</p> <p>Or you might want to keep it a bit simpler than that. In that case, you may want to try using <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/buttons-and-cards'>Adaptive Cards</a> with your bot. You could create logic where the bot sends an adaptive card to a space they just got added to, to allow the user to add some details like the RSS feed URL they want to use and then you store it on your side. You will need to add some kind of listener to <em>listen</em> to any membership creations on the bot. You have 2 ways to manage this:</p> <ol> <li>By creating a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/webhooks'>Webhook</a> using the bot&#39;s token, on the <code>memberships</code> resource with the <code>created</code> event.</li> <li>By Creating a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/using-websockets-with-the-webex-javascript-sdk'>Websocket</a> using the bot&#39;s token within our <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/browser'>JavaScript SDK</a>, on the same resource and event.</li> </ol> <p>The difference between these is that websockets are generally used when you do not want to use a public server URL, for example if you&#39;re working behind a firewall or other network restrictions. Whereas webhooks need a public URL (with no auth requirements) to be defined as the <code>targetURL,</code> that&#39;s where the webhook payload is sent. In any case, whichever option you decide to use, once the listener gets triggered you can then send an adaptive card that has some options that the user can fill in. As a visual example, here is a very simple one that looks like this:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5b0aeacf6884a683/rss-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>The JSON for this is below:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;$schema&quot;: &quot;http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json&quot;, &quot;type&quot;: &quot;AdaptiveCard&quot;, &quot;version&quot;: &quot;1.3&quot;, &quot;body&quot;: [ { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;ColumnSet&quot;, &quot;columns&quot;: [ { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;Column&quot;, &quot;width&quot;: 2, &quot;items&quot;: [ { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;TextBlock&quot;, &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Register your RSS Feed notification&quot;, &quot;weight&quot;: &quot;Bolder&quot;, &quot;size&quot;: &quot;Medium&quot; }, { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;TextBlock&quot;, &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Enter URL&quot;, &quot;wrap&quot;: true }, { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;Input.Text&quot;, &quot;id&quot;: &quot;myName&quot;, &quot;placeholder&quot;: &quot;Feed URL&quot; } ] } ] } ], &quot;actions&quot;: [ { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;Action.Submit&quot;, &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Submit&quot; } ] } </code></pre> <p>Adaptive cards are explained in detail <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/buttons-and-cards'>here</a>, with some samples too. Worth a read if you&#39;ve never used them before. We also have the <a data-type='internal' to='/buttons-and-cards-designer'>Buttons and Cards Designer</a> to build your own card if you wish. Ours above is quite basic, there are many more options you can use to make it more visually (and functionally) appealing. The basic (pseudo) flow works like this:</p> <ol> <li>First, create a Webhook (or websocket) on the <code>attachmentActions</code> resource, same way as we discussed earlier.</li> <li>This gets triggered every time someone interacts with an action on your card.</li> <li>In the above case, the action is the <strong>Submit</strong> button, the JSON contains an <code>actions</code> array with a <code>Action.Submit</code> type. That&#39;s your action.</li> <li>Once the user enters their RSS feed and submits, your webhook/websocket gets triggered and you can then proceed with registering the notification set up for them.</li> </ol> <p>The code samples we&#39;ve explained in this blog don&#39;t currently have any of this functionality, but we thought we should at least mention how you can go about it if you plan on doing something like this.</p> <p>Furthermore, to scale this app you&#39;ll likely have to store some information. What you store and how/where you store it is up to you. A viable approach might be to use a DB to store the RSS feed URL the user entered, along with some other details such as the roomId (the <code>memberships</code> webhook/websocket returns that) and maybe some user data to identify the user who created the notification so you can match it to that user every time that&#39;s required in your flow. Of course, you should ensure there are no legal ramifications with the data you may decide to store (most notably any user data).</p> <p>And that&#39;s that, We hope this helps!</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>As always, should you have any queries about this or any other Webex Developer related topics, please don&#39;t hesitate to reach out to our team. We&#39;re dedicated to helping developers wherever possible, any time. You can reach out through the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support channels</a> 24/7.</p> <p>Happy coding! <strong>The Webex Developer Team</strong></p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter - End of Year 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter - End of Year 2024" /> <p>Greetings, Webex Developers! This edition has all the latest news as we get close to the new year. Keep reading to discover all the new updates.</p> <h6>🧑🏻‍💼The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Agents</h6><p>In the latest addition to the “The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs” blog series, Developer Evangelist, Joe Zanini shows us how to get started building a custom desktop with the Agents APIs and the associated webhooks. He also covers the use cases for custom desktops in Webex Contact Center, pointing out where the sweet spot is for leveraging the Agent APIs.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis-agents'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📆Create a Meeting Scheduler as a Webex Service App</h6><p>In a new how-to blog post by Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti, learn how Webex Service Apps can automatically schedule meetings for users within an organization with a sample Python application. This will take you step-by-step for quickly creating the app and running your own demo using a developer sandbox.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/creating-a-meeting-scheduler-as-a-webex-service-app'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🚛Webex Application Transfer Portal Usage Hands-on</h6><p>Developer Support Engineer, Sandip Banerjee, also has a new helpful blog post that is a guide for using the Webex Application Transfer Portal. This tool allows administrators to transfer integrations, bots, service apps, and embedded apps between users within their organization. This comes in handy when someone who maintains specific apps leaves the company or assumes a new role, and a new user will be taking over the responsibility.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-application-transfer-portal-usage-hands-on'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>🖥️Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On Wednesday, January 15, 2025, at 1:00PM EST, join us for a retrospective webinar, <strong>“Kicking off 2025 with Key Platform Advancements”</strong>, as we look back into the exciting new features and updates introduced to the Webex for Developers platform over the past year. This session will provide developers with an overview of the enhancements designed to streamline integrations, improve user experience, and expand the capabilities of your applications. Don&#39;t miss out on this chance to elevate and stay ahead with the latest in Webex extensibility.</p> <p><a href='https://evangelism.webex.com/weblink/register/rd3b39a5fd6e46e5493a58d0b66c68635' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register for the live webinar →</a></p> <p>In case you can&#39;t make the live event, you can always watch the session recording later or check out all the past sessions on our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a>.</p> <h6>🚀Boost.space Integrates with Webex for Seamless Data Synchronization and Workflow Management</h6><p>In a new partner blog post from CCO &amp; Director of Boost.space, Vít Bilinec, you will explore their powerful integration that was recently listed on the Webex App Hub. Boost.space is a data synchronization platform, and their integration allows Webex users to connect to more than 2000+ third-party applications and analyze, manage, and automate processes. The blog covers how the Boost.space app works, the developer journey on the Webex platform, and the App Hub approval process.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/boost-space-integrates-with-webex-for-seamless-data-synchronization-and-workflow-management'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>👩🏻‍💻Webex Recordings Downloader Demo</h6><p>From time to time, there may be a need to download your past Webex Meetings recordings, which can be tedious when doing it manually one at a time. In another beneficial how-to blog post, Developer Support Engineer, Jeff Marshall, walks us through a Python application that demonstrates how an admin or compliance officer can bulk download Webex Meeting Recordings using the developer APIs.</p> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-recordings-downloader-demo'>Read the blog →</a></p> <h6>📞Developer βeta: Webex Click-to-Call</h6><p>New in the Developer βeta program is Webex Click to Call, which is designed to provide a user-friendly calling experience for guest users. This powerful feature eliminates the need for downloads, accounts, and authentication, to ensure customers can connect with your enterprise effortlessly with just click of a button, improving overall customer satisfaction and engagement. Get started with early access today!</p> <p><a href='https://cs.co/webexdeveloperbeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Join the βeta →</a></p> <h6>📱Mobile SDK Update (iOS and Android): APIs to Boost Incoming Call Audio</h6><p>In the recent Webex Mobile SDK v3.14 SDK update, receiver-side audio quality for Webex and PSTN calls can now be enhanced. This new feature results in a better overall experience for Webex Calling users when talking to non-Webex users. Check out the developer guides on the official Webex GitHub to get all the details and watch the helpful Vidcasts from our SDK engineers to get started quickly.</p> <p><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/Bandwidth-Extension-Support' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Read the iOS Guide →</a>&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;<a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk/wiki/Bandwidth-Extension-Support' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Read the Android Guide →</a></p> <p><a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/d38edaff-11b0-46e7-8b3a-760830dafba3' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Watch iOS Vidcast →</a>&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; <a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/fa6276c2-60e8-4304-ba29-e4b124140f43' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Watch Android Vidcast →</a></p> <h6>🛠️Webex Contact Center: Desktop SDK Changes</h6><p>Please take note of some breaking changes announced on <em>November 14, 2024</em> for the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/desktop'>Webex Contact Center Desktop SDK</a>:</p> <ul> <li>Starting on <strong>May 16, 2025</strong>, the JavaScript SDK will be updated to a major version where the old methods will be <strong>deprecated</strong> and replaced by their <strong>newer v2 versions</strong>. Although the functionalities will remain the same, developers need to transition to using the updated methods: <code>acceptV2</code>, <code>endV2()</code>, <code>cancelTaskV2()</code>, <code>pauseRecordingV2()</code>, <code>resumeRecordingV2()</code>, <code>wrapupV2()</code>, <code>consultV2()</code>, <code>consultEndV2()</code>, <code>consultConferenceV2()</code>, <code>exitConference()</code>, <code>consultTransferV2()</code>, <code>blindTransferV2()</code>, <code>vTeamTransferV2()</code>, and <code>buddyAgentsV2()</code>. This change is necessary to ensure compatibility and leverage the improvements made in the newer versions of these methods.</li> <li>Starting on <strong>January 16, 2025</strong>, the functions <code>Desktop.actions.getWrapUpCodes()</code> and <code>Desktop.actions.getIdleCodes()</code> will be <strong>deprecated</strong> and replaced by a paginated version of the function to fetch AUX codes. The new function, <code>Desktop.agentConfigJsApi.fetchPaginatedAuxCodes(\\{workType, page, pageSize, search, customFilter})</code>, will handle the fetching of AUX codes. The <code>workType</code> parameter should be set to either <code>WRAP_UP_CODE</code> or <code>IDLE_CODE</code> to specify the type of AUX code that needs to be retrieved. This transition is part of an effort to improve the efficiency and functionality of AUX code retrieval within the system.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Full Contact Center API Changelog →</a></p> <h6>📝Webex API Recent Changelog Hits</h6><p>There are also two very important changes that were recently listed in the Webex API Changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Breaking Change - November 21, 2024:</strong> The values of the <code>errorCodes</code> field returned by the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/call-routing/get-a-trunk'>Get a Trunk</a> endpoint will be changing on January 24, 2025. Please see the full changelog for the new code values. </li> <li><strong>Breaking Change - November 12, 2024:</strong> As highlighted in the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/app-programming-interface-behavior-changes'>API Behavior Changes document</a>, the <code>rooms/meetingInfo</code> API may not return information after an organization was moved to the Webex Suite Meetings Platform. As explained, the reason is that in WSMP, there is only a loose concept of a space meeting. The meeting does not happen in the space but must be scheduled via the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting'>/meetings REST endpoints</a>. The meetings REST endpoint also provides the SIP dial info for the meeting. Please utilize this REST endpoint to avoid service disruption.</li> </ul> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Full Webex API Changelog →</a></p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Creating a Meeting Scheduler as a Webex Service App ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc3cb2df63daa0133/673e3b5b7a428c18bdabc338/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Creating a Meeting Scheduler as a Webex Service App" /> <p><a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>Webex Service Apps</a> are machine accounts that can access the Webex APIs on behalf of an organization instead of individual users. This makes them optimal for running mission-critical integrations and long-term tasks for a Webex org. Many popular Webex Service Apps are administrative integrations, such as automated <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/webex-calling-provisioning-apis'>provisioning</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/exploring-the-webex-calling-reports-and-analytics-apis'>active reporting</a> use cases. They are also commonly used for <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/compliance'>Compliance Officer</a> integrations that continuously maintain regulatory policies, eDiscovery, and other security tasks inside of Webex Messaging, Meetings, and Calling.</p> <p>Another great way some of our largest enterprise customers are leveraging Service Apps is to automate the scheduling of Webex meetings for anyone within an organization. For example, a Human Resources Management (HRM) tool that streamlines the scheduling of job interview and onboarding sessions in Webex Meetings. With a Service App, these meetings are scheduled on behalf of the organization, which eliminates the need for a specific administrator to authorize the HRM integration on their own account to schedule meetings across the organization. This scenario is also an ideal fit for Service Apps because the meeting scheduler integration is a critical component of the HRM tool and used on a full-time basis.</p> <h6>Getting Started with the Demo</h6><p>To get familiarized with how the basic parts come together, this blog will take you through a step-by-step demo for creating a Webex Service App meeting scheduler using a sample Python application. When trying these steps on your own, you will need to have few things to start:</p> <ol> <li>Admin access to Webex (Control Hub). You can get this with a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/developer-sandbox-guide'>Webex Developer Sandbox</a>. </li> <li>Make a couple test user accounts in the sandbox org that the Service App will schedule meetings for. The easiest way is to <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/v71ztb/Add-Users-Manually-in-Control-Hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>manually add users</a>.</li> <li><a href='https://www.python.org/downloads/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Python 3.x</a> installed on your machine.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Step 1: Create a Webex Service App</h6><p>To start, a Service App needs to be created in the developer portal. Have the credentials ready your sandbox admin and test users:</p> <ol> <li>Login to <a>developer.webex.com</a> using credentials from one of your (non-administrator) sandbox test users.</li> <li>Up on the top right corner of the page, click your avatar and then select <strong>My Webex Apps</strong>.</li> <li>On the <strong>Create a New App</strong> page, find the <strong>Service App</strong> card and click <strong>Create a Service App</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8c8556f2fbf45d59/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Fill out the webform to register a new service app. Pay extra attention to the <strong>scopes</strong> section to ensure the app has admin permission to schedule meetings:<ul> <li><strong>App Name:</strong> meeting-scheduler-demo</li> <li><strong>Icon:</strong> <em>Select any color icon.</em></li> <li><strong>Description:</strong> “Demo app only”</li> <li><strong>Contact Email</strong>: Use the email from the test user login. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbafba8a0e95dc524/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li><strong>Scopes</strong>: For this demo app, we only need to select the <code>meeting:admin_schedule_write</code> scope. In a real-world scenario, the meeting scheduler app would likely require the <code>read</code> scope and potentially other scopes. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt516456f6a685c9a8/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ul> </li> <li>Click the <strong>Add Service App</strong> button to finish registration: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte882db486a251276/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <h6>Step 2: Service App Authorization</h6><p>After successfully registering the Service App, you are taken to a page that contains a <strong>Client ID</strong> and <strong>Client Secret</strong>, which are required for all Service Apps. This is also where you request an admin to authorize the Service App in Control Hub:</p> <ol> <li>Copy &amp; paste the <strong>Client ID</strong> and <strong>Client Secret</strong> values into a notepad for later use. Do note, this client secret is only shown once.</li> <li>Click <strong>Request admin authorization</strong>. Keep this tab open, as we will be going back to it. For this demo, we also need to act as the administrator inside Control Hub to authorize the Service App that was just created: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6c9f5b9117f777b0/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Open an incognito browser tab and login to <a href='https://admin.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>admin.webex.com</a> using the administrator credentials for your sandbox.</li> <li>On the left navigation pane in Control Hub, look under the <strong>Management</strong> section and select <strong>Apps</strong>.</li> <li>On top of the <strong>Apps</strong> page, select the <strong>Service Apps</strong> tab. </li> <li>Click the <strong>meeting-scheduler-demo</strong> app, which will open the details on the far right. The details include the description and scopes that were entered when the Service App was created.</li> <li>Slide the thumb button to enable <strong>Authorize</strong> then click <strong>Save</strong> at the bottom.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Step 3: Retrieve the Access and the Refresh Token</h6><p>After the admin authorizes the Service App registration, the test user can now retrieve the access tokens for the APIs. The tokens are used like a traditional integration and the same token expiration policies apply - 14 days for the access token and 90 days for the refresh token:</p> <ol> <li>Refresh the tab that displayed the <strong>Client ID</strong> and <strong>Client Secret</strong>.</li> <li>In the <strong>Org Authorizations</strong> section, select the name of your sandbox org from the dropdown menu.</li> <li>Paste in the <strong>Client Secret</strong> value from your notepad in the field below, then click <strong>Generate tokens</strong>.</li> <li>Copy &amp; paste the <code>refresh_token</code>and <code>access_token</code> values in your notepad for later use in the demo app. <em>Both values are only shown once.</em></li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Step 4: Install and Configure the Sample Python App</h6><p>Now that the access and refresh tokens are ready, we can download the sample app and using a code editor, insert the tokens into the Python code and configure the meeting. When complete, the app will automatically schedule a meeting for the next day with your test user host and no attendees:</p> <ol> <li>Download <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/archive/refs/heads/main.zip' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>simple_service_app</a> from GitHub and unzip the file to install it.</li> <li>Open a command line window and navigate to the <code>simple_service_app-main</code> directory that was just installed. Keep this window open.<ul> <li><code>cd simple_service_app-main</code></li> </ul> </li> <li>Now open the <code>serviceapp.py</code> file in an external code editor (such as VS Code):<ol> <li>Go to <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L25' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 25</a> of the code and replace the text with the <code>clientID</code> value from your notepad.</li> <li>On <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L26' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 26</a>, replace the text with the <code>secretID</code> value from your notepad.</li> <li>On <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L27' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 27</a>, replace the text with the <code>access_token</code> value from your notepad.</li> <li>On <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L28' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 28</a>, replace the text with the <code>refresh_token</code> value from your notepad.</li> <li>Scroll to <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L67' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 67</a>, after <code>&#39;title&#39;:</code> replace the text and give your meeting a unique name.</li> <li>On <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/simple_service_app/blob/main/serviceapp.py#L70' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>line 70</a>, after <code>&#39;hostEmail&#39;:</code> replace the text with the email address of a test account from your sandbox, which does not necessarily have to be the same account that created the Service App. This will tell the Service App to schedule the meeting with your test user as the host.</li> <li>Save the <code>serviceapp.py</code> file.</li> </ol> </li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Step 5: Run the Sample Service App</h6><p>With all the Service App components added to the Python code, the sample app is now ready to be initialized:</p> <ol> <li>Go back to the command line window in the <code>simple_service_app-main</code> directory.</li> <li>Install <a href='https://pypi.org/project/requests/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Requests</a> library for Python (if needed) with the following command, <code>pip install requests</code>.</li> <li>Launch the <code>serviceapp.py</code> file from that location with this command, <code>python3 serviceapp.py</code>.</li> </ol> <p>A successful launch will return a <code>statusCode 200</code> along with the newly created meeting details in JSON format:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">{&#39;id&#39;: &#39;7f36776aa9034d6091ef00dcee83ced2&#39;,&#39;meetingNumber&#39;: &#39;26607444195&#39;,&#39;title&#39;: &#39;My Service App Meeting,&#39;password&#39;:…,…} </code></pre> <h6>Step 6: Verify the Scheduled Meeting</h6><p>You can quickly confirm that the Service App scheduled the meeting for the test user with one more API call.</p> <ol> <li>Go back to the browser and login to developer.webex.com<em>as the test user that is the meeting host</em>.</li> <li>Navigate to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/list-meetings'>List Meetings API</a> reference page.</li> <li>Make an API call to list meetings for the test user by clicking the orange <strong>Run</strong> button (scroll down, along the right side).</li> </ol> <p>The response should return a <code>200/OK</code> and provide the meeting information that was scheduled by the Service App for the test user:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltaf4b32e2c666443d/service-apps-meeting-scheduler-blog-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>As this demo showed, Webex Service Apps can act as a Webex administrator to schedule meetings for users within an organization. There are countless ways automated meeting scheduling functionality can be incorporated into larger organizational applications, such as virtual training, remote consultations, and wellness programs. With Service Apps, they can safely run on a long-term basis independent of any individual users.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? No Problem!</h6><p>We are happy to provide you with support for any of the features in this article. If you need help or have any questions, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>. Until next time, happy developing!</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex Recordings Downloader Demo ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blted1b66d8b295ada5/67361e2d3c066b8222e9f75c/webex-recording-downloader-blog-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex Recordings Downloader Demo" /> <p>From time to time there may be a need to download all Webex Meetings recordings. For example, to host them on an internal resource or to free up space on your Webex service. This blog post will go over how to bulk download years&#39; worth of recordings locally using the Webex APIs and a Python application.</p> <p>The APIs that are used to accomplish this are <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/recordings/list-recordings-for-an-admin-or-compliance-officer'>List Recordings For an Admin or Compliance Officer</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/recordings/get-recording-details'>Get Recording Details</a>. The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/integrations-and-authorization#scopes'>scopes</a> required for these APIs are <code>meeting:admin_recordings_read</code> for an Admin or <code>spark-compliance:meetings_read</code> for a Compliance Officer.</p> <h6>How the Recordings Downloader Works</h6><p>The Python application will need to be run twice. The first run will collect all recording IDs and the associated host email for the recordings and store the info in a <code>.csv</code> file. The second run will read the <code>.csv</code> file, query each recording to get the download link and then download the recordings to a folder called <code>Downloaded-Recordings</code> within the project folder. The app is broken into three Python files. The <code>recording.py</code> file is the main controller file and is what you would run to start the app. The <code>list_recordings.py</code> file is run when you choose option 1 and has the logic to collect all recording data and save it to a <code>.csv</code> file. The <code>download_recordings.py</code> file has the logic that reads the recording data from the <code>.csv</code> file and downloads the recordings locally.</p> <p>On the first run you will be prompted to provide your access token. You can copy your personal access token from the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/getting-started'>Access the API</a> doc page on the developer portal after you&#39;ve logged in. The personal access token is meant for testing purposes and is only valid for 12 hours from the time that you login to the developer portal. This is what would be seen when running the app for the first time. Depending on how your Python installation is done you would either type <code>python recordings.py</code> or <code>python3 recording.py</code> to start the app.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6a75f95ceb4805a4/webex-recording-downloader-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>After entering the access token it is stored in the <code>token.json</code> file and will be read from there for future API requests being made.</p> <p>The code for this is:</p> <pre><code class="language-python">tokenPath = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) filename = os.path.join(tokenPath, &#39;token.json&#39;) with open (filename, &#39;r&#39;) as openfile: token = json.load(openfile) bearer = token[&quot;token&quot;] if bearer == &quot;&quot;: print(&quot;No stored token. \nEnter your access token.\n&quot;) token = input(&quot;&amp;gt; &quot;) while token == &quot;&quot;: print(&quot;No token entered. Try again.\n&quot;) token = input(&quot;&amp;gt; &quot;) bearer = {&quot;token&quot;:token} with open(&#39;token.json&#39;, &#39;w&#39;) as updateToken: json.dump(bearer, updateToken) else: print(&#39;Current Token: &#39;+str(bearer)) </code></pre> <p>Next the application will prompt to select options to either list recordings or download recordings. On the first run choose option 1 to collect recording data. There are also prompts to provide the meeting site URL and the number of weeks to pull for.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltdd344cfb0557be65/webex-recording-downloader-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>From here the <code>list_recordings.py</code> file is run. The API can return data for 30 days per request. The logic to handle this uses the <code>datetime</code> Python module to calculate 30 days before the current time and on each request, it will go back another 30 days until the number of weeks that were entered has been reached.</p> <p>Initial <code>to</code> and <code>from</code> times are set using the following:</p> <pre><code class="language-python"> to_time = datetime.datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0) from_time = to_time - datetime.timedelta(days=30) end_time = from_time - datetime.timedelta(weeks=int(weeks)) </code></pre> <p>After the request has completed then it will calculate new <code>to</code> and <code>from</code> times to make the next request with.</p> <pre><code class="language-bash"> else: to_time = from_time from_time = to_time - datetime.timedelta(days=30) </code></pre> <p>The <code>to</code> time is set to the previous <code>from</code> time and then a new <code>from</code> time is calculated going back 30 more days. After this completes the application will terminate. Run it again and this time select option 2 and it will begin downloading all recordings that were pulled in the previous step. The logic for this is to read each row of the <code>.csv</code> file to get the recording ID and the host email and use that to construct the URL to get the recording details. It then reads the <code>recordingDownloadLink</code> from the response, which is the link to download the recording. The recording is downloaded and saved locally. This loops until there are no more rows to pull from the <code>.csv</code> file.</p> <pre><code class="language-python"> recordingDownloadLink = None with open (&#39;recordings.csv&#39;, &#39;r&#39;) as csvfile: recs = csv.reader(csvfile) for row in recs: id = row[0] hostEmail = row[1].replace(&#39;@&#39;,&#39;%40&#39;).replace(&quot;+&quot;, &quot;%2B&quot;) print(&quot;RecordingId: &quot;+id+&quot;, HostEmail: &quot;+hostEmail) url = &#39;https://webexapis.com/v1/recordings/&#39;+id+&#39;?hostEmail=&#39;+hostEmail result = requests.get(url, headers=headers) downloadLink = json.loads(result.text) links = downloadLink[&#39;temporaryDirectDownloadLinks&#39;] recordingDownloadLink = links[&#39;recordingDownloadLink&#39;] print(&quot;Download Link: &quot;+recordingDownloadLink) if recordingDownloadLink != None: try: recording = requests.get(recordingDownloadLink) if recording.status_code == 200: fileName = recording.headers.get(&#39;Content-Disposition&#39;).split(&quot;&#39;&#39;&quot;)[1] print(&quot;Filename: &quot;+str(fileName)) with open(&quot;Downloaded-Recordings/&quot;+fileName, &#39;wb&#39;) as file: file.write(recording.content) print(fileName+&quot; saved!&quot;) elif recording.status_code == 429: retry_after = recording.headers.get(&quot;retry-after&quot;) or recording.headers.get(&quot;Retry-After&quot;) print(&quot;Rate limited. Waiting &quot;+str(retry_after)+&quot; seconds.&quot;) time.sleep(int(retry_after)) else: print(&quot;Unable to download, something went wrong!&quot;) print(&quot;Status Code: &quot;+str(recording.status_code)) except Exception as e: print(e) else: print(&quot;something went wrong.&quot;) </code></pre> <h6>Optional Step: Create an Integration</h6><p>You can also create an <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/integrations'>Integration</a> and use it to generate a longer life access token as well as a refresh token. The refresh token can be used to programmatically generate and store a new access token if the current one expires. This application is capable of handling token refreshes by adding the integration&#39;s <code>client_id</code>, <code>client_secret</code> and <code>refresh_token</code> to the .env file. If the current token stored in the <code>token.json</code> file has expired the application will use the details in the <code>.env</code> file to generate a new access token. The logic to generate a new access token is controlled by the HTTP status code that&#39;s returned. If the status code is a 401, which would mean the current access token is no longer valid, then the app will attempt to generate a new access token and store it.</p> <h6>Get the Code</h6><p>The full code for this demo application can be found at <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/WebexRecordingsDownloader' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/WebexSamples/WebexRecordingsDownloader</a>.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>This is provided as a demo with no warranty. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex Application Transfer Portal Usage Hands-on ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt3d5aa126e608a927/672ce7c3a26dfe264e1dacf5/application-transfer-portal-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex Application Transfer Portal Usage Hands-on" /> <p>You can transfer Webex applications like Integration, Service App, Embedded App, or Bots between users via the Application transfer portal at <a href='https://applications.webexbots.cloud/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://applications.webexbots.cloud/</a>, managed by the Webex Developer Support team. Only a full administrator of a Webex org can manage this tool, and transfers must stay within the same org.</p> <p>This blog post provides a comprehensive guide for administrators on how to transfer an application from one user to another and addresses some common questions about this tool.</p> <h6>Walkthrough of the Application Transfer Portal</h6><p>The application transfer portal mentioned above can be reached at <a href='https://applications.webexbots.cloud/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://applications.webexbots.cloud/</a>, and it is utilized to manage various types of apps available in Webex, such as Webex Integrations, Service Apps, Embedded Apps, and Webex Bots.</p> <p>A full administrator must sign in via the Webex page using the provided URL to access the app transfer portal. After authorization, a welcome message appears in the top-left panel, and the user is directed to the <strong>Org Application</strong> page listing available applications in their Webex org.</p> <p>The left-hand side panel of the portal lists three options as described below.</p> <h6>Org Application page</h6><p>This is also the portal&#39;s home page, listing all the applications of the organization. It shows active users, inactive users, and apps from past employees. Even orphaned apps can be transferred to an active user within the Webex organization.</p> <h6>My Application Page</h6><p>This lists all active applications owned by the current authorized administrator user in the portal.</p> <h6>Search Page</h6><p>The Search page lets you refine a Webex application using various options:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Created By (personEmail):</strong> This filter is applicable to all types of applications, including Webex Integration, Service App, Embedded App, and Webex Bot. To display an application, it is necessary to input the email address of its creator.</li> <li><strong>Created By (personId):</strong> Similar to <strong>Created By (personEmail)</strong>, but it requires the creator&#39;s person ID. This ID can be obtained using the Webex REST API&#39;s <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/people/list-people'>/list-people</a> endpoint.</li> <li><strong>ApplicationId:</strong> Use this identifier to locate a particular application by its unique ID, which can be accessed on the app details page in the Webex Developer portal.</li> <li><strong>Integration (clientId):</strong> This filter is specifically for Webex Integration. To use it, you need to supply the Integration Client ID from the Integration details page on the Webex Developer portal.</li> <li><strong>Bot (personId) and Bot Email:</strong> These filters apply solely to Bots. The Bot email corresponds to the Bot&#39;s username, and you can retrieve the Bot&#39;s person ID using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/people/list-people'>/list-people</a> API.</li> </ul> <p>These filters help you efficiently find and manage Webex applications.</p> <h6>How to Transfer an Application Through the Portal</h6><p>The Search page lets you locate and transfer specific Webex applications within the same Webex organization. You can also move apps from the <strong>Org Applications</strong> or <strong>My Applications</strong> pages by selecting their corresponding checkboxes.</p> <p>For large orgs with many active applications, the <strong>Seach</strong> page really simplifies finding the required app for transferring.</p> <p>To transfer the applications:</p> <ol> <li>Once the required apps are listed to be transferred on the <strong>Search</strong> page or in the other app details pages, select one or multiple apps using the corresponding checkbox.</li> <li>Click the highlighted <strong>Transfer App</strong> button on the top panel of the portal.</li> <li>Enter the <strong>New Owner</strong> email in the text box and select <strong>Execute Transfer</strong>. Please ensure the new owner&#39;s email belongs to the same org.</li> <li>After a successful transfer, an acknowledgment appears. From there, the administrator should ask the new app owner to check the <a data-type='internal' to='/my-apps'>/my-apps</a> page to confirm the transfer.</li> </ol> <p>By following these four straightforward steps, a full administrator can efficiently transfer any Webex application to a new user within their organization using this portal.</p> <h6>FAQs</h6><p><strong>Q.</strong> Can only a full administrator of a Webex org transfer an application successfully, or can other admin types like Device Admin, Site Admin, or Partner full administrator do it too?</p> <p><strong>A</strong>. No, only a full administrator of an org can access this portal and transfer the applications.</p> <p><strong>Q</strong>. Is it possible to transfer multiple apps at once through this portal?</p> <p><strong>A.</strong> Yes, this tool allows the transfer of multiple Webex apps. Simply check the boxes for the apps you want to transfer.</p> <p><strong>Q</strong>. Is it possible to transfer multiple apps to multiple users at once through this portal?</p> <p><strong>A</strong>. No, many-to-many operation currently not implemented in this portal but is planned for a future enhancement.</p> <p><strong>Q</strong>. How long should it take to get an app transferred to the new owner once the task is completed?</p> <p><strong>A</strong>. It should be an almost real-time update. The new application owner can check under their account on the Webex Developer portal&#39;s <a data-type='internal' to='/my-apps'>/my-apps</a> page.</p> <p><strong>Q</strong>. Is it possible to transfer an application to someone outside of the user&#39;s org?</p> <p><strong>A</strong>. No. A full administrator of the org can only transfer the apps to an internal user.</p> <p><strong>Q</strong>. Can an application be transferred if its owner has left the company?</p> <p><strong>A</strong>. Yes, such an application is referred to as an orphan application. If it remains active within the Webex organization, it can be successfully identified and transferred to another member of that organization.</p> <h6>Engage with us</h6><p>In case you have any further queries on this or if you are still facing some difficulties while trying to transfer an application to someone, please reach out to our Developer Support team following the instructions provided on our <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support</a> page.</p> <p>You can also join our <a href='https://community.cisco.com/t5/webex-for-developers/welcome-to-the-webex-for-developers-forum/m-p/4558386#M321' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developer Community</a> forum which has dedicated topics, discussion groups, and announcements. We encourage you to tell us about your experience using the Application transfer portal in our community forum.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Agents ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc3d816cf6b074549/672bc05a3d58d09cb27c641f/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Agents" /> <p>Welcome to the second installment of our blog series, “<a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis-address-book'>The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs</a>”. In this series we are covering the entirety of the RESTful APIs available for the Webex Contact Center, providing insights into their execution and impact from a user&#39;s perspective. In this edition we will be going over the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents'>Agents APIs</a>, Webhooks, and the use cases that drive their engagement by Webex Contact Center developers.</p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Agents</h6><p>An agent is a person who works in a contact center and serves as an interface between customers and businesses. Agents are the most frequent human contact a customer has with a business for solving problems, placing orders, or answering questions about related products and services. Agents can interact with customers using the Webex Contact Center via various channels like voice, instant messaging, Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, SMS, Email, and more.</p> <p>Agents utilize many tools while being effective at managing customer inquiries. These tools include CRM (Customer Relationship Management) software, help desk software, SMS management tools, telephones, soft phones, computers, wallboards, predictive dialers and customer satisfaction surveys. Though the Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop consolidates many of these tools into one place, developers are encouraged to use the available developer toolsets to enhance the agent experience.</p> <h6>The Agent Desktop</h6><p>The Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop is where agents receive and manage interactions with business customers. They can handle tasks like calls, chats, emails, and more all from one interface in the browser. Agents can access the Desktop and assist customers remotely if they have access to a browser and credentials for their Webex agent user account. They have access to many of the tools mentioned above in the form of custom widgets or out of the box set setup.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf8613a8e1ee71a38/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Custom Agent Desktop with Webex Contact Center RESTful APIs</h6><p>Third-party developers have been successful at using the available Webex Contact Center RESTful APIs to build custom desktop experiences and CTI (Computer Telephony Integration) connectors that work in a CRM or support tools. For example, <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/consilium-uniagent-for-zendesk-crm-consilium-software' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Consilium&#39;s UniAgent for Zendesk</a> solution allows Webex Contact Center Agents to use the Webex Contact Center agent desktop functionality with a custom version of the desktop embedded in Zendesk. This is done through a combination of a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/unlocking-the-power-of-custom-widgets-in-webex-contact-center'>custom headless widget</a> and Webex Contact Center <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/guides/integrations'>integration</a>.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt73551e3c59d2d7a6/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>A subset of the Agents APIs can be used to develop these kinds of integrations, and below we will be going over them and how to get started building custom solutions.</p> <h6>The Agents REST APIs</h6><p>Above, an agent is described as a person that works in a contact center. In the context of the APIs, the Agent resource encapsulates the entities that handles <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/tasks-call-control'>Tasks</a> through interactions with customers. Webex Contact Center Administrators and Supervisors can also carry the role of an Agent and trigger the Agents APIs. Agents can be humans or bots operating via the APIs.</p> <h6>Get Agent Activities</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-activities'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-activities</a></p> <p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-activities'>Get Agent Activities API</a> can be used to get all Agent activities created after a given timestamp epoch. The API returns JSON objects sorted by start time and can be filtered by agent id, team id, and channel type. This API can be used in a reporting tool or confirm findings in a reporting tool. It requires an administrators access token and the scope <code>cjp:config_read</code>.</p> <h6>Buddy Agent List</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/buddy-agents-list'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/buddy-agents-list</a></p> <p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/buddy-agents-list'>Buddy Agent List API</a> produces a list of agents in a given state and media according to an agent profile setting. In the agent desktop the agent can request a consult or transfer a customer to an available agent based on status. Developers can mimic that behavior using this API and allow agents to set values in a custom input for the media type (Telephony, chat, social, email) or state (Available, Idle) parameters in the API call&#39;s request body before producing a list of available agents to transfer or consult with.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte7d0a262a9d22539/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-4.jpeg" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Login</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/login'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/login</a></p> <p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/login'>Login API</a> is used to log an agent into the Webex cloud. The Login process makes an agent active and visible to administrators and supervisors who use tools like Analyzer and the Supervisor Desktop to monitor how many agents are online and available to assist customers. This process is not to be confused with the OAuth 2.0 flow that is required for users to authorize integrations in the previously mentioned custom desktop integrations.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt563596fca6e8ee5f/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte7c28a6c3aad1a2b/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>You can see from the above photo of the supervisor agent view (see the agent view below) that after the agent authenticates via Webex, they have included the role, dial number/extension, and team which map to parameters that are included in this APIs request body.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt424532011cbd0d66/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Logout</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/logout'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/logout</a></p> <p>Logout is the programmatic inverse of login. We are telling the Webex cloud that we are disconnecting and that as an agent, we are no longer available to assist customers. This option is also available when clicking on the icon in the top right corner of the cloud-based Webex Contact Center agent desktop application. The API does require a logout reason in the request body.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8a11674e17b29502/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Reload</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/reload'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/reload</a></p> <p>When developers are building custom desktops, we have to think about times where we lose network connectivity. This API helps agents re-establish the lost connection to the Webex Cloud session/agent desktop without having to go through the login process to establish a new connection.</p> <h6>State Change</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/state-change'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/state-change</a></p> <p>This API allows the user to toggle between states (Available, Idle). The request body requires a State (Available or Idle) which can be provided via an input from the user, and an Auxiliary Code which can be obtained by listing out the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/auxiliary-code/list-auxiliary-codes'>Auxiliary Codes</a> from the API.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbf20eff78c776a70/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis---agents-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Get Agent Statistics</h6><p><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-statistics'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-statistics</a></p> <p>This API is going to give stake holder several stats on agents in a given time period. Administrators and Supervisors are going to know answers to questions like how many customers an agent handled, how many customers were offered to an agent, how many of those customers were rejected by an agent, how many times did an agent transfer a customer, etc. This is a good API for reporting tools.</p> <h6>Webhooks</h6><p>The Agents API also has associated Webhook events. The events are triggered by Agent Login, Agent Logout, and Agent State Change. The Webhooks require <code>cjp:config, cjp:config_read</code>.</p> <h6>WebSocket Option</h6><p>Your application can receive notifications during operations like Agent Login, Agent Logout, and Agent State Change by registering a bi-directional WebSocket Connection with the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/notification/subscribe-notification'>Subscribe Notification API</a>. This API can be used with an integration that is scoped for <code>cjp:user</code>.</p> <p>This information is important in the context of this API. When developing a custom desktop, if a developer wants to include webhooks, the Agent State Change API, and necessary Auxiliary Codes API, they will need to include an onboarding step that allows an administrator with permissions to read configurations to authorize the application through the OAuth 2.0 flow for setup. Alternatively, the developer can use the Agent State Change API, or Webhooks, and set up a WebSocket connection with an Agent token. See this sample <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-agent-desktop-api-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>starter code</a> with values hard coded. Developers can choose the path forward given the above information.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>
