<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Enhance Mobile End User Experience with Seamless Meeting Movement and External Camera Support ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte5b0ffa3f915f58d/66c3584c45395d5a79bb68f1/mobile-sdk-312-1.jpeg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Enhance Mobile End User Experience with Seamless Meeting Movement and External Camera Support" /> <p>The Webex Mobile SDK is a powerful toolkit that allows developers to integrate Webex&#39;s robust video conferencing and collaboration capabilities into their own mobile applications for <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/ios'>iOS</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/android'>Android</a>. With the release of version 3.12, the SDK introduces two groundbreaking features that enhance user experience and productivity: seamless meeting movement and support for external cameras on iPadOS. In this blog, we will explore these new features and see how they can transform the way you connect and collaborate within your mobile apps.</p> <h6>Seamless Transition for Uninterrupted Productivity</h6><p>Imagine needing to switch from your desktop to your mobile device during an important virtual consultation or transferring a call to a more conducive device while using IoT technology in the field. With the latest iteration of the Webex Mobile SDK, these transitions are effortlessly smooth.</p> <p>This innovative feature allows users signed into the Webex mobile or desktop app to move their active meetings to a custom app integrated with the Webex Mobile SDK, or vice versa, with unmatched ease. The transition is invisible to other participants and maintains the fidelity of the meeting, ensuring that collaboration remains uninterrupted.</p> <h6>Empowering Experts on Demand</h6><p>In the realm of IoT, the &#39;<a href='https://blog.webex.com/video-conferencing/empowering-frontline-workers-with-webex-expert-on-demand' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Expert on Demand</a>&#39; (XoD) systems stand to gain significantly from this feature. Service technicians, healthcare professionals, or manufacturing experts can initiate a call on an IoT device and move it to a desktop or mobile for a more in-depth discussion, ensuring that expertise is always within reach.</p> <h6>Use Cases: Where Mobility Meets Innovation</h6><p>The applications for seamless meeting movement are vast and varied. Financial advisors, architects, educators, and executives can all benefit from the ability to switch devices seamlessly during critical engagements.</p> <h6>Watch Move Meeting in Action!</h6><p>Check out Move meeting in action in this video.</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/bd43edac-bc63-4814-b40f-eb4bc7ee2233" width="100%" height="100%" title="Move Meeting" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>External Camera Support on iPadOS</h6><p>With Apple&#39;s recent revelation, iPadOS now embraces external cameras, and the Webex Mobile SDK v3.12 is quick to capitalize on this enhancement. For iPads equipped with USB-C, this means a world of UVC (USB Video Class) compliant cameras is now at your disposal.</p> <h6>Imagine the Business Implications</h6><p>Real estate agents, event organizers, and remote educators can now leverage professional-grade camera setups for enhanced video quality in mobile Webex meetings. Document scanning also becomes more powerful with the flexibility of an external camera.</p> <h6>Technical Elegance Meets Practical Application</h6><p>The v3.12 SDK update empowers developers with a structured list of all available camera devices, built-in or external. When a UVC camera is connected, the <code>CameraDeviceManager</code>&#39;s callbacks notify your application in real-time.</p> <h6>Control at Your Fingertips</h6><p>The SDK&#39;s <code>Phone.updateSystemPreferredCamera</code> API allows users to manually select their camera source, enabling on-the-fly adjustments to suit the video call&#39;s needs.</p> <h6>Seamless Integration, Ready for Action</h6><p>To enjoy these capabilities, your iPad must be running iOS 17 or above. With the simple act of plugging in a USB camera, the Webex iOS SDK v3.12 triggers an automatic notification to your app, enabling an effortless switch between camera sources.</p> <h6>Watch External Camera Support in Action</h6><p>See the external camera support in action in our demo video.</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/6cdc9906-2693-4478-a99e-744446493fe3" width="100%" height="100%" title="External Camera Meeting" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <p>To check and try out code, please visit SDK documentation <a href='https://cisco.sharepoint.com/sites/DeveloperEvangelism/Docs/Blogs/Developer%20Portal%20Blogs/Draft/here' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>.</p> <h6>Explore the Webex Mobile SDK v3.12 Codebase</h6><p>For those eager to dive into the code and explore the capabilities, visit the GitHub repository at <a href='https://cisco.sharepoint.com/sites/DeveloperEvangelism/Docs/Blogs/Developer%20Portal%20Blogs/Draft/iOS' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>iOS</a> and <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk-example' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Android</a>.</p> <p>With these groundbreaking features, Webex Mobile SDK v3.12 is setting a new standard in virtual collaboration and video conferencing. Whether you&#39;re switching devices mid-meeting or leveraging high-definition external cameras on your iPad, the future of seamless, integrated communication is here. Dive into the code, explore the capabilities, and transform the way you connect and collaborate.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Rapidly Adapt Your CX Workflows With Webex Contact Center Flow Designer ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltbfd70d890e89fae6/66b24336bc06cc2e3e6bdc12/flowdesigner_evolvecx-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Rapidly Adapt Your CX Workflows With Webex Contact Center Flow Designer" /> <div><Callout type="info">This blog was co-authored by Naveen Kumar H N</Callout></div> <p>In today’s fast-paced technology landscape, customer experience (CX) is a key differentiator for enterprises. The ability to adapt and evolve CX workflows rapidly and seamlessly, introducing the most effective capabilities for customers, can make the difference between leading the market and lagging. Enterprises are eager to learn how to implement these changes to production workloads safely and effectively while adhering to controlled enterprise change management processes. Flows are like any software artifacts that need to go through a well-defined pipeline process involving planning, building, and testing.</p> <p>Over the last several quarters, the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer platform has introduced several features: Flow Versioning, Percentage Allocation of Flow Traffic, Subflows and Dynamic Variable Support - which empower developers and administrators to implement change management processes effortlessly. This blog explores the context of these capabilities, discusses use cases, and illustrates their impact on evolving your CX journey; Take advantage of the latest capabilities that Webex Contact Center has to offer.</p> <h6>Evolution of Change Management</h6><p>Historically, change management in CX workflows (previously known as contact center scripts) has been a delicate balancing act. The need to introduce new features and improvements had to be weighed against the risk of disrupting existing production workloads. Techniques like Blue-Green deployments and A/B testing revolutionized this process in broader disciplines like software development:</p> <ul> <li>“Blue-Green deployments” involve maintaining two environments (Blue and Green) to allow seamless transitions between versions.</li> <li>“A/B testing” enables comparison between different versions to determine the most effective approach.</li> </ul> <p>CX workflows should be no different. Webex Contact Center Flow Designer has integrated these methodologies into the platform, providing developers with the tools needed to manage changes with precision and confidence. These methods ensure that updates in your workflows can be rolled out gradually, maximizing value while minimizing risk and optimizing performance.</p> <p>Flow Versioning enables developers to confidently perform Blue/Green deployments using &quot;Dev,&quot; &quot;Test,&quot; or &quot;Live&quot; versions, ensuring seamless transitions and rollback to previous versions without downtime. Flow Percentage Allocations allows you to A/B test different experiences, feature sets, or a combination of the two. Combining these with subflows and dynamic variable support for activities, you can build a robust pipeline setup for your teams, to test multiple flavors of the flow without duplicating the overall experience.&#xa0;&#xa0; We will look at these features in detail.</p> <h6>Flow Versioning – Streamlining Development and Deployment</h6><p>Flow Versioning introduces the ability to apply version labels to a flow, offering unprecedented flexibility in developing, testing, and deploying new enhancements to your CX. This feature enables the creation of a formally defined, pipeline driven promotion process from development to production, facilitating Blue-Green deployments for CX flows.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt1ff8754b3268fc45/flowdesigner_evolvecx-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Flow Versioning allows switching environments on the Entry Point level</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2bc6ce268be9eea5/flowdesigner_evolvecx-3.gif" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Applying a Version Label to a Flow</em></p> <h6>Using Flow Versioning</h6><br/> <ol> <li><strong>“Dev” (Development)</strong>: Begin by creating and testing new flow enhancements by assigning the “Dev” Version Label to your flows. Attach the &#39;Dev&#39; version label of the Flow to a test Entry Point to ensure it does not impact production calls.</li> <li><strong>“Test” (Staging)</strong>: Once the flow is thoroughly tested, promote it to the “Test” environment by applying the “Test” version label while publishing the flow. This creates an additional copy of the flow for staging that allows for further validation without affecting live customer interactions.</li> <li><strong>“Live” (Production Deployment)</strong>: After successful testing, the flow can be promoted to the production environment by assigning the &#39;Live&#39; version label. This controlled rollout minimizes risks and ensures a seamless transition.</li> </ol> <p>The above versions can be assigned from the Entry Point for all contacts, to the Flow version label that is being used – allowing for maximum flexibility. Suppose you want to introduce an update to the Flow - change the flow and publish it again with the Dev tag, preventing any impacts to Live traffic. Go through the promotional process outlined above.</p> <p>Flow Versioning not only supports Blue-Green deployments but also creates a structured pipeline for continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), ensuring that new enhancements are delivered efficiently and reliably.</p> <p>For more information on Flow Versioning, see: <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide#flow-versioning' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Flow Versioning for Flow Designer</a></p> <h6>Percentage Allocation – Mastering Traffic Distribution &amp; A/B Testing</h6><p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta744fc8f5358f2fd/flowdesigner_evolvecx-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Percentage Allocation of traffic follows a Weighted Round Robin distribution</em></p> <p>The Percentage Allocation feature empowers developers to distribute call traffic across different branches within a flow. This capability is instrumental in implementing A/B testing methodologies, enabling a weighted allocation of traffic to various experiences – while providing valuable data for reporting and feedback loops.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt10352c956fdcf61e/flowdesigner_evolvecx-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>40-30-30% Traffic Split between DTMF, TTS and Bots (Virtual Agents)</em></p> <p>Developers can now allocate specific percentages of calls to different queues, or experiment between traditional IVR, Next-Generation Text-to-speech (TTS) or conversational virtual agents in the contact paths. This capability also allows trying out different post-call surveys, or Agent Screen pop applications to see what impact it has on Experience metrics for both callers and agents. Using this activity effectively allows for granular control and optimization of CX workflows over time, using feedback loops via reporting.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt2e13108af0462d91/flowdesigner_evolvecx-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>70-30% traffic split for Agent Screenpops (Old vs New Application experiences for agents)</em></p> <h6>Using Percentage Allocation</h6><p>In the example below, we are A/B testing two contact paths between a traditional menu and the all-new Cisco Virtual Agents available on Flow Designer.</p> <p>Global Variables assigned to the output of the nodes enables us to report directly on the contacts that traversed specific paths, helping us compare the business outcomes achieved, for example, the self-service duration, CSAT or NPS with the caller between the two or more experiences.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt11f1ad5e60b1cae5/flowdesigner_evolvecx-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Capturing custom data on chosen paths for reporting</em></p> <p><strong>Recommendations</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong>Define Allocation Percentages</strong>: Within the Flow Designer, specify the percentage of call traffic to be directed to each branch. For instance, allocate 50% to the existing flow and 50% to a new experimental flow.</li> <li><strong>Monitor and Analyze</strong>: Continuously monitor the performance of each branch to gather insights and compare results using Global Variables and an Analyzer Report to calculate the business impact. This data-driven approach facilitates informed decision-making. For more information on creating Analyzer Reports, see: <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/tajemk/Cisco-Webex-Contact-Center-Analyzer-User-Guide' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Create a Custom Visualization on Analyzer</a>.</li> <li><strong>Adjust Allocations</strong>: Based on the analysis, adjust the percentage allocations dynamically. For instance, increase the traffic to the better-performing branch and decrease or deactivate the other.</li> </ol> <p>Percentage Allocation allows for precise control over CX workflows, enabling enterprises to test new features and improvements on a small scale before a full rollout, thereby reducing risk and enhancing overall performance.</p> <p>For more information on Percentage Allocation see: <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide#task-template_2da0579d-5c10-4021-8b5d-61e8220bf5da' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Percentage Allocation for Flow Designer</a>.</p> <h6>Subflows – Enhancing Modularity and Reuse</h6><p>Subflows introduce a modular approach to building and managing complex CX workflows – especially when packaging a new capability and wanting to reuse it across your flows.</p> <p>Developers can create independent logical functionalities as Subflows and reuse them across multiple main flows. This modularity simplifies the development process, enhances collaboration among teams, and ensures consistency across the organization.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt05fbbd0a2a5b1431/flowdesigner_evolvecx-8.gif" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Subflows are activities on the Flow Canvas</em></p> <p>A good example of this is a new Subflow pointing to a new HTTP(S) endpoint, or a subflow using the new Virtual Agent activity – allowing to test new &gt;API services or new AI agents in the contact path, respectively.</p> <h6>Best Practices for Subflows</h6><br/> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt11dea84ff6870133/flowdesigner_evolvecx-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Common Subflows in use – BusinessHours, QueueTreatment, CollectCallerInfo, etc.</em></p> <ol> <li><strong>Create Independent Functionalities</strong>: Develop subflows for specific tasks or functionalities that can operate independently within the main CX flow. Some examples include: Business Hour checks, Common Queue treatments and common API calls (HTTPS) to external services.</li> <li><strong>Reuse Across Main Flows</strong>: Integrate these subflows as new activities into various main flows as needed, ensuring that common functionalities are consistent and easily manageable.</li> <li><strong>Collaborate Effectively</strong>: Different teams can work on various subflows simultaneously, streamlining the development process and fostering collaboration. Develop them independently in parallel – integrate them in one main flow.</li> </ol> <p>Subflows allow developers to break down complex flows into manageable parts, promoting modularity and reusability – and most importantly saves time through increased efficiencies.</p> <p>The setting “Propagate changes to all flows” allows for easy cascading of changes to all parent flows. Disabling this setting when making a subflow change ensures that a change in one subflow does not disrupt all the flows consuming it.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta3432e98fc280768/flowdesigner_evolvecx-10.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Choosing to pull the latest updates from Subflows as a Setting.</em></p> <p>For more information on Subflows see: <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide#concept-template_2812e465-bde2-4bf8-b133-b64bbddff95b' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Subflows for Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</a>.</p> <h6>Dynamic Variable Support – Enabling Adaptive Flows</h6><p>Dynamic Variable support allows developers to specify the behavior of activities within a flow through variables. This enhancement enables the creation of highly adaptable and reusable flows. By defining activities via dynamic variables, developers can tailor flows to different business verticals, and change their behavior dynamically for different environments (Dev, Test, Live), altering their functionality based on data injected into the flow at runtime.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9fb3ed33bdac7762/flowdesigner_evolvecx-11.gif" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Using Dynamic Variables in activities such as Business Hours, GoTo Flows, GoTo Entry Points</em></p> <h6>Implementing Dynamic Variables</h6><br/> <ol> <li><strong>Define Variables</strong>: Create dynamic variables to control various aspects of the flow’s behavior.</li> <li><strong>Apply Variables in Activities</strong>: Use these variables within activities to modify their functionality based on the current environment or real-time data.</li> <li><strong>Adapt Flows Dynamically</strong>: Adjust the values of these variables as needed to adapt the flow to different conditions or requirements.</li> </ol> <p>Dynamic Variable support enhances the flexibility and adaptability of CX workflows, allowing developers to create flows that can evolve and respond to changing circumstances without the need for extensive rewrites. It also minimizes the overall number of flows or subflows created, significantly easing the manageability of flows.</p> <p>For more information on using Dynamic variables in Flow activities, see: <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide#Cisco_Concept.dita_5ba6029e-c256-4c16-8fbf-40f8370bd968' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Dynamic Variable support in Flow Designer Activities</a>.</p> <h6>Comprehensive Use Case: Implementing New AI-powered Virtual Agents</h6><p>Let us consider a comprehensive use case where an enterprise implements a new AI-powered Cisco virtual agent to improve its customer support experience.</p> <h6>Step 1: Developing the Virtual Agent</h6><p>Using Flow Versioning, the development team creates a new flow for the virtual agent in the “Dev” environment. They label this version as “Dev” and conduct extensive testing to ensure that the virtual agent can handle various customer queries effectively.</p> <h6>Step 2: Testing in a Controlled Environment</h6><p>Once the virtual agent flow is stable, it is promoted to the Test environment and labeled &#39;Test.&#39; Here, a subset of real customer interactions is routed to the virtual agent using the Percentage Allocation feature. By allocating a small percentage of calls to this flow, the team can gather valuable performance data and customer feedback without impacting live interactions.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte9ff554e9fe45f40/flowdesigner_evolvecx-12.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Sending 40% of the traffic to a new AI bot (Virtual Agent) and 60% to traditional IVR.</em></p> <h6>Step 3: Analyzing Results and Adjusting</h6><p>The team monitors the virtual agent’s performance in the Test environment, using data to refine and improve the flow. Adjustments are made dynamically using the Dynamic Variable support, allowing for real-time tweaks based on customer interactions and feedback. The output variables in the activity allow for reporting on these values in Global Variables. Global Variables are reportable on Analyzer as a part of all historical and real-time reports (these custom fields are automatically available as a part of the Contact Session records captured by the Webex Contact Center data platform).</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta34ed939e49fdff9/flowdesigner_evolvecx-13.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><em>Activity Output variables allow reporting on the percentage and description per call.</em></p> <h6>Step 4: Rolling Out to Production</h6><p>Satisfied with the virtual agent’s performance, the team promotes the flow to the Live environment and labels it &#39;Live.&#39; The Percentage Allocation feature is then used to gradually increase the traffic directed to the virtual agent, starting with a small percentage, and scaling up as confidence in the flow’s performance grows.</p> <h6>Step 5: Continuous Improvement</h6><p>With the virtual agent now live, the team continues to monitor its performance and gather feedback. Subflows are used to modularize specific functionalities, making it easy to update and improve individual components of the virtual agent without disrupting the entire workflow.</p> <h6>Advantage: Adapt and Futureproof</h6><p>By leveraging Flow Versioning, Percentage Allocation, Subflows, and Dynamic Variable support, enterprises can achieve true enterprise-grade change management for their CX workflows while remaining future proof, continuously adapting their CX to the needs of the hour. These features enable:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Controlled Rollouts</strong>: Minimize risks by testing changes in smaller batches before full-scale deployment.</li> <li><strong>Continuous Adaptation</strong>: Continuously evolve CX workflows with data-driven insights from A/B testing.</li> <li><strong>Enhanced Collaboration</strong>: Improve collaboration among teams through modular subflows.</li> <li><strong>Future-Proofing</strong>: Introduce AI capabilities and other innovations in a controlled manner, ensuring readiness for future advancements.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>Webex Contact Center Flow Designer’s new features—Flow Versioning, Percentage Allocation, Subflows, and Dynamic Variable support—represent a significant leap forward in CX change management. By adopting these capabilities, developers can implement changes with confidence, ensuring a seamless and optimized customer experience. These features provide the flexibility to test and refine new enhancements, control rollouts through precise traffic distribution, and build modular, adaptable workflows that can evolve with changing business needs.</p> <p>With Flow Designer, enterprises can continuously adapt their CX workflows, integrate cutting-edge AI capabilities, and future-proof their customer interactions. Embrace these features today to transform your CX strategy, stay ahead of the competition, and deliver exceptional experiences that meet the ever-evolving expectations of your customers. Your journey towards a more agile, responsive, and customer-centric future begins here with Webex Contact Center Flow Designer.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We’ve Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Build your first Webex Connect Flow: A Step-by-Step Guide ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5e995b513db2df4c/66a3c1ab379d6375ac1b6e0f/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-2.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Build your first Webex Connect Flow: A Step-by-Step Guide" /> <p>Webex Connect is a powerful Communications Platform as a Service (CPaaS) built to enable enterprises to automate digital interactions at scale. Developers can integrate channels such as SMS and WhatsApp, technologies such as AI and payments, and systems into applications.</p> <p>In addition to its powerful API capabilities, Webex Connect helps developers to work quicker and smarter through the Flow Builder, which is used to build, configure, deploy, and iterate workflows that automate communication processes across the customer journey. By embracing the Flow Builder, developers can expedite the creation of communication-powered solutions for the business units they serve.</p> <p>This blog will walk you through creating, configuring, testing, and troubleshooting your first Webex Connect flow using the Flow Builder.</p> <p>Before we dive in, ensure you have the following:</p> <ul> <li>A Webex Connect account - you can create a Webex Connect Developer Sandbox account via the <a href='https://cpaas.webex.com/products/webex-connect/developer-hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex CPaaS Developer Hub</a>.</li> <li>An HTML5 capable web browser such as Firefox, Chrome, Safari, or Edge.</li> <li>Postman, an HTTP/REST API test client, for API interaction.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>What We’ll Build</h6><p>Our objective is to create a flow that notifies a patient of their appointment and allows them to respond via SMS. To do this, first, we need to access the Webex Connect Flow Builder.</p> <h6>Get started with the Flow Builder</h6><br/> <h6>Navigate to the Service Dashboard</h6><p>At the highest level, Webex Connect lets you organize flows by projects called Services. Typically, these would be created for each of your application customer interactions and journeys.</p> <p>For now, let&#39;s just access the auto-created default service:</p> <ol> <li>From the left-side navigation bar, click on the Services icon: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltef57be2b63b3a062/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>Choose the default &quot;My First Service&quot; This should take you to the service Dashboard, which provides an overview of your service&#39;s activity and configuration, including analytics on recent traffic activity, access to the REST API docs/tools, and the Flow Builder itself. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt40b917fe1b9508d5/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <h6>Start Building a Flow</h6><br/> <ol> <li><p>Select the <strong>Flows</strong> tab, then go ahead and click <strong>Create flow</strong>. Give the flow a name. For this lab, let&#39;s create our flow using the &quot;Appointment&quot; template: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9784b622eef15330/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> This will open up the Flow Builder, which will automatically open the <strong>Configure Webhook</strong> property page.</p> </li> <li><p>Our flow will be triggered by an incoming <a href='https://developers.imiconnect.io/reference/custom-event-v2' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>webhook</a> - i.e., an <code>HTTP POST</code> with some JSON-formatted initial data. You can view your flow&#39;s auto-generated webhook URL here: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt76a99659dde0d40a/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> Webhooks are a very common way for applications to send events and data to each other; for example, a health clinic&#39;s patient system could send a batch of webhooks to this flow each day based on a query of all patients booked for appointments the next day. Go ahead and give your webhook a name - can be anything, perhaps &quot;Appointment Webhook&quot;</p> </li> <li><p>The trigger webhook will need to deliver actionable data from an application to the flow, such as the recipients information. Define the expected JSON contents (just the keys) by pasting this sample webhook payload into the <strong>PROVIDE SAMPLE INPUT</strong> area:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;Phone&quot;: &quot;&quot;, &quot;Name&quot;: &quot;&quot;, &quot;Appt&quot;: &quot;&quot; } </code></pre> </li> <li><p>Click <strong>PARSE</strong>. If the data is parsed correctly, it should look like this: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7c0f0f60f2f268ee/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> <li><p>That&#39;s all the trigger configuration needed for now. Go ahead and click <strong>Save</strong>, which should bring you to the Flow Builder main screen.</p> </li> </ol> <p>You can see that a fairly complete flow has been automatically created, including event, data and logic nodes and logical interconnections needed to orchestrate them. The gist of what this flow does and how it works can be gleaned with just a quick inspection.</p> <p>Feel free to play around in the Flow Builder for a bit: check out the <strong>Utilities</strong>/<strong>Channels</strong>/<strong>Integrations</strong> tabs, try out the bottom toolbar options, peek into some of the nodes (double-click), etc.</p> <p>Note: If you make a change (e.g., dragging-dropping a new node onto the canvas) and can&#39;t manage to undo it (i.e., with Ctrl+Z), you can always delete the flow and recreate it from the template.</p> <h6>Send the Initial SMS</h6><p>We&#39;ve already configured the flow&#39;s triggering webhook (we&#39;ll learn how to test it a bit later), the next step in the sequence will be to send the initial notification SMS to the patient based on the webhook&#39;s data variables:</p> <ol> <li>Double-click on the <strong>Send SMS</strong> node to open it and view the configuration page.</li> <li>Delete the place-holder contents of the <strong>Destination</strong> field. Replace it by opening the <em>Start</em> collection on the right side and clicking <strong>inboundWebhook.Phone</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7de762413b6e617b/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>In the <strong>FROM NUMBER</strong> field, select the (default, only) Sender ID: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7d2e3533afc87b3e/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> This is a phone number associated with your Webex Connect Service - i.e., the &#39;Caller ID&#39; the patient will see for the SMS.</li> <li>In the <strong>MESSAGE</strong> field, delete <code>$(name)</code> and <code>$(dateTime)</code> from the message text, and replace with <code>inboundWebhook.Name</code> and <code>inboundWebhook.Appt</code>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt75aaf4b1b69811fa/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-10.gif" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> <li>You can now <strong>Save</strong> the configuration.</li> </ol> <h6>Receive the Patient Response</h6><p>Once the initial reminder SMS has been sent to the patient, the flow will need to await the patient&#39;s response (if any!):</p> <ol> <li>Open the <strong>Receive</strong> node configuration.</li> <li>In the <strong>Receive SMS</strong> section, select the inbound <strong>NUMBER</strong> where we are expecting the patient&#39;s response to arrive (this would be the same number the initial SMS was sent from).</li> <li>Choose ***** for the <strong>KEYWORD</strong>.</li> <li>Replace the <strong>FROM NUMBER</strong> with <strong>inboundWebhook.Phone</strong> (under the <em>Start</em> variables), i.e., the patient&#39;s phone number. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt82ffdb5456243b95/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-11.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <div><Callout type="info">The **MAXTIMEOUT** value of **600** means that the flow will wait a maximum of 600 seconds (10 minutes) for the patient's reply.</Callout></div></li> <li>Go ahead and <em>Save</em>.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Check the Response</h6><p>Sending the initial response will have a number of results:</p> <ul> <li>The user replies with &#39;A&#39; to keep the appointment.</li> <li>The user replies with &#39;B&#39; to cancel the appointment.</li> <li>The user replies with something unexpected.</li> <li>The user never replies.</li> </ul> <p>The <em>Branch</em> node can make <em>if/then/else</em> decisions about which branch of the flow to follow next:</p> <ol> <li>Open the &quot;Check User Response&quot; branch node config.</li> <li>We don&#39;t actually need to configure anything here (the template provided the current values), but by inspecting the <em>Confirm</em> and <em>Cancel</em> conditions, we can see that the node is checking if the received message content output variable from the previous receive node <code>($(n11.receive.message))</code> &quot;Equals&quot; <strong>A</strong> or <strong>B</strong>. <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt3a2661c8e7ffce01/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-12.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <p>A default &quot;None of the Above&quot; condition is also there too.</p> <h6>Report on Progress</h6><p>As this flow could actually take a number of minutes to reach its final end point, it might be nice if we could monitor its progress.</p> <p>This is possible by using the <em>HTTP</em> node type to send an <em>outbound</em> message to an external service – here’s a handy, free hook bin service: <a href='https://webhook.site/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webhook.site</a></p> <p>In a real flow, the external service would be a reporting, analytics or dashboard application that would receive the notification + data, then update its state tracking on the appointment notification request. However, for our purposes, we&#39;ll just use the hook bin to accept the message so we can inspect the HTTP/JSON contents of the outbound webhook:</p> <ol> <li><p>Open a new browser tab and navigate to: <a href='https://webhook.site/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webhook.site</a>. (Feel free to use another hook/request bin.) It should display an auto-generated unique URL where webhooks can be directed: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf62b010371d072c2/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-13.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> Copy this to your clipboard, and/or keep this tab open. <strong>Important</strong>: You must also select the option to enable <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>CORS</a>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc2332bdf4cdc9d05/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-14.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> <li><p>In the Flow Builder, open the top-most <strong>HTTP</strong> node (the one on the &quot;Confirm&quot; branch.)</p> </li> <li><p>Change the <strong>METHOD</strong> to <strong>POST</strong>.</p> </li> <li><p>Paste your hook bin&#39;s unique URL into the <strong>ENDPOINT URL</strong> field.</p> </li> <li><p>For the <strong>BODY</strong> we&#39;ll just relay all the data from the original triggering webhook, <em>PLUS</em> a <em>Status</em>: Confirmed field indicating how the interaction with the patient is proceeding:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;Phone&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Phone)&quot;, &quot;Name&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Name)&quot;, &quot;Appt&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Appt)&quot;, &quot;Status&quot;: &quot;Confirmed&quot; } </code></pre> <div><Callout type="info">We're getting the run-time data values from the **Start** variables list on the right-hand side.</Callout></div></li> <li><p>Open the <em>Node Outcomes</em> group in the lower right: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt11e0a4a9123e6b8a/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-15.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> Notice that an <em>HTTP</em> node type has two defined outcomes: <code>onerror</code> and <code>oncomplete</code>. This results in corresponding branches in the Flow Builder that will need to be handled (already in place from the template): <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd9fe7df88d030fe2/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-16.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> <li><p>Go ahead and <strong>Save</strong> this node.</p> </li> <li><p>Repeat the steps above for the <em>HTTP</em> node on the <em>Cancel</em> branch, but this time sending <code>Status: Cancelled</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;Phone&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Phone)&quot;, &quot;Name&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Name)&quot;, &quot;Appt&quot;: &quot;$(n2.inboundWebhook.Appt)&quot;, &quot;Status&quot;: &quot;Cancelled&quot; } </code></pre> </li> </ol> <h6>Final Configurations</h6><p>The five remaining nodes that we haven&#39;t configured yet are all SMS nodes:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7f997c317bb551f0/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-17.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Configure all of these with the same <strong>DESTINATION</strong> and <strong>FROM NUMBER</strong> values as the initial SMS node:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt3e75fe7fa2ac9e26/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-18.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Publish Live</h6><p>The flow is complete and should now be ready to publish!</p> <ol> <li><p>Since we&#39;re in dev/test mode, click on the <em>Settings</em> gear icon in the upper right. Under <strong>General / Advanced</strong> settings, enable <em>Descriptive logs</em>. This will give us detailed information about the inputs, outputs and any errors for each flow node, which will help greatly with any needed troubleshooting!</p> <div><Callout type="info">Once your flow is complete, tested and stable you will likely want to disable *Descriptive logs* to avoid having any sensitive enterprise or customer data written to the logs.</Callout></div></li> <li><p>From the Flow Builder overview, click on <strong>Save</strong> in the top-right corner: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5bdd8cb57085568f/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-19.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> During the save process, the system checks that the flow is valid and correctly configured. If there is a problem, you may see an error/warning message in the top-right: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt584cbd83c3366a81/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-20.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> Clicking on the error will select the offending node, allowing you to correct its configuration and re-save.</p> </li> <li><p>Finally, click <strong>Make Live</strong>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt0ebd9630fc1b0ff3/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-21.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> Entering a comment is optional, but can be useful - e.g., for versioning.</p> </li> </ol> <h6>Test the Flow</h6><p>With the flow live and ready to interact with enterprise systems and patients/customers, it&#39;s time to give it a test run!</p> <p>If you recall, the first thing we did after creating the flow was to configure the triggering <em>inbound</em> Webhook:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd4650f6bffe16a89/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-22.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Since we don&#39;t have an actual enterprise back-end system programmed to send a real webhook, we need a way to send the webhook message ourselves, for this we will use <a href='https://www.postman.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Postman</a>.</p> <div><Callout type="info">You can also use [Curl](https://curl.se/) from the terminal, or almost any other HTTP tool to make the webhook *HTTP POST.*</Callout></div> <p>Let&#39;s configure and send the <em>HTTP POST</em> request needed to trigger our flow:</p> <ol> <li><p>Open Postman, and click the &quot;+&quot; button to create a new request.</p> </li> <li><p>Select <strong>POST</strong> from the method dropdown.</p> </li> <li><p>In the URL field, paste in your triggering webook&#39;s URL. You can retrieve this by going back to the Flow Builder by double-clicking the trigger <strong>Webhooknode</strong> and grabbing the <em>WEBHOOK URL</em>: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt76a99659dde0d40a/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> <li><p>Select the <strong>Body</strong> tab. Choose <strong>raw</strong> type, and then <strong>JSON</strong> format from the dropdown.</p> </li> <li><p>For the request body itself, copy the sample input <em>JSON BODY</em> from your trigger <em>Webhook</em> node and paste, inserting some test data (you can use your mobile number for <em>Phone</em>, being sure to include the country code but not a &quot;+&quot;, e.g &quot;1&quot; for the US or 44 for the UK):</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;Phone&quot;: &quot;14055551212&quot;, &quot;Name&quot;: &quot;Jane Doe&quot;, &quot;Appt&quot;: &quot;March 4, 2022&quot; } </code></pre> <p> The final request should look like this: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltcdf7e5f4da8f316f/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-23.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> <li><p>Now you can click Send to fire off the webhook.</p> </li> </ol> <h6>Verifying and Troubleshooting</h6><p>If all went well, a number of things should happen:</p> <ol> <li>You should receive an appointment reminder SMS on your mobile phone.</li> <li>Replying with &quot;A&quot; or &quot;B&quot; should result in the appropriate acknowledgement SMS message.</li> <li>After the patient reply step, checking your hook bin web page you should see an <em>HTTP POST</em> message has arrived, containing the JSON &quot;progress&quot; message configured in the flow&#39;s <em>HTTP</em> node.</li> <li>If after sending the webhook something unexpected happens (including nothing!), you can click on the <em>Debug</em> &quot;bug&quot; icon to examine the logs and drill into specific node operations for errors and clues: <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4afba31c5bbcecb2/webex-connect---how-to-build-your-first-flow-24.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></li> </ol> <h6>Congratulations and Next Steps!</h6><p>Congratulations on completing your first Webex Connect flow!</p> <p>Hopefully this walkthrough has showcased how the Flow Builder enables enterprise developers to work in a more efficient way to accelerate IT roadmaps and better meet the needs of their organizations.</p> <p>This is just the beginning—continue exploring additional templates, channels, nodes, use cases, and API capabilities. Consider requesting full access to unlock more enterprise features and even book a demo to deepen your understanding of Webex Connect.</p> <p>In this blog, we not only introduced you to the basics of Webex Connect but also equipped you with the knowledge to build more complex flows and integrations.</p> <p>For more Developer Resources, you can visit the <a href='https://cpaas.webex.com/products/webex-connect/developer-hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex CPaaS Developer Hub</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Leveraging the Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop SDK in Your Custom Widgets ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltae2f4decac7fd10f/66a27b1ce91a1715b2159551/agent-desktop-sdk-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Leveraging the Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop SDK in Your Custom Widgets" /> <p>Welcome back to our series on enhancing the Webex Contact Center experience through custom widgets! In our previous posts, we&#39;ve <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/unlocking-the-power-of-custom-widgets-in-webex-contact-center'>explored the power of custom widgets</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/developing-with-webex-contact-center-header-widgets-an-rss-feed-reader-example'>developed header widgets with an RSS feed reader</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/enhancing-agent-productivity-by-creating-navigation-widgets-in-webex-contact-center'>created navigation widgets to boost agent and supervisor productivity</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-contact-center-widget-bundling-with-webpack'>bundled our widgets with Webpack</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/enhancing-webex-contact-center-widgets-with-dynamic-store-variables'>enhanced widgets with dynamic $STORE variables</a>. Today, we&#39;re diving into the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/desktop#javascript-sdk-and-modules'>Webex Contact Center Desktop SDK</a>, a powerful tool that allows you to request up-to-date information from the Desktop and integrate it seamlessly into your custom widgets.</p> <h6>Introduction to the Webex Contact Center Desktop SDK</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/desktop#javascript-sdk-and-modules'>Desktop JavaScript SDK</a> is an <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wxcc-desktop/sdk?activeTab=readme' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>npm package</a> that provides a robust interface for interacting with the Webex Contact Center Desktop. With this SDK, you can request essential data such as agent details, assigned tasks, task specifics, browser locale, and authentication tokens for Single Sign-On (SSO) integration. This capability opens a world of possibilities for creating more dynamic and responsive embedded widgets.</p> <h6>Key Features of the JS SDK</h6><ul> <li><strong>Native Integration into the Desktop</strong>: Integrated seamlessly when invoked by widgets that are rendered within the Desktop application.</li> <li><strong>Data Requests</strong>: Fetch data to be passed to your widgets through properties and attributes.</li> <li><strong>Complex Operations</strong>: Perform advanced operations by consuming and manipulating system data within your widget.</li> <li><strong>Asynchronous Event Subscription</strong>: Subscribe to asynchronous events and access data within the payload.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Getting Started with the SDK</h6><p>To get started, you&#39;ll need to install the SDK package from npm:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm install @wxcc-desktop/sdk </code></pre> <p>Once installed, you can import the SDK into your project:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">import { Desktop } from &#39;@wxcc-desktop/sdk&#39;; </code></pre> <p>Next, let’s take a look at some code from our sample application.</p> <h6>Sample Application</h6><p>The sample application provided in the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/tree/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Contact Center API Samples repository</a> demonstrates how to integrate and utilize the Webex Contact Center Desktop JavaScript SDK within a custom widget. This application showcases various functionalities such as initializing the SDK, fetching agent information, handling agent states, making outbound calls, updating CAD (Call Associated Data) variables, and managing interactions through events like transfers and recording pauses. The sample app is designed to help developers understand how to leverage the SDK to build robust and interactive contact center solutions, providing a comprehensive example of real-time agent interaction management and customization within a web-based interface.</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/e98497f6-8740-4323-8805-e988af3662a3" width="100%" height="100%" title="Desktop JS SDK Sample Widget" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>Sample Application Code Tour</h6><p>Now, let’s take a short tour through our sample application and highlight some of the features of the SDK the application is utilizing. The source code lives in the “<a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>src/sa-ds-sdk.js</a>” file.</p> <h6>Importing the Library: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L1' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 1</a></h6><p>Initializes the SDK for use within the widget.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">import { Desktop } from &#39;@wxcc-desktop/sdk&#39;; </code></pre> <h6>Initialization and Setup: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L294' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 294</a></h6><p>Initializes the SDK for use within the widget.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">Desktop.config.init(); </code></pre> <h6>Fetching Agent Information: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L366' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 366</a></h6><p>Retrieves the latest data about the current agent and logs it.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">const latestData = Desktop.agentStateInfo.latestData; </code></pre> <h6>Retrieving Task Information: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L373' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 373</a></h6><p>Fetches the interaction ID and other task-related information from the current task map.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">const currentTaskMap = await Desktop.actions.getTaskMap(); </code></pre> <h6>Initiating a Transfer: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L393-L404' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 393-404</a></h6><p>Initiates a transfer to a specified virtual team (vteam) using the interaction ID.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">await Desktop.agentContact.vteamTransfer </code></pre> <h6>Pausing Recording: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L409' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 409</a></h6><p>Pauses the recording for a given interaction using the interaction ID.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">await Desktop.agentContact.pauseRecording </code></pre> <h6>Making an OutDial Call: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L420-L439' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 420-439</a></h6><p>Initiates an outbound call to a specified destination using the provided entry point ID.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">await Desktop.dialer.startOutdial </code></pre> <h6>Updating CAD Variables: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L443-L461' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 443-461</a></h6><p>Updates the CAD (Call Associated Data) variables for a given interaction.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">await Desktop.dialer.updateCadVariables </code></pre> <h6>Changing Agent State: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L464-L486' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 464-486</a></h6><p>Changes the agent&#39;s state to either &#39;Available&#39; or &#39;Idle&#39; and updates the UI accordingly.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">await Desktop.agentStateInfo.stateChange </code></pre> <h6>Subscribing to Agent Contact Events: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/widget-samples/desktop-js-sdk-sample/src/sa-ds-sdk.js#L489-L508' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Line 489-508</a></h6><p>Subscribes to various agent contact <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/desktop#asynchronous-events'>events</a> to handle actions like wrap-up, hold, and unhold.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">Desktop.agentContact.addEventListener </code></pre> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>The Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop SDK is a powerful tool that enables developers to create more dynamic, responsive, and context-aware widgets. By leveraging methods to fetch access tokens and agent information, and subscribing to asynchronous events, you can significantly enhance the functionality and user experience of your custom widgets</p> <p>Stay tuned for more insights and examples in our ongoing series on developing with Webex Contact Center. As always, we encourage you to explore the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/desktop#javascript-sdk-and-modules'>SDK documentation</a>!</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – July 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt21d3ca7f3f79e9ee/66a3c630b286e58a34216312/july-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – July 2024" /> <p>Hello again, Webex Developers! We do have some interesting things to share with you this month, for both Webex and Webex Contact Center. So, relax, grab your favorite beverage, and enjoy the latest developer news for July.</p> <h6>📇The A-Z of Contact Center APIs: Address Book</h6><p>The developer content for Webex Contact Center keeps rolling in! For the <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/the-a-z-of-webex-contact-center-apis-address-book'>first blog post</a> of the <em>A-Z series of Webex Contact Center APIs</em>, Developer Evangelist, Joe Zanini, focuses on the Address Book APIs. In this article, Joe goes over what the Address Book is from a user perspective, along with exploring the APIs and potential integration use cases for developers.</p> <h6>🪪Runtime Agnostic Webex OAuth for JavaScript Projects with Auth.js</h6><p>In <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/runtime-agnostic-webex-oauth-for-javascript-projects-with-auth-js'>another helpful blog post</a> about getting things done easier, Ashesh Singh from the Webex Solutions Developer Team shows us how to simplify user authentication in our JavaScript applications using the new Webex OAuth provider with Auth.js. Learn how this versatile open-source authentication solution can be a great choice for JavaScript apps requiring OAuth functionality.</p> <h6>📺Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p><em>Attention Webex Calling developers!</em> In our most recent webinar in July, <strong>Creating Enhanced Workflows with the Webex Calling APIs,</strong> we presented a comprehensive overview of the entire Calling platform: APIs, use cases, and App Hub success stories. The session showcased the full developer landscape that are represented in the three pillars of Webex Calling APIs – Provisioning, Call Control, and Call Reporting - and the business value for building integrations. Check out our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a> to watch the recording of the Calling API session. You can also find all our previous webinars or register for upcoming live sessions there.</p> <h6>📱New Developer Vidcasts: Webex Mobile SDK</h6><p>The Webex Mobile SDK had some great features added in the latest update. Engineers from the Mobile SDK team recently recorded two informative Vidcasts on the new functionality that was recently released:</p> <ul> <li>Watch: <a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/6cdc9906-2693-4478-a99e-744446493fe3' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>iOS SDK: External camera support overview</a><ul> <li><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/USB-Camera-Support-on-iPad' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Dev guide</a></li> </ul> </li> <li>Watch: <a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/bd43edac-bc63-4814-b40f-eb4bc7ee2233' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Android &amp; iOS SDK: Move meeting between devices</a><ul> <li><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space#move-meeting' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Dev guide</a></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>🧪Webex Developer βeta Program Activity</h6><p>Early adopters rejoice! The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/webex-developer-beta-program'>Webex Developer Beta Program</a> lets you take a sneak peek and test out our upcoming features before they are released. We currently have one active beta feature you can start trying out and provide feedback on:</p> <ul> <li>Webex Web Widgets: the beta is testing password and captcha flows in Meeting and Space widgets, as well as Improved Space Meeting flows.</li> </ul> <p>To get started, head over to the Developer Beta Program <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperBeta' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>information page</a>.</p> <h6>💬Unified Webex Developer Community Forum</h6><p>Webex and Webex Contact Center developers now have a unified forum! We&#39;re thrilled to announce that the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community</a> forum has expanded to include dedicated topics for Webex Contact Center APIs and integrations. We encourage Webex Contact Center developers to utilize the combined forum to engage in discussions, exchange knowledge, and seek assistance.</p> <h6>🗓️Webex Contact Center API: Upcoming Changes</h6><p>As noted in the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Contact Center API changelog</a> on <em>July 10, 2024</em>, the scopes <code>cjp-analyzer:config_read</code> and <code>cjp-analyzer:read</code> are supported by some APIs, however since these scopes cannot be provisioned for integrations, the support for these will be removed soon. The following APIs will be affected by this change:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/search/search'>Search API</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/tasks-call-control/get-tasks'>Tasks API</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-activities'>Get Agent Activities</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/agents/get-agent-statistics'>Get Agent Statistics</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/queue-statistics/get-queue-statistics'>Get Queue Statistics</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/estimated-wait-time/get-estimated-wait-time'>Get Estimated Wait Time</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>📒Webex API Changelog Highlights</h6><p>As usual, the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Webex API Changelog</a> also has several recent entries and we still recommend checking this page frequently to stay up to date. Here are some latest items you can find there:</p> <ul> <li><strong>July 19, 2024 - NEW:</strong> Users can obtain scheduling permissions via the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-preferences/get-scheduling-options'>Get Scheduling Options</a> API and update them using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-preferences/update-scheduling-options'>Update Scheduling Options</a> API with the <code>delegateEmails</code> parameter. Additionally, users can add new delegate emails with the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-preferences/insert-delegate-emails'>Insert Delegate Emails</a> API and remove existing ones with the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meeting-preferences/delete-delegate-emails'>Delete Delegate Emails</a> API.</li> <li><strong>June 28, 2024 – Breaking Change:</strong> Due to security concerns the <a href='https://developer.cisco.com/docs/webex-xml-api-reference-guide/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex XML API</a> won&#39;t support username/email+password authentication effective Nov 30, 2024 for CI native organizations (organizations managed through Control Hub only). Instead authentication must happen via the Common Identity system and the use of <a href='https://developer.cisco.com/docs/webex-xml-api-reference-guide/getloginticket/#getloginticket' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>session login ticket</a>. As a reminder the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/webex-xml-api-deprecation-announcement'>Webex XML API has been End of Life and End of Service</a> since March 31, 2024. Some customers got an extension.</li> <li><strong>June 27, 2024 – Breaking Change:</strong> Starting <em>August 12th, 2024</em>, the <code>callingLineId</code> and <code>routingProfile</code> fields will be removed from the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/call-routing/test-call-routing'>Test Call Routing</a> endpoint&#39;s response payload.</li> <li><strong>June 27, 2024 – NEW:</strong> Starting from July 19th, 2024, a new field, <code>Location_ID</code>, will be added to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-billing'>Wholesale Billing Reports</a> API, and this applies to both Customer and User report types.</li> </ul> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Address Book ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8bc0f929f569cca9/6696a0b3ec61e9a7f7bfe542/wxcc-address-book-api-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs: Address Book" /> <p>This is the beginning of a series of blogs called “The A-Z of Webex Contact Center APIs”. In this blog series we will be exploring the entirety of an API and adding context to the effects of executing the API from the perspective of a user. There are two main goals here. First, we want to educate the developer community about what is possible with Webex Contact Center developer tools. Lastly, we want to provoke curiosity amongst Webex developers and expand on the art of possible.</p> <p>The Webex Contact Center Address Book is a tool available to agents that allows them to select an entry to dial instead of manually entering a phone number when placing a call. Administrators will create an address book and add it to a Desktop Profile that an agent is assigned to. Admins must enable outbound dialing within the dial plan of the desktop profile assigned to an agent that is intended to make outbound calls.</p> <p>An admin can create an address book from Control Hub. The Control Hub even provides a way for administrators to manage address books in bulk. Below we will go over a way to programmatically manage address books with the Webex Contact Center RESTful APIs.</p> <h6>Managing Address Books In Control Hub</h6><p>Before we dive into using the API, it is important to know the expected experience and outcomes of creating an Address Book in the Control Hub. Control Hub is the central interface that administrators utilize to manage a Webex organization, manage users, assign service, view analytics and more.</p> <p>To create an address book in the Control Hub an administrator would navigate to the <em>Contact Center &gt; Desktop Experience &gt; Address Book</em> and click on Create Address Book.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt1c2a29e8c89eabb2/wxcc-address-book-api-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Then the administrator is prompted to fill out a form requiring inputs for the name, a description, Parent Type and Entries for the Address book. The Parent Type defines if the Address Book is available to all sites in an organization, or a specific site in an organization. The Entries are the actual names and phone numbers of contacts in the Address Book.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc0fefe076695ada5/wxcc-address-book-api-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Once an Address Book is created, it becomes visible in the Address Book section in the Control Hub.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt086548b8f12eafe9/wxcc-address-book-api-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Then we can drill into the Address Book that we created and manage entries.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte88f2c8033b8e843/wxcc-address-book-api-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Administrators can also use the Control Hub to add Address Books to an organization in bulk by following the instructions <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/31e39g/Bulk-Operations-in-Webex-Contact-Center' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>.</p> <h6>Using the Address Book API</h6><p>Getting started with the APIs for the address book will require an Organization ID. The <code>orgId</code> can be obtained from <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/k5pal8/Look-Up-Your-Organization-ID-in-Control-Hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Control Hub</a>, or an <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/authentication-cc#step-1-requesting-permission'>access token</a> obtained via the OAuth 2.0 flow for a Webex Contact Center integration application.</p> <h6>Address Books</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book'>Address Book API</a> supports CRUD (create, read, update and delete) operations so developers and administrators can execute the same functionality we see in the Control Hub, both programmatically and in bulk.</p> <p>The required parameters in the path and body when executing the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/create-a-new-address-book'>Create an Address Book</a> API are Orgid, Name, and Parent Type.</p> <p>Developers can leverage the Address Book IDs provided in the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/list-address-books'>List Address Books API</a> to do things like, get Address Book details, update an Address Book name, or an update an Address Book description:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/create-a-new-address-book'>Create Address Book</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/get-specific-address-book-by-id'>Get Address Book by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/update-specific-address-book-by-id'>Update Address Book by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/delete-specific-address-book-by-id'>Delete Address Book by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/list-address-books'>List Address Books</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Entries</h6><p>There is also an associated set of APIs, that supports CRUD operations, for an Address Book’s associated entries that an agent can use to make outbound calls. There is also an API for <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/list-address-book-entrys'>listing</a> an Address Book’s entries to get the Entry Id. With Entry Id, a developer can get details about a contact in the Address Book and use them in integrations and automations.</p> <p>The required parameters in the path and body when using the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/create-a-new-address-book-entry'>Create an Address Book Entry</a> API are Orgid, Name, and Phone Number.</p> <p>Developers can leverage the filter, search, and attributes query parameter available in the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/list-address-book-entrys'>List Address Book Entry</a> API to do things like, get an entry by ID, lookup an entry by a supported attribute (id,name,number), or filter entries by a search keyword:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/create-a-new-address-book-entry'>Create Address Book Entry</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/get-specific-address-book-entry-by-id'>Get Address Book Entry by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/update-specific-address-book-entry-by-id'>Update Address Book Entry by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/delete-specific-address-book-entry-by-id'>Delete Address Book Entry by ID</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/list-address-book-entrys'>List Address Book Entry</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Bulk Operations</h6><p>Additionally, there is bulk operation support within the API set available to developers and administrators:</p> <ul> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/bulk-save-address-book-entrys'>Bulk Save Address Book Entry</a></li> <li><a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/bulk-export-address-books'>Bulk Export Address Books</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Integrations</h6><p>When registering an integration where the Address Book APIs are intended to be used, be sure to select <code>cjp:config_write</code> or <code>cjp:config_read</code> scopes.</p> <h6>Potential Use Case</h6><p>A potential use case for the Address Book API is when a Webex Contact Center organization administrator would like to synchronize an address with data from a CRM or Directory in an automated fashion. <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/address-book/bulk-save-address-book-entrys'>The Bulk Save Address Book Entry API</a> would be the perfect candidate to accomplish this. Look at this <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/tree/main/address-book-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>sample code</a> to see one way to accomplish this.</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>
