<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Runtime Agnostic Webex OAuth for JavaScript Projects with Auth.js ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt0eefa32f4b9cdf9a/669587af1e4e7ee859b66e2a/banner.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Runtime Agnostic Webex OAuth for JavaScript Projects with Auth.js" /> <p><a href='https://authjs.dev/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Auth.js</a> (previously NextAuth.js) is an open-source authentication solution tailored for JavaScript web applications, boasting essential security features such as server-only cookies, CSRF protection, and encrypted JWT sessions. Its current iteration includes built-in OAuth support for over 82 prominent services, including Webex, and offers compatibility with 23 databases/ORMs like MySQL, Postgres, Prisma, Drizzle, and MikroORM. Moreover, Auth.js exhibits versatility across different runtimes such as Node.js, Deno, Bunt, and Serverless, while seamlessly integrating with popular frameworks like Next.js, SolidStart, and SvelteKit.</p> <p>These combined attributes make it an exceptionally developer-friendly choice for JavaScript applications requiring OAuth functionality. In this post, we&#39;ll guide you through setting up Auth.js in a TypeScript SvelteKit project for Webex OAuth. Note that as of this writing, SvelteKit support in Auth.js is experimental. Please refer to the <a href='https://authjs.dev/reference/sveltekit' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>documentation</a> before replicating anything.</p> <h6>Installation</h6><p>If you do not have an existing <a href='https://kit.svelte.dev/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>SvelteKit</a> project, create one using <code>create-svelte</code> as shown below:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm create svelte@latest authjs-webex-oauth </code></pre> <h6>Setting Environment Variables</h6><p>To set up environment variables for your Webex integration, follow these steps:</p> <ol> <li><p><strong>Register Your Integration</strong>: Refer to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/integrations#registering-your-integration'>Registering your Integration on Webex</a> guide. Note down your Client ID and Client Secret provided during registration.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Create <code>.env</code> File</strong>: Create a <code>.env</code> file in the root directory of your project if it doesn&#39;t exist already.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Assign Variables</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Set <code>WEBEX_CLIENT_ID</code> to your Webex Client ID obtained from the Webex developer portal.</li> <li>Set <code>WEBEX_CLIENT_SECRET</code> to your Webex Client Secret obtained during integration registration.</li> <li>Define <code>WEBEX_SCOPE</code> with the required scopes for your integration. Include at minimum <code>spark:kms</code> and <code>spark:people_read</code>.</li> <li>Generate a random 64-character string and assign it to <code>AUTH_SECRET</code> in the <code>.env</code> file for secure session management.</li> </ul> </li> </ol> <p>Example <code>.env</code> file:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">WEBEX_CLIENT_ID=your_webex_client_id WEBEX_CLIENT_SECRET=your_webex_client_secret WEBEX_SCOPE=spark:kms spark:people_read AUTH_SECRET=random_64_character_long_string </code></pre> <p>Ensure these variables are securely managed and not exposed in version control or publicly accessible locations.</p> <h6>Add the Package</h6><p>Inside the project directory (i.e., <code>authjs-webex-oauth</code> here), add the Auth.js package as a project dependency:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm install @auth/sveltekit </code></pre> <h6>Add a New Authentication Handler</h6><p>Create a new handler under <code>src/lib/server/handlers/authentication.ts</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">import { SvelteKitAuth } from &#39;@auth/sveltekit&#39;; import Webex from &#39;@auth/sveltekit/providers/webex&#39;; import { AUTH_SECRET, WEBEX_CLIENT_ID, WEBEX_CLIENT_SECRET, WEBEX_SCOPE } from &#39;$env/static/private&#39;; const { handle, signIn, signOut } = SvelteKitAuth(async (event) =&gt; { return { secret: AUTH_SECRET, providers: [ Webex({ style: { logo: &#39;/webex.svg&#39;, bg: &#39;#fff&#39;, text: &#39;#000&#39; }, clientId: WEBEX_CLIENT_ID, clientSecret: WEBEX_CLIENT_SECRET, authorization: { params: { prompt: &#39;select_account&#39;, scope: WEBEX_SCOPE } } }) ] }; }); export const authentication = handle; export { signIn, signOut }; </code></pre> <h6>Add a New Authorization Handler</h6><p>Create a new handler under <code>src/lib/server/handlers/authorization.ts</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">import type { Handle } from &#39;@sveltejs/kit&#39;; import { redirect } from &#39;@sveltejs/kit&#39;; export const authorization: Handle = async ({ event, resolve }) =&gt; { // Protect any routes under /authenticated if (event.url.pathname.startsWith(&#39;/authenticated&#39;)) { const session = await event.locals.auth(); if (!session) { // Redirect to the signin page throw redirect(303, &#39;/auth/signin&#39;); } } // If the request is still here, just proceed as normal return resolve(event); }; </code></pre> <h6>Add a Hook Sequence</h6><p>Modify or add the server-side hooks file at <code>src/hooks.server.ts</code>.</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">import type { Handle } from &#39;@sveltejs/kit&#39;; import { sequence } from &#39;@sveltejs/kit/hooks&#39;; import { authentication as authenticationHandle } from &#39;$lib/server/handlers/authentication&#39;; import { authorization as authorizationHandle } from &#39;$lib/server/handlers/authorization&#39;; export const handle: Handle = sequence(authenticationHandle, authorizationHandle); </code></pre> <h6>Usage</h6><p>Once configured, any routes prefixed with <code>/authenticated</code> will automatically benefit from the protection provided by the handle hook. To verify functionality, navigate to any route in your running application (<code>npm run dev</code>).</p> <p>You have the flexibility to extend the sequence with additional middleware-like functions and implement more sophisticated authorization logic within the respective handler files. The current setup establishes authorization based on paths, but an alternative per-component approach is also viable and can complement or replace path-based techniques.</p> <p>Note that Auth.js utilizes JWT by default for session storage in the absence of a configured database adapter. For enhanced session management, consider integrating your preferred <a href='https://authjs.dev/getting-started/database' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>database adapter</a> on the server side.</p> <h6>Wrapping Up</h6><p>This article provided a brief overview of the new Auth.js package for Webex OAuth. JavaScript project owners are encouraged to use this package to simplify their workload when authenticating with Webex. To explore other community offerings or learn more about our developer platform, please visit <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/'>Webex Developers</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex Developers: A Look Back at Cisco Live Las Vegas 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt92de69a9f15fe3d3/667c32507589924372077a6c/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex Developers: A Look Back at Cisco Live Las Vegas 2024" /> <p>Hello, fellow Webex enthusiasts and developers! The above picture is just part of the Webex for Developers team who worked Cisco Live this year: Bagavathi Desika Vinayagam, Jeff Marshall, Luz Delgado-Macias, Phil Bellanti, Joe Zanini, and myself, Adam Weeks.</p> <p>As I sit back and reflect on the whirlwind of innovation and connection that was Cisco Live Las Vegas 2024, I&#39;m filled with an immense sense of pride and excitement for what we, as a community, have achieved. It was a week where the bright lights of Vegas were matched by the bright minds of developers, partners, and tech aficionados from around the world.</p> <h6>Innovative Learning Sessions</h6><p>Our Webex Developer sessions were the talk of the town, with each classroom brimming with eager learners. We kicked off with DEVNET-1282, where Product Manager, Devinder Kathuria explored the vast potential of the Webex Developer Platform. The &#39;sidebar&#39; apps segment was particularly well-received, as attendees visualized the future of personalized applications.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8307169b60826002/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Devinder Kathuria sharing the Webex Developer Platform Strategy</em></p> <p>The Cisco U. Theatre was packed to the rafters for CISCOU-1033, where evangelist Phil Bellanti showcased the practical uses of Webex Platform APIs. The real-world scenarios resonated with the audience, who left with actionable knowledge to enhance their collaboration capabilities.</p> <p>AI took center stage in DEVNET-2127, where we unveiled how AI and Webex are revolutionizing industries. The integration of AI from Machine Learning to GPTs combined with Cisco Webex SDKs and APIs opens new integration possibilities, from healthcare to retail.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blteb7779c25ef1b94d/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Adam Weeks on stage for DEVNET-2127 AI Session</em></p> <p>And let&#39;s not forget the hands-on workshop, DEVWKS-2040, where we got our hands dirty with Webex Service Apps. The small group setting allowed for an intimate and detailed learning experience.</p> <h6>Dynamic Booth Engagements</h6><p>Our two booths within the Webex showcase were buzzing hubs of activity. The Webex for Developers booth was a developer&#39;s playground, with live coding demos that turned heads and sparked conversations. The Webex Integration Partners booth allowed attendees to experience and try out some excited applications and integrations from our <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex App Hub</a>.</p> <p>This year&#39;s Cisco Live Las Vegas 2024 was a landmark event for our team, as we introduced live coding and developer centric demos for the first time at the Webex for Developers booth. These demos were designed to be succinct, engaging, and packed with actionable insights. Here&#39;s a snapshot of the innovative demos that captivated our audience:</p> <h6>Build a Bot Demo</h6><p>We demonstrated how to quickly create a Webex messaging bot capable of intelligent interactions and handling interactive cards.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt15d96c7c033260ff/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Phil Bellanti shows us how to build a Webex Bot</em></p> <h6>Build an Embedded App</h6><p>Attendees saw the power of Webex Embedded Apps in action, enhancing meetings and messaging with seamless integrations.</p> <p>&#xa0;</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltae3c03405e1a1cda/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Joe Zanini building a Webex Embedded App</em></p> <h6>Build and Use a Service App</h6><p>We showcased the creation of a Service App, illustrating how to schedule meetings on behalf of others with admin-level API access.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6fb5d1e18ab2d2f1/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Phil Bellanti shows us the power of Webex Service Apps</em></p> <h6>Developer AI Assistant Preview</h6><p>Our new AI Assistant for the Webex Developer Portal was previewed, demonstrating its ability to streamline access to documentation and code generation.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9675b7ea79d109d6/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Faisal Siyavudeen gave us a hands-on preview of the AI Assistant</em></p> <h6>Contact Center Widgets</h6><p>The demo highlighted the integration of custom Agent Desktop Widgets, such as an RSS feed reader, to keep contact center agents informed.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9a1950ed5ea97002/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Adam Weeks building a Webex Contact Center Desktop Widget</em></p> <h6>Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</h6><p>We introduced the Contact Center Flow Designer, showcasing how to easily create complex workflows with low-code/no-code solutions.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd17e06dcd4f93ba0/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Joe Zanini shows us how to incorporate an external API in Flow Designer</em></p> <h6>Instant Connect</h6><p>The capabilities of Webex Instant Connect were revealed, teaching how to instantly create meetings for real-time virtual interactions.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9711217b2ba895cf/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-10.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Clay Ver Valen shows us how to utilize Instant Connect</em></p> <h6>Webex Meetings JavaScript SDK</h6><p>The session focused on using the Webex Meetings JavaScript SDK to embed a fully functional meeting interface into web applications.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt97c3a5dbea1f9e54/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-11.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Adam Weeks walked through the Webex Meetings JS SDK</em></p> <p>The debut of these live coding demos was a game-changer, providing a dynamic platform for developers to learn and engage with the Webex ecosystem. The energy and excitement around these sessions were a clear indication of the vibrant future ahead for Webex developers.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6dc67a893cbabfdc/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-12.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Adam Weeks digging into the code</em></p> <p>As we forge ahead, these live coding demos will undoubtedly become a highlight of Cisco Live, reflecting our dedication to empowering developers with the skills and tools they need to innovate.</p> <h6>Our Vision, Your Voice</h6><p>In addition to coding demos, we had a special guest, Athena Perez, a leader from the UI/UX team shared an insider’s view of the new “Bring Your Own” framework. They also encouraged developers to sign up for the <a href='https://forms.office.com/r/Z9w7Dk31PT' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>UX Feedback for Developers</a> their team is working on!</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt01894c39a48c9e72/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-13.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Special Guest Athena Perez</em></p> <h6>Webex Integrations Partners</h6><p>The Webex Integration Partners booth was equally impressive, highlighting the success stories and innovative solutions built on the Webex platform.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltdc96a4bfd0c2ebc6/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-14.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>Bagavathi Desika Vinayagam showcases Webex App Hub Integrations</em></p> <h6>Record-Breaking Attendance and Impactful Connections</h6><p>We hit an all-time high in session attendance, a testament to the growing interest and dedication within our developer community. The live demos drew in curious minds and the apps shared by our App Hub partners were nothing short of inspiring!</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7a83042797615812/cisco-live-us-2024-wrapup-15.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> <em>A packed house for Phil Bellanti’s CiscoU Session</em></p> <h6>Looking Ahead with Lessons Learned</h6><p>As we look to the future, we&#39;re already brainstorming ways to enhance our booth experiences and refine our demo strategies. The feedback on the noise levels has been invaluable, and we&#39;re exploring new tech to ensure our voices carry through the buzz of excitement next time.</p> <h6>A Heartfelt Thank You</h6><p>I want to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone who joined us, engaged with us, and shared their passion for Webex at Cisco Live Las Vegas 2024. Your energy and curiosity are the driving forces behind these events, and I&#39;m already counting down the days until we meet again at <a href='https://www.webexone.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex One</a>!</p> <p>Stay connected with us on the <a href='https://community.cisco.com/t5/webex-for-developers/bd-p/disc-webex-developers' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Developers community forum</a> and keep the spirit of innovation alive!</p> <p>Until next time, let&#39;s continue to code, connect, and create a future that&#39;s more collaborative than ever before.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – June 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltb7465b83e3bd4e11/6675a34212a787dbcd665c74/june-2024-webex-for-developers-newsletter---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – June 2024" /> <p>Greetings, Webex developers! We have some great new content to share this month, particularly for the Webex Contact Center platform. Let’s jump right in and take a gander at all the latest news for June.</p> <h6>🍥Introducing the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</h6><p>Webex Product Manager, Arunabh Bhattacharjee published a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/design-delightful-customer-experiences-with-webex-contact-center-flow-designer'>recent blog post</a> to introduce the Contact Center Flow Designer platform for workflow orchestration and automation. With its intuitive visual canvas, discover how Flow Designer simplifies the development process to encourage collaboration between developers and business stakeholders, enabling the creation of applications that provide superior customer experiences.</p> <h6>💻Flow Designer: Integrating Third-Party APIs with the HTTP Integration Connector</h6><p>In another <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/contact-center-flow-designer-integrating-third-party-apis-with-the-http-integration-connector'>helpful blog post</a> about Flow Designer, Webex Developer Evangelist, Joe Zanini shows us how to build a custom connector to plug in third-party APIs for other services to run alongside Webex Contact Center call handling. This allows Webex Contact Center customers to engage in custom experiences that enhance service in call routing queues.</p> <h6>📺Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On Wednesday June 26th at 2:00PM ET, join our public webinar on <strong>Harnessing Webex Connect to Upgrade Your SMS Experience with Branded RCS Messaging</strong>, designed for developers who work with SMS and are looking to explore richer messaging channels. In this session, we will take you through the capabilities of RCS, why consider adding the channel to your communications mix, and how to send RCS messages through Webex Connect. You can register for the live event or watch the recording later from our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a>.</p> <p>Also, in case you didn’t catch the last webinar in May, <strong>Transform Calls into Experiences: Tap into the Webex Web Calling SDK</strong>, the recording is available to <a href='https://app.vidcast.io/share/73d00cff-83a7-458e-9857-9c6e29b11943' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>watch now</a>.</p> <h6>📦Contact Center Widget Bundling with Webpack</h6><p>In Joe Zanini’s <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-contact-center-widget-bundling-with-webpack'>latest blog</a>, explore how to create Web Component Widgets for the Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop, with a comprehensive guide on using Webpack for efficient bundling of static resources. Joe does this with a practical GitHub example for you to start elevating the Agent Desktop experience with custom widget integrations right off the bat.</p> <h6>💰Enhancing Webex Contact Center Widgets with Dynamic $STORE Variables</h6><p>Continuing the topic of Webex Contact Center widgets, Adam Weeks shows us in a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/enhancing-webex-contact-center-widgets-with-dynamic-store-variables'>new article</a> how dynamic <code>$STORE</code> variables enhances the creation process to make more efficient workspace for agents. Learn how they capture everything from user settings to customer data, equipping agents with a wealth of information at their fingertips.</p> <h6>💥Webex Integration Partners at Cisco Live 2024</h6><p>Webex Integration Partners are helping organizations redefine what’s possible with transformative technologies that seamlessly integrate with Webex software and devices. In a <a href='https://blog.webex.com/hybrid-work/webex-integration-partners-cisco-live-2024/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>new blog post</a> by Colm Mcnelis, he explains how Webex Partners hit the ground running at Cisco Live in Las Vegas, by connecting with customers and wowing event-goers with awesome demos and showcases.</p> <h6>📋Webex Contact Center API Changelog Highlights</h6><p>There are number of important items that were recently listed in the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Webex Contact Center API Changelog</a>. We recommend bookmarking that page to keep tabs on future entries.&#xa0; These are some of the latest entries found on the Contact Center API changelog:</p> <ul> <li><strong>May 30, 2024 - WARNING:</strong> The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/auxiliary-code'>Auxiliary Codes APIs</a> have been updated to support the inclusion of the <code>burnoutInclusion</code> property.</li> <li><strong>May 30, 2024 - WARNING:</strong> The <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/users'>Users APIs</a> have been updated to support the inclusion of the <code>userLevelBurnoutInclusion</code> property.</li> <li><strong>May 30, 2024 - NEW:</strong> <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/users/bulk-partial-update-users'>Bulk partial update Users</a> has been added to conveniently update the entity by passing in only the properties that need updating.</li> <li><strong>May 30, 2024 - NEW:</strong> <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/auxiliary-code/bulk-partial-update-auxiliary-codes'>Bulk partial update Auxiliary Codes</a> has been added to conveniently update the entity by passing in only the properties that need updating.</li> <li><strong>June 12, 2024 - DEPRECATION:</strong> The Agent Profile APIs will be replaced with <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/desktop-profile'>Desktop Profile APIs</a>. All operations done with Agent Profile APIs will be possible with <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/desktop-profile'>Desktop Profile APIs</a>.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>📒Webex API Changelog Highlights</h6><p>As usual, the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Webex API Changelog</a> also has several recent entries and we still recommend checking this page frequently to stay up to date. Here are some latest items you can find there:</p> <ul> <li><strong>May 23, 2024 - NEW:</strong> A Compliance Officer can now list recordings that have been purged from the recycle bin using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/recordings/list-recordings-for-an-admin-or-compliance-officer'>List Recordings For an Admin or Compliance Officer</a> API with the <code>status=purged</code> parameter.</li> <li><strong>May 30, 2024 – NEW:</strong> In the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/workspace-call-settings'>Workspace Call Settings</a> API, we&#39;ve added multiple endpoints that let you manage all Professional Workspace call settings.</li> <li><strong>June 18, 2024 – NEW:</strong> As a Compliance Officer, you can now access Webex Calling recordings using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings'>Converged Recordings</a> API. You can <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/list-recordings-for-compliance-officer'>List Recordings for Compliance officer</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-details'>Get Recording Details</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/delete-a-recording'>Delete a Recording</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/converged-recordings/get-recording-metadata'>Get Recording metadata</a>.</li> </ul> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Enhancing Webex Contact Center Widgets with Dynamic $STORE Variables ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltadf82e1a3cab0716/6658b6d69518af7a84667578/wxcc-widgets-data-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Enhancing Webex Contact Center Widgets with Dynamic $STORE Variables" /> <p>As Webex developers, creating a productive and collaborative workspace for Contact Center agents is paramount. One of the key features that can significantly bolster this effort is the use of dynamic <code>$STORE</code> variables. These variables allow for real-time customization of agent widgets based on contextual data provided by the Webex Contact Center platform.</p> <p>Today, we&#39;re exploring the transformative potential of <code>$STORE</code> variables and how they can be integrated into agent widgets for a more connected and efficient workspace.</p> <h6>Harnessing $STORE Variables for Tailored Agent Experiences</h6><p><code>$STORE</code> variables serve as conduits of context, carrying vital information that can be rendered in real-time within your customized widgets. They capture everything from user settings to customer data, equipping agents with a wealth of information at their fingertips.</p> <p>Utilizing these dynamic variables within your widgets can create a responsive and engaging environment for agents, leading to improved customer interactions and streamlined workflows.</p> <h6>Real-World Applications and Advantages</h6><p>Incorporating <code>$STORE</code> variables into your widgets can take many forms. Here are some scenarios where they can make a real difference:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Adaptive Interface Elements</strong>: Widgets that respond to the <code>$STORE.app.darkMode</code> variable can automatically adjust their theme to align with the agent’s display preferences, reducing visual fatigue and enhancing focus.</li> <li><strong>Contextual Agent Insights</strong>: Variables like <code>$STORE.agent.agentName</code> can pull in agent names for a personalized touch that fosters connection and rapport from the moment the interaction begins.</li> </ul> <p>The introduction of <code>$STORE</code> variables into widgets not only customizes the agent&#39;s environment but also paves the way for:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Optimized Agent Workflows</strong>: With less time spent navigating for information, agents can focus more on the customer.</li> <li><strong>Targeted Customer Solutions</strong>: Access to real-time data enables agents to provide more accurate and personalized service.</li> <li><strong>Elevated Productivity</strong>: A workspace that adapts to both agent and customer needs leads to more efficient operations.</li> </ul> <p><code>$STORE</code> variables are updated in real-time so that your widgets are constantly up to date with the Webex Contact Center desktop. One thing to note, these <code>$STORE</code> variables are only available for Web Component widgets, not for iFrame widgets. For a walkthrough of building a Web Component widget, take a look at my previous blog: <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/developing-with-webex-contact-center-header-widgets-an-rss-feed-reader-example'>Developing With Webex Contact Center Header Widgets: An RSS Feed Reader Example</a>.</p> <h6>$STORE Variables: The Agents of Change</h6><p><code>$STORE</code> variables are the secret sauce that can transform an ordinary agent widget into a powerhouse of productivity and personalization. They provide a stream of real-time data that widgets can utilize to present information that is current and relevant to the task at hand.</p> <p>Here&#39;s a rundown of the top-level <code>$STORE</code> variables and how they can be leveraged in agent widgets:</p> <h6>$STORE.agent</h6><p>This namespace includes details about the agent such as their state (e.g., Available, Busy), skills, and queue membership. Widgets can use this data to show or hide features relevant to the agent&#39;s status or to provide alerts when their attention is needed elsewhere.</p> <h6>$STORE.agentContact</h6><p>This variable holds information about the current customer interaction tasks. It contains details such as the list of tasks that are assigned to an agent at a given time. Widgets can use this information to prepare the agent with tools and information specific to the tasks they are assigned with.</p> <h6>$STORE.app</h6><p>Application-level settings and preferences such as locale, theme, and layout configurations are housed here. A widget, for example, could adjust its language and theme to match the agent&#39;s settings, ensuring a consistent experience across the Contact Center platform.</p> <h6>$STORE.auth</h6><p>Here we find authentication-related data like the agent&#39;s token. This data is crucial for widgets that need to access external systems or APIs securely on behalf of the agent, ensuring that sensitive information is handled properly.</p> <h6>$STORE.generalNotifications</h6><p>General notifications encompassing system alerts and other important messages are available within this variable. Widgets designed to keep agents informed can tap into this stream of notifications, making sure that agents are aware of system-wide announcements or updates.</p> <h6>$STORE.dynamic</h6><p>Determines whether the Desktop is loaded in the connector view (smaller viewing area) or desktop view (larger viewing area).</p> <h6>Integrating $STORE Variables: An Overview</h6><br/> <h6>Step 1: Grasp $STORE Variables</h6><p>Begin by getting to grips with the available <code>$STORE</code> variables. Familiarize yourself with their functionality and potential applications by examining the Webex Developer <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/desktop#get-started'>documentation</a>.</p> <h6>Step 2: Configure the layout file</h6><p>Your widget&#39;s behavior is influenced by the <code>layout.json</code> file. This is where you define which <code>$STORE</code> variables to pass through. Here’s a sample <code>layout.json</code> Configuration:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;comp&quot;: &quot;custom-widget&quot;, &quot;script&quot;: &quot;http://localhost:8000/custom-widget.js&quot;, &quot;properties&quot;: { &quot;theme&quot;: &quot;$STORE.app.darkMode&quot; }, &quot;attributes&quot;: { &quot;agent&quot;: &quot;$STORE.agent.agentName&quot; } } </code></pre> <p>Note that you can pass both attributes and properties to your Web Component. To read about the differences, <a href='https://open-wc.org/guides/knowledge/attributes-and-properties' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Open Web Components has a handy article</a>. For variables that are in flux, like the agent status, I recommend utilizing properties as Web Components make it easier to adjust to property changes.</p> <h6>Conclusion: An Invitation to Innovate with $STORE Variables</h6><p>The opportunity to elevate your Contact Center widgets through <code>$STORE</code> variables is exciting and boundless. By tapping into these dynamic data points, you create an environment that&#39;s not just reactive but predictive, offering agents an unparalleled level of support.</p> <p>While I’ve only highlighted some of the top-level <code>$STORE</code> variables, documentation for all of the variables can be found in the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/desktop#get-started'>developer guide</a>. For more information on custom widgets, see the <a href='https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/voice_ip_comm/cust_contact/contact_center/webexcc/SetupandAdministrationGuide_2/b_mp-release-2/b_cc-release-2_chapter_011.html#topic_8230815F4023699032326F948C3F1495' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Desktop Layout</a> section in the Provisioning chapter of the Cisco Webex Contact Center Setup and Administration Guide.</p> <p><strong>Embark on your journey with <code>$STORE</code> variables and witness the transformation of your Contact Center widgets. We&#39;re eager to hear about your creations and the positive impact they have on agent and customer experiences alike. Let&#39;s shape the future of Webex Contact Center customization together!</strong></p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex Contact Center Widget Bundling with Webpack ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt06104114a5278df8/663cebd2aea329b14760efc4/webex-contact-center-webpack-cheatsheet---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex Contact Center Widget Bundling with Webpack" /> <p>A Custom Agent Widget in the Webex Contact Center Agent Desktop is a third-party application that is configured in a desktop layout file that is accessible via Webex Contact Center admin in Control Hub. Previously, I covered all of the different types of Widgets available in my blog <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/unlocking-the-power-of-custom-widgets-in-webex-contact-center'>Unlocking the Power of Custom Widgets in Webex Contact Center</a>. Some of the most powerful types of Widgets are built with Web Components.</p> <p>Custom Web Component Widgets work best when they bundle all of their static resources (CSS, JavaScript, markup, and images) in a single file using a bundle library for consumption in the Agent Desktop experience. Think of this almost like a code compiler, but for web code! While developing I use the VS Code plugin <a href='https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ritwickdey.LiveServer' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Live Server</a> for hosting locally (this saves the step of having to deploy your code somewhere) and <a href='https://webpack.js.org/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webpack</a> for bundling.</p> <h6>Let’s Get Ready to Bundle</h6><p>First, navigate to the project directory in Terminal (I am on Mac). Then, run the following command:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm init -y </code></pre> <p>This will install a <code>package.json</code> file in our project to keep track of all dependencies. Then run the next command:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npm install webpack webpack-cli --save-dev </code></pre> <p>The <code>--save-dev</code> command will add Webpack to the <code>package.json</code> file as a dependency.</p> <p>To align with best practices, at this point, I will set up a custom Webpack configuration file. I will add a file to the project directory called <code>webpack.config.js</code>, which will serve as a JavaScript configuration for directing Webpack on how I want my component bundled:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta406581e651631ef/webex-contact-center-webpack-cheatsheet---blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>I can tell Webpack where the file that I want to be bundled is in the folder hierarchy with an entry property. I can tell Webpack what I want the bundle file to be named, and where to put it in my project with an <code>output</code> property. In my configuration file, I’ve chosen to use the standard convention of putting the bundle in the <code>dist</code> folder (short for “distribution”). The <code>path</code> module must be imported because Webpack requires the use of an absolute path when telling it where to put the bundled file:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">const path = require(&#39;path&#39;); module.exports = { entry: &#39;./src/agent-data.js&#39;, output: { filename: &#39;bundle.js&#39;, path: path.resolve(__dirname, &#39;./dist&#39;) }, mode: &#39;none&#39; } </code></pre> <p>Then, in the Terminal, I can run Webpack with the following command:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">npx webpack </code></pre> <p>As a result, there will be a new folder in the project called <code>dist</code> and a new JavaScript file in <code>dist</code> called <code>bundle.js</code> that we can host and point our agent desktop at. For more details on how to configure your desktop to import this bundle, be sure to read the blog <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/developing-with-webex-contact-center-header-widgets-an-rss-feed-reader-example'>Developing With Webex Contact Center Header Widgets: An RSS Feed Reader Example</a>. I’ve prepared a small code example of a Widget being bundled by Webpack that you can review in this GitHub <a href='https://github.com/Joezanini/agent_id_store' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>repo</a>. Happy coding folks!</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ What to Expect for Webex Developers at Cisco Live 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7fc693360a96d96e/663e86e0044f23f56359fd3e/webex-developers-at-cisco-live-las-vegas-2024-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="What to Expect for Webex Developers at Cisco Live 2024" /> <p>Greetings Webex developers and fellow tech enthusiasts! There’s a lot of anticipation for the upcoming Cisco Live in Las Vegas, on June 2-6, 2024. We&#39;re thrilled to announce the line-up of live sessions that will bring a variety of Webex developer related content throughout the entire event. This includes classroom sessions, a hands-on workshop, and booth exhibits with live demos, to help enhance your skills, gain insight into latest platform features, and provide an opportunity to network with other industry professionals. Let’s see what we have in store for Webex developers this year!</p> <h6>Classroom Sessions</h6><br/> <ul> <li>DEVNET-1282: <strong>Unleashing Creativity with Webex Developer Platform Products</strong> - <em>Monday, Jun 3, 10:00 am - 10:45 am PDT</em>.<ul> <li>This session, aimed at developers, navigates the realm of the Webex Developers Platform, which spans several products to satisfy different developers&#39; use cases. Starting with a quick introduction to Embedded Apps, public and private apps and how these apps solve different problems for customers. Participants will gain insights into the revolutionary &#39;sidebar&#39; apps and their personalized applications. Next, we will move to SDKs and integrations and how they power exciting collaboration use cases. Finally, highlighting one of our most powerful products, Webex Instant Connect, that allows users to have WebRTC powered video communications.</li> </ul> </li> <li>CISCOU-1033: <strong>Integrating Your Business: Mastering Webex APIs for Messaging, Meetings, and Calling</strong> - <em>Monday, Jun 3, 2:30 pm - 3:00 pm PDT</em>.<ul> <li>This session will be held at the <strong>Cisco U. Theatre</strong> in the Learning and Certification area in The World of Solutions.</li> <li>The presentation focuses on the practical use of Webex Messaging, Meetings, and Calling APIs, offering attendees an opportunity to learn how they can enhance and extend their collaboration capabilities. It will cover a range of real-world scenarios, providing attendees with a clear understanding of how Webex integrations can be leveraged to streamline communication and improve workflow efficiency.</li> </ul> </li> <li>DEVNET-2127: <strong>AI Innovations with Cisco Webex: Transforming Industries through Smart Applications</strong> - <em>Tuesday, Jun 4, 11:00 am - 11:45 am PDT</em>.<ul> <li>This presentation will showcase how the power of AI and Webex can be harnessed to meet the evolving demands in this new and exciting technological era. Discover the game-changing integration of AI technologies, like Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPTs), with Cisco Webex SDKs, and how they&#39;re making waves in healthcare, finance, retail, and manufacturing. Learn how developers are utilizing Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, and Image Recognition to create applications that enhance communication, improve operational efficiency, and provide personalized customer experiences.</li> </ul> </li> <li>DEVNET-2675: <strong>Implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization for Webex Integrations</strong> - <em>Wednesday, Jun 5, 1:00 pm - 1:45 pm PDT</em>.<ul> <li>OAuth is a powerful way to allow users to grant permission over their accounts to third parties. Join the Webex Developer Evangelism team for a walk-through of how to create an OAuth flow so your Webex Integrations users can authorize your app to run on their accounts or simply authenticate with Login with Webex.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Hands-On Workshop</h6><br/> <ul> <li>DEVWKS-2040: <strong>Deploying Webex Service Apps</strong> - <em>Tuesday, Jun 4, 11:00 am - 11:45 am PDT</em>. <ul> <li>In this workshop, participants will learn all about Webex Service Apps, which enable integrations to request administrator permission for accessing the Webex REST APIs on behalf of an organization instead of a user. We will get hands-on with creating and deploying a Service App from the developer perspective. Participants will also see how a Webex administrator approves and manages Service Apps for their organization inside of Control Hub.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <p>Visit the <a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/global/learn/session-catalog.html#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Cisco Live Session Catalog</a> for scheduling information. </p> <h6>Webex Developer &amp; Integration Booths at the Event</h6><p>In addition to the learning sessions, we&#39;ll also have two booths at the Webex exhibit in World of Solutions area that will showcase the Webex Developer platform and our App Hub integration partners.</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>Webex Developers Booth</strong>: Experience innovation in action at Cisco Live Vegas 2024 with the Webex for Developers booth! Introducing our latest feature: live coding demos. Join us for a series of 30-minute, hands-on sessions where you&#39;ll witness the power of Webex integrations and APIs brought to life by our product and engineering maestros. Dive into the world of real-time problem-solving and get a sneak peek at the future of collaborative technology. These live demos are a must-see – tailored for developers, by developers. Stay tuned for our schedule and be sure to follow us on social media for exclusive updates. Let&#39;s code, connect, and create at Cisco Live!</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Webex Integration Partners Booth</strong>: This booth will be showcasing our App Hub integration partners that have built solutions on the Webex platform. We will be introducing new ways to leverage Webex in your workflows with some live demonstrations and to talk about success stories from our integration partners.</p> </li> </ul> <p>We are looking forward to seeing you at Cisco Live in Las Vegas! Don&#39;t forget to <a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/global/learn/session-catalog.html#/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>register</a> for the sessions and workshops that interest you most. For more information about the event, check out the <a href='https://www.ciscolive.com/global.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>official Cisco Live website</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Contact Center Flow Designer: Integrating Third-Party APIs with the HTTP Integration Connector ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt91db263b6083bb07/663ce8e42ff97d9376703acc/flow-designer-apis---blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Contact Center Flow Designer: Integrating Third-Party APIs with the HTTP Integration Connector" /> <p>There is a lot going on under the hood of most contact center technology stacks during day-to-day operations. A contact center agent serves hundreds of customers daily and handles a lot of sensitive data. A customer’s time and experience are extremely valuable and can make or break potential revenue for any organization. Though speaking to a representative is still the top preferred engagement channel for customers, there are still ways that developers can build applications and services that make digital-first experiences. These experiences can build the confidence of an agent to handle sensitive data, are comfortable for agents to use, and can streamline the “Zero to Hello Agent” time for customers with important support needs. The Webex Contact Center Flow Designer is an integration surface that provides development teams with the tools necessary to plug in third-party APIs for congruent technologies to run alongside Webex Contact Center call handling and routing strategy software.</p> <h6>Pre-requisites For Setting Up a Flow Designer Connector</h6><p>Best practices ask a developer’s third-party API to either be set up with a path for an integration to be registered To ensure a smooth integration process within the Flow Designer, it is recommended that developers prepare their third-party API to support one of two authentication methods:</p> <ul> <li><strong>OAuth Authentication</strong>: Ideally, the third-party API should have a dedicated endpoint that allows for the registration of the integration on your platform. This endpoint should facilitate an OAuth authentication flow, enabling users to securely connect their third-party services with the Webex Contact Center.</li> <li><strong>Basic Authentication</strong>: Alternatively, the API can provide a Basic Authentication method, which requires a username and password for access.</li> </ul> <p>Once the third-party API is ready to support one of these authentication methods, the Webex Contact Center Administrator can then proceed to configure the integration connector by following the provided setup instructions. This involves accessing the necessary authorization credentials and applying them within the Flow Designer to establish the connection.</p> <h6>Setting Up Third-Party API Custom Connectors in Control Hub</h6><p>To set up a third-party connector in Control Hub:</p> <ol> <li>An organization administrator should log into Control Hub at <a href='https://admin.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://admin.webex.com</a>.</li> <li>Navigate to <strong>Services</strong> &gt; <strong>Contact Center</strong> &gt; <strong>Tenant Settings</strong> &gt; <strong>Integrations</strong> &gt; <strong>Connectors</strong>.</li> <li>On the Custom Connectors Card click Set Up or Add more</li> <li>In the <strong>Name</strong> field, enter a relevant name for the connector that a user can associate with the service when discovered in the Flow Designer HTTPS node setup.</li> <li>Choose an authentication type from the <strong>Authentication Type</strong> drop-down (<strong>OAuth</strong> or <strong>Basic Auth</strong>).</li> <li>In the <strong>Resource Domain URL</strong> field, enter the URL of the third-party service API (HTTPS Required).</li> <li>If your API uses OAuth 2.0, choose either <strong>Client Credentials</strong> or <strong>Password Grant Types</strong>:<ol> <li>In the <strong>Client ID</strong> field, enter the third-party API service client ID issued for the integration.</li> <li>In the <strong>Client Secret field</strong>, enter the Client Secret.</li> <li>In the <strong>Token URL</strong> field, enter the token URL of the authorization server.</li> <li>In the <strong>Scope</strong> field, enter the scope for the client credentials grant.</li> </ol> </li> <li>If your API uses basic auth and the grant type is password grant:<ol> <li>In the <strong>Username</strong> field, enter the username of the service account.</li> <li>In the <strong>Password</strong> field, enter the password of the service account.</li> <li>In the <strong>Validation URL</strong> field, enter the URL to validate the username and password.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Click <strong>Done</strong> &gt; <strong>Close</strong>.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Discovering The Connector in the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</h6><p>Now that the connector is set up, Webex Contact Center customers can leverage your software from the Flow designer.</p> <p>To access the connector in your sandbox org:</p> <ol> <li><p>Login to the Webex Control Hub at <a href='https://admin.webex.com/login' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://admin.webex.com/login</a>.</p> </li> <li><p>Go to <strong>Service</strong> &gt; <strong>Contact Center</strong> &gt; <strong>Customer Experience</strong> &gt; <strong>Flows</strong> and either select an existing flow or create a new flow.</p> <div><Callout type="info">When in the Flow Designer application make sure that the **Edit** option is toggled on.</Callout></div></li> <li><p>From the <strong>Activity Library</strong> in the left navigation pane, select an HTTP request node from the <strong>Flow Control</strong> section of the options.</p> </li> <li><p>Click on the node in the Flow Builder, and under <strong>HTTP Request Settings</strong>, toggle on <strong>Use Authenticated Endpoint</strong>.</p> </li> <li><p>On the <strong>Connector</strong> drop-down, the custom connector you just created should be available to use:</p> <p> <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd01b7cd05e9cbd2d/flow-designer-apis---blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> </li> </ol> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – April 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt649bdd1909e75d7b/662fbfff85518c5a5a55a8c4/W4D_Newsletter_banner.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – April 2024" /> <p>Hello, Webex Developers. As usual, we have a lot of interesting stuff going on recently. In this month&#39;s edition, we will get you caught up on all the latest news, updates, and other tidbits. Let’s jump right into things, shall we?!</p> <h6>🦾Leveraging AI Across Verticals: Use Cases for Enhanced Webex Integrations</h6><p>Looking for ways to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to make amazing Webex integrations? In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/navigating-the-ai-landscape-industry-specific-applications-for-webex'>new blog post</a> from the leader of Webex Developer Evangelism, Adam Weeks, learn how to harness the power of AI in conjunction with Cisco Webex SDKs to open up a world of possibilities for developers to create cutting-edge applications.</p> <h6>📊Exploring the Webex Calling Reports &amp; Analytics APIs</h6><p>In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/exploring-the-webex-calling-reports-and-analytics-apis'>recent article</a> by Webex Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti, discover how Reports and Analytics APIs for Webex Calling can provide detailed call data and metrics to drive performance and decision-making. See how these APIs power integrations that automate large bulk reporting tasks and transform raw Webex Calling metrics into strategic organizational assets.</p> <h6>🛠️Working with the SDKs on the Updated Webex Meeting Suite Platform</h6><p>The updated <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/m61d8eb/Webex-App-%7C-About-the-Webex-Suite-meeting-platform' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Meeting Suite Platform</a> (WMSP) makes SDK integrations even more powerful! In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/changes-to-the-meetings-server-api-and-sdks-as-they-relate-to-the-webex-suite-meeting-platform'>helpful new blog post</a>, Software Engineer, Raffaele Lagana, provides a great overview of the <strong>WMSP</strong> and the steps required to migrate existing Webex SDK workflows over to the updated environment. </p> <h6>📺Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On May 15th at 1:00PM ET, join our public webinar where we will <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Tap into the Webex Web Calling SDK</a>. This session is ideal for developers who are looking to integrate basic Webex Calling features into their applications or for current users who want to update their systems with the latest Webex technology. Learn how to effortlessly integrate audio calling capabilities into your solutions, enhancing the way your users connect and collaborate. <a href='https://cisco.webex.com/weblink/register/r4d5879627fcb06c7bc511a6ec34847d3' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register here</a> for the live event.</p> <p>Also, in case you missed our last webinar, Webex Contact Center Flow Designer for Developers, you can watch the recording on our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a>.</p> <h6>📣Announcing the Webex Web Meetings SDK V3</h6><p>We are pleased to announce the launch of the updated Webex Meetings SDK V3 that includes some great new features. In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/announcing-the-launch-of-webex-web-meetings-sdk-v3'>new blog post</a> by Software Engineer, Kesava Krishnan Madavan, learn all about everything new in the SDK, such as enhanced media management capabilities, powerful video and audio effects, and access to our industry-leading transcription system.</p> <h6>🚰Updated iOS SDK Kitchen Sink App with SwiftUI</h6><p>Get ready to unlock the full potential of mobile app development with the updated Webex iOS Kitchen Sink app, now powered by SwiftUI! 🚀 In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/revamping-the-ios-kitchen-sink-ui-for-enhanced-developer-experience-with-swiftui'>blog post</a> by Software Engineer, Akshay Agarwal, he unveils the sleek, responsive new interface of this demo app, with a refreshed modular design that includes all the latest industry standards that mobile developers expect.</p> <h6>📝Webex API Changelog Highlights</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Webex API Changelog</a> has several recent entries listed. We always recommend checking that page frequently to stay up to date. Here are some important ones to note:</p> <ul> <li><strong>April 23, 2024 - NEW:</strong> We&#39;re pleased to introduce a new webhook resource to our Service App&#39;s framework, allowing you to receive notifications for the authorization and deauthorization of your Service Apps. This update simplifies lifecycle management and reduces the need for manual status checks. For setup instructions and more details, please visit our <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/webhooks/create-a-webhook'>Webhooks Reference Page</a>.</li> <li><strong>April 17, 2024 – BREAKING CHANGE:</strong> As previously stated in the change log published on March 18, 2024, partners should start using the new <code>packages</code> field, which accepts a list of packages. Cisco will be deprecating and removing the support for the existing <code>package</code> field in the Wholesale Subscriber Provisioning <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-provisioning/provision-a-wholesale-subscriber'>POST</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-provisioning/update-a-wholesale-subscriber'>PUT</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-provisioning/get-a-wholesale-subscriber'>GET</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-provisioning/list-wholesale-subscribers'>LIST</a> and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/wholesale-provisioning/precheck-a-wholesale-subscriber-provisioning'>PreCheck</a> APIs on the 10th of May 2024.</li> <li><strong>March 25, 2024 – BREAKING CHANGE:</strong> As SDK users on versions prior to 3.11.0 (iOS, Android) and prior to 2.60.0 (Browser SDK) must upgrade to these or later SDK versions by July 1st, 2024. Cisco is revamping our backend systems to the Webex Meetings Suite Platform with a mandatory password requirement to join Webex meetings. Earlier SDK versions do not support this security update and you risk that your users cannot join meetings. If you cannot meet this mandatory upgrade by the designated time, please reach out to <a href='mailto:devsupport@webex.com' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>devsupport@webex.com</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Be sure to also keep tabs on the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/changelog/webex-contact-center'>Webex Contact Center API changelog page</a>, to stay current on new &amp; upcoming revisions to the Contact Center developer platform.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Navigating the AI Landscape: Industry-Specific Applications for Webex ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt7b221f006bae01de/66215b4781c8849ade37d157/ai-integrations-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Navigating the AI Landscape: Industry-Specific Applications for Webex" /> <p>Harnessing the power of artificial intelligence (AI), including advanced technologies like Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPTs), in conjunction with Cisco Webex SDKs opens a world of possibilities for developers aiming to create cutting-edge applications. By incorporating AI technologies such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), Image Recognition, and the sophisticated text generation of GPTs, developers can build solutions that not only streamline communication and collaboration but also drive innovation within various industry verticals. Here are some compelling use cases where AI, including the capabilities of GPTs, can transform how organizations operate and interact.</p> <h6>Healthcare</h6><p>AI technologies can revolutionize patient care through smarter, more responsive services. Remote patient monitoring can utilize ML and NLP to sift through patient data and wearable device inputs, providing actionable insights that help in timely healthcare interventions. AI could detect a needed intervention, and then automatically connect the patient to a remote physician via a <a href='https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collaboration-endpoints/webex-desk-series/index.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Desk Pro</a> device. Virtual health assistants, powered by Speech Recognition and NLP, and built with <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/bots'>Webex Bots</a> offer a conversational experience that simplifies the process of scheduling appointments and symptom checking. Virtual health assistants can also leverage the advanced language generation capabilities of GPTs to provide more natural and informative interactions, going beyond simple responses to offering detailed explanations, advice, and empathy, much like a human caregiver. During telehealth sessions, AI can transcribe consultations, highlight key points, and generate follow-up tasks or prescription orders, all being displayed in real-time via a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/embedded-apps'>Webex Embedded App</a>.</p> <h6>Finance</h6><p>The finance sector benefits greatly from AI through enhanced security and customer service. Real-time fraud detection systems use ML algorithms to spot irregular transaction patterns, preventing fraudulent activities by utilizing the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/compliance'>Webex Compliance APIs</a>. All of these activities could be tracked and displayed in a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/embedded-apps'>Webex Messaging Embedded App</a>. Moreover, automated customer service solutions employ NLP and Webex Bots to efficiently handle inquiries, account information requests, and aid in transactions without human intervention. GPTs can be employed to enhance automated customer service solutions, enabling the generation of complex, natural-sounding responses and comprehensive financial advice, elevating the customer experience with high-quality, personalized communication.</p> <h6>Retail</h6><p>Personalized shopping experiences are the future of retail. AI-driven ML models can analyze historical purchase data and browsing habits to recommend products tailored to each customer&#39;s preferences. Integrating Webex Meetings into retail applications can provide a platform for virtual shopping assistants. These assistants can offer live product showcases or personalized styling sessions with customers. An AI-powered <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs'>Webex Contact Center</a> can handle customer inquiries at scale, using machine learning to direct customers to the right information or service agent, based on their purchase history and preferences.</p> <h6>Manufacturing</h6><p>In the realm of manufacturing, Machine Learning algorithms are pivotal for predictive maintenance, analyzing sensor data to predict and schedule timely repairs, thus reducing costly downtime. This proactive approach is complemented by Image Recognition, which enhances quality control by identifying defects in real time. Both technologies seamlessly integrate with Webex, where custom bots can promptly alert technicians, and the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/webex-meetings-sdk-web-introduction'>Meetings SDK</a> can offer live video streams for immediate oversight, ensuring a streamlined, efficient production workflow. &#xa0;</p> <h6>Wrapping Up</h6><p>By integrating AI with the powerful communication tools offered by the Webex Developer Ecosystem, developers can craft applications that not only meet but exceed the evolving needs of these verticals. The innovation potential is vast, and as AI technology, especially GPTs, continues to progress, so will the capabilities of applications and bots within the Webex ecosystem.</p> <p>For developers seeking to create the next generation of collaborative and interactive applications, the combination of AI and Webex SDKs provides a robust foundation. Explore how you can incorporate these technologies into your solutions and drive your industry forward by exploring our <a data-type='internal' to='/'>Developer Portal</a>.</p> ]]>
...
</description>
