<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Exploring the Webex Calling Reports and Analytics APIs ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4b60c6c62979fe74/662293bc528fc167c05594cf/webex-calling---reports-analytics-apis-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Exploring the Webex Calling Reports and Analytics APIs" /> <p><a href='https://www.webex.com/suite/enterprise-cloud-calling.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Calling</a> is an enterprise-grade, cloud phone system with a full range of features for businesses of all sizes. The Webex Calling platform also offers a wide set of APIs for building powerful integrations that extend and enhance out-of-the-box functionality. These integrations can automate bulk operations, real-time call actions, and other tasks that run on a long-term basis, which makes them particularly useful for large enterprises and service providers.</p> <p>The Webex Calling APIs fall into three fundamental categories that correlate with the stages of phone call interactions - pre-call setup, in-call management, and post-call analysis. First, the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/guides/webex-calling-provisioning-apis'>Provisioning APIs</a> that manage initial calling configurations and onboarding before calls are made. These are mainly administrator-level functions that are otherwise done manually, one at a time in Control Hub. The second category contains the <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-calling-getting-started-with-call-control-apis'>Call Control APIs</a>, for managing real-time actions during calls and furnishing data on current and past calls. This article will concentrate on the third category, which is for managing post-call processes with the <strong>Reports &amp; Analytics APIs</strong>. We will explore how integrations can leverage both the Reports APIs to generate and retrieve comprehensive call reports for a Webex Calling organization, and the Detailed Call History API to efficiently gather detailed historical call information.</p> <p>To get a better idea of what kind of integrations can be built with these APIs, there are some great examples listed in the <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex App Hub</a>. One of these integrations is from our partner, <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/imagicle-call-analytics-imagicle' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Imagicle</a>. Their app utilizes the APIs in intuitive ways to extend the standard Webex report tools with over 50 different reports that analyze telephone traffic, costs, and customer service performances. Another reporting integration is from our partner, <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/microcall-cdr-reporting-micro-tel-inc' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Microcall</a>. Their app gathers call detail records (CDRs) to power dashboards for managers, to help them maintain their voice infrastructure and make data-driven decisions.</p> <h6>Report Templates</h6><p>There are a variety of <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nmug598/Reports-for-Your-Cloud-Collaboration-Portfolio#Cisco_Concept.dita_6136cd51-f6a4-427f-9da9-0cfb89be6330' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Calling report templates</a> available for administrators to configure inside Control Hub. Once they are setup in Control Hub, these templates can be used by integrations to create reports via the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports'>Webex Reports API</a>, which is available for organizations with <a href='https://www.cisco.com/go/pro-pack' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Pro Pack for Cisco Webex</a>. To get familiarized with how report templates work in Control Hub, check out this <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nmug598/Reports-for-Your-Cloud-Collaboration-Portfolio' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>help article</a> first.</p> <p>Each report template contains different types of Webex Calling data to track several kinds of statistical details. The data included in these reports are generated the following day, which can be up to 24 hours after a call has completed. The standard report templates for Webex Calling are as follows:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Detailed Call History Report</strong> – contains a comprehensive log of call information, such as timestamps, call duration, call status, and the identities of both the initiator and receiver of the calls, that can be used to view high-level trends or inspect specific call types. More information about the Call History Report can be found in the <a href='https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/unified-communications/webex-calling/220377-understand-detailed-call-history-report.html' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>support docs</a>.</li> <li><strong>Calling Media Quality Report</strong> - contains metrics for media quality of calls, such as latency, jitter, and packet loss for each call leg that had an established Webex Calling media session. This report can be leveraged to monitor and assess the quality of voice and video calls within an organization to improve the user experience.</li> <li><strong>Calling Engagement Report</strong> - provides insights into how users in an organization are utilizing the Webex Calling system, including valuable metrics such as call volume, usage patterns, and adoption rates over time. This is used to better understand the ways employees are interacting with the system, identify trends in calling behavior, and evaluate the effectiveness of the tools provided.</li> <li><strong>Calling Quality Report</strong> - contains quality metrics for calls made or received by users specifically within the Webex Calling app, such as jitter, latency, and packet loss. This helps administrators to better pinpoint and troubleshoot quality issues on the client side.</li> <li><strong>Call Queue Stats Report</strong> – provides details of call queues that have been set up in an organization, such as the number of incoming calls, wait times, call abandonment rates, and the efficiency of call handling by agents. This report can be instrumental for managers to assess how well their call queues are operating and identify areas for improvement.</li> <li><strong>Call Queue agent stats report</strong> – provides detailed analysis of all the agents that have been assigned to call queues in an organization, to get insight on an agent’s number of calls handled, average handle time, and service level achievements. Supervisors can utilize this report to monitor and optimize agent productivity, assess workload distribution, and ensure that customer service objectives are met.</li> <li><strong>Auto-attendant stats summary</strong> – details statistics of calls routed to auto-attendants in an organization, such as the volume of calls received, the number of calls handled by the auto-attendant, and caller selections within the menu. This data helps administrators understand how effective the auto-attendant is at managing incoming calls and identify any changes that might be needed to improve caller experience and call routing efficiency.</li> <li><strong>Auto-attendant business &amp; after-hours key details</strong> – contains information about calls routed to auto-attendants during specified business and after-hours periods. This report breaks down the interaction patterns of callers with the auto-attendant, showing which menu options are selected during different times of the day. This can help administrators discern call distribution and caller behavior during office hours versus after-hours, enabling them to tailor the auto-attendant system for improved efficiency and customer service.</li> </ul> <p>For organizations that want to tailor their reports with specific data, <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nmug598/Reports-for-Your-Cloud-Collaboration-Portfolio#reference_rs5_z52_nsb' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>custom templates</a> can also be configured and setup inside Control Hub.</p> <h6>Traversing the Reports APIs</h6><p>Once the templates are in order, the APIs can be leveraged to create a report. To work with the Reports APIs, an administrator-level integration with the <code>analytics:read_all</code> scope will be required. For more information on getting started with the Reports API, check out the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/admin#reports-api'>administrator developer guide</a>.</p> <p>Generally, the first endpoint used in a workflow is the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/report-templates'>List Report Templates API</a>, for retrieving all the templates from the administrator’s organization. An example JSON response from this API will look something like this:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;items&quot; : [ { &quot;Id&quot; : 130, &quot;title&quot; : &quot;Agent Activity&quot;, &quot;service&quot; : &quot;Calling&quot;, &quot;maxDays&quot; : 31, &quot;identifier&quot; : &quot;queueStats&quot;, &quot;validations&quot; : [ { &quot;field&quot; : &quot;templateId&quot;, &quot;required&quot; : &quot;yes&quot; } ] } ], &quot;numberOfTemplate&quot; : 1 } </code></pre> <p>Each template listed in the response body has a unique ID value that is used in subsequent API calls for creating and managing reports.</p> <p>Next in this workflow, the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports/create-a-report'>Create a Report API</a> is used to generate a new report from a chosen template. The <code>templateId</code> retrieved in the last API call is the only required parameter for this endpoint. A <code>startDate</code> and/or <code>endDate</code> can also be optionally included, to specify the range of the report.</p> <p>In this example, the process is initiated with an API call to <code>/v1/reports</code> with the following content:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;templateId&quot;: 130, &quot;startDate&quot;: &quot;2024-02-01&quot;, &quot;endDate&quot;: &quot;2024-02-05&quot; } </code></pre> <p>The new report gets created and the response body will look something like this:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;items&quot;: { &quot;id&quot;: &quot;YWE0MzFmZWM0ZmE&quot; } } </code></pre> <p>Be sure to make note of the report <code>id</code> that is included in the response, which is needed in the next step to check the status of the report and get the download URL. </p> <p>While the report is being generated, the <code>status</code> can be checked with the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports/get-report-details'>Get Report Details API</a>, using the ID you noted in the previous step. An example response can look like this:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &quot;id&quot;: &quot;YWE0MzFmZWM0ZmE&quot;, &quot;title&quot;: &quot;Agent Activity&quot;, &quot;service&quot;: &quot;Calling&quot;, &quot;startDate&quot;: &quot;2020-02-01&quot;, &quot;endDate&quot;: &quot;2020-02-05&quot;, &quot;siteList&quot;: &quot;calling.example.com&quot;, &quot;created&quot;: &quot;2024-04-01 17:13:39&quot;, &quot;createdBy&quot;: &quot;Yzf6GbAmQMD0YeB&quot;, &quot;scheduledFrom&quot;: &quot;API&quot;, &quot;status&quot;: &quot;done&quot;, &quot;downloadURL&quot;: https://downloadservicebts.webex.com/api?reportId=YWE0MzFmZWM0ZmE } </code></pre> <p>In this example, the report <code>status</code> is <code>done</code> and a link is provided in the <code>downloadURL</code> property that can be used to retrieve the report. If the report is still in the process of being generated, the <code>status</code> will indicate <code>&quot;In progress&quot;</code>.</p> <p>Each report can be downloaded up to 30 times and organizations may keep up to 50 reports at any time. After creating and downloading a report, it should be then deleted to make room for the next report using the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports/delete-a-report'>Delete a Report API</a>. This endpoint only needs the <code>reportID</code> value to delete a report. When a deletion is successful, the API returns a <code>200</code>-response code.</p> <h6>Webex Detailed Call History API</h6><p>For scenarios that require quicker retrieval of call detail records, perhaps before the Webex-generated reports are compiled the next day, there is another API available. The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/reports-detailed-call-history'>Webex Detailed Call History API</a> provides a more expedient, programmatic way to retrieve <strong>call detail records</strong> (CDRs) for calls completed from 48 hours to as recent as 5 minutes ago.</p> <p>The first step to start using the Webex Detailed Call History API is to enable user access in the “Administrator roles” section of Webex Control Hub, as shown here:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc5fcb98857c2174d/webex-calling---reports-analytics-apis-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Once the API access is granted in Control Hub, integrations will just need to enable the <code>spark-admin:calling_cdr_read</code> and the <code>spark-admin:locations_read</code> scopes to start using the API.</p> <p>While the Detailed Call History API works much like the other Webex APIs, the endpoint has a unique “analytics” URL: <code>analytics.webexapis.com/v1/cdr_feed</code>.</p> <p>There are four query parameters accepted here: <code>startTime</code> (required), <code>endTime</code> (required), <code>locations</code> (optional filter by locations within an organization), and <code>max</code> (optional number of results per page). The Detailed Call History API returns the CDRs in JSON format, providing over 50 points of data. This example response body shows the data that can be obtained from a Webex Calling CDR:</p> <pre><code class="language-json"> &quot;items&quot;: [ { &quot;Answer indicator&quot;: &quot;Yes&quot;, &quot;Answer time&quot;: &quot;2024-03-14T11:01:17.551Z&quot;, &quot;Answered&quot;: &quot;true&quot;, &quot;Authorization code&quot;: &quot;107&quot;, &quot;Call ID&quot;: &quot;SSE1101163211405201218829100@10.177.4.29&quot;, &quot;Call outcome&quot;: &quot;Success&quot; &quot;Call outcome reason&quot;: &quot;Normal&quot;, &quot;Call transfer Time&quot;: &quot;2024-03-14T18:21:29.707Z&quot;, &quot;Call type&quot;: &quot;SIP_ENTERPRISE&quot;, &quot;Called line ID&quot;: &quot;CALLEDCLIDGOESHERE&quot;, &quot;Called number&quot;: &quot;2002&quot;, &quot;Calling line ID&quot;: &quot;YOURCLIDGOESHERE&quot;, &quot;Calling number&quot;: &quot;2001&quot;, &quot;Client type&quot;: &quot;SIP_TOLLFREE&quot;, &quot;Client version&quot;: &quot;1.0.2.3&quot;, &quot;Correlation ID&quot;: &quot;8e8e1dc7-4f25-4595-b9c7-26237f824535&quot;, &quot;Department ID&quot;: &quot;4370c763-81ec-403b-aba3-626a7b1cf264&quot;, &quot;Device MAC&quot;: &quot;6C710D8ABC10&quot;, &quot;Dialed digits&quot;: &quot;1246&quot;, &quot;Direction&quot;: &quot;ORIGINATING&quot;, &quot;Duration&quot;: 36, &quot;Final local SessionID&quot;: &quot;82bb753300105000a0000242be131609&quot;, &quot;Final remote SessionID&quot;: &quot;cfe67b8a00105000a0000242be131609&quot;, &quot;Inbound trunk&quot;: &quot;InTrunk&quot;, &quot;International country&quot;: &quot;US&quot;, &quot;Local call ID&quot;: &quot;113104021:0&quot;, &quot;Local SessionID&quot;: &quot;82bb753300105000a0000242be131609&quot;, &quot;Location&quot;: &quot;Richardson&quot;, &quot;Model&quot;: &quot;8851-3PCC&quot;, &quot;Network call ID&quot;: &quot;BW2356451711108231501755806@10.21.0.192&quot;, &quot;Org UUID&quot;: &quot;408806bc-a013-4a4b-9a24-85e374912102&quot;, &quot;Original reason&quot;: &quot;UserBusy&quot;, &quot;OS type&quot;: &quot;na&quot;, &quot;Outbound trunk&quot;: &quot;OutTrunk&quot;, &quot;Release time&quot;: &quot;2023-10-12 21:22:32.621&quot;, &quot;Ring duration&quot;: 23, &quot;Redirect reason&quot;: &quot;Unavailable&quot;, &quot;Redirecting number&quot;: &quot;+13343822691&quot;, &quot;Related call ID&quot;: &quot;760583469:0&quot;, &quot;Related reason&quot;: &quot;CallQueue&quot;, &quot;Releasing party&quot;: &quot;Remote&quot;, &quot;Remote call ID&quot;: &quot;113103977:0&quot;, &quot;Remote SessionID&quot;: &quot;6bf2f47800105000a0000242be13160a&quot;, &quot;Report ID&quot;: &quot;0a0c2eb7-f1f6-3326-86f9-565d2e11553d&quot;, &quot;Report time&quot;: &quot;2020-05-14T11:01:52.723Z&quot;, &quot;Route group&quot;: &quot;RouteGrpAA&quot;, &quot;Site main number&quot;: &quot;+14692281000&quot;, &quot;Site timezone&quot;: &quot;-300&quot;, &quot;Site UUID&quot;: &quot;474d4f70-4ef5-4d52-9e1d-b207086629e0&quot;, &quot;Start time&quot;: &quot;2020-05-14T11:01:16.545Z&quot;, &quot;Sub client type&quot;: &quot;MOBILE_NETWORK&quot;, &quot;Transfer related call ID&quot;: &quot;2340586843:0A&quot;, &quot;User&quot;: &quot;John Andersen&quot;, &quot;User number&quot;: &quot;+81546668399&quot;, &quot;User type&quot;: &quot;User&quot;, &quot;User UUID&quot;: &quot;47f0d0c2-f05a-44cc-870d-7a3daf859c6c&quot; } ] } </code></pre> <p>This call data can then be used to build custom reporting integrations, power management dashboards, and more. For detailed information and a demo on how to use the Detailed Called History API, see this <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/webex-detailed-call-history-api'>helpful blog post</a> by Collaboration Technical Solutions Architect, Justin Haefner.</p> <h6>Have Any Questions? Ask Us!</h6><p>There was a lot of information covered here and naturally, questions may arise. The good news? Our <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by, ready and happy to assist. Alternatively, feel free to join or kick off a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Embedded Apps on Room Series Devices ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte240b2a440b80b31/6627d608528fc128dd55acfa/ea-collab-and-preso-mode-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Embedded Apps on Room Series Devices" /> <p>Today if you are a Cisco device user, you can interact with <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/embedded-apps'>Embedded Apps</a> such as <a href='https://www.slido.com/cisco-webex-polling' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Slido</a>, <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/shared-timer-cisco-systems-22689' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Shared Timer</a>, and <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/miro-miro-79512-22774' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Miro</a> in meetings if you a join a meeting with touch-capable devices such as the Board and Desk Pro series.</p> <p>Previously, users on <a href='https://roomos.cisco.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>RoomOS</a> devices were not able to view Embedded Apps once they were launched in a meeting. To enhance this experience, we are expanding the coverage of Embedded Apps on RoomOS devices as well. This will allow more users to be better involved in meetings, especially when Embedded Apps are initiated in those meetings.</p> <h6>Feature details</h6><p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6553652f2671a53d/ea-collab-and-preso-mode-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>RoomOS Devices</h6><p>An Embedded app can have one of 2 orientations based on how they appear on the Webex desktop app once initiated. The first is the main view orientation. Main view orientation is for apps that appear in the stage of the Webex app. Example of main view apps are Miro and Mural. There is also the side panel orientation, where, once the app is initialized, it appears in the right-side panel of the Webex app.</p> <p>Once a main view app is initialized from the Webex App desktop client (starting atbversion 44.12), users on Room OS device (starting at version 11.13.1.5) will be able to view a video stream of the initiator’s view (that is, what the initiator is seeing on their embedded app’s screen). Please note that this video stream has a lower priority than screen share, and therefore, if a user on the Webex app starts a screen share, that replaces the app’s video stream.</p> <p>For side panel apps, in this first iteration we support the Slido and Shared Timer apps. Those apps are loaded on the Room OS devices on the right panel of the screen. Due to the nature of the Room OS device, users are not be able to participate in polls initiated by the Slido app. For that reason, the Slido app on the Room OS device will show a QR code, and users can scan it with mobile devices to participate in polls if desired.</p> <h6>DX, MX, and SX Series Devices</h6><p>The same criteria apply to DX, MX, and SX devices, the only difference being that the Slido and Shared timer apps are not supported in this first iteration while apps rendered in the Webex main view are.</p> <p>&#xa0;</p> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Design Delightful Customer Experiences with Webex Contact Center Flow Designer ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt19fca14280936bf4/6627c5e6fb977c062736a903/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Design Delightful Customer Experiences with Webex Contact Center Flow Designer" /> <p>Today&#39;s customers expect a certain standard when interacting with a Contact Center. They expect a personalized experience that acknowledges their preferences, an understanding of their issue, and a swift, efficient resolution without repetitive information or unnecessary checks and processes. Furthermore, they prefer not to be shuffled between different teams due to a lack of available information, often leading to speaking with multiple agents to resolve their issues.</p> <p>By leveraging deep integrations with existing enterprise data, developers can differentiate customer experiences for Contact Centers by tying together disparate enterprise systems with the help of a single orchestration platform, leading to exceptional customer satisfaction.</p> <p>Webex Contact Center is powered by the Flow Designer platform for orchestration and automation, enabling developers to design robust, data-driven integrations effortlessly through a no-code low-code interface.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt5e4e39bc8d6490a2/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>With its intuitive, visual canvas, Flow Designer simplifies the development process, encouraging collaboration between developers and business stakeholders, enabling the creation of applications that provide superior customer experiences.</p> <p>This article details the specific interfaces offered by Flow Designer for integrations, and demonstrates how to incorporate personalization at every step, harnessing the platform&#39;s full capabilities.</p> <h6>Integrating Data Intelligence into Flow Designer</h6><p>To provide a seamless customer experience for Contact Center callers, various stages in a contact flow can leverage deep integrations for personalization:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Caller Identification:</strong> Quickly identify who the caller is and the reason for their call with the least amount of caller input, re-prompting, or tiring menus.</li> <li><strong>Customer Authentication:</strong> Workflows to ensure the customer’s authenticity is verified with the business, to complete the transaction.</li> <li><strong>Problem Identification:</strong> Efficiently pinpoint their issue without subjecting them to lengthy self-service navigation or extended hold times.</li> <li><strong>Data Retrieval Specific to the Problem:</strong> Gather all the relevant data needed automatically to resolve their issue.</li> <li><strong>Intelligent Routing Using Insights from Data:</strong> Direct the caller to the appropriate expert swiftly, ensuring that all pertinent information is readily available, before, during, and after the interaction with the bot or the agent.</li> <li><strong>Post-Contact Actions and Intelligence:</strong> Validate the caller&#39;s intent and how the service could have been improved. Automate actions within backend systems after concluding a call.</li> </ul> <p>The Flow Designer platform features a data-driven orchestration layer at its core, enhancing the Contact Center experience by making it more conversational and personalized. This involves selecting the optimal agent pools or queues and providing agents with key information, coupled with the capability to orchestrate post-call actions for callers.</p> <p>At a high level, Flow Designer can transform standard contact flows into highly personalized interactions for each caller. It achieves this by utilizing deep integrations with existing enterprise applications and tailoring experiences to individual caller profiles. The platform leverages intelligent data about the caller for custom orchestration, can exchange this data with virtual agents (bots), can employ intelligent routing through data-driven agent selection, equipping agents with the necessary context, and orchestrating post-contact actions with event flows that leverage connected data payloads.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt717d2731fa076e72/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Let us understand the interfaces that serve as points of integration when designing flows.</p> <h6>Interfaces for Designing Intelligent Contact Flows</h6><p>The Flow Designer canvas provides a range of activities (nodes) that can be connected to craft-specific experiences. Each activity includes an input and one or more outputs, depending on its functionality, and generates output variables that other activities can reference. Specific activities feature explicit interfaces for connecting to external systems and utilizing their data within the platform. These activities are seamlessly integrated to facilitate ongoing interactions with external applications throughout the contact lifecycle. A deep understanding of these interfaces unlocks use cases through integrations with external systems.</p> <h6>HTTP Activity</h6><p>The HTTP Activity serves as the crucial point for interfacing with external systems. It provides the ability to target an external system and configure common “Custom Connectors” centrally on Control Hub, which can then be invoked across flows. Data can be retrieved from external systems using HTTP (GET) and shared with them using other supported verbs (PUT/POST/DELETE). Effective use of the HTTP activity can determine the success of the orchestration.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt44b46c3c54aaab74/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>For more information, see <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/7fuy63/Set-up-integration-connectors-for-Webex-Contact-Center' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Setting up Integration Connectors for Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</a>.</p> <h6>Virtual Agent</h6><p>The Virtual Agent (VA) activity enables the transfer of custom data from Flow to a virtual agent when initiating a bot within the orchestration. It allows passing custom data to the VA, connecting with 3rd party systems from within the VA, and finally retrieving data from the VA, along with the transcript of the bot interaction. Customizing bot interactions for each customer starts with the use of &quot;Event State” and “Event Data&quot; within the Virtual Agent activity. This allows developers to send custom data payloads to Virtual Agents, which can then personalize messages and carry out backend &quot;fulfillment&quot; actions using this data by integrating with external systems. When the call is escalated from the VA, control is passed back into Flow along with the data that was used within the VA. This is critical for a connected experience.</p> <p>For more information, see <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n6gaghu/Configure-Virtual-Agent-Voice-in-Webex-Contact-Center' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Configuring Virtual Agents on Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</a>.</p> <h6>Dynamic Speech Activities</h6><p>The Flow Designer&#39;s media activities, such as &quot;Play Message,&quot; &quot;Collect Digits,&quot; &quot;Menu,&quot; etc., support dynamic text-to-speech (TTS), which enables the embedding of custom data within utterances for personalized interactions with callers. Using expressions to inject custom data effectively, along with Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to modify speech intonations, ensures personalization at the self-service stage of the call.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blta1a79bfd265663be/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Queue Activities</h6><p>The Queue activity enables the definition of Skills-Based Routing Queues, specifically in the configuration that uses &quot;TEXT&quot;-based skills. These can be used to route callers by leveraging custom data to identify suitable agents from the pool. Additionally, the “Queue To Agent” Activity can target the call to a specified agent using their ID or email, if data intelligence systems are leveraged to target a specific agent for the contact.</p> <h6>Screen Pop</h6><p>The Screen Pop activity allows the embedding of custom data into the chosen webpage via query parameters, which accept custom variables defined in Flow. Customizing Screen Pops per agent, team, queue, and customer is possible by using conditional or case statements before a Screen Pop activity.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt9a99cf6205719d48/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Subflows</h6><p>The new Subflow activity enables developers to package reusable functionality for use in any number of flows by providing an easy method to include this functionality, pass inputs into the subflow, and return outputs to the main flow. This allows developers to build modular, reusable structures in the form of subflows, dynamically passing data to change the subflow&#39;s behavior. It also increases the efficiency of building flows while providing the same interfaces (HTTP, Collect Digits, Screen Pop) as connections to external systems within the subflow.</p> <h6>Data Definitions for Effective Flow Design</h6><p>Understanding the types of data accessible within Flow is essential for personalization. Flow provides an extensive list of variable types and data definitions, across various data types. Each of the variables are tailored to personalization and customization:</p> <h6>Local Variables</h6><p>The cornerstone of personalization is defining custom variables to store business-specific and caller-specific information. Within Flow, local variables can be passed to other flows through the GoTo activity or the Subflow activity. They can also be displayed on the Agent Desktop, with customization options available in Flow Designer.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc9774fbf5db81d0b/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-7.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Global Variables</h6><p>These special variables are defined at the organization level and used across multiple flows, particularly for reporting purposes. When set within a flow, global variables can be reported in Analyzer. Local variables can be collected by global variables for use in reporting.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt28c35ad1b0fa40f4/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-8.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Caller Associated Data (CAD) Variables</h6><p>Both local and global variables can be marked as Agent Viewable or Agent Editable, controlling their visibility and editability on the Agent Desktop. Agent viewable variables appear on the Desktop, whereas agent editable variables can be modified on the Desktop. Post-call event flows will then reflect the updated variable values for Flow Designer to use.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf2114c9b93bdd473/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-9.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Activity Output Variables</h6><p>These variables are generated when a specific activity in Flow executes. They can be used alongside the user-defined local or global variables mentioned above.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8be8e49a19b33540/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-10.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Event Output Variables</h6><p>The Flow Designer supports &quot;Event Flows&quot; that include a wide range of event activities triggered by various scenarios, such as when the flow selects an agent, an agent connects, or a call ends. These activities facilitate the orchestration of post-call actions. The event activities provide various output variables that can be utilized to personalize the experiences of both agents and callers.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd7c81da24e07a15f/flow-designer-data-for-devs-blog-11.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Bringing it All Together: Add Intelligence to an Existing Flow</h6><p>Assuming you have built your initial flow with simple messages, menus, and call queuing for the agent, let us enhance this design across each stage of the contact flow. Here is how we would incorporate personalization at every step, transforming the customer experience into a differentiated orchestration that is data-driven:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Define a List of Custom Variables in Flow:</strong> Use Flow Designer to construct a data structure comprising customer data, agent data, and other relevant contact center information. Create flow variables to identify the customer, understand their issue, and determine the appropriate agent for queuing – and leverage Global variables for reporting on flow-related events and actions.</li> <li><strong>Leverage External Data Integrations Using the HTTP Activity:</strong> Utilize the caller’s identification (ANI) or prompt the caller to input digits (e.g., an Account ID) to interface with an external API (Application Programming Interface) or CRM (Customer Relationship Management) system. Update external systems with call information throughout the contact&#39;s lifecycle to record the progress.</li> <li><strong>Personalize Self-Service with Enhanced TTS (Text-To-Speech)</strong> Leverage the power of data by building expressions into every speech activity with the help of <code>{{expressions}}</code> and SSML into text-to-speech messaging, personalizing prompts for customers for a more conversational experience.</li> <li><strong>Provide the Right Information to the Agent:</strong> Use Caller Associated Data (CAD) variables within Flow Designer and make them viewable and editable for the agent on the canvas. Reorder the Agent visible information and order of the variables on the Interaction pane settings.</li> <li><strong>Surface the Right Applications to the Agent:</strong> Employ the Screen Pop activity within the Event Flows to transmit the correct data into third-party applications, aiding in customer identification. Use the query parameters and expressions to “<code>{{inject}}</code>” custom data within the screen pop URLs.</li> <li><strong>Leverage Widgets in the Desktop That Use These Variables:</strong> Widgets on the desktop can access and manipulate variables passed from Flow Designer through the Desktop Layout and Desktop JS SDK. This integration means that the pertinent data from Flow Designer can be utilized by third-party widgets on the desktop, thus enhancing the data connectivity for agents.</li> <li><strong>Utilize Event Flows for Post-Agent Actions:</strong> Employ Event Flows and Event Output Variables after calls to orchestrate custom post-contact actions by coupling these with conditions, and case statements to tailor it per agent, per queue, or even per caller. By leveraging the Feedback activity in tandem with the HTTP activity, one can integrate with external applications that utilize post-contact data for insights and analytics following the interaction.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>The Webex Contact Center Flow Designer provides a powerful platform for orchestrating and automating personalized customer interactions through deep data integrations and intelligent workflow automation. The use of HTTP activities, Virtual Agents, and Screen pops, along with Text-to-speech enabled activities enables developers to craft differentiated solutions that address specific customer needs while maintaining flexibility and scalability. By effectively leveraging these in different stages of the contact such as Customer Identification, Authentication, Payments, Problem Identification, Intelligent Routing, Desktop Integrations, and more, businesses can ensure a seamless and efficient customer experience that minimizes friction and enhances satisfaction. </p> <p>Looking ahead, Businesses should focus on enhancing data integration strategies, expanding the use of analytics for real-time decision-making within flows, and further customizing user experiences based on emerging customer trends. By doing so, companies can differentiate their CX and exceed customer expectations in an increasingly competitive landscape.</p> <h6>Ready to take your integrations to the next level?</h6><p>Spin up a Webex Contact Center sandbox at <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/sandbox_cc'>https://developer.webex.com/webex-contact-center/docs/sandbox_cc</a> with live numbers and out-of-box flows today and experience the future of integration development with Webex Contact Center Flow Designer!</p> <p>For more information on Flow Designer, register for our Webinar: Flow Designer for Developers at <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>https://developer.webex.com/webinars</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Announcing the Launch of Webex Web Meetings SDK V3 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt0e2c7456fd6190dc/662298bfb0544137b499bdd4/webex-meetings-sdk-v3-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Announcing the Launch of Webex Web Meetings SDK V3" /> <p>We are excited to announce our latest iteration of the Webex Meetings SDK: V3.0, with enhanced media management capabilities, powerful video and audio effects, and access to our industry-leading transcription system. Whether you&#39;re working on a small-scale project or a complex application, our simple yet powerful SDK is set to deliver an exceptional meeting experience. In this blog, we will be looking into the sparkling new features, exploring various use cases, and guiding you on how to get started.</p> <h6>What is a Webex Web SDK?</h6><p>Before diving into the new release, let&#39;s clarify what the Webex Web SDK is. An SDK, or Software Development Kit, is like a toolbox for developers. It contains all the necessary components, such as libraries, documentation, code samples, and guides, that developers need to integrate specific features into their applications. The Webex Web SDK is one such kit designed to embed Webex&#39;s powerful meeting capabilities directly into web apps, offering users a seamless video conferencing experience without ever leaving your application.</p> <h6>Key Features of the Meetings V3 SDK</h6><p>Are you ready to boost your web app&#39;s meeting features like never before with the new Meetings V3 SDK? We&#39;ve made everything simpler and more powerful. Check out these cool upgrades:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Instant Media Magic:</strong> Add awesome effects in a snap! Blur your background, swap it with a virtual one, or cut out the background noise to keep everyone focused.</li> <li><strong>Smarter Captions:</strong> Be integrative and inclusive with Closed Captions. Foreign speakers or attendees with disabilities can keep up in real time.</li> </ul> <p>And that&#39;s not all – we&#39;ve freshened up our Kitchen Sink app too. It&#39;s now easier to find and play with features, including all these fantastic new updates.</p> <h6>Real-World Applications for the Meetings SDK</h6><p>The Webex Meetings SDK V3 unlocks a world of potential for various industries. Here&#39;s how it can be put to great use:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Educational apps</strong> can create engaging virtual classrooms for students and teachers.</li> <li><strong>Medical apps</strong> can offer private and secure telehealth appointments.</li> <li><strong>Banking apps</strong> can connect customers and agents smoothly for document processing and consultations.</li> </ul> <p>Best of all, you can get started on building your app with a free sandbox right away.</p> <h6>The Shelve Apps Powered by the Meetings SDK</h6><p>Here are some of the shelve applications that are utilizing the capabilities of the Meetings SDK to provide seamless meeting experiences:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Webex Web Client:</strong> Using the Web SDK, the Webex Web client brings the ultimate experience of Webex meetings to your web browser. <a href='https://web.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Visit the Webex Web Client here</a>.</li> <li><strong>Webex Widgets:</strong> Also utilizing the Web SDK, these widgets integrate meeting features directly into your website or service with minimal effort. <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/widgets'>Learn more here</a>.</li> <li><strong>Webex Instant Connect:</strong> Offering a quick meeting experience through the Web SDK, Instant Connect simplifies patient and doctor interactions. <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/sv0h2ab/Webex-Instant-Connect' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Learn more here</a>.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>What’s Next?</h6><p>Our efforts don&#39;t stop here. We are already working on more advanced SDK features including:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Multi-Stream Media</strong> - This will help you set the layout of your application as required instead of just using the presets offered by Webex. We will be announcing a beta program for this soon. Stay tuned by signing up to <a href='https://gobeta.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>the Webex Beta Program</a>.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Quick Start</h6><p>To get started with the Webex Meetings SDK quickly, please refer to this <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Introduction-to-Webex-Meetings' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>introductory guide</a>.</p> <h6>Packages</h6><br/> <ul> <li><a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/webex' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>NPM package</a></li> <li><a href='https://unpkg.com/webex@3.3.1/umd/webex.min.js' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>CDN Package</a></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Helpful Links</h6><br/> <ul> <li><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Web SDK Documentation</a></li> <li><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Migrating-SDK-Version-1-or-Version-2-to-Version-3' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Migrating from SDK V1/V2 to V3</a></li> <li><a href='https://webex.github.io/webex-js-sdk/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Kitchen Sink App</a></li> <li><a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/tree/next/docs/samples' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Source code of Kitchen Sink app</a></li> </ul> <p>In addition, here&#39;s a vidcast with an overview of the new features:</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/e88ad798-d911-4e25-a5ba-c4f75740d2c3" width="100%" height="100%" title="Web Meeting SDK New Features" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <h6>Webinars</h6><p>We, the Developer Platform Web Team have planned for a series of Webinars on our SDK portfolios and the first of many to come was broadcasted a week ago through our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>Webex Developer Portal Webinars</a> space.</p> <p>The following webinar shows a live coding demo of Webex Meetings SDK V3:</p> <div style="padding-bottom:56.25%; position:relative; display:block; width: 100%"> <iframe src="https://app.vidcast.io/share/embed/bcd28aa8-ab52-46bc-8ca8-3c2aa41f8f83" width="100%" height="100%" title="Live Coding Demo for Meetings SDK V3" frameborder="0" loading="lazy" allowfullscreen style="position:absolute; top:0; left: 0;border: solid; border-radius:12px;"></iframe> </div> <br/> <p>Here&#39;s the link to the repository where the demo app of our live coding from the Webinar is published: <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-js-sdk-meeting-demo' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Samples: Meetings SDK Demo</a>.</p> <br/> <h6>Future Webinars</h6><p>Here are some of the future Webinars that can be expected from our team:</p> <ul> <li>Webex Meetings – Multi-Stream Support</li> <li>Webex Calling SDK</li> <li>Web Widgets</li> <li>Embedded Apps</li> <li>Guest Calling with Webex Calling SDK</li> <li>Contact Center SDK Flows</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Need Some Help? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are excited to provide you with support for these features. If you need help, the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and happy to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://cs.co/WebexDeveloperCommunity' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex for Developers Community Forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Changes to the Meetings Server API and SDKs, as they relate to the Webex Suite Meeting Platform ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf1868625b5569271/6616e1a7fffe40894e1e47f0/space-meetings-migration-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Changes to the Meetings Server API and SDKs, as they relate to the Webex Suite Meeting Platform" /> <p>Hello Webex Developers! We&#39;re excited to announce significant updates to the Webex SDKs that streamline the process of starting and joining meetings in spaces. These changes are designed to improve your development experience and provide users with a more secure and integrated meeting experience.</p> <p>As of the latest SDK release, we&#39;ve streamlined the meeting functionalities within spaces, which means that starting and joining a space meeting is now more straightforward and consistent across the board. These changes affect our Webex <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/browser'>Browser/JS SDK</a>, <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/ios'>iOS SDK</a>, and <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/sdks/android'>Android SDK</a>. To ensure a smooth transition, we&#39;ve prepared comprehensive migration guides that walk you through the process step-by-step.</p> <h6>What&#39;s New?</h6><p>The recent updates introduce a unified method for handling space meetings, which simplifies the codebase and reduces complexity for developers. These changes are effective from the following versions of each SDK:</p> <ul> <li>Browser SDK <strong>v2.60</strong></li> <li>Mobile SDKs <strong>v3.11</strong></li> </ul> <br/> <h6>What to Expect</h6><p>Here&#39;s a quick overview of what to expect for the migration:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Unified Meeting Objects:</strong> We have unified the meeting objects for space meetings, which means that the steps taken in all the listed SDKs to work with meetings will be similar, regardless of whether you’ve working with space meetings or regular scheduled meetings.</li> <li><strong>Enhanced Security:</strong> Meeting Password is now mandatory for non-invited guests.</li> <li><strong>Revised API Calls:</strong> Starting and joining meetings now require the creation of meetings through the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings'>/meetings</a> API, even for meetings in spaces. This is to align with how regular scheduled meetings are created.</li> <li><strong>Improved User Experience:</strong> The updates offer a seamless user experience for participants joining meetings, whether they&#39;re using Webex on a browser, iOS, or Android device.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Migration Guides</h6><p>To help you migrate to the new meeting in spaces experience, we have provided extensive migration documentation. Please refer to the following resources based on your development platform:</p> <ul> <li>Webex Browser/JS SDK Migration Guide: <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space</a></li> <li>Webex iOS SDK Migration Guide: <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space</a></li> <li>Webex Android SDK Migration Guide: <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space</a></li> <li>General Overview and Use Cases: <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/space-meetings-migration'>/docs/space-meetings-migration</a></li> </ul> <p>Each guide provides a detailed explanation of the changes, including code snippets and best practices to ensure that your migration is as smooth as possible. We’ll go into more detail on each one below.</p> <h6>Get Started</h6><p>Let’s get into it. We’ll highlight some of the main changes and how you can work through them. If you have any questions or are unsure about something, you can always reach out to the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Developer Support</a> team. For this blog’s purposes, we assume you’ve worked with our SDKs before and are comfortable with the technologies and terminology used. If you haven’t, check out our SDKs (and everything else we provide) on the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs'>Developer Portal</a>.</p> <p>We’ll start with the points that are common to all 3 SDKs, then move on to the specific cases and code snippets for each one individually.</p> <h6>Create a Developer Sandbox</h6><p>First, we recommend creating a developer sandbox to play around with and test this migration. The developer sandbox will come with all the usual features, but it will be created within the new Meeting Suite Platform, so that you can test these new features and see the changes compared to the old platform. Head over to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/space-meetings-migration'>space migration page</a> and create the sandbox request.</p> <p>Once you request the sandbox, it will be set up in the background. This may take up to 24 hours.</p> <h6>Test Out the APIs</h6><p>Once you’ve created your sandbox, you should start by testing out the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/meetings'>Meetings REST APIs</a> (herein referred to as <em>Meetings API</em>), to see what’s changed there. The changes are listed in the migration documents but let me give you the highlights below.me give you the highlights below.</p> <h6>Create a New Meeting</h6><p>One of the main changes is that if you want to create a meeting from the context of a space through the API, you now will be creating the meeting within your own meeting site. In other words, the meeting creator’s licensing and site selection dictates where the meeting will be hosted. This is irrespective of whether you’re part of the space’s owning org or an external org.</p> <p>Now, creating a meeting in a space through the API involves adding the <code>roomId</code> to the POST API request to <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/create-a-meeting'>/meetings</a> API. As mentioned, the licensing that the meeting creator has assigned determines the meetings site of the meeting, regardless of what org and site the space’s creator resides in.</p> <p>Similarly, you’re also going to see that “Instant meetings” (created by adding the <code>roomId</code> and <code>adhoc=true</code> fields in the API) will be created in the API caller’s preferred meeting site and org, which again is not necessarily going to be the same meeting site as the space creator’s meeting site. These changes should be taken note of, to ensure smooth implementation. If you plan to get data on these meetings later (for example, reporting data), you will need to be part of the meeting site where said meeting was hosted.</p> <p>The caveat to all this however, is if you’re using a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/service-apps'>Service App</a> to create meetings. Service Apps work independently of any user, therefore when you create a meeting using a Service App token, you need to add the <code>hostEmail</code> parameter so that the backend logic can determine who the host user is and create the meeting on behalf of that user. That user’s licensing and site will then determine where the meeting is hosted and what capabilities it will have.</p> <div><Callout type="info">The key change you’ll see is that you will not be able to use `roomId/spaceId` anymore within the SDKs to join meetings. You will need to use the `meetingId` or the SIP URI, both of which are found through the Meetings API. </Callout></div> <h6>Additional Points to Keep in Mind</h6><p>One point to note is that in the scenario you have users within a space from multiple external organizations than your own (as the space creator), there may be a period where your org and site may be on the new Webex platform, but other attendees may not yet be on it. This can lead to slightly different experiences (both with the SDKs and native clients), but the overall usability shouldn’t be impacted. Of course, reach out to our <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Developer Support</a> team in case of any queries or concerns.</p> <h6>The Browser SDK</h6><p>As mentioned above, the use of <code>roomId/spaceId</code> to join meetings has been removed. Instead, you’re asked to use the meeting’s <em>SIP URI</em> or <code>meetingId</code>, found with the Meetings API or by using <a href='https://webex.github.io/webex-js-sdk/api/#getallmeetings' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>getAllMeetings()</a> directly in the SDK. You can check if a site is on the Webex Suite Meeting Platform from the SDK by querying the following key. The label “unified” is the shorter internal reference to WMSP meetings:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">webex.meetings.config.experimental.enableUnifiedMeetings </code></pre> <p>This is a boolean and tells you whether your SDK implementation is working on the new platform, by returning <em>true</em>. If you don’t get a value of <em>true</em>, you can set it to <em>true</em>. Of course, this is best taken care of after you init and then register.</p> <p>Once you’ve confirmed that this toggle returns <code>true</code>, you can proceed to creating your meeting object as below:</p> <pre><code class="language-javascript">webex.meetings.create(“YOUR_DESTINATION”) .then((meeting) =&gt; { console.log(meeting); }); </code></pre> <p>Pretty straightforward as you can see, the code is the same as before so no changes there. However, if you now enter your <code>roomId/spaceId</code> as the destination, you’re going to get an error message stating the following, “*Using the space ID as a destination is no longer supported. Please refer to the <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-Unified-Space-Meetings' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>verifyPassword() migration guide</a> to migrate to use the meeting ID or SIP address.</p> <h6>Verify the Meeting Password</h6><p>As you probably know from the native client application functionality, if you are not part of a space, you generally won’t be able to join any meetings within it. However, there may be cases where you might like to have some users be part of a specific meeting within that space, without being a member of the space.</p> <p>If that’s the case, then you usually need to safely share the meeting password with them. Then, when they authorize through the SDK, and the meeting object is created, they will be required to enter the meeting’s password. You can use the <a href='https://webex.github.io/webex-js-sdk/api/#meetingverifypassword' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>verifyPassword()</a> function to subsequently verify the password entered by the user. Nothing new as it’s been around for a few releases already, but here is a quick code snippet showing how to use it.</p> <div><Callout type="info">At this point the expectation is that the meeting object is already created, called `meeting` below. </Callout></div> <pre><code class="language-javascript">if (meeting &amp;&amp; meeting.passwordStatus === &#39;REQUIRED&#39;){ meeting.verifyPassword(&#39;User_entered_PW&#39;) .then((res) =&gt; { if (res.isPasswordValid) { console.log(&#39;Password is verified&#39;); } }) .catch((err) =&gt; { console.log(&#39;error&#39;, err); throw (err); }); } </code></pre> <p>It’s a simple code sample as you can see, but you can, of course, make it more robust by checking if a captcha is required for example, or any other combination of password and CAPTCHA. If you want to know more about this, you can check out <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Implementing-Password-and-Captcha-Verification-Flows' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>this wiki</a> as it goes into more detail. Also, worth noting that if the user is not part of the space, they may still be put in the lobby until the host admits them. This may depend on the site’s security settings configured in Control Hub, see <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/ov50hy/Webex-best-practices-for-secure-meetings:-Control-Hub' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a> (search for “lobby”).</p> <div><Callout type="info">Don’t forget that you can always invite participants to the meeting through the SDK, using the [invite](https://webex.github.io/webex-js-sdk/api/#meetinginvite) function within the meeting object. </Callout></div> <h6>Reclaim the Host</h6><p>This is a newer feature within the SDK, that allows participants to reclaim the host role. The Migration Guide already does a good job of explaining how to use it, so I’ll just leave the link reference to it <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-js-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space#reclaim-the-host-role' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>.</p> <p>Essentially, it’s using the <a href='https://webex.github.io/webex-js-sdk/api/#membersassignroles' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>assignRole()</a> function and this allows you to set the role of the member/participant to “Moderator”, also passing the <code>hostKey</code> so that it can be validated.</p> <p>At this point, once all the above is taken care of, you can consider your Browser SDK migration complete. As always, please ensure to test your company’s use cases (at least the most common ones) to confirm that all is working as expected. Testing is key to all we do as developers!</p> <h6>The Mobile SDKs</h6><p>This information applies to all our Mobile SDKs and therefore we’ll discuss them together.</p> <p>The respective migration guides for each (here they are again for reference: <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>iOS SDK</a> and <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk/wiki/Migration-to-improved-meetings-associated-with-a-space' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Android SDK</a> migrations) are detailed and provide some sweet code samples to help you get into it. We’ll highlight the key points for them, just to give you a point of reference.</p> <h6>Room/Space IDs are Gone Here Too</h6><p>As with the Browser SDK, the main changes apply to how we’ve removed the ability to use <code>roomId/spaceId</code> to “dial” into a meeting. Now you must use either the meeting number, SIP URI, or meeting URL. As mentioned, the migration guides have detailed code samples for each OS.</p> <p>Essentially, your <code>webex.phone.dial()</code> method should pass in one of the above as dial Inputs, along with the Media Options and <code>CompletionHandler</code>.</p> <p>If you try passing a <code>roomId/spaceId,</code> you’re going to get a <code>CANNOT_START_INSTANT_MEETING</code>error. I’ve highlighted the same error below while debugging our <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk-example' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Android KitchenSink Sample App</a>, to give you an idea. The <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk-example' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>iOS KitchenSink App</a> will also return the same error:</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt75453313a0d014a8/space-meetings-migration-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>And while on the KitchenSink app, it would be worth testing with that, if you’d like to check out these changes. It’s got all the bells and whistles of the SDK, including the new features we’re highlighting.</p> <p>As an example, it also allows the user to manually choose which input to use to dial in, see screenshot below (again, on Android, but the iOS KitchenSink App has the same functionality). You can debug this in the app’s code and see what it actually does (exact code line for my breakpoint on the Android KitchenSink App is <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-android-sdk-example/blob/bd8568ce01829f71754102339f11533e15356f08/app/src/main/java/com/ciscowebex/androidsdk/kitchensink/WebexViewModel.kt#L388' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>here</a>). This serves as a convenient debugging tool, and you can use it to inspect the flows. Of course, in a production application this would be handled directly in the code logic without the need for manual processing, but you get the idea.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt406a231ad1ebd528/space-meetings-migration-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Moving on, the other significant changes are in how the meetings are created, and that’s by using the Meetings API, as explained earlier for the Browser SDK. So, we won’t repeat it here. Same goes for the user who creates the meeting, their licensing will dictate which meeting site the meeting will be hosted on.</p> <h6>Other Features Worth Pointing Out</h6><p>Here are some additional features available in the SDK:</p> <ul> <li>Password/CAPTCHA verification</li> <li>Join meeting as Host</li> <li>Reclaim Host Role</li> <li>Make another participant host</li> <li>Invite another participant</li> </ul> <p>All those are detailed in the migration guides too, with clear code samples. And that’s the Mobile SDKs Migration!</p> <h6>General Tips</h6><p>Some tips that we’re sure you already know but are always worth being reminded of:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Review the Documentation:</strong> Take time to carefully read through the migration guides to understand the changes and how they apply to your applications.</li> <li><strong>Test your Implementation:</strong> Before rolling out changes to production, thoroughly test your updated code to ensure everything works as expected.</li> <li><strong>Stay informed:</strong> Keep an eye on the <a data-type='internal' to='/blog'>Webex Developer Blog</a> and subscribe to our newsletter for the latest updates and best practices.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>We&#39;re Here to Help!</h6><p>We understand that migration to a new system can sometimes be challenging. Our team is dedicated to making this transition as smooth as possible. If you have any questions or need assistance, don&#39;t hesitate to reach out to us through the <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support channels</a>.</p> <p>Happy coding, and we look forward to seeing how you integrate these exciting new changes into your applications!</p> <p>-- The Webex Developer Team</p> ]]>
...
</description>
