<title>
<![CDATA[ Deciphering Topic Modeling Evaluation in Webex Contact Center: Exploring Clusters and Label ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt54eb79935ef52850/660c19ec6c4a3927d0e4631c/new_topic-model-evaluation-webex-developer-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Deciphering Topic Modeling Evaluation in Webex Contact Center: Exploring Clusters and Label" /> <div><Callout type="info">Prasad N Kamath, *Director, Software Engineering*, was a contributor to this blog. </Callout></div> <p>In Webex Contact Center, where a vast amount of customer interactions occurs through various channels like phone calls, and multiple digital channels, topic modeling plays a crucial role in optimizing the operations, enhancing agent performance, and ultimately delivering a more satisfactory customer experience in various ways. Dive into the depths of topic modeling where unsupervised machine learning unveils hidden patterns in vast textual data, from understanding its core principles to navigating complex evaluations, clusters, and natural language labels. The importance of topic model evaluation cannot be overstated as it serves as a critical step in ensuring the effectiveness and reliability of the generated models. Explore the challenges of subjectivity in evaluation and the crucial collaboration needed among experts. With a blend of quantitative metrics and qualitative assessments, discover how various types of topic modeling evolve as an indispensable tool, contributing to knowledge extraction. The blog unveils the challenges, intricacies, and interdisciplinary collaboration required for meaningful insights into the dynamic landscape of natural language processing.</p> <h6>Introduction</h6><p>In the ever-expanding landscape of natural language processing, the quest to extract meaningful information from vast datasets has led to the prominence of topic modeling. Topic modeling is an unsupervised machine learning method that is utilized to categorize, understand, and summarize large collections of textual information. It helps in discovering hidden thematic structures in a vast corpus of text, enabling researchers to discern patterns in unstructured data. The role of topic modeling in Webex Contact Center is pivotal in enhancing operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. The integration of topic modeling in Contact Center brings about a paradigm shift in how customer interactions are managed. However, the effectiveness of a topic model is not solely determined by its ability to extract topics but also by how well those topics are evaluated, organized into clusters, and assigned natural language labels. Evaluating the effectiveness of topic models, understanding topic clusters, and generated topic labels can be a daunting task where the nuances of topic clusters, and crafting natural language topic labels pose intricate challenges. This blog aims to simplify these concepts, offering insights into how best to evaluate topic models and understand their outputs.</p> <h6>Understanding the relation between Topic Modeling and Contact Center</h6><p>Before we delve into the evaluation of topic models, it is crucial to understand what topic modeling is all about. At its core, topic modeling identifies topics in a collection of documents and thus provides a structured representation of the content. It is based on the premise that each document comprises a mixture of topics, and each topic is a collection of words with certain probabilities which can also be represented by a well-formatted natural language label. Internally, the topic modeling algorithm mostly uses an unsupervised mechanism to form distinct clusters of textual information and then discovers the latent themes for each of them which gets further refined in the form of WordCloud or meaningful labels. Supervised processing can also be used in topic modeling with pre-discovered themes or categories. Guided topic modeling is one such pattern where both Supervised and/or Unsupervised approaches can be taken to model the topics.</p> <p>In the context of Webex Contact Center and that way in any Contact Center solution, the role of topic modeling is pivotal in enhancing operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. Topic modeling augments the contact center in various ways:</p> <ul> <li>Automated Categorization: Topic modeling algorithms enable contact centers to automatically categorize and classify incoming customer queries or issues (as part of conversations). This automation streamlines the routing of inquiries to the appropriate departments or agents, ensuring a quicker and more accurate resolution.</li> <li>Agent Training and Knowledge Management: By analyzing customer interactions, topic modeling helps identify recurring issues, concerns, or frequently discussed topics. This information is invaluable for agent training and knowledge management. It allows contact centers to prioritize training on specific topics, ensuring that agents are well-equipped to handle common customer queries.</li> <li>Improving First Contact Resolution (FCR): Topic modeling aids in identifying the primary topics or issues raised by customers. This information empowers agents to address concerns promptly during the initial contact, thereby improving First Contact Resolution rates. Customers benefit from quicker issue resolution, leading to higher satisfaction levels.</li> <li>Enhanced Customer Experience: Understanding the topics that are most relevant to customers allows contact centers to tailor their services and communication strategies. This customization contributes to an enhanced overall customer experience, as customers feel understood and receive more personalized support.</li> <li>Monitoring Trends and Emerging Issues: Topic modeling enables contact centers to monitor trends and identify emerging issues in real time. By staying proactive and addressing emerging concerns promptly, contact centers can prevent potential escalations and demonstrate a commitment to customer satisfaction.</li> </ul> <p>Thus, the integration of topic modeling in contact centers brings about a paradigm shift in how customer interactions are managed. By leveraging advanced algorithms to extract meaningful insights from textual data, contact centers can optimize their operations, enhance agent performance, and ultimately deliver a more satisfactory customer experience.</p> <h6>Understanding Topic Clusters and Generated Topic Labels</h6><p>Topic clusters are groups of similar topics generated by the topic modeling algorithm. Topic modeling aids in summarizing large volumes of text by distilling the main themes into manageable clusters. It enhances search and retrieval systems by associating documents with relevant topics, improving the accuracy of information retrieval as well as facilitating efficient content management. Topic clusters can be visualized using Dimensionality Reduction methods like t-SNE and UMAP, which help in understanding the proximity and overlap between different topics.</p> <p>Natural Language Topic labels, on the other hand, are the phrases that characterize a topic. They provide a succinct summary of the content represented by each topic cluster. These labels are generated by a Language Model based on the major keywords that have the highest probabilities (or likelihood) within each topic. The top words with the highest probabilities usually define the theme of the topic. The generated coherent labels represent the theme in a human-interpretable pattern which should also be cohesive to the topic cluster members.</p> <h6>Evaluation of Topic Modeling</h6><p>The importance of topic model evaluation cannot be overstated as it serves as a critical step in ensuring the effectiveness and reliability of the generated models. Evaluation metrics help gauge how well the models perform on actual datasets and whether their outputs align with the goals of the specific application or task. Evaluating these models is essential for several reasons:</p> <ul> <li>Topic model evaluation helps validate the accuracy and appropriateness of the model in capturing meaningful topics within the given dataset. The evaluation should cover both quantitative and qualitative aspects of topic models and generated topics.</li> <li>Assessing the quality of topics generated by a model is crucial for its practical utility. Evaluation metrics help determine whether the identified topics are coherent, relevant, and distinct. This ensures that the model produces meaningful insights rather than hallucinated or irrelevant themes. Understanding and interpreting the results of topic models are crucial for practical applications. Evaluation metrics help assess the interpretability of topics, ensuring that the generated themes align with the expectations and requirements of end-users.</li> <li>Topic models contain parameters that influence their performance. Evaluation provides insights into the impact of different parameter choices on the model&#39;s effectiveness. Optimizing these parameters is essential for achieving the best possible results in terms of topic quality and coherence.</li> <li>Evaluation facilitates the comparison of different topic models or variations of the same model. Researchers and practitioners can use evaluation metrics to identify which model performs better in terms of topic quality, coherence, and applicability to specific tasks or domains.</li> <li>Evaluating topic models helps assess their robustness and stability across different datasets or variations in input parameters. A robust model should consistently perform well across diverse scenarios, providing reliable results.</li> </ul> <p>Evaluating topic models can be challenging since it&#39;s mostly an unsupervised learning technique in the real world. Moreover, topic modeling algorithms mostly rely on mathematics and statistics. Mathematically we aim to reach a high intra-cluster (within-cluster) similarity and a low inter-cluster (between-cluster) similarity. However, mathematically optimal topics are not necessarily &#39;good&#39; from a human point of view. For data understanding, the topics created need to be human-friendly. So, just blindly following the inherent math behind topic model algorithms can lead us to misleading and meaningless topics. There are various aspects that ought to be considered, such as Topic Cluster Composition, Topic Member Cohesion &amp; Topic Cluster Separation, Topic Label Relevance, etc. On the other hand, qualitative human evaluation of topic modeling is also impracticable to very large datasets with thousands of topics. There are, however, several methods to evaluate the performance of topic models. Some of them are:</p> <ul> <li><p>Topic Coherence: It represents the &#39;quality of human perception&#39; about topics in an objective, and easy-to-evaluate number. It assesses how well a topic is &#39;supported&#39; by a text set. It measures the semantic coherence of words within a topic. Higher coherence scores indicate more interpretable and meaningful topics. However, this method cannot correlate Natural Language Topic Labels with the member text set and instead works with keywords only.</p> </li> <li><p>Perplexity: It is also known as &#39;held out log-likelihood&#39; as logarithm gets used to calculate it. The idea is to train a topic model using the training set and then test the model on a test set that contains previously unseen documents using its predictive ability. This metric does not provide good results for human interpretation.</p> </li> <li><p>Topic Diversity: It assesses the variety of topics generated. A diverse set of topics reflects a more comprehensive representation of the dataset.</p> </li> <li><p>Internal Validation: This evaluation mechanism uses internally available clustering information to assess the goodness of the clusters. Internal validation measures rely on the compactness and the separation of the cluster partitions. Predominantly most of the indices used in internal clustering validation combine compactness and separation measures.</p> <ul> <li>Silhouette Score: It represents the intra-cluster and inter-cluster variation. The Score can vary between -1 (incorrect clustering) and 1 (dense clustering). A score of 0 indicates overlapping clusters. It is higher when Topic Clusters are dense and well separated. Silhouette Score is more popular for Centroid-based clustering algorithms like K-Means (biased towards Spherical Clusters).</li> <li>Validity Index: This index is used in Density-based clustering. It assesses clustering quality using the relative density connection between pairs of objects. The Score can vary between -1 and 1 with higher values indicating a ‘better’ clustering. (it is different from relative validity which is a fast approximation-based score used to compare results across different combinations of hyper-parameters). This index can assess any number of arbitrarily shaped clusters.</li> <li>Miscellaneous Indices: Indices like the Dunn Index, DB Index, and CH (Calinski-Harabasz) Index are more useful for comparing various clustering models in Centroid-based Clustering.</li> </ul> <div><Callout type="info">In Density-based Clustering "Sample Probability" can also be used to assess the quality of the generated clusters. It shows the strength with which each sample becomes a member of its assigned cluster. Noise points have zero probability. </Callout></div> </li> <li><p>External Validation: It validates the clustering output against an external reference.</p> </li> <li><p>Manual Evaluation: This involves human evaluators who rate the quality and relevance of the topics generated along with the generated labels. It might be time-consuming but often provides the most reliable evaluation.</p> </li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Evaluation of Topic Clusters and Topic Labels</h6><p>Evaluating topic clusters and labels is largely a qualitative process. Here are some steps to follow:</p> <ul> <li>Diversity: Good topics should be different from each other. If many topics seem similar, it might signify an issue with the model, or the number of topics chosen.</li> <li>Completeness: A good topic should cover a concept or an idea completely. If a topic seems to cover more than one concept, it might indicate that the model isn&#39;t able to distinguish between them effectively.</li> <li>Understandability: Check if the topics make sense. Is the label in each topic properly representing the theme of the topic? Are the major keywords in each topic semantically related?</li> <li>Relevance: The topic labels (&amp; in turn major keywords) should be relevant to the overall content of your corpus.</li> </ul> <br/> <h6>Challenges &amp; Proposed Approach</h6><p>Subjectivity in the evaluation poses a major challenge in Topic Modeling. Evaluating topic modeling goes beyond quantitative metrics as standard evaluation metrics may not always capture the subjective nature of topics. If a topic model is used for a measurable task, such as classification, then its effectiveness is relatively easier to calculate. However, if the model is used for a more qualitative task, such as exploring the semantic themes in an unstructured corpus, then evaluation is more difficult. It involves understanding the semantic coherence, diversity, and relevance of identified topics which suggests a combination of quantitative and qualitative assessments. On top of that, the generated Topic Clusters may not always take a &#39;Spherical shape&#39;. Most of the time in the Contact Center world the clusters are of an &#39;Arbitrary&#39; pattern due to the nature of the domain-specific conversations. While quantitative measures like various indices, probability, perplexity, and coherence are helpful, the qualitative evaluation of topic clusters and natural language labels by human annotators or equivalent still remains a reliable method of evaluation.</p> <p>The following algorithm has laid out a similar mixed evaluation approach for the Centroid-based and Density-based clustering models where we have used a combination of interpretation-driven qualitative (akin to judgment-based) and quantitative approaches.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt08e0e770c79c677a/new_topic-model-evaluation-webex-developer-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt8896b134d02d1f48/new_topic-model-evaluation-webex-developer-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>As part of the quantitative evaluation calculate the recommended score and index (as per the Clustering Model) for each topic cluster. The prescribed algorithm has already chosen the most appropriate set of metrics based on their popularity, applicability, and interpretability. Depending on the predefined configurable thresholds for each metric, the clusters have been graded accordingly.</p> <p>During the qualitative assessment, we have used multiple pre-trained natural language models to calculate the cluster members&#39; logical (aka Entailment) and semantic alignment (semantic similarity) with the respective topic label. Here also we have used configurable thresholds for both entailment score and angular similarity to grade the clusters.</p> <p>Finally, we have aggregated all the categories as per configurable weighting of quantitative and qualitative assessments and graded the overall topic modeling.</p> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>Topic modeling is a powerful tool that assists in uncovering hidden structures in text data, and its evaluation, although challenging, is crucial for the success of your machine-learning project. The intricacies of topic modeling evaluation, topic clusters, and generated natural language topic labels highlight the interdisciplinary nature of this field. As technology advances, addressing these complexities becomes pivotal for the continued refinement of models and the extraction of meaningful insights from the ever-expanding sea of textual data. It mandates persistent collaboration between domain experts, linguists, and data scientists. Embracing the challenges, researchers and practitioners contribute to the evolution of topic modeling, making it an indispensable tool in the quest for knowledge and understanding within the vast realms of natural language processing. By leveraging advanced Topic Modeling algorithms, Contact Centers in turn can optimize their operations, enhance agent performance, and ultimately deliver a more satisfactory customer experience.</p> ]]>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Revamping the iOS Kitchen Sink UI for Enhanced Developer Experience with SwiftUI ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt4551c6a9d3007f93/65fc914cfc8631eb1ed735b2/kitchensink-ios-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Revamping the iOS Kitchen Sink UI for Enhanced Developer Experience with SwiftUI" /> <p>The <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk-example' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex iOS Kitchen Sink</a> application, known for demonstrating the versatility and capabilities of the Webex iOS SDK, has undergone a transformative update that pushes the boundaries of modern app design and functionality. As the tech world continuously evolves, so does the need for industry-standard, efficient, and easily testable code. With the latest revamp using SwiftUI, the Kitchen Sink app not only serves as a comprehensive example for using the Webex iOS SDK but also sets a benchmark for production-ready application design.</p> <h6>Why Revamp?</h6><p>In the challenging environment of software development, staying up to date with the latest technologies is crucial. The original Kitchen Sink UI, while functional, required a refresh to match the current industry standards and expectations. By incorporating SwiftUI, we have significantly improved the development experience, offering modularity, ease of testing, and a sleek, responsive interface that is both faster and more efficient.</p> <h6>Modularity and Testability</h6><p>One of the key features of the revamped Kitchen Sink application is its modular design. We’ve meticulously restructured the codebase to ensure that all Webex SDK-related code resides within a dedicated ‘Webex’ folder, making it incredibly straightforward for developers to navigate and understand the structure. Each class is self-contained, promoting better organization and modularity, which, in turn, enhances testability. </p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt37b21b87e3cc6f19/kitchensink-ios-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Copy-Paste Friendly Code</h6><p>Recognizing the importance of ease of use, the new Kitchen Sink codebase is designed to be copy-paste friendly. Developers can effortlessly extract the code snippets they need for implementing Webex SDK APIs in their own apps. This reduces the learning curve and accelerates the development process. Users can re-use the Messaging UIs for their application to enhance the UX.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt08128aa7982d6aee/kitchensink-ios-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>The Benefits of SwiftUI</h6><p>SwiftUI is Apple’s latest framework for declarative UI structure design. By leveraging SwiftUI in the Kitchen Sink app, we’ve unlocked a realm of benefits:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Faster Development</strong>: SwiftUI’s declarative syntax simplifies UI development, allowing developers to create complex interfaces quickly and with fewer lines of code.</li> <li><strong>Enhanced Performance</strong>: SwiftUI is optimized for performance, ensuring that the Kitchen Sink UI is responsive and smooth.</li> <li><strong>Live Previews</strong>: Developers can now immediately see the effects of their code changes, thanks to SwiftUI’s live preview feature, thereby speeding up the iteration process.</li> <li><strong>Cross-platform Consistency</strong>: SwiftUI enables the Kitchen Sink app to maintain a consistent look and feel across all Apple devices, promoting a unified user experience.</li> </ol> <br/> <h6>Production-Ready Application</h6><p>The revamped Kitchen Sink is not just a sample app — it’s a production-ready blueprint. The use cases and UI are crafted to align closely with the real-world requirements of customers using the SDK. By presenting a polished and fully functional application, developers can derive inspiration for their projects, ensuring that their apps are up to par with the highest industry standards.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf556b71153587667/kitchensink-ios-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <h6>Conclusion</h6><p>The revamp of the Kitchen Sink UI is a testament to our commitment to providing developers with the best tools and examples to work with the Webex iOS SDK. With a focus on modularity, testability, and the adoption of SwiftUI, the Kitchen Sink app is poised to inspire and facilitate the creation of top-tier applications. By embracing these changes, developers can now look forward to a more intuitive and efficient coding experience as they integrate Webex functionalities into their apps.</p> <h6>GitHub Repository</h6><p>For those eager to dive into the code and explore the new Kitchen Sink UI, visit the GitHub repository at <a href='https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk-example' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://github.com/webex/webex-ios-sdk-example</a> and start leveraging the power of SwiftUI in your Webex SDK projects today.</p> ]]>

</description>

<title>
<![CDATA[ Webex for Developers Newsletter – March 2024 ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt763a01e711986781/61f8604bd970ea1bb42acf6f/Picture1.jpg?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Webex for Developers Newsletter – March 2024" /> <p>Hello Webex Developers! We have some great stories, updates, and other tidbits in this month&#39;s newsletter that will bring you up to date. So, let’s get right to it and catch up on all the latest news in the Webex Developer community.</p> <h6>⚙️Creating Navigation Widgets in Webex Contact Center</h6><p>Continuing our blog series about the customization of Webex Contact Center widgets, we now turn our attention to the broad possibilities offered by navigation widgets in <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/enhancing-agent-productivity-by-creating-navigation-widgets-in-webex-contact-center'>our latest post</a> from the leader of Webex Developer Evangelism, Adam Weeks. Learn how to easily add tabs to the main menu, personalize with Momentum icons, and configure the <code>layout.json</code> file for an optimized agent desktop experience.</p> <h6>🔐Traversing Webex Contact Center API Authorization with Ease</h6><p>The Webex Contact Center platform offers a streamlined authorization process designed to protect and simplify user authorization for integrations. Get acclimated with the authorization flow for the Contact Center APIs in a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/navigating-webex-contact-center-api-authentication-with-ease'>new blog post</a> by Senior Developer Evangelist, Phil Bellanti. In this article, you will learn how to configure <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/webex-contact-center'>Contact Center integrations</a>, select the proper scopes, leverage the OAuth2 grant flow for secure API transactions, and manage tokens effectively.</p> <h6>📺Webex Developer Public Webinars</h6><p>On April 24th at 1:00PM ET, join our public webinar for an <a href='https://evangelism.webex.com/weblink/register/r031a0e52e15892c8edbc367bbaaf61da' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Introduction to the Webex Contact Center Flow Designer</a>. Flow Designer is a no-low, no-code orchestration platform and developer ecosystem for building custom integrations in Webex Contact Center. We will cover a variety of use cases, run a live demo, and have our great partner, Journey ID, join us to showcase an amazing Flow Designer powered Customer Authentication workflow. <a href='https://evangelism.webex.com/weblink/register/r031a0e52e15892c8edbc367bbaaf61da' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Register</a> for the live event today!</p> <p>Also, in case you missed our last public webinar, <strong>Upgrade Your App with Webex Meetings SDK V3</strong>, you can now watch that and other past recordings on our <a data-type='internal' to='/webinars'>webinars page</a>.</p> <h6>☁️Practical Guide to Hosting a Webex Integration on AWS</h6><p>Have you built a Webex integration application and ready to take on the task of hosting it in the cloud? AWS is a very popular choice for hosting, with an extensive amount of service offerings for managing applications at scale. For a quick start on hosting a Webex integration in AWS, check out <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/practical-guide-to-hosting-a-webex-integration-on-aws'>this new blog</a> by Community Technical Manager, Eugene Morozov. You will be guided step-by-step to deploy a moderately complex application in AWS using <em>Elastic Beanstalk</em> and <em>Code Pipeline</em>.</p> <h6>🕵️Introducing SCIM2.0: Streamlined User Identity Management on Webex</h6><p>In a <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/introducing-scim2-0-revolutionizing-user-identity-management-on-webex'>recent blog</a> by Engineering Product Manager, Janelle Allen explains that Webex now leverages the SCIM2.0 standard to streamline user identity management and automate provisioning tasks. Janelle goes through what the SCIM 2.0 standard entails and the potential ways it can foster more innovative solutions.</p> <h6>🦾The AI-Powered Webex Suite</h6><p>As Webex Suite is built on an extensible platform, it benefits from top-notch AI innovations, built-in security, and a single pane of glass management via <a href='https://www.webex.com/control-hub.html"' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Control Hub</a>. In a <a href='https://blog.webex.com/collaboration-devices/new-ways-to-collaborate-ai-powered-webex-suite/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>new blog</a> by Director of Product Marketing, Manu Parhar, learn the ways Webex is revolutionizing collaboration with eight new “out of the box” AI workflows for every industry.</p> <h6>📝Webex API Changelog Highlights</h6><p>The <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/changelog'>Webex API Changelog</a> has several recent entries listed. We always recommend checking that page frequently to stay up to date. Here are some important ones to note:</p> <ul> <li><strong>March 20, 2024 - NEW:</strong> New attributes, <code>createJoinLinkAsWebLink</code> and <code>createStartLinkAsWebLink</code>, have been added to the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/meetings/join-a-meeting'>Join a Meeting</a> API, which can be used to specify <code>webLink</code> as a <code>joinLink</code> or a <code>startLink</code>. Those are typically useful if mandatory user login is configured in Control Hub.</li> <li><strong>March 18, 2024 – UPCOMING BREAKING CHANGES:</strong> In the near future, there will be some important changes to the Webex Calling APIs, Wholesale Subscriber Provisioning APIs, and OAuth methodology for integrations. Please check the full API changelog for detailed information on these update notices.</li> <li><strong>March 7, 2024 - NEW:</strong> In the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/virtual-line-call-settings'>Virtual Line Call Settings API</a>, we&#39;ve added multiple endpoints that let you manage all Virtual Lines call settings.</li> </ul> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Navigating Webex Contact Center API Authentication with Ease ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt6fd65e60318c64eb/65f892cd6119726102646a5e/wxcc-auth-blog-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Navigating Webex Contact Center API Authentication with Ease" /> <p>Cisco understands that secure API interactions are fundamental for all enterprise developers. The Webex Contact Center platform is no exception, offering a streamlined authorization process designed to protect and simplify user authorization for integrations. This article will provide a high-level summary of how integrations are configured and authorized for the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/webex-contact-center'>Webex Contact Center APIs</a>.</p> <p>Keep in mind that Webex Contact Center has a robust set of APIs that can power a variety of integration use cases. For example, a <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/tree/main/call-recording-samples' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>call recording application</a> utilized by a banking &amp; finance contact center, where conversations must be archived for compliance requirements. Another example is an integration that utilizes the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/tree/main/configuration-samples' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Configuration APIs</a> to automate contact center provisioning, for bulk onboarding of agents and teams. To learn more about the Contact Center integration APIs, check out this <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/introducing-the-webex-contact-center-apis-and-developer-portal'>introductory blog</a>.</p> <h6>Authorization for Integrations</h6><p>Webex uses the <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/real-world-walkthrough-of-building-an-oauth-webex-integration'>OAuth2 grant flow</a> standard to securely authorize integrations. The grant flow is a multi-step process that essentially goes like this:</p> <ol> <li>The integration directs the end-user to the Webex authorization server with a request that includes the application&#39;s identity, requested permissions (scopes), and a redirect URI.</li> <li>The end-user logs in (if not already authenticated) and grants the requested permissions to the integration.</li> <li>Upon consent, Webex issues an authorization grant code to the integration via the “redirect URI”.</li> <li>The integration exchanges the authorization grant for an access token by making a server-to-server request to the Webex token endpoint.</li> <li>With the access token, the integration can interact with the Webex API on behalf of the authorized user, within the scope of the granted permissions.</li> </ol> <p>This process ensures that user credentials are not shared with the integration, providing a secure method for authentication and authorization.</p> <h6>Configuring a Webex Contact Center Integration</h6><p>Those who have previously created <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/integrations'>integrations</a> for the Webex suite on <a href='http://developer.webex.com/' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>developer.webex.com</a> will notice the steps are quite similar for creating Webex Contact Center integrations. When creating a new Webex Contact Center integration, it starts on the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs'>Webex Contact Center for Developers</a> portal. After logging into the Contact Center for Developers portal, simply hover the cursor over the avatar on the top-left corner and click “My Webex Apps”.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt40490ac878e5c62e/wxcc-auth-blog-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>On the “My Apps” page, click the blue “Create a New App” to start registering the integration.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt047e865989a8e5c5/wxcc-auth-blog-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>This lands on the “New App Integration” registration form. The integration will need a name and a short description in the specified fields. </p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltebd3f94365ac14a6/wxcc-auth-blog-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>The remaining fields are more technical. First, the &quot;Redirect URI&quot;, which is used to point the end-user&#39;s client back to the integration and tell Webex where to send the authorization code upon completion of the grant flow. The value can contain one or multiple URIs for the hosted integration app and must be HTTPS. </p> <p>The last part of the form is for selecting the level of access the integration will require, called “scopes”. For example, a <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/journey-data-service'>Customer Journey Data Service (CJDS)</a> integration that retrieves and modifies engagement data would utilize the <code>cjds:admin_org_read</code> and <code>cjds:admin_org_write</code> scopes. When the integration is initiated, these scopes appear as permission requests that the end-user will need to accept to grant the application access to their Webex account. As a general rule, developers should only select the minimal number of scopes required for that specific integration to operate. To read more about Webex Contact Center APIs scopes and definitions, see the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/guides/integrations#scopes'>overview guide</a>.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltc3249e99ba4c3af1/wxcc-auth-blog-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Once the terms are accepted, the “Add Integration” button can be clicked. </p> <h6>API Access and Refresh Tokens</h6><p>After completing those steps, the integration application is now enabled to authorize with the Webex Contact Center platform and obtain an API access token &amp; refresh token. Both tokens are essential for maintaining a secure and continuous interaction with the Webex Contact Center APIs. The access token is used for short-term access and the refresh token enables long-term access by allowing the application to refresh the access token as needed. </p> <p>All of the steps for authentication and retrieving the tokens are documented <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/authentication-cc#step-1-requesting-permission'>here</a>.</p> <p>Once the grant flow is complete, the tokens are sent in a JSON payload that will look something like this: </p> <pre><code class="language-json">{ &#39;access_token&#39;: &#39;Yzd9abc55ef459fe67_D0C2_g6abc12e-4711-9rf8-6543-d33d0394gz55&#39;, &#39;expires_in&#39;: 1209599, &#39;refresh_token&#39;:Yzc7adce67c62d7709ge6n_D0C2_g6abc12e-4711-9rf8-6543-d33d0394gz55&#39;, &#39;refresh_token_expires_in&#39;: 6322470, &#39;token_type&#39;: &#39;Bearer&#39;, &#39;scope&#39;: &#39;cjp:user spark:people_read cjp:config cjp:config_read&#39; } </code></pre> <p>The values for the expiration of the tokens are output in seconds. For clarity, the initial access token expires in 14 days and the refresh token expires in 90 days. Keep in mind, once the refresh token expires, the user will need to reauthorize the integration again. However, whenever as long as the refresh token is used to refresh access tokens, the refresh token expiration timer will be reset back to zero. This allows the refresh token to essentially be used in perpetuity and the user will not need to reauthorize the application. For more information, <a data-type='internal' to='/blog/real-world-walkthrough-of-building-an-oauth-webex-integration'>this blog</a> has a great overview of the entire OAuth process for Webex integrations and developer strategies for implementing it. </p> <p>The final part of the token JSON payload provides the scopes associated with the token, that were configured when the integration was created on the portal. These scope values can be leveraged by an integration to conditionally present features, access data, or other actions dependent on permission levels. </p> <h6>Data Inside the Token</h6><p>The token values in the payload also contain helpful “hidden” data - the <code>orgID</code> that correlates to the organization the authorized user belongs to. The <code>orgID</code> value is a required parameter for many of the API endpoints, including the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/users'>Users API</a>. The only other method for obtaining an <code>orgID</code> is through the <a data-type='internal' to='/docs/api/v1/people/get-my-own-details'>/people API</a> with the <code>spark:people_read</code> scope and returns it in a Base64 encrypted format. However, the token string from the JSON payload already reveals the unencrypted <code>orgID</code> value. This makes it an ideal place to retrieve it from without having to perform another API call or further decryption.</p> <p>The <code>orgID</code> is always found after the final “<code>_</code>” in a token string. To see how the encoded <code>orgID</code> can easily be separated from the token, check out the <a href='https://github.com/WebexSamples/webex-contact-center-api-samples/blob/main/app-auth-sample/server.js#L147' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>app-auth-sample</a> in Webex CC Github repo, starting on line 147:</p> <pre><code class="language-js">let [accessToken, ciCluster, orgId] = loginDetails.access_token.split(&#39;_&#39;); </code></pre> <p>Now that the <code>orgID</code> has been retrieved, it can be used for subsequent API calls. In this example cURL script, the <code>orgID</code> is sent in a GET query to the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/api/v1/users/list-users'>List Users API</a> with the <code>cjp:config_read</code> scope:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">curl --request GET \ --url &#39;https://api.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/organization/g6abc12e-4711-9rf8-6543-d33d0394gz55/v2/user?page=0&amp;amp;pageSize=10&amp;amp;filter=id%3D%3D57efb0e6-5af0-4245- d3c5045cdb6e&amp;amp;attributes=id%2Cactive&#39; \ --header &#39;Accept: application/json&#39; \ --header &#39;Authorization: Bearer Yzd9abc55ef459fe67_D0C2_g6abc12e-4711-9rf8-6543-d33d0394gz55&#39; </code></pre> <p>The response for that API query would look something like this:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">[ { &quot;active&quot;: false, &quot;agentProfileId&quot;: &quot;8e6bb6da-2a78-4768-bef9-7e229f92af22&quot;, &quot;broadCloudUserId&quot;: &quot;1dq21e23-1234-5578-9a83-2afdae0d4ba1&quot;, &quot;ciUserId&quot;: &quot;1dq21e23-1234-5578-9a83-2afdae0d4ba1&quot;, &quot;contactCenterEnabled&quot;: false, &quot;createdTime&quot;: 1617536244000, &quot;dbId&quot;: &quot;1dq45f23-1234-6r18-9a83-2atuiy0d4bh1&quot;, &quot;defaultDialledNumber&quot;: &quot;1234567890&quot;, &quot;email&quot;: &quot;johnwick@company.com&quot;, &quot;externalIdentifier&quot;: &quot;121212&quot;, &quot;firstName&quot;: &quot;John&quot;, &quot;id&quot;: &quot;93912f11-6017-404b-bf14-5331890b1797&quot;, &quot;imiUserCreated&quot;: false, &quot;lastName&quot;: &quot;Wick&quot;, &quot;lastUpdatedTime&quot;: 1617536244000, &quot;mobile&quot;: &quot;1234567890&quot;, &quot;multimediaProfileId&quot;: &quot;f53c8b54-46ca-43f6-ba05-08426a46e23d&quot;, &quot;organizationId&quot;: &quot;f53c8b54-46ca-43f6-ba05-08426a46e23d&quot;, &quot;preferredSupervisorTeamId&quot;: &quot;e27d2b54-46ca-43g6-ba65-08426e46e23d&quot;, &quot;siteId&quot;: &quot;1dq21e23-1234-5578-9a83-2afdae0d4ba1&quot;, &quot;skillProfileId&quot;: &quot;f53c8b54-46ca-43f6-ba05-08426a46e23d&quot;, &quot;subscriptionId&quot;: &quot;04d0bdf6-6d6a-4aae-8a8a-71c9152e6478&quot;, &quot;teamIds&quot;: &quot;[\&quot;f53c8b54-46ca-43f6-ba05-08426a46e23d\&quot;,\&quot;a53c8b54-46ca-43f6-ba05-08426a46e23f\&quot;]&quot;, &quot;timezone&quot;: &quot;America/New_York&quot;, &quot;userProfileId&quot;: &quot;1dq21e23-1234-5578-9a83-2afdae0d4ba1&quot;, &quot;version&quot;: 1, &quot;workPhone&quot;: &quot;1234567890&quot;, &quot;xspVersion&quot;: &quot;xsp-24.0&quot; } ] </code></pre> <p>Again, you will find many other Contact Center API endpoints that require the <code>orgID</code> and this is just one example. Having that value right from the start will make things more efficient. </p> <h6>Questions? We Got You Covered!</h6><p>We are continually updating our developer platform with new features, tools, and documentation for building powerful Contact Center integrations. If you need help along the way, our <a data-type='internal' to='/support'>Webex Developer Support Team</a> is standing by and ready to assist. You can also start or join a conversation on the <a href='https://community.cisco.com/t5/contact-center/bd-p/j-disc-dev-contact-center' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Contact Center API Developer Community forum</a>.</p> ]]>

<item>
<title>
<![CDATA[ Enhancing Agent Productivity by Creating Navigation Widgets in Webex Contact Center ]]>
...
</title>
<description>
<![CDATA[ <img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltf870ad64dfe47510/65eb47eba991866239e7bb03/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-1.png?width=900&height=317&fit=crop" alt="Enhancing Agent Productivity by Creating Navigation Widgets in Webex Contact Center" /> <p>Building on our blog series about the customization of Webex Contact Center widgets, we now turn our attention to the broad possibilities offered by navigation widgets. Unlike other widget types, navigation widgets provide developers with an entire page to customize, including its own unique URL path. This ability opens up a world of opportunities, allowing developers to integrate comprehensive views into external data sources, such as dashboards or databases, directly within the Webex Contact Center. Let&#39;s find out how you can harness the full potential of navigation widgets for an improved agent desktop experience.</p> <div><Callout type="info">You can find out more information about all of the different Webex Contact Center agent desktop widget types [here](/blog/unlocking-the-power-of-custom-widgets-in-webex-contact-center). </Callout></div> <h6>Full Page Power</h6><p>Navigation widgets are not confined to a small portion of the screen; they command an entire page. This expansive canvas enables developers to design more complex and rich interfaces, integrating full-scale applications right into the Webex Contact Center. Agents can access these applications without toggling between different browser tabs or systems, streamlining their workflow and increasing productivity.</p> <p>One of the standout features of Webex Contact Center is the ease with which agents can access various tools and applications needed for their daily tasks. Navigation widgets enhance this accessibility by adding customized tabs to the side main menu of the Webex Contact Center desktop. With just a click, agents can access the custom page without leaving the Contact Center environment.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt826f240e03a0bc97/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-2.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text.">.</p> <p>One example of proper utilization of these full-page navigation widgets is <a href='https://apphub.webex.com/applications/novelvox-agent-accelerator' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Agent Accelerator</a> which is a uniquely integrated, unified agent desktop interface that empowers agents with a single pane of glass view by unifying information from multiple disparate systems including core-industry apps, backend systems, databases, CRMs, and more. The integrations fuel new efficiency among agents and enable faster resolution of queries without spending time on unnecessary screen toggling. Furthermore, having effortless access to complete customer information helps drive personalization and higher customer satisfaction.</p> <h6>Create Your Navigation Widget</h6><p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltd1f6a4bf36ce4cf2/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-3.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."> </p> <p>As mentioned in the previous blogs, Agent Desktop customization begins with editing the desktop layout file. If you&#39;re familiar with the <code>layout.json</code> file, you might recognize that it can appear quite complex at first glance. However, once you understand its structure, particularly the &quot;<code>agent</code>&quot; section outlined above, it becomes a powerful tool for customization. All the adjustments we&#39;ll be making should be nested within the &quot;<code>agent.area.navigation</code>&quot; array. For each Navigation Widget, there are two key property objects to consider: &quot;<code>nav</code>&quot; and &quot;<code>page</code>.&quot; The &quot;<code>nav</code>&quot; object is where you define the widget&#39;s presence in the main menu, while the &quot;<code>page</code>&quot; object provides the space to fully flesh out the widget&#39;s page configuration.</p> <h6>Easy Navigation Access</h6><p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blt93a2a1a15f0e1385/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-4.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>The custom tabs you add to the navigation bar aren&#39;t just gateways to information; they&#39;re also customizable elements that reflect your organization&#39;s branding and user interface preferences. You have the power to configure the icon, text, and URL for each navigation widget, providing a seamless and personalized experience for your agents.</p> <p>For the icon, you can quickly customize it using <a href='https://momentum.design/icons' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Momentum Icons</a>—a comprehensive icon library that&#39;s part of the Momentum Design System. These icons are optimized for Cisco&#39;s ecosystem and do not require an additional library to be loaded, thus maintaining your application&#39;s performance.</p> <p>To incorporate Momentum Icons into your navigation widget, follow these simple steps:</p> <ul> <li>Visit the Momentum Design Icons page: <a href='https://momentum.design/icons' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Momentum Design Icons</a></li> <li>Browse and select an icon that best represents the function of your custom page.</li> <li>Use the icon&#39;s name in your <code>layout.json</code> configuration for the navigation widget.</li> </ul> <p>Here&#39;s a snippet of how you might configure a navigation widget with a Momentum icon:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">&quot;nav&quot;: { &quot;label&quot;: &quot;Custom Page&quot;, &quot;icon&quot;: &quot;dashboard&quot;, &quot;iconType&quot;: &quot;momentum&quot;, &quot;navigateTo&quot;: &quot;custom-page-sample&quot;, &quot;align&quot;: &quot;top&quot; } </code></pre> <p>In the above example, “<code>dashboard</code>” is the name of the Momentum icon chosen to represent a custom dashboard. You’ll also notice “<code>custom-page-sample</code>” is the value for “<code>navigateTo</code>”. This is the path to your custom page. So, if <a href='https://desktop.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/custom-page-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://desktop.wxcc-us1.cisco.com</a> is the location of your agent desktop, the path to your page will be <a href='https://desktop.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/custom-page-sample' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>https://desktop.wxcc-us1.cisco.com/custom-page-sample</a>.</p> <h6>Grid Layout</h6><p>Before we get into the specifics of <code>layout.json</code> for Webex Contact Center, let&#39;s touch on the underlying technology that makes these layouts possible—<a href='https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_Grid_Layout/Basic_Concepts_of_Grid_Layout' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>CSS Grid Layout</a>. This CSS layout method is designed for the two-dimensional layout of items on a webpage, making it perfect for arranging elements into rows and columns. Some basic concepts that are utilized in Webex Contact Center include:</p> <ul> <li>Containers and Items: In CSS Grid, the parent element becomes a grid container with child elements as grid items.</li> <li>Columns and Rows: You can define the number and size of rows and columns in your grid.</li> </ul> <p>Now, let&#39;s translate these CSS grid concepts into the realm of Webex Contact Center&#39;s <code>layout.json</code> configuration.</p> <h6>1x1 Grid Example</h6><p>For a straightforward layout that focuses on a single task or view, a 1x1 grid is ideal. This layout showcases one widget in full view, making it the center of attention for the agent. In this example, we are loading a page in an iFrame which takes up the full view.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/blte678ea002bb059ef/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-5.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Here is the code that you can use to generate this page:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">&quot;page&quot;: { &quot;id&quot;: &quot;iframe-widget&quot;, &quot;widgets&quot;: { &quot;iframe1&quot;: { &quot;comp&quot;: &quot;agentx-wc-iframe&quot;, &quot;attributes&quot;: { &quot;src&quot;: &quot;https://example.com&quot; } } }, &quot;layout&quot;: { &quot;areas&quot;: [[&quot;iframe1&quot;]], &quot;size&quot;: { &quot;cols&quot;: [1], &quot;rows&quot;: [1] } } } </code></pre> <h6>2x2 Grid Example</h6><p>A slightly more complex layout, such as a 2x2 grid, can facilitate access to multiple tools and data sources simultaneously. In this example, we have 4 different iFrame widgets (all pointing to the same URL for brevity) being displayed on our custom page.</p> <p><img src="https://images.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltd74e2c7e18c68b20/bltea123c69d67c7391/dxdoc-3339-wxcc-navigation-widgets-6.png" alt="Image described in surrounding text."></p> <p>Here is the layout code that results in the above view:</p> <pre><code class="language-json">&quot;layout&quot;: { &quot;areas&quot;: [ [&quot;iframe1&quot;, &quot;iframe2&quot;], [&quot;iframe3&quot;, &quot;iframe4&quot;] ], &quot;size&quot;: { &quot;cols&quot;: [1,1], &quot;rows&quot;: [1,1] } } </code></pre> <h6>Diving Deeper</h6><p>These are just some basic examples to get you started with custom page layouts. Be sure to check out our <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs/desktop'>Desktop Guide</a> for more information on the Agent Desktop customization. For the full reference, visit the <a href='https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/n5595zd/Webex-Contact-Center-Setup-and-Administration-Guide#Cisco_Concept.dita_a9771889-dbb1-4760-823e-cbb2536a2bda' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>Webex Contact Center Setup and Administration Guide</a> and search for the “layout” section.</p> <h6>Wrapping Up</h6><p>Navigation widgets are a game-changer for developers looking to enhance the Webex Contact Center agent desktop. By providing a full page for customization and the ability to link to external data through unique URL paths, they open up new possibilities for creating an immersive and efficient workspace. Whether you&#39;re embedding complex dashboards or displaying critical data interfaces from external systems that your agents can interact with, navigation widgets empower you to bring everything together in a cohesive and accessible manner.</p> <p>Stay tuned for our next entry in this series, where we will continue to explore the vast customization options available in Webex Contact Center. In the meantime, we encourage you to experiment with the <code>layout.json</code> file and witness the transformative impact of navigation widgets on your Contact Center operations.</p> <p>For further guidance and inspiration, remember to visit the <a data-type='internal' to='/webex-contact-center/docs'>Webex Contact Center for Developers Portal</a> and join the conversation with our vibrant <a href='https://community.cisco.com/t5/contact-center/webex-contact-center-apis-developer-community-and-support/td-p/4558270' rel='noopener noreferrer' target='_blank'>developer community</a>. Let&#39;s build a seamless and powerful agent experience, together.</p> ]]>
...
